author: vieiralucas
body: ## Summary Fixes three production request-path panics found by the 2026-06-18 code-quality audit. Each is reachable from malformed-but-accepted input and drops the client connection (DoS): 1. **S3 `UploadPartCopy`** (`s3/service/multipart.rs`) - a `x-amz-copy-source-range` with `start > end`, or any range over a 0-byte source object, underflowed `len()-1` and sliced past the buffer. Now range-validated -> `InvalidArgument`. Brings it to parity with the guards the GetObject range path already has. 2. **SQS `ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch`** (`sqs/service/messages.rs`) - an out-of-range `VisibilityTimeout` overflowed `now + Duration::seconds(..)`. The single-op `ChangeMessageVisibility` already rejects values outside `0..=43200`; the batch loop did not. Now emits a per-entry `InvalidParameterValue` failure (valid entries in the same batch still succeed). 3. **S3 `SelectObjectContent` `WHERE ... LIKE`** (`s3/select.rs`) - the `LIKE` offset came from a `to_uppercase()` copy whose byte length can differ from the original (e.g. `U+FB00` -> `FF`), so slicing the original could panic on a non-char-boundary. Replaced with a case-insensitive ASCII-keyword search over the original bytes. ## Test plan - `cargo test -p fakecloud-s3 --lib select::tests::parse_where` - multibyte-column LIKE no longer panics + case-insensitive LIKE. - `cargo test -p fakecloud-e2e --test s3 s3_upload_part_copy_bad_range_returns_error_not_panic` - inverted range + empty-source copy both error, server stays responsive. - `cargo test -p fakecloud-e2e --test sqs sqs_change_message_visibility_batch_rejects_out_of_range` - out-of-range entry soft-fails with `InvalidParameterValue`, valid entry in same batch succeeds. - `cargo clippy -p fakecloud-s3 -p fakecloud-sqs -p fakecloud-e2e --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes three request-path panics in S3 and SQS that could drop client connections. Adds strict validation and safe parsing so malformed input returns errors instead of crashing. - **Bug Fixes** - S3 UploadPartCopy: validate `x-amz-copy-source-range`; reject `start > end`, `end` past last byte, and any range on empty sources with `InvalidArgument` (parity with GetObject). - SQS ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch: enforce `VisibilityTimeout` in `0..=43200`; out-of-range entries return `InvalidParameterValue` while valid entries succeed. - S3 SelectObjectContent WHERE ... LIKE: replace `to_uppercase()` offset logic with an ASCII case-insensitive keyword search on original bytes at char boundaries to avoid char-boundary panics; LIKE stays case-insensitive. Written for commit 077f6bce910155006bce9564f944525cc0653c62. Summary will update on new commits.

author: rtelenta
body:
## What

- Adds a "Send Test" button to the template editor header that sends the current template to the logged-in user's own email address
- Enforces a hard cap of 100 test emails per user per rolling 24-hour window (429 with a `resetAt` timestamp when exceeded)
- Uses the existing email delivery service; sample data from the editor's JSON field is applied as Handlebars variables before sending

## Why

Template authors need to verify inbox rendering before sending to real recipients. The MJML preview pane shows compiled output but can't replicate inbox-specific behaviour (fonts, image blocking, dark mode). Sending to self closes that gap without exposing arbitrary-recipient send functionality.

author: jmerrillorg
body:
## Purpose

PR #99 adds a governed internal mail provider configuration boundary for AUTHOR_DRAFT_READY_FOR_REVIEW notifications. It connects the PR #98 injected internal delivery adapter to a separate internal notification gate so J Merrill Publishing can receive internal review notifications only when explicitly enabled and safely configured.

This does not send anything to the author, create an author-facing send event, mark author email as sent, create an Opportunity, activate Flow D, run diagnostics, open the AI execution gate, or authorize production automation.

## Files changed

- azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner/src/author/authorDraftReviewNotificationPersister.js
- azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner/src/author/internalAuthorDraftReviewNotificationMailer.js
- azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner/src/author/internalAuthorDraftReviewNotificationProviderConfig.js
- azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner/test/authorDraftReviewNotificationDelivery.test.js
- azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner/test/internalAuthorDraftReviewNotificationProviderConfig.test.js
- docs/operations/int-pub-005-stage0-diagnostic-production-readiness-plan.md
- docs/operations/int-pub-005-stage0-diagnostic-ai-activation-decision-record.md

## Internal notification provider configuration

- Adds a separate internal notification gate through JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED.
- Defaults to disabled unless JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED is exactly true.
- Supports a governed injected-provider mode with JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER=injected.
- Requires internal @jmerrill.one sender/reply-to values when enabled.
- Rejects @jmerrill.pub as an active internal notification sender.
- Does not hardwire Gmail, Outlook, ACS, SendGrid, Graph mail, SMTP, or any new live third-party provider.

## Environment variables

- JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED: defaults disabled; must equal true for live internal delivery.
- JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER: currently supports injected.
- JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_FROM: required when enabled; must be internal @jmerrill.one.
- JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_REPLY_TO: optional; if set, must be internal @jmerrill.one.

JM1_AI_EXECUTION_ENABLED is separate and was not opened or modified.

## Default disabled behavior

When JM1_INTERNAL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED is not true, the system can prepare the internal notification and safe log payload, returns INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_DISABLED, and does not call the provider.

## Recipient rules

- Live recipient must be exactly publishing@jmerrill.one.
- Author cannot appear in To, CC, or BCC.
- CC and BCC must be empty.
- Unapproved recipients fail closed.
- publishing@jmerrill.one remains the internal notification recipient and required future visibility mailbox.

## Dataverse logging behavior

Uses the PR #98 jm1_executionlogs safe persistence path. Safe log payloads can record disabled, prepared, sent, or failed internal notification state with event type, delivery intent, recipient, diagnosticId, intakeReferenceCode, safe subject, safe draft preview, safe provider name, optional internal provider message ID, and author email status AUTHOR_EMAIL_NOT_SENT.

Log payloads exclude manuscript text, extracted content, prompt body, raw model response, provider secrets, tokens, keys, headers, author-facing send claims, Opportunity fields, and Flow D fields.

## Fail-closed rules

Fails closed for disabled live gate, wrong notification type, wrong recipient, author in To/CC/BCC, unapproved recipients, DRAFT_ONLY mismatch, PENDING_HUMAN_APPROVAL mismatch, missing future copy/log flags, missing or malformed diagnosticId, missing intakeReferenceCode, missing draft preview, unsafe manuscript/prompt/raw model content, author-facing send flags, author sent markers, Opportunity fields, Flow D trigger fields, secrets/tokens/keys/headers, missing provider config, unknown provider, missing injected provider, provider rejection, and required Dataverse logging failure.

## Safety exclusions

- No diagnostic run occurred.
- JM1_AI_EXECUTION_ENABLED remained closed.
- Internal notification gate is separate from the AI execution gate.
- No author email was sent.
- No author was included as To/CC/BCC.
- No author-facing mail API path was introduced.
- No author-facing send event was created.
- No draft was marked sent.
- No Opportunity was created.
- Flow D remains inactive.
- Production activation remains unauthorized.
- Future author-facing send must copy or internally mirror to publishing@jmerrill.one and log the send event in Dataverse.

## Validation

- cd azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner && node --test test/internalAuthorDraftReviewNotificationProviderConfig.test.js test/authorDraftReviewNotificationDelivery.test.js: passed, 75 tests / 8 suites.
- cd azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner && node --test test/internalAuthorDraftReviewNotificationProviderConfig.test.js test/authorDraftReviewNotificationDelivery.test.js test/authorDraftReviewNotificationBuilder.test.js test/authorDraftSendPreparationBuilder.test.js test/authorDraftApprovalDecisionModel.test.js test/authorDraftPersister.test.js test/authorDraftSchemaManifest.test.js test/authorDraftFieldMap.test.js test/authorResponseDraftBuilder.test.js test/humanReviewDecisionModel.test.js test/diagnosticReviewPersister.test.js test/diagnosticReviewBuilder.test.js test/diagnosticQueueSelector.test.js test/providerAbstraction.test.js test/diagnosticSchemaValidator.test.js test/noQuotationValidator.test.js: passed, 391 tests / 53 suites.
- cd azure-functions/diagnostic-ai-runner && node --test: passed, 731 tests / 128 suites.
- Requested node --check list plus src/author/internalAuthorDraftReviewNotificationProviderConfig.js: passed.
- npm run type-check: passed.
- npm run lint: passed with existing app/layout.tsx custom-font warning.
- npm run build: passed with existing custom-font warning and existing edge-runtime static generation warning.
- git diff --check: passed.
- Azure app setting check confirmed JM1_AI_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false.

## Blockers / remaining governance

- Live internal provider credentials/config are not set by this PR.
- This PR supplies the governed configuration wrapper and injected provider boundary; actual Azure app settings for internal delivery still need separate governed configuration before live internal email can be sent.

body: ## Summary Fixes #5750. When Orca Mobile asks a paired older desktop runtime for `speech.models.list`, the runtime can return the raw authorization failure `Method 'speech.models.list' is not available to mobile clients`. Mobile now maps that legacy-runtime response to actionable guidance: update the paired desktop Orca app to use mobile voice settings. ## Screenshots No screenshot. This is a text-only error mapping covered by a unit test. ## Testing - [x] `pnpm --dir mobile test mobile-dictation-setup -- --runInBand` - 11 tests passed, covering legacy denial mapping, `method_not_found` mapping, unrelated `speech.models.list` failure preservation, and malformed missing-message fallback. - [x] `pnpm --dir mobile exec tsc --noEmit` - [x] `pnpm --dir mobile lint` - [x] `pnpm --dir mobile exec oxfmt --check src/dictation/mobile-dictation-setup.ts src/dictation/mobile-dictation-setup.test.ts` - [x] `PATH="$(mise where node@24)/bin:$PATH" pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` - [x] `PATH="$(mise where node@24)/bin:$PATH" pnpm typecheck` - [x] `PATH="$(mise where node@24)/bin:$PATH" pnpm build` - [ ] `PATH="$(mise where node@24)/bin:$PATH" pnpm lint` - failed in `lint:switch-exhaustiveness` while running `tsgolint` with `SIGSEGV`/`fatal error: fault`; that check scopes `src/main`, `src/preload`, `src/shared`, `src/relay`, `src/cli`, `src/renderer/src`, `config`, and `tests`, not the changed mobile files. - [ ] `PATH="$(mise where node@24)/bin:$PATH" pnpm test` - failed with 34 failed files / 113 failed tests in unrelated root suites, including git/relay timeout failures, native-runtime/node-pty tests, hosted review integration tests, and renderer timeout tests; no failures were reported in the changed mobile dictation files. ## AI Review Report Reviewed the current Orca main branch and confirmed `speech.models.list` is already registered and mobile-allowlisted on the desktop runtime. The remaining user-facing failure mode is compatibility with older paired desktop runtimes that return a forbidden/method-unavailable response. The change is scoped to the mobile RPC wrapper and preserves normal RPC failure propagation for unrelated errors. Cross-platform check: no shortcuts, path handling, shell behavior, or Electron platform branches are touched; this runs in the shared mobile TypeScript layer. ## Security Audit No new auth, command execution, filesystem, IPC, dependency, or secret handling. The existing runtime authorization failure remains enforced by the desktop runtime; mobile only remaps the displayed error when the failure explicitly references `speech.models.list` and either `method_not_found` or `not available to mobile clients`. ## Notes - X handle: @wolfie_ - SSH/remote/local: applies equally to any paired desktop runtime, local or remote, because it maps the mobile RPC response after transport returns. - Current desktop releases already include the speech setup RPC. This PR improves the fallback for users paired to older desktop builds. ---

author: pragyan2002
body:
The packaged app could fail with "Not allowed to load local resource:
.../app.asar/renderer/index.html" when the renderer's index.html did not
exist at the single hard-coded relative path. Depending on how
electron-builder lays out the asar, the compiled main process can sit at
either app.asar/out/main or app.asar/main, which shifts where the
renderer is found.

Probe the known candidate locations (relative to __dirname and to
app.getAppPath()) and load the first that exists, logging a clear error
and a did-fail-load diagnostic if none are present instead of showing a
blank window.

author: kadyapam
body:
## What

Adds the **durable `noetl.event` writer** for the noetl/ai-meta#103
`PUBLISH_ONLY` sole-writer cutover: an opt-in worker consume-loop
(`src/materializer.rs`) that drains the `noetl_events` JetStream stream with
**deferred ack** and acks each batch **only after** `events/project` durably
inserts it.

## The durability gap this closes

The prior `system/event_materializer` playbook acked messages **on fetch**
(`ack: on_success`), before `events/project` ran. A transient project failure
(server restart mid-drain) lost the **acked-but-unmaterialized** events — the
one gating item the #103 cutover comments flagged for a safe prod flip.

## Why a worker loop, not playbook deferred-ack

The playbook step model can't hold an ack handle across the
drain→build→project steps cleanly:
- the handles (one per message) ride playbook state across atomic blocks on
  **different pods**;
- a batch over the inline-context budget stages to the result store as a `_ref`
  (the documented `{{ drain_events.count }}` stall);
- concurrent cron-triggered drains **split batches**.

One in-process loop owns the consumer and has none of that. It drains with
`AckMode::Defer` (noetl-tools 3.13), POSTs `events/project`, and acks **only on
2xx**. On any failure it leaves the batch un-acked → JetStream redelivers after
ack-wait → **no event lost**. Serial → ordering preserved, no batch split;
idempotent `events/project` (ON CONFLICT) makes redelivery a no-op double-write,
never a duplicate row. Per `data-access-boundary.md` it never touches `noetl.*`
directly — drains a NATS stream, writes through the server API.

## Surface

- `NOETL_MATERIALIZER_ENABLED` (default **off**; system pool only) +
  `_BATCH` / `_TIMEOUT_MS` / `_IDLE_SLEEP_MS` / `_ERROR_BACKOFF_MS` knobs.
- Observability triad: `noetl_worker_materializer_{drained,projected,duplicates,acked,project_errors}_total`
  + `_cycle_duration_seconds`.
- `NOETL_MATERIALIZER_FAULT_FAIL_FIRST` — chaos/validation knob (default 0) to
  exercise the redelivery path deterministically. Never set in prod.

## Validation (kind, gate-on sole writer)

- **Happy path**: execution COMPLETED; materializer cycles
  `drained=N projected=N acked=N duplicates=0`; rows == distinct ids;
  stream unprocessed=0 — **sole writer, zero loss**.
- **Fault before ack**: `FAULT-INJECT: skipping project + ack; batch will
  redeliver` fired → after ack-wait the batch **redelivered** and projected+acked
  → execution COMPLETED; rows == distinct ids; unprocessed=0 — **loss=0 across a
  mid-drain failure, no duplicates (idempotency holds)**.

## ⚠️ Depends on noetl-tools 3.13 (crate-publish cascade)

`Cargo.toml` requires `noetl-tools = "3.13"` (the `AckMode::Defer` +
`SourceClient::ack` API in noetl/tools#71). **This PR's CI build is red until
noetl-tools 3.13.0 publishes** (semantic-release on the tools merge). Merge

body:
## Summary

Adds a spoiler-guard toggle on the **Matches** screen, next to the "{n} matches" count in the header. Scores are **blurred by default** and revealed when the eye toggle is switched on. The choice is remembered **per session** (`sessionStorage`), so opening a fresh tab hides scores again.

The default direction resolves a small ambiguity in the request: **default off = scores hidden (blurred); toggle on = scores revealed.**

## Changes

- **`src/pages/Matches.tsx`** — `showScores` state backed by `sessionStorage` (key `wc2026-show-scores`, default `false`); eye toggle button in the header; conditional `mxp-hide-scores` class on the page root. Mirrors the existing `oddsHidden` pattern but uses `sessionStorage` for per-session persistence.
- **`src/pages/matches.css`** — `.mxp-scores-toggle` button styling and `.mxp-hide-scores .mc-row .score { filter: blur(7px) }`. Blurring preserves the score's layout footprint (no card shift on reveal) and respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **`src/components/Icon.tsx`** — added `eye` / `eyeOff` glyphs.
- **`src/i18n/en.ts`** — `showScores` / `hideScores` labels (button title + aria-label); other locales fall back to English automatically.

## Verification

- `tsc -b` passes.
- Dev server compiles and serves the Matches page (HTTP 200).
- Note: `vite build` fails on a pre-existing `workbox-window` resolution error from the PWA plugin (reproduces on the clean tree without these changes) — unrelated to this work.

author: endodirectmaster-cmyk
body:
## Problema

Depois do hotfix #391 (token do prescritor de **produção** recuperado, `POST /api/memed/token → 200`), voltou a aparecer **"Módulo Memed aberto"**, mas a **tela trava e não renderiza nada**.

## Diagnóstico (confirmado empiricamente)

`GET /api/memed/token` em produção retornava:

```json
{"configured":true,"color":"#0a7d68",
 "script":"https://integrations.memed.com.br/...sinapse-prescricao.min.js",  ← SDK de HOMOLOGAÇÃO
 "allow":["rodolphomend@gmail.com"]}
```

- Logs da Vercel confirmam `POST → 200` (e os 400 antigos eram **"já cadastrado"**, comportamento **só de produção**) → `MEMED_API_BASE` é produção, **token é de produção**.
- O front, porém, carregava o **SDK de homologação**. **Token de produção + SDK de homologação = o módulo "abre" mas o iframe não autentica → tela travada/branca** (bate com a doc Memed *"O módulo da Memed não carrega"*; `integrations.memed.com.br` é **só homologação**).
- URLs oficiais (Memed → Front-end → Configurações → URLs): homologação `integrations.memed.com.br/.../sinapse-prescricao.min.js` · **produção `partners.memed.com.br/integration.js`** (formato bem diferente).

## Correção

**`api/memed/token.js`** — o default do `MEMED_SCRIPT` deixa de ser fixo no de homologação e passa a ser **derivado do ambiente do `MEMED_API_BASE`** (produção → `partners.memed.com.br/integration.js`), pra nunca dessincronizar. `MEMED_SCRIPT` (env) ainda sobrescreve.

**`index.html` `prescMemedLaunch`** —
- aguarda o `MdSinapsePrescricao` aparecer (poll ~8s): o loader de produção `integration.js` injeta o SDK de forma **assíncrona** (≠ do `.min.js` que já o define no `onload`);
- a Promise **só resolve quando o módulo renderiza de fato** → **"Módulo Memed aberto" deixa de ser mentiroso**;
- **timeout ~20s** com erro claro ("SDK e token de ambientes diferentes") em vez de tela travada;
- reabertura mostra o módulo direto (`core:moduleInit` não redispara).

## Validação

- `node scripts/ci-validate.js` ✅ (inline scripts, `node --check` em api/lib, 12/12 funções)
- **Não dá pra testar Memed de produção no preview** (login da Memed prod + allowlist = e-mail do médico). Após o deploy, o `GET /api/memed/token` deve passar a retornar `partners.memed.com.br/integration.js`; o teste real é o médico (rodolphomend@) abrir o Consultório em produção.

## Observações
- Não precisa setar `MEMED_SCRIPT` na Vercel (o código deriva), mas continua valendo como override.

author: raphaelfh
body:
## Problem

Multi-user data extraction was broken. In the example project every run sat at `stage=proposal, status=pending` with **zero** reviewer decisions ever, which made the reviewer-centric UI misreport:

- **"0/1 reviewer"** even when a reviewer was actively working — the counter counts `ReviewerDecision`s, which only exist from `REVIEW`.
- **Phantom %** for a second reviewer — in `PROPOSAL` the form pre-fills from the *shared* AI proposals and progress counted them, so a reviewer who had accepted nothing still saw e.g. "55%".
- **Accept never sticks / spinner churn** — an AI suggestion's accepted-status derives from the (empty) reviewer-state pointer, so it never reached a durable state.

## Root cause

The QA-unified `HITLSessionService` parks runs in `PROPOSAL`, and nothing advanced extraction runs to `REVIEW` (the per-section AI path stays in `PROPOSAL` by design; "Submit for review" was rarely used). The reviewer/accept/progress surfaces all assume `REVIEW`.

## Fix (frontend-orchestrated advance)

`PROPOSAL` becomes a transient seeding stage; `REVIEW` is the collaborative surface.

- **`useAutoAdvanceToReview`** (new hook) advances `PROPOSAL → REVIEW` once the run has proposals or the reviewer makes a first edit. Kept on the frontend because per-section AI extraction is called once per section and hard-requires `PROPOSAL` — a backend per-call advance would break batch extraction. `advance_stage` already materializes each user's `human` proposals into their own decisions, so typed values survive; AI proposals stay as suggestions to accept.
- **Reviewer badge** gated to non-`PROPOSAL` stages.
- **"Run AI"** disabled once in `REVIEW` (backend already rejects it — defense in depth).
- Existing **stuck runs self-heal** on next open.

Decision recorded in **ADR 0010**; `docs/reference/extraction-hitl-architecture.md` updated.

## Testing

- Frontend vitest full suite: **532/532** (83 files).
- New `useAutoAdvanceToReview` test (5) + `HeaderMoreMenu` `canRunAI` gate (2).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean · eslint clean · docs-CI (markdownlint/cspell/frontmatter) clean.
- Architectural fitness: all checks OK.
- Backend `test_run_lifecycle_service` 10/10 (validates the `advance_stage` + materialize path the fix relies on); local DB at head `0026`.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- Set project `reviewer_count = 2` (Consensus settings) for "both reviewers must decide" semantics — new runs pick it up; the existing runs self-heal to `REVIEW` but keep their frozen `reviewer_count=1`.

author: amilcarex
body:
Hace que `strapi-plugin-mcp-suite` conviva con el **MCP nativo de Strapi 5.47+** sin duplicar tools, y endurece la seguridad de los content-ops. Cubre los 6 puntos del roadmap de convivencia. Todo probado end-to-end en un Strapi 5.48.1 real.

## Cambios

### 1. Gating config-driven + toggle `contentOps` (`c5fe21b`)
Gating desde `config/plugins.ts` (env vars como override). Flag `contentOps` para apagar el CRUD. Fix de versión hardcodeada de `__health` (ahora lee del `package.json`).

### 2. Auto-supresión con `coexistence` (`4cb74bd`)
`coexistence: "auto" | "standalone" | "extend-native"`. En `auto`, si el nativo está activo (Strapi ≥5.47 + `server.mcp.enabled`), auto-suprime `contentOps`.

### 3. Bridge al `/mcp` nativo (`9ff3d4e`)
`extend-native` registra los diferenciadores en `strapi.ai.mcp` → un solo `/mcp` sirve CRUD nativo + schema authoring + layout + media/graphql. Incluye converter JSON-Schema→Zod.

### 4. Enforcement de permisos del token en content-ops (`8e8af37`) — **Security**
Guard `assertCanMutate`: un token **read-only** ya no puede crear/editar/borrar/publicar vía MCP (era una vía de escalación). `custom` exige la action correspondiente; sin token / tipo desconocido → bloquea (fail-closed).

### 5. `discard_draft` (`8e8af37`)
Nueva content-op (descarta el draft, revierte a published) — paridad D&P con `discard_<model>_draft` del nativo.

### 6. README (EN + ES) (`8e8af37`)
Sección "Convivencia con el MCP nativo": los 3 modos, gating config-driven, y la distinción admin-token vs content-API-token. Reposiciona el plugin como **complemento** del nativo.

## Verificación en vivo (Strapi 5.48.1)
- **auto**: plugin expone 19 tools, 0 CRUD.
- **extend-native**: `/mcp` pasa de 24 → 41 tools (24 nativas + 17 del plugin); las bridged ejecutan OK.
- **security**: read-only bloqueado en mutaciones (test).

## Tests
333 verdes (defaults preservan el comportamiento previo; deployments existentes no cambian).

## Notas
- Nueva dep `zod` (deduplicada a la instancia del SDK nativo).
- El MCP nativo usa **admin tokens** (`kind=admin`), distintos de los content-API tokens del plugin — documentado.

body:
## Summary

Per the user's standing UX preference — **popovers over inline-table expansion** — convert the two shipped budget panels that expand *inside* the table to **Headless UI `Popover`** panels: the **WLT-22-1 drill-down** (line items behind a category's "this month so far") and the **WLT-21-2 year-spread** (12-month chart). The ledger/table stays a table; only the expanding detail moves to anchored popovers.

## Linked artifacts

- Fix triage: `docs/fixes/budget-popovers.md` (hygiene, P3, affects **WLT-22** + **WLT-21**)
- Preference: user feedback 2026-06-18 ("use popups wherever applicable and not inline table")

## Changes per area

### Frontend
- `app/(app)/budget/BudgetClient.tsx` — the two inline `<tr>` expansions → `Popover`/`PopoverButton`/`PopoverPanel anchor`. **Portal-anchored** (no table-cell clipping) and **portal-aware** (the drill panel's nested recategorize `Menu` doesn't close the parent popover — the reason a hand-rolled outside-click overlay was rejected). Focus/Escape/outside-click via Headless UI; drill panel `max-h-[60vh] overflow-auto` for tall histories; year panel wider for the chart. The year toggle keeps its descriptive, toggling label via an `sr-only` span.

**Behavior change (intended):** one popover open at a time (Headless UI closes others on outside-click), replacing "expand several rows at once." **Logic preserved:** lazy-load once per category per load, `budget_spread_viewed` / `category_drilldown_viewed` fired once per category per load (idempotent on toggle-close), and the recategorize reconcile (drop the drill cache + refetch the open source so it updates live).

## Test plan

- [x] Component tests updated — budget suite **22 green**, incl. a **new regression guard**: the opened drill + year panels are **portaled out of the budget `<table>`** (`budgetTable.contains(panel) === false`) — a revert to inline rows fails it.
- [x] All existing open/close/content/event/reconcile assertions pass unchanged against the popover implementation.
- [x] Full suite **236 green**; lint + typecheck + `pnpm build` clean (`/budget` registered; bundle 6.7→11.2 kB from Popover, expected).
- [x] Accessibility — Headless UI manages `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` + focus; year toggle's descriptive label preserved via `sr-only`.

## Review handoff

**Engineer (Claude):** Implementation complete. **Codex** should review + extend the gated real-path E2E to **recategorize from inside the drill popover** (the nested-popover interaction — confirm the picker opens and the parent popover stays open), and confirm the year/drill open + reconcile through session→RLS→render. Architect-compliance: no architecture change (UI-only, no schema/read change).

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Reviewer findings: all BLOCKERs addressed
- [ ] Security CRITICAL findings: zero
- [ ] Disputes: zero unresolved
- [ ] Human approval recorded

author: rodneydean
body:
🛡️ **Sentinel Security Update**

### 🚨 Severity: HIGH

### 💡 Vulnerabilities Found
1.  **Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR):** The `MpesaController` trusted user-provided `organizationId` from URL parameters and request bodies. A malicious authenticated user could potentially view or claim payments belonging to other tenants.
2.  **Denial of Service (DoS):** Multiple outbound request sites (ShortUrl streaming, M-Pesa, Scryme) lacked timeouts and response size limits. This could lead to server hang or memory exhaustion if upstream services are slow or return massive payloads.

### 🔧 Fixes Implemented
- **IDOR Protection:**
    - Updated `MpesaController` to use `@v2Context()` to retrieve the authenticated `organizationId` and `memberId`.
    - Removed manual `organizationId` and `memberId` inputs from sensitive endpoints: `search-unclaimed`, `claim`, and `verify-safaricom`.
    - Added `@RequirePermission` decorators to ensure only authorized users can perform these actions.
    - Updated `MpesaService` to include `organizationId` filters in database queries to ensure tenant isolation.
- **DoS Mitigation:**
    - Standardized `axios` requests with `timeout: 10000` and `maxContentLength` (1MB to 50MB depending on context) across `ShortUrlController`, `MpesaClient`, and `ScrymeChatApiClient`.
- **Frontend Alignment:**
    - Updated `apps/pos` hooks and components to match the new, more secure API signatures.

### ✅ Verification
- **Code Inspection:** Verified that all sensitive M-Pesa routes now derive tenant context from the session.
- **Architectural Check:** Confirmed that `axios` configuration now includes defensive bounds.
- **Frontend Check:** Verified that POS components correctly call the simplified API endpoints.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: jakobimatagi
body:
## What

Attaches a **value/winner breakdown to every historical trade**, inline inside the per-team transaction-feed dropdowns on the Activity tab (not a separate section). For each trade you now see:

- **Who won** — each side's haul priced on the trade scale, with a winner badge and verdict line.
- **Per-asset value-now** — every player/pick, with the asset's source labeled.
- **Picks resolved to players** — a traded pick shows the player drafted with it (e.g. `2026 2nd → Player`), valued by that player today.
- **Value source labels** — `FC` / `RA` / `DO` / `est` tags per asset (and a "via …" summary), so it's always clear where a number came from, including fallbacks.

### Value lens toggle (FantasyCalc / RosterAudit / Dynasty Oracle)
A tab-level toggle reprices every trade under a chosen lens. Each card precomputes `views.fc` / `views.ra` / `views.oracle`, so flipping is instant and the winner logic stays in the tested engine. FC/RA are dollar-scale markets (÷100 → trade scale); **Dynasty Oracle** is the app's own internal model value on a ~0–100 points scale (used as-is, no ÷100).

### Value "then" (point-in-time)
Neither FantasyCalc nor RosterAudit exposes a dated historical endpoint (verified), so we snapshot values ourselves **going forward**:
- `api/snapshot-values.js` — daily Vercel cron, writes `value_snapshots` / `pick_value_snapshots`.
- `fetchTradeValueSnapshots` reads them for the `(was N)` lens.
- Trades predating the first snapshot are tagged **"Outside snapshot frame"** and show value-now only.

## Why
"Who won this trade?" is the question people actually ask of trade history. Value-now + pick resolution answers it today with zero new infra; the snapshot pipeline layers in true point-in-time verdicts as history accumulates.

## Notable implementation detail
Pick→player resolution (`buildDraftResolver`) matches a pick's season against **both** `draft.season` and the draft's `start_time` year — Sleeper's `draft.season` is offset (a completed 2026 rookie draft can be labelled `2025`), which had caused used picks to wrongly render as "unused". Falls back to `draft_order` + rosters when `slot_to_roster_id` is missing.

## Reviewer notes
- **Requires setup before "value then" works:** apply `docs/migrations/value_snapshots_schema.sql`, then set `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (optional `CRON_SECRET`) in Vercel. Until snapshots accumulate, every trade reads "Outside snapshot frame" — by design.
- The Oracle lens uses `internalValue` (pure model) rather than the market-anchored fused `dynastyValue`; easy to switch if preferred.
- Unused/future picks use a static estimate (no drafted player to price); used picks use the real drafted-player value.

## Testing
- `src/lib/tradeReview.test.mjs` — 9 tests covering pick resolution (incl. the season-offset and `draft_order` fallbacks), value-now scoring/winner, the RA and Oracle lenses, and snapshot-based value-then.
- Full suite: **186/186 pass**. `npm run build` clean.

author: johnleider
body:
Adds a custom markdownlint rule (`meta-length`) that flags frontmatter `meta.title` over 60 characters and `meta.description` over 160 characters — the lengths search engines actually display before truncating. It parses frontmatter with `front-matter` (the same library the docs build uses), so the measured length matches what ships in the rendered `<title>`/`<meta>` tags.

The rule is wired into the existing `lint:md`/`fix:md` scripts via `--rules` and configured in `.markdownlintrc` (thresholds are config-driven, so adjusting a limit is a one-line change). No new dependencies.

Also shortens the 19 existing pages whose descriptions exceeded 160 characters (mostly blog monthly-updates plus a few component pages) so the rule passes clean. Titles were already all within range.

author: copilot
body:
O jogo já estava funcional, mas ações críticas (principalmente bloqueio e compra) ainda estavam rápidas/difíceis de ler visualmente e o menu inicial não refletia o fluxo esperado com opção de configurações. Esta proposta melhora clareza de estado na mesa e consistência de animação sem alterar regras centrais da partida.

- **Escopo do problema**
  - Bloqueio precisava de feedback sonoro/visual dedicado e de mais legibilidade temporal sobre quem foi bloqueado.
  - Direção da rodada, entrada no jogo (menu) e encaixe da carta comprada na mão precisavam de um UX mais claro.

- **Feedback de bloqueio (som + foco no alvo)**
  - Adicionada trilha sonora específica para `skip` (`playCardSound("block")`).
  - Fluxo de `skip` passa a exibir burst `"BLOQUEIO"` ancorado no jogador afetado, com destaque visual temporário no alvo (`.opponent.blocked` / `.you-label.blocked`).
  - Aplicação do efeito agora aguarda breve janela de leitura antes de avançar turno (`await showBlockBurst(...)`).

- **Indicador de direção com leitura circular**
  - `renderDirection()` passou de `>>/<<` para `↻/↺` com container circular na seta.
  - Ajustes de estilo para reforçar direção de jogo com melhor scan visual.

- **Menu inicial com entrada completa**
  - Menu inicial agora contém ações explícitas de **Jogar** e **Configurações**.
  - `Configurações` permanece placeholder por ora, com hint textual “Configurações em breve.” (sem lógica de configuração acoplada).

- **Compra encaixando direto na mão**
  - Removido comportamento de “entrada extra” após compra (`recentHandInsert`/`markHandInsert`), eliminando troca de animação após chegada.
  - A carta comprada agora entra diretamente na mão do humano e bots após o voo principal.

```js
if (card.type === "skip") {
  const blockedPlayer = (currentPlayer + direction + players.length) % players.length;
  await showBlockBurst(blockedPlayer);
  advanceTurn();
}
```

author: cfpramod
body:
## Why

openclearance is a **public OSS repo**, so by design it must carry **no Cloudflare API token and no GitHub Actions deploy workflow** (a deploy token on a public repo is the exposure we avoid; the earlier GH-Actions PR #10 was correctly abandoned for this reason). This adds a token-safe path: openclearance.org publishes with the **operator's own local wrangler auth**.

## What

- **`package.json` `deploy` script:** `astro build && wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=openclearance --branch=main --commit-dirty=true`. Uses the operator's locally installed, `wrangler login`-authenticated wrangler. Project name matches `wrangler.toml`.
- **`scripts/hooks/post-merge`** (committed hook, no creds): runs `npm run deploy` when local `main` is updated with site changes. **Guarded** to fire only on `main` (feature-branch merges/pulls ignored) and only when site files changed (`src/`, `public/`, `astro.config.mjs`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`).
- **`scripts/install-hooks.sh`** (opt-in): symlinks `.git/hooks/post-merge` to the committed hook. Only the operator who deploys runs it once; ordinary contributors who build/test are unaffected. Idempotent.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** documents the flow: merge PR on GitHub, `git pull` on `main`, the site deploys via local wrangler. The CF token never touches this public repo.

## Verification (for OM-CR)

- **Zero token/secret in the repo:** `grep -rniE "CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN|CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID|api[_-]?token|secret|password"` over all changed files returns nothing. No GitHub Actions deploy added.
- **Hook deploys only locally, with the operator's own auth:** the `deploy` script invokes the operator's local wrangler; no credentials are read from or stored in the repo.
- **Guard correct:** branch-guarded to `main`; path-guarded to site files; opt-in install. Installer tested end-to-end in a throwaway repo (symlink resolves, executable, correct relative target).
- **Gates:** `astro build` green; `npm run conformance` green.
- **Scope:** 4 files only (`package.json`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `scripts/hooks/post-merge`, `scripts/install-hooks.sh`). No em/en-dashes in committed copy (repo style).

author: thatbyteguy
body:
This fixes a bug in the Solaris xattr backend's retry loop.

In `lib/sysxattrs.c`, the loop advances `bufpos` after a successful partial write, but subsequent retries continue to pass the original `size` value to `write()` rather than the remaining byte count.

As a result, if a short write occurs, the next iteration can attempt to write more bytes than remain in the source buffer.

The fix changes:

```c
write(attrfd, (char*)value + bufpos, size);
```

to:

```c
write(attrfd, (char*)value + bufpos, size - bufpos);
```

This matches the corresponding logic in `read_xattr()` and the existing retry-loop pattern used elsewhere in the file.

Notes:

* Solaris-specific code path
* No behavioral changes on successful full writes
* Build and test results unchanged after the fix
* The issue appears to date back to the initial Solaris xattr implementation

author: kadyapam
body:
## What

Wires `NOETL_MATERIALIZER_ENABLED` on the system worker pool so the Rust
worker's in-process CQRS materializer loop (noetl/worker#115) runs there.

The loop drains `noetl_events` with **deferred ack** and acks each batch only
after `POST /api/internal/events/project` durably inserts it — the
**ack-after-materialize** durability boundary for the noetl/ai-meta#103
`PUBLISH_ONLY` sole-writer cutover. Replaces the ack-on-fetch
`system/event_materializer` playbook (which acked before the insert and could
lose events on a transient project failure).

## Changes

- **kind (dev)** `worker-system-pool-deployment.yaml`: `NOETL_MATERIALIZER_ENABLED=true`
  — shadow-safe while the server gate is off (`events/project` is idempotent
  `ON CONFLICT`, so the drain only logs duplicates, never loss).
- **prod** `worker-system-pool-deployment-prod.yaml`: wired but `false` — **no
  production default changes on apply.** Inline-documented staging order: flip
  materializer ON (shadow) first, then flip the server's
  `NOETL_EVENT_INGEST_PUBLISH_ONLY`.

The pod already carries `NATS_URL`, `NOETL_SERVER_URL`, and
`NOETL_INTERNAL_API_TOKEN`, so no new secrets are needed.

Validated on kind (gate-on, sole writer): happy path drained==projected==acked
zero-dup; fault-before-ack → redeliver → materialize, loss=0. See noetl/worker#115.

Refs noetl/ai-meta#103

author: arthurfontana
body:
## Summary

Add `CLAUDE.md`, a comprehensive guide for Claude Code and other AI assistants working with this SAS-based reject inference system. This document serves as a knowledge base to prevent common mistakes and ensure consistency in future code modifications.

## Key additions

- **Project overview:** Explains the reject inference system for Vivo credit policy, the three-stage credit funnel, and why inference is necessary for missing data on rejected and non-converted applicants.

- **Execution model:** Documents the three-phase SAS workflow (phases 0/1/2), data flow between files, and the critical requirement that files must run sequentially in the same SAS session sharing macro variables.

- **Core metric definition:** Clarifies `prob_mau` (probability of default) as the central analytical metric and establishes four "golden rules" based on past errors:
  - Never divide `SUM(prob_mau)` by count of approvals
  - Never filter `FL_ALTAS=1` in granular base
  - Always filter `FL_APROVADOS=1` when comparing inferred vs. actual
  - Multiplication of `prob_conversao × prob_fpd` only valid in granular base, not aggregated

- **Architecture details:** Maps the three `.sas` files to their responsibilities, describes the hierarchical fallback mechanism for cell selection, and explains exponential extrapolation for tail ranges.

- **Key variables and segmentation:** Documents the segmentation hierarchy (`SCORE_HVI3 IDENTIFICA_GRUPO_MODELO CANAL_PCO_AJUSTADO`) and notes that score is the anchor (never collapsed).

- **Validated parameters:** Current calibration (`MARGEM_RELATIVA=0.40`, `ALPHA=0.07`, `PODER=0.75`) and their derived outputs (`MIN_N=230`, `MIN_EVENTOS=62`).

- **Technical pitfalls:** Warns about encoding (ISO-8859-1, not UTF-8), SAS macro limitations (`%DO` in open code), hierarchical join mechanics, and proper IC naming conventions.

- **Known issue:** Documents the PAP channel problem (~52% volume in MÉDIA group with 85x inflated conversion) as pending resolution.

## Notable details

- Emphasizes that no SAS runtime exists in this environment; all code review must be manual and syntactically careful.
- References `CONTEXTO.md` as the authoritative briefing document containing problem history and resolved errors.
- Clarifies that Phase 3 (simulation) is external to this repo and handled by the user's simulator.
- Specifies Portuguese Brazilian as the working language for comments and reporting.

body:
## Summary

- Treat `awaiting_final_action` as an already-committed merge review state for persistent review result callbacks.
- Update persistent delivery metadata/history when the callback arrives after the final-action hold is already pending.
- Avoid re-ingesting the same merge verdict or calling `on_reviewed` again, which would otherwise try to transition `awaiting_final_action -> reviewed`.

## Why

A real post-PR73 runtime run reached lane execution, gate, OpenCode persistent review, and final-action hold creation, then failed when the persistent review callback retried the review transition:

`InvalidTransitionError: cannot transition loop25z35_post_pr73_main_fullchain from awaiting_final_action to reviewed`

The authoritative local state was already `awaiting_final_action` with a pending final-action hold, so the callback should be idempotent.

## Proof Boundary

- Based on origin/main at f00399ee5fef6a5560564b073ce78c5d223d75d8.
- Proof level: local contract/integration validation plus real runtime failure evidence from loop-25z35.
- Not claimed: GitHub review truth, merge truth, ready_to_merge, pr_merged, live MemoryOS, full L8-L10 closure, full L1-L11 closure, production-ready groupchat, or overnight readiness.

body:
PR Summary


  Fixes two related bugs in the cosmetic Appearance system (suit/helmet):
  1. Removing a cosmetic suit/helmet via right-click never persisted — it silently reverted to the
  last-equipped item on respawn.
  2. New characters (and anyone with nothing cosmetically equipped) showed a hardcoded class skin or,
  after an earlier broken attempt, were fully invisible.

  Also fixes an unrelated build-toolchain regression that was blocking any of this from compiling.

  Changes by file

  src/GameServer/Cosmetics/CosmeticEquip.cpp / .hpp
  - ClearSlot now accepts engine slots 6 (Suit) and 12 (Helmet) in addition to dyes — resets
  SuitFlairId/SuitMeshId or HeadFlairId/HelmetMeshId and deletes the corresponding DB row (remapped to
  DB slot 22/23).
  - ApplyClassVisualFallback rewritten: when no cosmetic suit is equipped, SuitMeshId must still be a
  real, valid asm_id (-1 renders the character fully invisible — the client can't "swap to no mesh").
  Now picks a per-class, per-gender "default suit" mesh (asm_ids 1354-1357 male, 1482-1485 female,
  found via asm_data_set_assembly_meshes) instead of falling back to a specific named catalog skin or
  a single hardcoded mesh.
  - ApplyToPawn's DB persistence now checks sqlite3_step's result and logs/returns false on failure
  instead of silently swallowing write errors.
  - LoadFromDB/ClearSlot's collision-sizing fallback (1225) is now used only as a local lookup key for
  ApplyMeshCollisionData, never written back into the replicated SuitMeshId field.

  src/GameServer/TgGame/TgPlayerController/ServerAcceptNewProfileFromEquipScreen/TgPlayerController__S
  erverAcceptNewProfileFromEquipScreen.cpp
  - Detects SlotIndices[6]==0 / [12]==0 (the client genuinely sends 0 when the Appearance tab's
  Suit/Helmet icon is blanked via right-click) and calls CosmeticEquip::ClearSlot immediately, instead
  of treating 0 as "client didn't touch this slot" (which is correct for every other slot, but
  wrongly absorbed the only two slots players actually clear).
  - Forwards the cleared slots to the control server via a new cleared_cosmetic_slots field in the
  equip_save IPC event.

  src/ControlServer/PlayerSessionStore/PlayerSessionStore.cpp / .hpp
  - SaveEquippedDevices takes a new cleared_cosmetic_slots parameter; deletes the corresponding
  ga_character_devices row (DB slot 22/23) inside the same transaction as the rest of the equip save.
  - Added sqlite3_step result checking + error logging on the DELETE/INSERT loops, which previously
  failed silently.

  src/ControlServer/TcpSession/TcpSession.cpp
  - Parses cleared_cosmetic_slots from the IPC payload and passes it through to SaveEquippedDevices.

  Makefile
  - Added src/Utils/SehStub/SehStub.cpp to both DLL source lists.
  - No net change to CFLAGS/LDFLAGS versus master (several intermediate attempts were tried and
  reverted; ended up back at the original -static flags).

  src/Utils/SehStub/SehStub.cpp (new file)
  - Provides a stub __mingw_SEH_error_handler symbol to work around a missing symbol in the current
  mingw-w64-i686-crt toolchain build (a git-snapshot package, not a tagged release) that otherwise
  fails the link with -static.

  Test plan

  - [x] New character (each of the 4 classes, both genders) shows the correct class/gender default
  body, not invisible or a named skin.
  - [x] Equip a cosmetic suit/helmet, then right-click to clear it — confirm it visually reverts to
  the default immediately.
  - [x] Relog/respawn after clearing — confirm the default persists (doesn't revert to the
  previously-equipped item).
  - [x] Normal cosmetic equip/swap flow still works as before.


(God bless Claude, might have to remove the loggers after testing that it all works correctly)
PS: Not sure src/Utils/SehStub/SehStub.cpp is needed but I got a compiling error without it.
PS2: Most important data is in src/GameServer/Cosmetics/CosmeticEquip.cpp sine there you can fint the default armors for both male and female per class.

body:
## What

De-brand the **117** Shopify product handles that still embedded a supplier brand in their URL slug (`outsunny` ×113, `qaba` ×4 distinct). Round-2 follow-up to PR #208 (`fix-shopify-handles.mjs`), which only stripped `aosom`.

## Why

Google feed audit found 160 `<link>` entries (incl. variant dupes → 117 distinct products) with branded handles like `/products/...-outsunny-...`. These are public, Google- and customer-visible URLs — the same brand-leak class fixed for `title_en`, on the slug.

## How — `scripts/fix-shopify-handles-2.mjs`

- Strips the dash-anchored brand token (`(^|-)(outsunny|qaba)(-|$)`), renames via `PUT /products/{id}`.
- **Explicitly creates a 301** (`POST /redirects.json`) per rename. ⚠️ The REST Admin API does **not** auto-create redirects (verified live — the original brief's assumption was wrong); without this the 117 indexed URLs would 404.
- Dry-run by default, `--apply` to write. Backs up all originals to `data/shopify-backup/` (gitignored) before any write. 2 req/s throttle + 429 backoff. Idempotent (re-run skips renamed handles; existing 301 → 422). Collision-safe (uses the handle Shopify actually stored for the redirect target).
- Run under x64 node (see CLAUDE.md "Windows ARM64").

## Verification

- ✅ Dry-run reviewed (10 examples) + checkpoint before apply.
- ✅ Applied to **prod**: 117 renamed, 0 failed, 0 redirect failures.
- ✅ Re-scan: **0** branded handles remain on Shopify.
- ✅ 301 spot-check (primary domain): 3/3 old→301→new, new→200.
- ✅ Feed cache flushed via `POST /api/revalidate` (Google feed reaches 0 branded within CDN `s-maxage` ~10 min).
- ✅ `vitest`: **984 passed / 80 files**, exit 0.

author: mmadhu1623
body:
## Summary
Fixes incident INC0010638 for inventory-service high error rate.

## Root cause from log analysis
Live system RCA indicated intermittent request failures caused by database connection timeouts and connection pool exhaustion, propagating HTTP 500 responses to order-service.

## Exact bug identified in code
`inventory-service/app.py` intentionally injected random failures on every inventory request using `random.choice([True, False])`. When the random branch evaluated true, the service logged `Database Connection Timeout` and `ConnectionPoolExhausted` and returned HTTP 500. This created artificial intermittent failures matching the observed production symptom.

## Evidence from system logs
Observed error patterns referenced in the incident and mirrored directly in application code/logging:
- `Database Connection Timeout`
- `ConnectionPoolExhausted`

## Change made
Removed the random failure injection and always return a successful inventory response for the normal code path.

## Incident
- ServiceNow Incident: INC0010638

author: xcityusa
body:
Adds FastClaw as an OAuth 2.1 / OIDC client of an external IdP (auth.xcity.one / GoTrue) so users reach the Claws console via **Xcity SSO**, and their agents run on their own **xct-home TokenHub budget**. Ships **dark** — routes register only when `FASTCLAW_OIDC_*` is configured.

This is the Claws side of the cross-repo OAuth-SSO direct-entry feature (xct-home side merged in XcityUS/xct-home#57).

## Backend (`internal/setup/handlers_oidc.go`)
- `GET /auth/oidc/login` — authorization-code + PKCE (S256); state + verifier in short-lived httpOnly cookies; redirect to the IdP.
- `GET /auth/oidc/callback` — verify state; exchange code at GoTrue `/token?grant_type=pkce`; provision a passwordless `role=user` (keyed by email); issue `fastclaw_session`; then **best-effort** fetch the user's product-scoped TokenHub key from xct-home (`GET /api/me/integrations/key`, `Bearer <access_token>`) and bind it as a **user-scope `tokenhub` provider** so every agent inherits it. A key/entitlement failure logs but never blocks login.

## Config (`internal/config/env.go`)
`FASTCLAW_OIDC_ISSUER_URL` / `_CLIENT_ID` / `_REDIRECT_URL` / `_KEY_ENDPOINT` / `_SCOPES` (default `openid profile email tokenhub:key`). Daemon wires `SetOIDC`; `/api/status` exposes `oidcEnabled`.

## Frontend
"Sign in with Xcity" button on the login screen (gated on `oidcEnabled`); surfaces `?oidc_error` from the callback.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — clean.
- `go test ./internal/setup` — incl. 3 OIDC integration tests: full callback against stub IdP + key endpoints (exchange → provision → session → provider bind), state-mismatch CSRF rejection, authorize-URL construction.
- **Ran the real binary**: `/api/status` → `oidcEnabled=true`; `/auth/oidc/login` → 302 to `auth.xcity.one/authorize?...scope=…tokenhub:key` + state/verifier cookies; `/auth/oidc/callback` (bad state) → 302 `/?oidc_error=invalid_oidc_state`.

## Ops before go-live
1. Register OAuth client `xct-claws` + `tokenhub:key` scope in GoTrue (PKCE public client; confirm tokens carry `scope`/`azp`).
2. Set `FASTCLAW_OIDC_*` on the Claws deployment.
3. xct-home: set `INTEGRATION_KEY_CLIENTS=xct-claws:claws` + `CLAWS_CONSOLE_URL`.

⚠️ GoTrue PKCE field names assumed: `{auth_code, code_verifier}` at `/token?grant_type=pkce`; claims `scope`/`azp`. Verify against the live GoTrue build and adjust `exchangeOIDCCode` if needed.

body:
## Summary

Implements periodic JWT refresh every 7 days to ensure tokens never expire under normal operation. Includes 48-hour expiry fallback as safety net if weekly refresh fails during outages.

## Changes

**provider/main.go:**
- Rewrote `runJWTRefresher()` to track last successful refresh timestamp on disk (`~/.urnetwork/jwt_last_refresh`)
- Primary mechanism: refresh every 7 days from last successful refresh, regardless of token expiry
- Secondary fallback: refresh if token within 48h of expiry (catches repeated refresh failures)
- Startup jitter (0-9 minutes) desynchronizes fleet refresh attempts

**Documentation:**
- CHANGELOG.md: Added to Resilience section
- FORK_CHANGES.md: Added section 32 with full implementation details

## Benefit

- **No token expiry under normal operation** — 7-day refresh ensures continuous service
- **Multi-day outage resilience** — 48h expiry buffer provides recovery window if weekly refresh missed
- **Fleet-friendly** — startup jitter prevents synchronized refresh storms
- **All auth modes** — JWT-to-JWT renewal works equally for BUILD=jwt, BUILD=stable, BUILD=nightly

## What

`AttributionCapability` was already a registered `Capability`, but it lived
inside the catch-all `host.rs` module rather than in its own file like every
other first-class capability (`your.rs`, `approval.rs`, etc.). This moves it to
a dedicated `src/capabilities/attribution.rs`:

- New `src/capabilities/attribution.rs` — `ATTRIBUTION_CAPABILITY_ID`, the
  `Co-Authored-By` trailer / PR footer constants, `yolop_attribution_prompt()`,
  the `AttributionCapability` impl, and its test, with a module doc comment in
  the style of `your.rs` / `approval.rs`.

  host/environment/bash/setup concerns.
- `mod.rs` — adds `mod attribution;` and a dedicated re-export. `runtime.rs`
  imports are unchanged because the public path
  (`crate::capabilities::AttributionCapability`) still resolves.

## Why

Consistency and discoverability: capabilities in this repo follow a
one-module-per-capability convention, and attribution was the outlier buried in
a grab-bag module. No behavior change — same capability, same registration,
same system-prompt output.

Note: I also confirmed that `your` and `soft_approval` already contribute to the
system prompt via their capabilities' `system_prompt_contribution`
(`your.rs:65`, `approval.rs:109`), with no parallel hardcoded prompt path, so no

## Security

No security-relevant code changes — this is a pure module move. Capability
registration (TM-TOOL) is unchanged; attribution is prompt-only and exposes no

author: dsengupta0628
body:
**Problem** 

set_input_delay -reference_pin models the input arrival as a graph edge ref_pin --> input pin (introduced in commit 740fa7d1, port delay ref pin timing role). 

Sdc::ensureInputDelayRefPinEdges() builds the edge during levelization and sets a per-InputDelay guard **PortDelay::ref_pin_edges_exist_** to avoid duplicate edges on repeated levelization of the same graph.

But the guard is never reset when the graph is torn down. Sta::clearNonSdc() (reached via networkChangedNonSdc() - the path OpenROAD's resizer uses after netlist edits) deletes the graph, freeing the ref_pin  edge, but keeps the SDC. 
On the next rebuild the guard is still set, so ensureInputDelayRefPinEdges() skips edge re-creation. The input port loses its only arrival source and silently reports "No paths  found"

  **Fix**

Reset the guard flags at graph teardown so the edges are rebuilt with the new graph. New Sdc::inputDelayRefPinEdgesInvalid() clears the per-InputDelay flag (guarded by have_input_delay_ref_pins_), called from the clearNonSdc() modes loop just before delete graph_. The dedup guard is retained for the same-graph repeated-levelize case.

**Test**
 test/input_delay_ref_pin_rebuild.tcl: set_input_delay -reference_pin on in1, plain input delay on in2 (control), then calling sta::network_changed_non_sdc and re-report. Without the fix in1 reports "No paths found" after this call. Above fix resolves this

body:
## 개요
Closes #248

Grafana(bastion)에 데이터가 안 뜨던 문제 해결. **원인**: Prometheus 는 ClusterIP(서비스 CIDR)라 bastion 에서 라우팅 불가 + bastion 에 IAM·kubectl·`PROMETHEUS_URL` 모두 미구성(설계상 수동 단계가 채워진 적 없음). Prometheus 자체는 정상 수집 중(`up` 18개 전부 1) 확인됨.

## 변경
- **Prometheus internal NLB** ([prometheus/main.tf](infra/modules/cluster/prometheus/main.tf)): server.service 를 LoadBalancer + 내부 NLB annotations 로 노출. 고정 이름 `<project>-<env>-prometheus`, `source-ranges=VPC CIDR`(VPC 내부만). cluster→prometheus 로 `vpc_cidr` 전달.
- **bastion IAM** ([bastion.tf](infra/modules/ops/bastion.tf)): 인스턴스 프로파일 + `elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancers` 만(클러스터 RBAC 불필요).
- **런타임 배선** ([user_data](infra/modules/ops/templates/bastion_user_data.sh.tftpl)): NLB DNS 를 이름으로 해석 → grafana/k6 compose `.env` 에 `PROMETHEUS_URL`/`K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL` 주입 후 기동. **systemd timer(부팅+3분 주기)** 로 재해석 → 클러스터/NLB 재생성 시 자동 재배선(2단계·CD 플래그 불필요).

## 검증
- `terraform validate` 통과, tftpl 토큰 전수 확인.
- apply 후: monitoring NS 에 internal NLB 생성 → bastion 이 ~1-3분 내 `.env` 갱신 → Grafana 데이터 표시 예상.

## 비고
- NLB DNS 는 재생성 시 바뀌지만 bastion timer 가 자동 추종(고정 이름 조회).
- source-ranges 가 VPC CIDR 라 bastion(같은 VPC)만 접근. 외부 노출 없음.

#192 でライブ検証済みの staged Jules レーン (`npm run request:jules:staged`) を本番ワークフローに配線する。手動 dispatch ワークフロー `financials-explainer-jules.yml` の既定レーンを staged に切替え、旧 one-shot (`request:jules:fin`) は `mode=oneshot` の legacy fallback として温存。

| 観点 | 判断 |
|---|---|
| 配線先 | 手動 one-shot WF `financials-explainer-jules.yml`（手動 dispatch・少数銘柄・深掘り品質） |
| cron | **据置**。`financials-jules-request-cron.yml` は最大80銘柄 fire-and-forget。staged は1銘柄≈8分超を逐次占有しbulk不適 → `request:jules:fin` のまま |

author: mikemcdougall
body:
# Pull Request

## Issue Link
Related to honua-io/honua-server#1775

## Summary
Fixes the FeatureServer offline-sync bugs reported in #1775. The headline (HIGH-severity) bug: the GeoServices `synchronizeReplica` **download** direction was a no-op. `createReplica` (serverGen=N) → add a feature server-side → `POST .../FeatureServer/synchronizeReplica` with `syncDirection=download&replicaServerGen=N` returned `{"success":true,"syncDirection":"download","serverGen":N}` with **no `edits`/`layerServerGens` payload**, and `serverGen` echoed the client value (never advanced) — so changes committed after the replica was created were never delivered. The change-tracking engine itself was fine (`extractChanges` and the **upload** direction both work correctly); only the download-assembly path was not wired to it.

This change assembles the download delta through the same change-tracking path `extractChanges` uses, returns it in new `edits`/`layerServerGens` response fields, and advances `serverGen` to the live current generation so each change is delivered exactly once. It also fixes the minor `/replicas` enumeration lag by serving the list from the live registry (`IReplicaStore`) instead of the lagging `IReplicaRepository` snapshot.

## Changes Made
- Extracted the `extractChanges` per-layer delta assembly into a shared `BuildReplicaLayerChangesAsync` helper (preserves the `LastSyncGeneration == 0` full-extract fallback and the per-layer record-limit guard), and made `extractChanges` call it.
- Wired the `synchronizeReplica` download/bidirectional direction to that helper: it now assembles the server-to-client delta since the replica's last-sync generation (or the client-supplied `replicaServerGen`, or the post-apply generation for bidirectional uploads), returns it in `edits`/`layerServerGens`, and advances `serverGen` to the live current generation.
- Added `edits` (`LayerChanges[]`) and `layerServerGens` (`ReplicaInfoLayerServerGeneration[]`) to `SynchronizeReplicaResponse` (both use already source-gen-registered types, so AOT JSON is covered).
- Added `IReplicaStore.ListByServiceAsync`; implemented it in `CachingReplicaStore` (delegates to the authoritative write-through repository) and `DistributedReplicaStore` (in-process fallback registry). `/replicas` (`HandleReplicas`) now reads from the live `IReplicaStore` so create/unregister are reflected immediately.
- Tests: added `SynchronizeReplica_Download_DeliversPostReplicaChangesAndAdvancesServerGen` (createReplica → server-side add → download delivers the feature + serverGen advances + second download is empty) and `Replicas_AfterCreateAndUnregister_ReflectsLiveRegistryImmediately`. Updated the `IReplicaStore` test doubles (`InMemoryReplicaStore`, `ThrowingReplicaStore`) for the new method.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] Architecture tests pass
- [x] Manual testing performed

## Gate Impact
- [x] PR gates (build, test, governance)
- [ ] Nightly gates (conformance, performance, security)
- [ ] Release gates (packaging, publishing)
- [ ] Deploy gates (promotion, post-apply validation)

## Docs or Contract Impact

## Release/Deploy Impact

## Breaking Changes
None. The new `synchronizeReplica` response fields (`edits`, `layerServerGens`) are additive and omitted when null; the `/replicas` source change is internal.

The unserialize filter has a weakness to arbitrary class usage which can be combined with user input to create unserialization gadgets which are used in RCE vulnerability chains.

author: youxuanxue
body:
## 背景

排查 `vol-test` key / `volcengine`(newapi, channel_type=45)账号无法生成 seedance 视频时发现(根因另由 #861 修复——该账号的 `model_mapping` 缺 seedance)。账号 7 本身配置正确,但排查中翻出两个真实的潜伏 bug,都会**静默搞坏一个 newapi 账号并抛出莫名其妙的错误**,与我们想保留的上游行为无关。

## Bug 1 —— 账号创建无 platform 白名单(与分组不对称)

**影响**:账号可以存进一个非法 `platform` 字符串然后永不调度,且无任何诊断。

- 账号 create / batch / import 三条路径的 `platform` 只绑 `binding:"required"`——**没有 `oneof`**(`account_handler.go:103`/`:169`/`:2213`;`admin_service.go:2657`/`account_service.go:176` 原样存)。
- **分组**路径早已强制 `oneof=anthropic openai gemini antigravity newapi kiro grok`(`group_handler.go:87/132`)。于是分组拒绝 `"volcengine"`,账号却**接受**。
- `"volcengine"` 是经典陷阱:它是 **newapi** 平台上的 `channel_type`(45),不是独立平台。池成员判定是严格平台相等(`engine.IsOpenAICompatPoolMember` / per-platform 桶),所以 `platform="volcengine"` 的账号**进不了任何池**,每个请求都空池快失败 **HTTP 429 "No available accounts"**——完全看不出是平台字符串的问题。

**修复**:在 `tkValidateNewAPIAccountCreate` 里用 `engine.AllSchedulingPlatforms()`(可调度平台的单一真值源)校验 platform;该函数已被三条 create 路径调用(`account_handler.go:530` Create、`:1364` BatchCreate、`account_data.go:698` import)。未来新增平台自动纳入校验。非法平台现在返回清晰 400:`platform "volcengine" is not a valid account platform (must be one of: …)`。

## Bug 2 —— `GetBaseURL()` 对所有平台的空 base_url 都回退 `api.anthropic.com`

**影响**:非 anthropic 的 apikey 账号空 base_url 会把请求发到 Anthropic 主机,返回莫名其妙的 Anthropic 404/401,而不是干净失败。

- `Account.GetBaseURL()`(`account.go:748`)对**任何**平台的空 base_url 都返回硬编码 `"https://api.anthropic.com"`。newapi(VolcEngine Ark, channel_type=45)账号空 base_url 会 POST 到 `https://api.anthropic.com/api/v3/contents/generations/tasks`。
- `newapi_bridge_usage.go:72` 里的平台特定兜底(`if baseURL == "" && Platform != newapi`)因此是**死代码**——GetBaseURL 永不返回空。

**修复**:仅对 `anthropic` 平台(及 legacy 空 platform 行,历史上都是 anthropic)回退 anthropic 默认;其它平台返回 `""`,交给平台特定 resolver(newapi Ark/OpenAI 兜底)或干净的上游失败。

## Summary

- What changed: Adds `adapters/ios-keyboard/swift/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh`, an Xcode Cloud post-clone script that installs the Rust toolchain (with the `aarch64-apple-ios` and `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` targets) and `xcodegen`, then runs `make platform-build-ios`.
- Why: The iOS project is fully generated and intentionally gitignored — `KhmerIME.xcodeproj` (xcodegen), `Frameworks/KhmerIME.xcframework` (cargo + `xcodebuild -create-xcframework`), and `KhmerIMEKeyboard/Generated/*` (uniffi-bindgen). Xcode Cloud only clones committed files, so the build failed at `-resolvePackageDependencies` with "KhmerIME.xcodeproj does not exist". The post-clone hook regenerates all three artifacts before Xcode Cloud resolves packages and builds.

- In scope: Xcode Cloud CI bootstrap for the iOS keyboard build (single shell script).

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is an open-source control plane for managing AI agents and their work.
> - New companies receive role-specific onboarding instructions from the server onboarding assets.
> - The CEO bundle defines the CEO agent's scope, heartbeat, operating posture, and available-tool guidance.
> - Ambiguous scope and placeholder tooling guidance could cause a CEO agent to perform specialist work, cross role boundaries, or leave work without a durable continuation path.
> - The change therefore narrows CEO authority, makes delegation and lifecycle handling explicit, and documents safe configuration and tool use.
> - This pull request changes only the four CEO onboarding Markdown assets.
> - The benefit is clearer, safer, and more auditable CEO behavior without changing runtime code or other agent roles.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

No public GitHub issue exists for this focused instruction cleanup.

**Problem:** The generated CEO instruction bundle contained ambiguous individual-contributor guidance, weak role-boundary language, incomplete lifecycle guidance, and a placeholder `TOOLS.md`.

**Current behavior:** A newly onboarded CEO agent could interpret the bundle as permission to modify other agents' instructions, take over specialist execution, handle secrets inconsistently, or leave Paperclip work without an explicit wake-producing next step.

**Expected behavior:** The CEO bundle should constrain the role to decision, delegation, review, approval, unblock, escalation, and durable operating context; direct specialist work to the correct owner; use governed config and secret references; and describe valid issue lifecycle transitions.

author: aljobson
body:
## Why

The recurring backup pain (a file that wouldn't restore) is preventable: nothing checked that a freshly-created backup could actually be reopened. A backup you can't restore is worse than none.

## Change

- **`verifyBackupEnvelope(envelope, password, pin)`** round-trips the envelope through the **real binary on-disk encoding** (catches any format/serialization defect) and **decrypts BOTH seals** with the chosen backup password + PIN (catches a credential or KDF-param mismatch).
- **Export awaits verification before downloading.** On failure, nothing is saved and the toast says verification failed. Success toast: *"Backup verified ✓ and downloaded — it opens with this password or PIN."* Button shows *"Creating & verifying…"*.
- **Restore screen** now states plainly: *enter the backup password / backup PIN you chose when you created the file — not your app unlock PIN* (the exact confusion behind the unrestorable-looking file).

Cost: 2 extra Argon2id decryptions per export (a few seconds) — cheap insurance for a safety-critical, infrequent action.

## Test plan

- [x] `verifyBackupEnvelope` resolves for the right creds, throws for a wrong password or wrong PIN (real crypto)
- [x] Full `vaultBackup-opacity` suite 6/6 green (binary round-trip, real-crypto decrypt, legacy compat, garbage rejected, verify)
- [x] eslint clean

## 修复内容

### 1. 滚轮方向反转
- `wheelScroll` 中 mouse tracking 路径的 64/65 映射错误：`lines > 0` 对应 HarmonyOS 轴事件向下滚动，应发 button 65（wheel-down），不是 64

### 2. 粘贴需先按 Ctrl+V 的问题
根本原因：`module.json5` 缺少 `ohos.permission.READ_PASTEBOARD` 权限。HarmonyOS 读取其他 app 写入的剪贴板数据需要此权限，否则 `getData()` 静默失败。Ctrl+V 通过 IME 系统路径绕开了权限检查，所以先按 Ctrl+V 之后 Ctrl+Shift+V 才能工作。

添加权限声明后，`getData()` 可直接读取剪贴板，无需 Ctrl+V 前置。

author: sandrosmarzaro
body:
## Problema

A VPS edge precisou de **reset manual** porque o gateway congelou: o log parou em \`socket_created\` e nunca chegou em \`connection_opened\`. O processo seguia vivo, então:

- O healthcheck \`pidof bun\` continuava **healthy** (só prova que o processo existe, não que o WhatsApp está conectado).
- A política \`restart: unless-stopped\` **não reage a status de healthcheck** — Docker só marca o container unhealthy, nunca o reinicia.

Resultado: gateway vivo porém mudo, sem ninguém pra derrubá-lo. O mesmo acontece quando o orçamento de reconexão (5 tentativas) se esgota e o código fica ocioso.

## Fix

`ConnectionWatchdog` transforma o stall silencioso em **saída não-zero**, para a política de restart já existente recuperar do zero:

- **arma** ao iniciar uma tentativa de conexão (`connectToWhatsApp`) e em cada *close* reconectável;
- **desarma** no `connection_opened`;
- **expira** após 120s sem abrir → `process.exit(1)` → Docker reinicia;
- **desabilita** em estados terminais (`loggedOut`, `badSession`) que exigem re-pareamento humano, evitando crash-loop de credenciais.

Sem sidecar de autoheal, sem mudança no healthcheck, sem acesso ao docker.sock — só o mecanismo de restart que o compose já tem.

## Escopo

Cobre a falha observada (preso em `socket_created`) e o give-up de reconexão. O caso de **VPS inteira congelada** (SSH/ping mortos por exaustão de CPU/memória no box de ~1GB) é outro problema, fora deste PR.

## Testes

- `ConnectionWatchdog`: arma/expira/desarma/desabilita (fake timers, `process.exit` espionado).
- `ConnectionUpdateEvent`: desarma no open, desabilita no logout, arma em close reconectável.
- `Resenhazord2`: arma no `connectToWhatsApp`.

190 testes passam, typecheck/eslint/prettier limpos.

Adds `docs/design-system/03-spec/components/switch.md` — the design-system spec for the already-shipped `Switch` primitive (`console/src/components/primitives/Switch.tsx`).

## Why

Six existing, shipped console components had **no `03-spec/components/*.md` artifact** (avatar, menu, tooltip, popover, action-button, **switch**). This closes the Switch gap — part of getting the canonical components/primitives/rules firmly documented, not just landed. Doc-only; no product change.

## Contents

Mirrors the `segmented.md` template and is grounded entirely in verified source (`Switch.tsx` + the `.soup-switch` CSS + the showcase `.switch` recipe):
- **Anatomy** (row → `role=switch` track → thumb), with the tokens each part consumes.
- **Conceptual props**, **showcase → token mapping** (e.g. swatch `#fff` thumb → `--surface-raised`; adds the hairline frame, focus ring, disabled affordance the raw swatch omits).
- **States**, **`role=switch` a11y contract** (native button keyboard, `aria-labelledby`/`aria-label`, stylesheet reduced-motion).
- **Examples / anti-patterns** — distinct from `Checkbox`/`CheckboxField` (opt-into-a-set) and `Segmented` (one-of-N).
- **Enforcement hooks** — active reduced-motion guard noted; a `soup/no-raw-switch` rule and a behavioural suite flagged as **G3-pending** (no `tests/console/*switch*` exists yet).

## Verification (local, CI parity)

- `guard:doc-drift` ✅  `guard:design-system-hygiene` ✅  `design:token-drift` ✅ (PASS)
- `verify:console-design` ✅ — 14 design-guard files, 182 tests passed
- Diff scope: 1 file, +99 lines, no product/code/token change

Status line: `v3.0.0-draft · G2-locked direction · pending G3` (matches sibling specs).

author: vigneshashokan
body:
## What & why

xPts fast-follow (from #30). `player_gw_history` was populated **once** by the manual 2025/26 backfill; there was no ongoing capture, so when the new season plays out the model's serving window (`fpl-project`) would never advance and the training set would never grow. This adds **automatic, idempotent, self-healing** per-GW capture.

## How

Extends the existing `fpl-ingest` Deno function with a new `?source=history` route (no new function):

- Each run reads `bootstrap-static` events, computes the current season's `finished && data_checked` GWs **missing** from `player_gw_history`, and captures them — so a missed run or a late-settling midweek GW is caught automatically.
- Per missing GW: **one** `event/{gw}/live/` call (confirmed to carry all xG/bps/`defensive_contribution` fields), joined against the `fixtures` table (opponent/home) + bootstrap meta (position/team/price), upserted with `onConflict: 'season,player_id,fixture_id'`.
- A daily cron (`fpl-ingest-history`, 03:30 UTC) drives it — a cheap no-op on quiet days; lands **before** `fpl-project`'s 04:00 serving read.

### Pieces
- Pure transforms: `selectMissingGws`, `liveToHistoryRows`, `currentSeasonLabel`.
- Orchestrator: `ingestHistory` (reuses `fetchJson` + `startRun`/`finishRun`/`skipRun`; shows up in `ingestion_runs`).
- Enabling: widened the `ingestion_runs.source` CHECK + `startRun` type to allow `'history'`.

### Accepted approximations (per spec)
- **Double-gameweek → one aggregate row** on the player's first fixture (live gives GW-aggregate stats; no per-fixture xG).
- **`value` = current `now_cost`** (live has no per-GW price). Capture is only `finished && data_checked` GWs (never the live, mutable one).

## Testing
Deno toolchain (the function is excluded from repo jest/tsc): pure-transform tests (field mapping, DGW collapse, blank→no row, 0-minute rows, home **and** away, string coercion), self-healing GW selection, orchestrator skip/success bookkeeping, and the route dispatch. **Full suite 68/68**; `deno check **/*.ts` clean.

## Reviewed
Per-task spec+quality reviews + a final whole-branch review (opus) — **no Critical/Important**. The reviewer verified the `'history'` source is accepted end-to-end (Source guard + `startRun` type + the DB CHECK widening, incl. the auto-named constraint the migration drops).

## Deploy note
Merging triggers the Supabase CI (`supabase/**` path filter): it `db push`es the two migrations (CHECK widen + the new cron) and redeploys `fpl-ingest` with the new route. No workflow change needed (CI already deploys `fpl-ingest` by name).

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-18-per-gw-history-capture-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-18-per-gw-history-capture.md` (workspace repo).

- All additive + togglable; defaults preserve prior behavior.

body:
Adds `.claude/skills/cut-release/SKILL.md` — a lean, in-repo runbook for cutting and publishing an Atrium release, so the procedure is deterministic and rides into every worktree.

## What it captures
- The two load-bearing invariants: curated notes must live in the **tagged commit** (`notes → merge → tag`), the `v`-prefix on the notes filename is load-bearing, and the release is `draft: true` (a human publishes).
- A 6-step procedure + quick-reference command table.
- Environment gotchas (ZviBaratz `GH_TOKEN`, go/hooks PATH, stale golangci cache across worktrees, `just release` tags current HEAD, zsh `status`/`cd`).
- A **recovery path** for a bad tag / wrong notes filename (using `replace_existing_draft: true`, valid only while still a draft).
- The rationale for **rejecting a CI Anthropic-key step** for note generation, so it isn't re-introduced.

## How it was authored
Skill-authoring TDD. A no-guidance baseline agent already reconstructed the runbook from the repo + CLAUDE.md, so this is deliberately scoped as a **determinism/speed artifact**, not a heavyweight discipline skill. A skill-only comprehension test passed every probe; the recovery section closes the one gap it surfaced.

Distilled from the v0.7.0 release executed in this session (PR #161 → tag `v0.7.0`).
