author: rysweet
body:
## KEYSTONE de-fork — Phase 1

**Goal:** make the Rust `CognitiveMemory` usable with a **persistent** backend so consumers (e.g. Simard) can depend on this library instead of carrying a ~5,900-line private reimplementation of cognitive memory over `lbug`. Today the library only ships an in-memory `CognitiveMemory`; this PR closes that gap **upstream**, where bugs and features belong.

## Problem

- `CognitiveMemory` talked to its store only through the `GraphStore` trait but **hardcoded** `InMemoryGraphStore` — nothing persisted across restarts.
- The persistent `backends/ladybug_backend/` implements an *Experience* interface, **not** `GraphStore`, so it can't back `CognitiveMemory`. There was **no** persistent `GraphStore` implementation.

## What this PR does

### 1. `CognitiveMemory` is backend-pluggable (backward compatible)
The struct now holds a `Box<dyn GraphStore>`. Because `GraphStore` is object-safe and every recall path already filters in Rust, **all six memory submodules and the public API are unchanged** (dyn dispatch).

- `CognitiveMemory::new(agent)` — **unchanged**, still in-memory.
- `CognitiveMemory::with_store(agent, Box<dyn GraphStore>)` — plug in any backend.
- `CognitiveMemory::open_persistent(path, agent)` — durable LadybugDB instance (`#[cfg(feature = "persistent")]`). Recovers the auto-increment `temporal_index` / `sensory_order` counters from persisted data on open.

### 2. New persistent `GraphStore` over the **published** `lbug` crate
`src/graph/lbug_store/` adds `LbugGraphStore`, a full `GraphStore` implementation backed by `lbug = "=0.15.3"` (the same engine Simard uses), behind a new **off-by-default** `persistent` feature. It is modeled on the in-tree Kùzu backend but executes Cypher via lbug's native Rust API (`Database`/`Connection`/`QueryResult`/`Value`), porting the proven durability patterns from Simard's native module:

- **Dynamic schema** — node/rel tables created on first use; properties map to `STRING` columns (mirrors the in-memory backend so converters round-trip identically).
- **Reopen-safe** — catalog introspection (`CALL show_tables` / `table_info`) makes prior-process data visible after close + reopen.
- **Durability** — per-write `fsync` barrier (data file + parent dir) and `BEGIN/COMMIT` for multi-statement ops.
- **Injection-safe** — identifier validation (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`), `escape_cypher` for all values, type-safe `usize` limits.

### 3. Correct retrieval semantics
The recall bugs the consumer fork had are fixed/confirmed here:
- **Idempotent procedure storage** — `store_procedure` now dedups by name (updates in place) instead of accumulating duplicates.
- Tokenized multi-word OR-CONTAINS recall, case-insensitive matching, and **keyword-overlap** trigger matching were already correct in the library's Rust-side filtering — now covered by persistent-backend tests too.

## Tests (TDD — written first)
- `graph::lbug_store::tests` — GraphStore round-trips, escaping, unbounded limits, edges, **close+reopen persistence**.
- `cognitive_memory::tests::persistent_tests` — store+recall for episodes/facts/procedures/prospective triggers; tokenized multi-word recall; idempotent procedures; keyword-overlap trigger firing; agent isolation; metadata round-trip; **durability across close+reopen** with counter recovery.

Results:
- `cargo test` (default, in-memory) — **446 passed**, no warnings.
- `cargo test --features persistent` — **462 passed**, no warnings.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; new code is clippy-clean; `cargo doc` clean for both feature sets.

## Notes
- Additive and backward compatible — the in-memory path and existing consumers are unchanged; the Experience/`ladybug_backend` code is untouched.
- The `persistent` feature compiles the LadybugDB (Kùzu) C++ engine from source via `lbug`, so it needs `cmake` + a C++ toolchain. A **non-blocking** CI step runs the persistent tests (the C++ build is slow on shared runners).
- All `lbug` transitive deps (`cxx`, `rust_decimal`, `time`, `uuid`) are MIT/Apache-2.0 — within `deny.toml`'s allowlist.
- Pre-existing clippy lints surfaced by newer toolchains (e.g. in `in_memory_store.rs`, `hierarchical_memory/`) are left untouched as out of scope.

This is **phase 1**; a follow-up will migrate Simard to consume this library and retire its fork.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>



---

## Step 13: Local Testing Results

Outside-in testing was performed with the `qa-team` skill. This PR's substantive
change is a **Rust library** change (the `amplihack-memory` crate), and this repo
exposes **no `amplihack` Python console script** (its package is
`amplihack-memory-lib`, with no `[project.scripts]`). The real downstream user of
this change is a **Rust crate** (e.g. Simard) that consumes the library via a
cargo **git dependency** with the `persistent` feature. So the standard
`uvx --from git+...@<branch> amplihack <command>` pattern was adapted to its Rust
equivalent: an external consumer crate that depends on the **PR branch** over git
(not the working directory) and runs against the published `lbug = 0.15.3` engine.

External consumer `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
amplihack-memory = { git = "https://github.com/rysweet/amplihack-memory-lib.git", branch = "feat/issue-84-keystone-de-fork-task-for-amplihack-memory-lib-sim", features = ["persistent"] }
```

Resolved to PR-branch commit `7ecb118` + `lbug v0.15.3` (the exact published
crate Simard uses). Build compiled the LadybugDB C++ engine from source in 2m25s.

### Scenario 1 — basic persistent round-trip (most basic user-facing behaviour)
Command: `cargo run` against `git+https://github.com/rysweet/amplihack-memory-lib@feat/issue-84-...` → `./target/debug/consumer scenario1`

### Scenario 2 — durability + corrected retrieval semantics + in-memory regression (edge cases / integration)

**Note:** Scenario 2 initially flagged one assertion (`second store updated steps

### 1. SEO foundations (from `claude/sleepy-nightingale-2c67f2`)
The migrated Next.js site shipped with SEO gaps vs. the live Webflow site. This adds, with **no schema changes**:
- `src/lib/site-url.ts` — client-safe `SITE_URL`/`absoluteUrl`/`mediaUrl` + a `SITE_NOINDEX` flag for the pre-launch preview deployment.
- `src/lib/seo.ts` — `pageMetadata()` builder (description, canonical, Open Graph + `summary_large_image` Twitter card, robots) and a cached site-settings fetch.
- `src/components/structured-data.tsx` — JSON-LD builders (Organization/NGO, Restaurant, FAQPage, Event, BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList).
- `src/app/sitemap.ts` — dynamic sitemap of published pages/locations/events/journal posts.
- `src/app/robots.ts` — allow crawling, disallow `/admin` + `/api/`, advertise the sitemap; disallow everything when `SITE_NOINDEX` is set.
- `src/app/icon.svg` + `src/app/apple-icon.tsx` — favicon + Apple touch icon.
- `src/app/(frontend)/opengraph-image.tsx` — branded 1200×630 default OG card.
- Wired into the layout, home, `[...slug]`, location/event/journal detail pages, and the FAQ block.

### 2. Unify Pages SEO onto the shared `seoField` + per-page `noindex`
Pages previously declared its own inline `seo` group (title/description/image only), while Locations, Events and JournalPosts all use the shared `seoField`, which also exposes a `noindex` checkbox. This:
- Swaps Pages onto `seoField` (src/collections/Pages.ts) so CMS pages get the same per-page `noindex` control and a consistent admin sidebar SEO panel.
- Wires `noindex: page.seo?.noindex` into `pageMetadata()` on the home (`/`) and catch-all (`/[...slug]`) routes, emitting `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` when set. These were intentionally omitted from the original SEO pass because the field didn't exist on Pages yet.
- Widens `pageMetadata`'s `noindex` input to `boolean | null` to match the generated Payload type (consistent with how `title`/`description` are typed).

## Migration

Ships the required Payload migration `20260619_060311_add_pages_seo_noindex`, **generated against a clean database** (per project convention). Adds `pages.seo_noindex` and `_pages_v.version_seo_noindex`.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — passes.
- `pnpm build` — compiles successfully.
- `pnpm payload generate:types` — `noindex` now present on the Pages SEO type.
- `pnpm payload migrate` on a clean temp DB applied the full chain incl. the new migration; a follow-up `migrate:create` reports **"No schema changes detected"**, confirming the Drizzle snapshot is accurate.

## Reviewer notes

- This PR combines the SEO foundations branch (`3275ac5`) with the seoField/noindex follow-up. The SEO branch did not have its own PR, so both land here together.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is baked at build time and drives every canonical/OG/sitemap URL — production must set it to the final domain.
- Moving Pages SEO to the shared field relocates the SEO panel to the admin **sidebar** (matching the other collections).

author: bl4ko
body:
Extends the reusable image-build workflow so repos can publish **signed** images to the homelab Harbor alongside GHCR. Foundation for slocar (and all future image-publishing repos).

## What changed
- New inputs: `harbor-tags` (comma-separated Harbor tags to also push; empty = GHCR-only) and `sign` (cosign-sign the pushed Harbor image).
- New optional `secrets:` — `HARBOR_ROBOT_USER`/`HARBOR_ROBOT_TOKEN` (the `ci-push` robot) and `COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY`/`COSIGN_PASSWORD`.
- Conditional **Login to Harbor** (`harbor.xqx.uk`) when `harbor-tags` is set.
- The build pushes one build to **both** registries (GHCR tags unchanged, Harbor tags appended).
- When `sign: true`, **cosign** signs the pushed Harbor image **by digest** (one sig per image, deduped across tags) with the homelab key-based key.
- `cosign.pub` committed for later in-cluster verification (Kyverno/policy-controller).

## Backward compatible
Existing callers pass none of the new inputs/secrets → behaves exactly as before (GHCR-only, no signing). All new inputs default to off; secrets are `required: false`.

## Pins
- `sigstore/cosign-installer@v4.1.2` (SHA-pinned `6f9f1778`), consistent with the repo's pin policy.

## Notes
- Consumers pin shared-actions by commit SHA → callers (slocar, Phase 2) bump to this SHA to use it.

## Problem

Na iOS, będąc na Dashboardzie, gest swipe-back pokazywał dialog „Opuścić aplikację?". Klik „Wyjdź" zamykał dialog, ale **aplikacja zostawała otwarta** — przycisk był martwy.

- **Android** → `{ activity.finish() }` jak dotąd

Dialog wyjścia pokazuje się **tylko gdy istnieje akcja zamknięcia** (`exitApp != null`). Na iOS na Dashboardzie back nie robi nic widocznego — wyjściem z aplikacji zarządza OS (gest home). Mylący popup już się nie pojawia.

## Weryfikacja

Skompilowane wszystkie trzy źródła — `commonMain`, `iosSimulatorArm64`, `androidMain` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, podpisy `expect`/`actual` zgodne.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

First step of the Slice F (env_dirty removal / single-store) endgame: make the reverse-sync measurement and the `merge_method_env` dirty signal *precise* for shared containers.

`cheaply_unchanged` — the conservative value-identity test used by both the `MUTSU_VM_STATS` reverse-sync survey and `merge_method_env`'s precise `env_dirty` signal — had no `ContainerRef` arm, so the generic `_ => false` reported every `ContainerRef`/`ContainerRef` pair as "changed", even when both sides are the **same** shared cell.

That cell is the single-store design's identity primitive: `my @a := @b` already installs **one** shared `ContainerRef` into both the env entry and the local slot for both names. The missing arm meant:

- the reverse-sync survey counted `:=`-bound containers as **effective** stale pulls when they are in fact coherent. On a bound-container probe the survey now reports `effective=0 spurious=6` (was `effective=6 spurious=0`) — **proving `:=`-bound containers need no reverse-sync**, a key prerequisite finding for removing `env_dirty`;
- `merge_method_env` over-signalled `env_dirty` for a method that merged back the same cell, forcing a spurious caller locals pull.

## Change

```rust
(Value::ContainerRef(a), Value::ContainerRef(b)) => Arc::ptr_eq(a, b),
```

Same Arc → genuinely unchanged; distinct Arcs stay "changed" (conservative — never deep value equality).

## Tests

- Unit tests `cheaply_unchanged_tests` (same-cell → unchanged, distinct-cell → changed).
- `make test` 9203 passing.

author: jerryfane
body:
Fixes #309.

## Problem
Delegation validation returned generic, first-error-only messages (`"delegation action is required"`) with no entry/field identification, so a coordinator emitting a malformed `delegations[]` couldn't tell which entry/field to fix, and the single repair retry could only address one problem at a time.

## Fix
Field- and index-specific, **aggregated** validation errors. A typed `DelegationValidationError{Index,ID,Field,Msg}` renders `delegations[<i>] (id "<id>"): <field> <msg>` (blank id → `<missing>`); `validateAgentResult` now collects **all** per-delegation field failures and returns them via `errors.Join` before the graph check. The repair prompt surfaces them as a `Validation errors (fix every line):` checklist, and `delegationSchemaHelp` names the positional format. The single repair retry is unchanged; already-id-bearing graph/cycle/dup/ephemeral messages are byte-identical.

## Changes
- `internal/workflow/result.go` (+test): typed error, index loop, `errors.Join` aggregation, the 3 generic errors upgraded.
- `internal/prompts/prompts.go` (+test): repair checklist + schema-help hint.
- `skills/gitmoot/references/RESULT_CONTRACT.md` + `website/docs/reference/result-contract.md`: documented.

## Verification
- `go build/vet`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./internal/workflow/` — all green.
- `/code-review high --fix` — clean (the `validateDelegationTarget`/`Lifecycle` errors stay in their existing id-bearing form by design; only the 3 generic errors changed).
- **Live codex E2E** (isolated `--home`): a coordinator emitting a malformed `delegations[]` (d1 missing `prompt`, d2 missing `action`) produced, through the real engine, one aggregated error — `delegations[0] (id "d1"): prompt is required` + `delegations[1] (id "d2"): action is required` — in the `malformed_output` event, and `repair_retry` fired. Codex's valid output still passes (proven by the #310 runs).

author: newzlong
body:
## Problem (audit MEDIUM #10)
`parallel_delegate` caps a single call at 10 concurrent tasks and `subagent_spawn` caps the registry at 10 running sessions, but those limits are **independent with no process-wide ceiling**. One `parallel_delegate` (10 agentic loops) + a full `subagent_spawn` registry (10 background) → **~20 simultaneous agentic loops**, each issuing provider calls in a tight tool loop: an instant 429 storm against a rate-limited provider, uncapped spend against a paid one, 20× the memory of one conversation. The per-tool caps look safe in isolation but compose multiplicatively.

## Fix
One process-global `Arc<Semaphore>` (`MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTIC_LOOPS = 16`) shared by both tools via `tools::agentic_semaphore()`. Each acquires a permit **inside its spawned task, just before the agentic loop runs** (tasks still spawn immediately but queue on the global ceiling rather than all hammering the provider at once); the permit is held until the loop returns. Acquisition is graceful (`.ok()`) — the static semaphore never closes. No new config key (YAGNI — a safety ceiling, not a tuning knob).

## Tests
Pins that both tools draw from ONE shared semaphore (`Arc::ptr_eq`) sized to the const. Full lib suite green (4173).

## Risk / rollback
Low–Medium (`src/tools/**`) — additive backpressure; documented as a cost/rate guard, not a security boundary (single-user desktop threat model). Rollback = revert.

2026-06-19 architecture audit, MEDIUM #10.

author: jerryfane
body:
Fixes #310.

## Summary
Two built-in **coordinator recipe templates** — `review-panel` and `decompose-and-verify` — plus a small engine fix that makes a recipe's read-only verify/follow-up step runnable from a local `orchestrate`. Recipes are pure prompt-templates: the coordinator emits a `delegations[]` of **ephemeral** workers (no pre-registration), and Gitmoot runs the DAG + continuation.

- **`review-panel`** — fans a PR/change out to a panel of ephemeral reviewers with diverse lenses (no deps → parallel), then synthesizes one verdict. Self-contained (no pre-installed template required).
- **`decompose-and-verify`** — decomposes a task into file-disjoint parallel `implement` legs + a `deps`-gated `verify` step; the continuation gates on verify.

## Changes

author: srmadscience
body:
## What

The CGI `sysinfo.cgi` dump truncates the device `Name` column to ~16 chars and leaves it blank for many clients, so true device names were unavailable. This adds a second, best-effort fetch against the Velop's **JNAP `GetDevices3`** API to pull the full `friendlyName` for each device and store it in a new `velop.device.friendly_name` column.

## How

`cli.main()` → `fetch_sysinfo` → `parse.*` → **`enrich_friendly_names` (JNAP)** → `enrich` (OUI) → store.

- **`fetch.py`** — `fetch_jnap_devices()` POSTs `GetDevices3` (JSON API at `/JNAP/`, auth via the `X-JNAP-Authorization` Basic header the Velop expects). `jnap_url()` derives the endpoint from `router_url` unless `VELOP_JNAP_URL` overrides it.
- **`parse.py`** — pure `friendly_name_index()` builds a `{deviceID/MAC → friendlyName}` map; `enrich_friendly_names()` joins it onto device records by UUID, then MAC (primary + extras). Tolerates malformed payloads.
- **`store.py`** — new `friendly_name` column on `velop.device`. `MIGRATIONS` runs a plain `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` (CrateDB has **no** `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) and swallows the "already has a column" error so re-runs are idempotent.
- **`cli.py`** — JNAP fetch + enrich is **best-effort**: a network/auth failure logs a note and leaves `friendly_name` NULL rather than losing the snapshot.
- **`config.py`** — optional `VELOP_JNAP_URL`.

## Testing

- Full suite **56 passing** (4 new: UUID/MAC/extra_macs matching + junk payloads).
- Verified end-to-end against the live router + CrateDB: **48/70** devices named, including ones the CGI dump left blank (`Android`, `IPCAM`, `Celetons-iMac-1091`, …); migration adds the column to the pre-existing table idempotently.

## Note

`friendlyName` is Linksys's *derived* label, not always the raw DHCP hostname — for some devices it's synthesized. It's still the fullest name source the router exposes.

author: hp-100
body:
### Motivation

- 为了与现有 `DDPG-MIRT` MLP 基线并行比较，新增一个真正基于序列回放、burn-in 与 BPTT 的循环确定性策略 `RDPG-MIRT`，确保训练与评估都保持连续的隐状态传递并避免把 LSTM 仅当作单步模块使用。 
- 需要保存完整 episode、支持 burn-in/unroll 采样并以掩码计算时间步损失以保证正确的序列梯度传播和目标网络一致性。

### Description

- 新增循环 Actor/ Critic 与序列训练流水线，包括 `models/mirt_recurrent_actor.py`（提供 `init_hidden`, `forward_sequence`, `forward_step`，架构 `LayerNorm(75) -> LSTM(75,128) -> Linear/ReLU/Linear`）、`models/mirt_recurrent_critic.py`（LSTM 编码 state sequence 后 concat action -> Q）。
- 新增 `agents/sequence_replay_buffer.py`（episode 级保存、返回 `[B, burn+unroll, ...]` 片段与 `valid_mask`、不存 hidden）和严格实现 burn-in + unroll 的训练器 `agents/mirt_rdpg_trainer.py`（burn-in 无梯度、unroll BPTT、目标网络同 burn-in、Huber masked mean loss、延迟策略更新、soft update、梯度裁剪与 q_clip）。
- 新增评估策略 `evaluation/policies/rdpg_mirt_policy.py`、训练脚本 `scripts/train_mirt_rdpg.py`、配置 `configs/mirt_rdpg.yaml` 与单元测试 `tests/test_mirt_rdpg.py`，并接入 benchmark/CLI 支持 `RDPG-MIRT` 与 `--rdpg-mirt-checkpoint`。
- checkpoint 及 metadata 兼容性规则：新 checkpoint 包含 `actor_architecture = lstm_sequence_bptt`、`state_definition_version`、`hidden_dim`、`burn_in_length`、`unroll_length`、`theta_fit`、`action_mean`/`action_std`、`training_config` 等字段，并在结构不符时明确报错以避免用 MLP checkpoint 装载 RDPG 策略。

### Testing

- 已运行编译/测试：`python -m py_compile models/mirt_recurrent_actor.py models/mirt_recurrent_critic.py agents/sequence_replay_buffer.py agents/mirt_rdpg_trainer.py evaluation/policies/rdpg_mirt_policy.py scripts/train_mirt_rdpg.py` 和 `pytest -q`, 结果为 `39 passed`（全部通过）。
- synthetic smoke 优化耗时约 `1.4165s`，默认配置中的 `burn_in_length = 3`、`unroll_length = 5` 被用于验证訓練流程。
- 单次训练 batch 的真实 tensor shapes 为 `states=(8,8,75)`, `actions=(8,8,37)`, `rewards=(8,8,1)`, `next_states=(8,8,75)`, `dones=(8,8,1)`, `valid_mask=(8,8,1)`，并在一次 smoke 优化中观测到 LSTM 参数有非零梯度（`lstm_grad_nonzero True`, `grad_sum ~ 1.752013`）。
- 已验证训练与评估均持续传递 hidden（采集时跨步骤保留 hidden，验证/评估时 per-student `init_hidden()` 后逐步传递），且 RDPG checkpoint 在架构不匹配时会抛出明确错误，避免错误回退。

author: ndeloof
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #13853: `compose up --build --watch` rebuilt every `depends_on` dependency whenever a watched service changed.
- Root cause: `up --build` sets `BuildOptions.Deps=true` to build dep images at startup. The watch `rebuild()` path mutated the shared `*BuildOptions` to restrict `Services` to the watched service but never reset `Deps`, so `s.build()` switched back to `IncludeDependencies` and walked up the graph.
- Fix: `rebuild()` now works on a local copy of `BuildOptions` and explicitly sets `Deps=false`. The local copy also removes the data race on the shared pointer when concurrent file events fire.
- Bonus: `doBuildBake` was emitting `Image X Building` and tracking `expectedImages` for every service in the project, not just the ones in `serviceToBeBuild`. Filter those side-effects to the actual build set — `cfg.Targets` is still populated for every service so `additional_contexts: service:xxx` references keep resolving.

### Why not the approach in #13854

That PR also forced `IgnoreDependencies` in `selectWatchServices`, which strips dependency configs from the selected project. `create()` and `start()` need those configs (network membership, env interpolation) so the side-effects bleed into the restart path. Resetting `Build.Deps` and filtering the bake event leak is enough.

## Test plan

## Day 12: Doctor Appointment Management

### Features Implemented
* **View Assigned Appointments:** Created `GET /doctor/appointments` API allowing doctors to view their active appointments.
* **Date Filtering:** Implemented a query filter (`?date=YYYY-MM-DD`) so doctors can filter their schedule by specific days.
* **Cancel Appointments:** Created `PATCH /doctor/appointments/:id/cancel` API for doctors to cancel upcoming appointments.

### Security & Edge Cases Handled
* **Data Privacy (Query Select):** Configured the TypeORM QueryBuilder to explicitly select only safe patient data (ID and email), ensuring sensitive data like `password_hash` is never exposed to the frontend.
* **Strict Authorization:** The `doctorId` is extracted directly from the JWT token via `req.user.userId` rather than accepting it as a route parameter, preventing ID-spoofing.
* **Time-Bound Validation (Custom Edge Case):** Added validation comparing the appointment's scheduled time to the current server time to strictly prevent the cancellation of past appointments.
* **Idempotent Cancellations:** Added a check to throw a 400 Bad Request if an appointment is already marked as CANCELLED.

author: darriey
body:
## What

Gridded connectors required a pre-supplied `nc_path` and raised when none was given. Now they **fetch the source granule themselves**, so the gridded path works end-to-end — and the gridded community providers (grace/tws) **activate** in the SYMFLUENCE community routing instead of always falling back to native.

## New `cos/core/fetch.py`

- **`http_download(url, dest)`** — streamed anonymous download, atomic (`.part`→rename), cached. Verification prefers the OS trust store (`truststore`) and falls back to the system **`curl`** for hosts that ship an incomplete cert chain (e.g. `download.csr.utexas.edu`, which only validates via AIA-following clients).
- **`earthaccess_granules(short_name, version, temporal, bbox, dest)`** — Earthdata search + download (login via `~/.netrc`); raises `AuthRequiredError` when login fails so the routing falls back to native.
- **`cache_dir(config)`** — `config['cache_dir']` / `$COS_CACHE_DIR` / temp.

## Wired the GRACE family

Their `reduce_file` reads the raw mascon directly, so live-fetch = download + reduce:

| Connector | Source | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `csr_grace` | CSR RL0603 mascon (`LIVE_URL`) | anonymous |
| `gsfc_grace` | GSFC half-degree mascon (`LIVE_URL`) | anonymous |
| `grace` | JPL CRI mascon via `earthaccess` | Earthdata netrc |

`fetch_series` uses `config['nc_path']` **or** `self._live_fetch()`; one global mascon covers the record, so basin reduction + window-trim happen from a single file (cached).

## Live-validated end-to-end (no nc_path, no creds)

`csr_grace` live-fetched the **real CSR mascon** (curl fallback handled the cert chain) and reduced over the Amazon basin → **140 pts, TWS −324.9..+433.3 mm — identical to the prior manual-download validation**.

## Notes / scope

- The non-GRACE Earthdata gridded connectors (`mod16_et`, `modis_sca`, …) need tile mosaicking before their `reduce_file` can consume raw granules — out of scope here; they keep falling back to native. The reusable helper + the `EARTHDATA_SHORTNAME` pattern make adding them a small follow-up.
- Deps: `earthaccess` (`earthdata` extra + dev), `truststore` (`livehttp` extra), both in the mypy override.

## Tests

`cos/core/fetch` unit tests (cache, curl fallback, Earthdata auth error, no-results) + per-connector wiring tests (no path → live-fetch mocked to a fixture → reduce); the obsolete "download not wired" tests repurposed (the csr live smoke now downloads + reduces). **622 offline tests, 86% cov**; ruff + mypy clean.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Audited the codebase for silently swallowed errors and missing error propagation. Key fixes across 8 files:

**Critical initialization failures now surface instead of silently breaking:**
- `GameEngine` constructor throws if `document.getElementById(canvasId)` or `getContext('2d')` returns null — previously would crash with an opaque TypeError later
- `DOMContentLoaded` handler wraps `game.init()` in try-catch so initialization failures are logged

**Game loop no longer dies silently:**
- `gameLoop()` wraps `update()`/`render()` in try-catch — a single entity/system throwing no longer kills the entire animation loop
- `emit()` wraps each event handler so one failing handler doesn't prevent others from running

**Save/Load is now robust to storage and data corruption:**
```js
// Before: JSON.parse(corrupted) → uncaught exception; localStorage full → uncaught QuotaExceededError
// After:
loadGame() {
  try { saveData = localStorage.getItem(...) } catch { return }
  try { data = JSON.parse(saveData) } catch { return }
  if (!data.player) return;
  this.player.x = p.x ?? this.player.x;  // graceful fallback per field
}
```

**Null/undefined guards prevent opaque TypeErrors:**
- `Entity.addComponent()` validates component has a `name`
- `Entity.distanceTo(null)` → `Infinity` instead of crashing; `intersects(null)` → `false`
- `PlayerController.update()` bails if `entity.engine` is not yet set
- `NPC`/`Enemy` constructors validate `data` parameter, provide defaults for optional fields

**SpriteRenderer image loading reports failures:**
- Added `image.onerror` handler — previously a bad `imagePath` silently left `loaded=false` forever

**server.js security and error handling:**
- Path traversal fix: resolves file path and rejects anything outside project root
- Error classification: `ENOENT`→404, `EACCES`→403, `EISDIR`→400, other→500 (was: all→404)
- MIME type table for common asset types (png, jpg, json, svg, audio, fonts)
- `server.on('error')` handles `EADDRINUSE` instead of crashing with an unhandled error

author: csmittee
body:
## Summary

- **Bug A (R-150):** `touchReadOnce()` in ui.h — collapses 3 GT911 I2C reads per idle tick into one cached read (4ms window). GT911 clears its interrupt flag after each `_touch.read()`; the second and third reads in STATE_IDLE returned `isTouched=false` even with finger on screen, dropping brief taps. Fix: `checkServiceGesture()`, `getTouchedSlot()`, and the debug-hold block all call `touchReadOnce()` instead of `_touch.read()`.
- **Bug B (R-151):** Two-layer carry-over touch defence for STATE_GIFT_OPTION. Layer 1: entry guard raised 250ms → 500ms. Layer 2: `setState()` calls `resetGiftTouchDebounce()` on `STATE_GIFT_OPTION` entry, arming `_lastGiftTouchMs = millis()` at the exact moment of transition. `_lastGiftTouchMs` moved from static local inside `getTouchedGiftOption()` to module scope so it can be reset externally.
- **Bug C (R-152):** `PRODUCT_SELECTION_TIMEOUT` constant added to `firmware/config.h.example` (15s default). `g_cfg_sel` in ui.h now initialises from this constant. `config.h.example` created as the tracked template (config.h remains gitignored per R-86).

author: anyulled
body:
💡 What: Replaced the $O(N)$ `speakers.find()` array traversal in `getSpeakerByYearAndId` with a cached `Map` implementation allowing for $O(1)$ property access lookups. Also scrubbed existing JSDoc comments in the file per strict Bolt constraints.

🎯 Why: In components or build steps (like `generateStaticParams` or sitemap generation) that may process hundreds of talks and repeatedly look up speaker details by ID, repeatedly iterating over the speakers array using `.find()` results in $O(N \times M)$ time complexity. Building a map once and performing lookups from it scales significantly better.

📊 Impact: Reduces `getSpeakerByYearAndId` time complexity from $O(N)$ to $O(1)$, dropping the overall time cost from $O(N \times M)$ to $O(N + M)$ for batched lookups.

🔬 Measurement: Run `npm run test` and `npm run build` to verify no regressions in speaker rendering. Profiling a page that renders hundreds of talks (and looks up speaker data for each) will show less CPU time spent traversing the speakers array.

author: bingboom
body:
## What & why

PR 2 of the backport↔branch fix (PR 1 #405 was the resolver). Collapses **resolve → worktree → run-review → push** into one command, auto-creates worktrees for in-review targets, and makes it **structurally impossible for a backport to write the shared template** (the failure mode where BlockClaw guessed `docs/templates/page_eu/00_preface.rst`).

## Commands

```sh
# one-shot branch-targeted backport (dry-run unless --write; --push needs --write)
python tools/cloud_doc_backport.py run-review-branch \
  --cloud-doc "<url>" --page 00_preface.rst [--write] [--push]

# pre-create a worktree for every InReview branch
python tools/cloud_doc_backport.py sync-review-worktrees
```

## The three asks (夏冰)

1. **One command** — `run-review-branch`: resolve the cloud-doc's review branch → ensure its worktree → `run-review` against the worktree `_review` file → (with `--push`) commit + push to update its PR.
2. **A worktree for every in-review target** — `ensure_review_worktree` (idempotent: reuse existing, else fetch + `git worktree add`) on-demand in `run-review-branch`, plus `sync-review-worktrees` to pre-create one per InReview `Git_ref`.
3. **No more guessing into the template** — `derive_review_source_rel` *derives* the source path from the resolved `docs/_review/<model>/<region>` + `--page`; it is never an arbitrary path and is **hard-refused** if it would resolve to `docs/templates/` / `docs/_build/` or escape the review dir.

## Also fixes (live-caught)

`parse_document_id`: region is the **2nd** `_`-segment, so `JE-1000F_EU_en_0.8` → region `EU` (the language segment no longer widens it to `EU_en`, which had pointed the backport at a non-existent `docs/_review/JE-1000F/EU_en`).

## Live-verified (dry-run, real data)

```
run-review-branch --cloud-doc https://…/docx/OWytdlg1ZoUD… --page 00_preface.rst →
  BRANCH codex/review-id-recvhozfkgg7l0
  SOURCE docs/_review/JE-1000F/EU/page/00_preface.rst   (region correct)
  WORKTREE …/review-je1000f-eu  (reused the existing worktree)
  ran run-review; wrote=false pushed=false (dry-run); PR #150
```

## Safety

- [x] Dry-run by default; `--write` applies to the worktree `_review` file; `--push` (needs `--write`) is the only path with a remote side effect.
- [x] Template guard is structural (derived path) + hard-refusal, fully tested.

## Validation

```
python3 -m ruff check build.py integrations tools tests scripts   # All checks passed!
python3 tools/check_maintainability_guardrails.py                  # Guardrails OK
python3 tools/check_doc_link_integrity.py                          # 1257 links, 0 broken
python3 -m unittest                                                # Ran 1009 — OK
```

## Anti-debt

- [x] Pure helpers fully tested (path derivation incl. template/_build/escape refusals, worktree dirname, worktree-list parsing, ensure-worktree reuse-vs-create via injected git).

## Що

Третій+четвертий члени класу wall-clock/life-констант (після 3.3c-B decode, 3.3c-G carrier-TTL): fixed magic-таймаути відеошляху, що ламаються коли стадія біжить довше на 2 vCPU. Вісь — тривалість. Worst-case ~150 хв (модулі itvdn до 2 год).

Два атомарні коміти:

- **`7456ed3` task(3.3c-M2)** — audio-extract (`media.py extract_audio`, ffmpeg `-vn` mp3 re-encode). Прибрано flat `_EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_SEC=600`. Спільний private `_proportional_timeout`; `frame_extract_timeout_for` → делегат (doctests 3.3c-B збережені); новий `audio_extract_timeout_for` (floor 600 / budget 0.2 / cap 1800). `extract_audio(+timeout_sec)`; step_2_stt деривує з `file_metadata.duration_ms`.
- **`41416e4` task(3.3c-M1)** — STT HTTP timeout (elevenlabs scribe + deepgram, `httpx.Timeout(120.0)`). Новий `stt_timeout_for` у `stt/utils.py` (floor 120 / budget 0.1 / cap 1800); `STTRequest +duration_sec`; router проброс; per-request `timeout=` на `.post()`. Video передає ffprobe-тривалість.

## floor/cap (2 vCPU, 150-хв worst-case)

| | floor | budget | cap | @54хв | @150хв |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 STT | 120 | 0.1 | 1800 | 324s | 900s |
| M2 audio-extract | 600 | 0.2 | 1800 | 648s | 1800s (cap=150-хв-бюджет) |

Обидва ≪ `worker_job_timeout` (21600).

## Audio-нога M1 — A1 (без рефактору)

Тривалість pure-audio відома лише **post-STT** (`result.audio_duration_sec`); `probe_metadata` video-only. `duration_sec=None` → `stt_timeout_for(None)` повертає **cap 1800** — покриває 150-хв pure-audio worst-case без ffprobe-рефактору audio-пайплайну. - `openai_stt` (вторинний rung) — межа input-size (DD-3.3c-E), не timeout; не чіпано.
- Client-side chunking — НЕ потрібен: Scribe приймає 10год/3ГБ + parallelise всередині.
- M3 (LLM SDK 900s 🟢), M4 (presentation 60s) — поза цією таскою.

**DD-3.3c-J — webhook-async STT** для довгого аудіо (sync HTTP кілька хв крихко на proxy/LB). Надійність, не capability.

- ruff + ruff-format clean; mypy --strict 138 / no issues.
- doctest: media.py 3 / stt/utils.py 1 passed.

author: rejifald
body:
## What

Fills the one auth scheme core's built-ins don't cover: **request signing**. Core ships bearer / apiKey / basic / cookieSession / oauth2 — none sign requests, which AWS APIs, S3-compatible object stores, and many SigV4-protected endpoints require.

- **`awsSigV4(opts)`** → an `AuthStrategy` whose `apply()` signs the fully-built request (method · canonical URI · sorted query · headers · payload hash) and attaches `Authorization` + `x-amz-date` + `x-amz-content-sha256` (+ `x-amz-security-token` for STS).
- **`signRequestV4(params)`** → the pure signer, exported for out-of-band use (presigned URLs, custom flows).

## Correctness is proven, not assumed

`signRequestV4` is unit-tested against the **official AWS `aws-sig-v4-test-suite` `get-vanilla` vector** — it produces the published signature `5fa00fa31553b73ebf1942676e86291e8372ff2a2260956d9b8aae1d763fbf31` exactly. So this is a verified SigV4 implementation, not just "it runs."

## Details

- **Payload hash**: no body → empty-payload hash; string body → SHA-256 (exact bytes); non-string → `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD` by default (`signBody: true` hashes `JSON.stringify(body)`).
- **Crypto**: platform Web Crypto (`crypto.subtle`) → runs on Node 20+, edge (Workers/Deno), and the browser; `node:crypto` fallback for Node 18. **Zero runtime deps.**
- Credentials are `Secret`s resolved at call time (an agent never sees them); signing happens on the final request after templating/query-building, so it matches the bytes sent.

## Tested & documented

- **6 tests**: the official vector, query canonicalization, and strategy behavior (header attachment, body hashing, session token). ✅
- `check:types` ✅, `tsup` build ✅, prettier ✅, `check-docs-links` ✅ (92 routes).
- Docs: [`integrations/aws-sigv4.mdx`](apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/aws-sigv4.mdx) + a new **Authentication** group in the integrations index.

First of the four you picked (SigV4 · Sentry · Next.js · Vercel AI SDK) — the rest follow as separate PRs. Honest note: generic per-API HMAC isn't included (each vendor canonicalizes differently → no single contract); a one-off scheme is a small custom `AuthStrategy`.

## What

Three pixel-level rendering bugs in prose markdown (`internal/render/markdown.go`), all pure functions with golden ANSI assertions:

1. **Heading style drop (high)** — a heading containing an inline span (`` `code` ``, `**bold**`, `*italic*`) lost its bold/white/underline for the rest of the line, because `inline()` emits `\x1b[0m` after each span. Now the heading style is re-asserted after every inline reset.
2. **Numbered lists unstyled (med)** — only `- `/`* `/`+ ` bullets were styled; `1.` / `2)` ordered lists rendered as undistinguished prose. Added an ordered-list branch (cyan marker, original ordinal + delimiter preserved).
3. **Spaced asterisks italicized (med)** — `\*([^*]+)\*` matched `a * b * c` and shell globs. Now require flanking (CommonMark), applied to italic and bold star patterns.

## Verification

- TDD: 3 failing tests written first (red), confirming all three bugs incl. two that the audit had only flagged (rate-limited verifiers), then fixed (green). Plus a regression guard for real `*italic*`/`**bold**`.
- Real-output eyeball confirms heading style re-asserts after the code span, ordered markers styled, spaced asterisks left raw.
- `make check` + `go test -race ./internal/render/` green; gofmt clean.

## Deferred (on purpose)

Underscore-italic `_x_`: naive support would italicize `snake_case` identifiers (CommonMark disallows intraword underscore emphasis) — a net regression for low value.

author: yunneom
body:
## Why

Production deploys are blocked. The project is under a Hobby **team** on Vercel whose members don't include the repo's commit authors (`yunneom` / automated). Vercel's Git integration refuses the auto production deploy:

> The deployment was blocked because the commit author does not have contributing access to the project on Vercel.

Making the repo public did not help (the team-collaboration restriction still applies). Upgrading to Pro is undesirable pre-revenue.

## Fix

A CLI deploy authenticated with the account owner's `VERCEL_TOKEN` is attributed to the **token owner**, not the commit author — so it sidesteps the block. The existing `preview-deploy.yml` already proves this works (preview deploys succeed via the same token).

This adds `production-deploy.yml`: on push to `main`, run `vercel pull/build/deploy --prod` with the existing `VERCEL_TOKEN` / `VERCEL_ORG_ID` / `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` secrets. Skips cleanly if secrets are missing; concurrency group avoids overlapping prod deploys.

Once merged, this same push triggers the workflow → production (7iq.vercel.app) finally gets the 6-test launch.

- [ ] On merge: workflow runs, `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod` succeeds, 7iq.vercel.app serves the hub

author: marchouze
body:
## What

Makes the L3 inverse index `returnDataObligationsForProduct` (Phase B, PR #1456) **binding** at the NPA gate: a product cannot reach approval unless it **captures — or tracks as a deferred gap on its accounting dimension — the return-cell data it owes**. Marc's goal: "so that a product, when created, knows what information it must have available for the returns to be populated."

## How it composes with the gate policy (D-NPA-GATE-POLICY-REDESIGN)

For each **currently-effective** product, every PRODUCT-SPECIFIC required product-attribute (`<thisProductId>#<attr>`, `required: true`) the L3 index says it owes is checked against the product's declared scope:

| disposition | result |
|---|---|
| attribute captured in scope | ok |
| not captured, **no** tracked gap | **BLOCK** (added to `missing[]`) |
| not captured, a `ProductDeferredGap` on the `accounting` dimension **names** it | pass **with open condition** ("approved subject to tracked gap") |

Never silently passes.

## Keyed off `resolveEffectiveApprovals` (not raw ProductApproved)

The binding reuses the **shared** supersession-aware resolver `resolveEffectiveApprovals` (now exported from `product-approval-attestation-integrity.ts`), so it enforces **only on currently-effective products** — never on withdrawn / retired / superseded approvals (per D-LEGACY-PRODUCT-APPROVAL-SUPERSESSION). On the live store that means exactly **1** product is asserted (`prd:bank:fx:otc-vanilla`); the 8 dead legacy approvals are transparently skipped, not enforced.

Proven by the test `SKIPS a WITHDRAWN product that would otherwise FAIL` — the same non-capturing widget that FAILs when effective passes (asserted=0) once withdrawn.

## Honest scope today (no overclaiming)

Against the **live BA 100 contract**, every product that feeds it owes:
- one **required** product-attribute `tradingBookDesignation` — a **bare, product-agnostic trade-level designation** (the per-instrument `bookDesignation` field), out of this gate's scope by the same boundary `recon:ba-return-cell-contract` already uses; and
- an **optional** `<productId>#balanceSheetClassification`.

So the count of PRODUCT-SPECIFIC **required** attributes enforced **today is legitimately ZERO**, and the gate passes the one effective product cleanly **and says so** in its output. The **mechanism** is the deliverable; it **auto-tightens** the instant Phase C marks any `<productId>#attr` requirement `required: true`. No product-attribute obligations were fabricated to look busy (Engineering Charter cmd 3 + 5).

## New enforcing recon gate

`recon:npa-return-data-obligation-integrity` — blocking, wired into `ci:recon:domain` + `package.json`. F-031 permission-gate carve-out added (read-only replay).

```
recon:npa-return-data-obligation-integrity — 1 effective product(s) asserted, 0 fail, 0 warn, 8 info
recon:npa-return-data-obligation-integrity OK
```

## Tests (17 new)

- gate-check unit tests: captured / missing (**the mandatory negative BLOCK test**) / deferred-by-gapId / deferred-by-title / scope-boundary (ignores optional, bare, co-feeder, gl/projection).
- recon tests: BLOCK negative; pass-with-tracked-gap; **withdrawn-skipped + retired-skipped (the `resolveEffectiveApprovals` proof)**; re-approval re-enforces; empty store; real BA 100 contract → 0 product-specific required attrs → pass.

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` (full project) — clean
- `bun run lint` — clean
- new + sibling gates green on the clean CI-seeded store: `npa-return-data-obligation-integrity` OK, `product-approval-attestation-integrity` OK, `ba-return-cell-contract` 4597 asserted / no violations, `ba-form-numbering` 0 fail.
- `citation-gate` — 0 violations.

> The remaining `ci:recon:infra` / `ci:recon:domain` local failures are the pre-existing home-store-baseline class documented in `run-recon-suite.ts` (event-store-append-only archive-partition gap + v2-parity / golden-source gates that read the populated home store); they pass on a clean CI runner and are unrelated to this change. My new gate is NOT among them.

Authority: `D-BA-RETURN-DATA-CONTRACT` (CEO 2026-06-19), `D-NPA-GATE-POLICY-REDESIGN`, `D-LEGACY-PRODUCT-APPROVAL-SUPERSESSION`.

author: kdwevedi
body:
## Problem

On tenants with `enable_keycloak`, the converge's first compose-up ("Start DIGIT stack") waits on `keycloak: condition: service_healthy`. But the keycloak DB secret (`KC_DB_PASSWORD`) is written to `.env` only **after** that — in the OpenBao block ~480 lines later. So:

1. The first compose-up starts keycloak with the compose-default password.
2. When `.env` later changes (the OpenBao block writes the real secret), keycloak + keycloak-postgres get **recreated**; keycloak races its DB and fails the healthcheck inside compose's dependency-wait.
3. The whole play **aborts** (`dependency failed to start: container keycloak is unhealthy`), silently **skipping every post-compose-up task** — configurator build, overpass, lay-digit-ui, etc.

Net effect on a real deployment: nightly converges only ever rebuilt **digit-ui** (a *pre*-compose-up task). **Configurator and overpass/turbopass never auto-rebuilt** — they stayed as whatever was last built by hand.

## Fix

Add a gated, idempotent **"Keycloak prep"** block immediately before the compose-up that:
- brings up OpenBao + keycloak-postgres,
- unseals OpenBao,
- writes the `KEYCLOAK SECRETS` block to `.env`,
- aligns the keycloak DB-user password to the OpenBao value,

so the dependent compose-up finds keycloak able to start healthy and the play runs to completion. Reuses the same OpenBao tasks/patterns already in the playbook; all gated on `enable_keycloak | default(false)` so keycloak-free tenants are unaffected.

## Validation (bomet reference box)

- Before: play aborted at the keycloak compose-up (~`ok=40`); configurator stuck at a stale build, overpass/turbopass not recreated.
- After: play reached `ok=89`; **configurator rebuilt from develop**, **overpass + turbopass recreated** (first time), **keycloak stayed healthy (no recreate)**, smoke green.

The durable counterpart to the on-box `bomet-redeploy.sh` heal that was papering over this.

author: benartzi4
body:
## Summary

On `/manager/create`, clicking a genre or release-decade chip made the button visibly "shake"/jitter.

**Cause:** the chips' `:hover` rule lifted the element with `transform: translateY(-1px)`. When the cursor rests near a chip's bottom edge, the 1px lift moves the chip's hit-area up and out from under the pointer (into the 0.6rem grid gap), which toggles `:hover` off → the chip drops → the pointer is over it again → `:hover` on → lift → … This loop, smoothed by `transition: transform 100ms`, reads as the box shaking. Both the Genres and Release-decade chips share the `.genre` class, so both were affected.

**Fix:** give the hover "raised" feedback via `box-shadow` instead of a geometry-changing `transform`. The chip's hit-area no longer moves, so hover can't oscillate. Verified on the live page that overriding the hover transform to `none` keeps the chip's box stationary; confirmed clicking a chip causes no page reflow (the only layout shift on the page is the initial genre-list load, unrelated to this).

## Test plan

- Open `/manager/create`, hover and click genre chips and decade chips with the cursor near the bottom edge — no shaking; chips raise smoothly via shadow.
- Selected/hover/unselected visual states still read clearly.
- `npx prettier --check` passes on the edited CSS.

author: iprithv
body:
PairComparison.calculateFrequencyWeightedSimilarity iterated over every unique item in listA and called listB.contains(item) on a List, making the intersection computation O(|uniqueA| × |listB|). Inline the combined weight calculation and use a HashSet for listB membership, computing intersection and union weights in a single pass over the unique items.

This removes the transient combinedWeights map and the quadratic scan while producing the exact same similarity score.

resolves #501

author: mtojek
body:
MCP server names containing characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` (e.g. dotted names like `awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server`) are forwarded verbatim to LLM providers. Bedrock validates tool names against `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$` and rejects the entire request with HTTP 400, breaking the agent turn.

Add `SanitizeToolName()` that replaces invalid characters with underscores. Apply it in both `EncodeToolID` (aibridge proxy path) and `newMCPTool` (chatd agent path). The original tool name is preserved for calling the remote MCP server.

Fixes #26325

> [!NOTE]
> PR generated by Coder Agents on behalf of @mtojek.

<details><summary>Implementation details</summary>

Two code paths construct tool names sent to LLM providers:

1. **aibridge proxy path** (`aibridge/mcp/tool.go`): `EncodeToolID` builds `bmcp_<server>_<tool>`. Server/tool components are now sanitized before encoding.
2. **chatd agent path** (`coderd/x/chatd/mcpclient/mcpclient.go`): `newMCPTool` builds `<slug>__<tool>`. Both slug and tool name components are now sanitized, while `originalName` is preserved for remote MCP server calls.

Both paths reuse `mcp.SanitizeToolName()` which applies `regexp.MustCompile("[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]").ReplaceAllString(name, "_")`.

</details>

author: ossewawiel
body:
## 🎁 S8 — Redeem points (member redemption with a reward)

Closes #19

Members redeem points for a reward — a self-service deduction that records **what** the points bought. Sibling of `spend`, not a rename: own `kind=redeem`, carries a required `reward`, member-initiated.

### 🌐 Endpoint
`POST /accounts/{account_id}/redeem` — member-own / admin-any · `201` new / `200` idempotent replay · `409` insufficient_balance · `404` unknown account · `403` cross-account member.

### 🧩 ~90% reuse, one real cost
| Piece | What S8 did |
|-------|-------------|
| 🗄️ Table-rebuild migration | the only new cost — SQLite can't `ALTER` a `CHECK`; `create→copy→drop→rename` widens `kind` to include `redeem` + adds nullable `reward`. FK-safe inside goose's default txn (nothing references `transactions`). up/down round-trip verified. |
| 🔐 Atomic no-negative guard | reused the S2 in-tx guard — widened its trigger to `spend OR redeem` |
| ⚠️ Sentinels | **none new** — reused `ErrInsufficientBalance` (message generalised; code stays `insufficient_balance`) |
| 🧮 Balance | made the deduction set **explicit** (`WHEN kind IN ('spend','redeem') THEN -points ELSE 0`) so a future kind can't silently be deducted |
| ♻️ Idempotency · 🪪 token identity | free (`UNIQUE(ref)` · `authorizeTarget`) |

`NewTransaction`/`Transaction.kind` stay `[earn,spend]` (redeem has its own endpoint); only `LedgerEntry.kind` widens. Redeem is **not** audited (consistent with earn/spend).

### ✅ Invariants proven — INV-24 … INV-28
deducts & counts · below-zero → 409 · concurrent + redeem-vs-spend no overdraw (`-race`) · member-own/admin-any + reward recorded · idempotent on ref.

### 🚦 Quality gate — all green
`gofmt` · `go vet` · `golangci-lint` (0 issues) · `go build` · `go test -race ./...` (exit 0) · Schemathesis (exit 0, 10104 cases) · ACCEPTANCE INV-24..28 ✅ · PROMPT_LOG · SOLUTION · README synced.

author: gtrabanco
body:
## Summary

Adds the *pull* direction to cross-device card transfer and guards `recoverFromUrl()` against silent card overwrites.

- **Pull transfer (new):** a card-less device opens a receive slot at `/activar`, shows a QR encoding `/activar?recv=CODE`, and polls every 3 s; the card-holding device scans, deposits its card; the generator adopts it. Covers the vehicle-screen case (car browser shows QR, phone scans, car loads phone's card).
- **Push transfer (existing):** `device_codes` table and all existing endpoints are byte-unchanged.
- **Collision guard:** `recoverFromUrl()` now classifies the current card as equal / trivial / non-trivial before adopting an incoming `?card=&k=` card. Non-trivial collisions show feature-10's explicit-choice conflict dialog, generalized for the no-account (local card-id + secret) path. Trivial cards are replaced silently; same card is a no-op.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `migrations/0014_receive_slots.sql` | New additive table (pull direction) |
| `src/pages/api/receive-slot/index.ts` | `POST /api/receive-slot` — create slot |
| `src/pages/api/receive-slot/[code]/deposit.ts` | `POST` — scanner deposits card (atomic write-once) |
| `src/pages/api/receive-slot/[code].ts` | `GET` — generator polls (atomic consume-once) |
| `src/lib/api.ts` | `createReceiveSlot`, `depositToReceiveSlot`, `pollReceiveSlot` |
| `src/pages/activar.astro` | Receive generator mode + scanner deposit / no-card branches |
| `src/pages/index.astro` | Collision guard in `recoverFromUrl()`; conflict dialog mode param |

## Manual verification needed before merge

- `recv:happy` — two-context browser flow (empty window generates, card window deposits, empty window adopts)
- `collision:non-trivial` — card-with-marks lands on `?card=&k=` → dialog; keep-incoming deletes local + adopts; keep-existing closes dialog
- `collision:trivial-silent` — empty minted card silently replaced
- `collision:group-owner` — discard a group-owner card → confirmation step → departure settled
- QR scannability on a real phone camera
- `push:happy` regression — unchanged push flow still works

## Known issues / tracked decisions

- [#27](https://github.com/gtrabanco/bingo-ev/issues/27) — `pollReceiveSlot` maps transient 5xx to `gone` (postponed; workaround: regenerate slot)
- [#28](https://github.com/gtrabanco/bingo-ev/issues/28) — QR render logic duplicated between `index.astro` and `activar.astro` (postponed)
- `decisions.md` D1 — shoulder-surf secret exposure (accepted; same trust posture as push code)
- `decisions.md` D3 — group-beats-solo auto-resolves in local mode (accepted; reuses feature-10 semantics verbatim)

Closes #29

author: markwhitfeld
body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/ngxs/store/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) — every Cypress spec has a Playwright equivalent; full integration suite (`yarn integration:ng22`) passes locally
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) — `.plans/cypress-to-playwright.md` records the plan, decisions, deferred follow-ups, and a Cypress→Playwright API translation table

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

```
[ ] Bugfix
[ ] Feature
[ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
[ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
[x] Build related changes
[x] CI related changes
[ ] Documentation content changes
[x] Other... Please describe: e2e test runner replacement (Cypress → Playwright)
```

## What is the current behavior?

`yarn integration:ng22` was broken on Node 22.22.3 (the toolchain version bumped in the v22 release work). Cypress 13's V8 bytecode loader has explicit per-Node-major patching that only handles up to Node 19, so on Node 22 it fails immediately with:

```
Error: Invalid or incompatible cached data (cachedDataRejected)
    at v (...Cypress\resources\app\index.js:1:2139)
```

Bumping to Cypress 14 (which officially supports Node 22) fixed `yarn integration:ng22`, but exposed adjacent friction:

- TypeScript 6.0 (required by Angular 22) reports `moduleResolution=node10` and `downlevelIteration` as deprecated, breaking Cypress's ts-node and webpack-preprocessor compile passes. Suppression needed in two tsconfigs.
- Cypress's installer download pipeline is heavy (~189 MB chromium-flavored Electron binary per CI run).
- The CI-only Cypress install adds a hard Node-version coupling we'll have to re-fight every major Node release (Cypress 14 → 15 already raised the Node floor again).

Issue Number: N/A — surfaced during the v22 release work on `chore/release-v22`.

## What is the new behavior?

**Cypress is replaced with [@playwright/test](https://playwright.dev/).** End-to-end coverage is preserved 1:1; the runner, config, and yarn-script shape change.

### Spec migrations (3 files, all line-for-line equivalents)

| Old (Cypress) | New (Playwright) |
|---|---|
| `cypress/e2e/list-page.cy.ts` | `e2e/list-page.spec.ts` |
| `cypress/ssr/ssr.cy.ts` (HTTP-only via `cy.request()`) | `e2e/ssr/ssr.spec.ts` (HTTP-only via `request` fixture, no browser) |
| `integrations/hello-world-ng22/cypress/e2e/index-page.cy.ts` | `integrations/hello-world-ng22/e2e/index-page.spec.ts` |

### Configuration

- Two `playwright.config.ts` files (root + integration), `defineConfig` from `@playwright/test`.
- Root config branches on **both** `SSR` and `CI` env vars to mirror today's webServer behavior: `SSR=true` runs SSR specs against the `node dist-integration/server/server.mjs` server; `CI=true` uses the static built bundle; the local default (`!SSR && !CI`) uses `nx serve integration` — same dev-server you get with `yarn e2e` today.
- Integration config is simpler — only the static-server webServer, no SSR/dev branches.
- Playwright's built-in `webServer` config replaces `start-server-and-test` entirely; that devDependency is removed.
- chromium-only project (parity with current Cypress CI behavior — see deferred section for multi-browser).
- Artifacts: `trace: 'on-first-retry'`, `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'`, `video` defaults to off.

### Yarn scripts (root)

**Removed:** `cy:open`, `cy:open:ssr`, `cy:run`, `cy:run:ssr`, `cy:run:chrome`, `cy:run:chromium`, `start-test`, `e2e:chrome`, `e2e:chromium`.

**Replaced/added:**

- `yarn e2e` → `playwright test --ui` (UI mode for local debugging)
- `yarn e2e:ssr` → `cross-env SSR=true playwright test --ui`
- `yarn e2e:headless` → `playwright test` (new — local headless)
- `yarn test:ci:e2e` → `cross-env CI=true playwright test`
- `yarn test:ci:integration:ssr` → `cross-env CI=true SSR=true yarn build:integration && playwright test`

### Yarn scripts (`integrations/hello-world-ng22/`)

- `cy:open`/`cy:run` removed.
- `yarn e2e` → `playwright test --ui`
- `yarn e2e:ci` → `playwright test`
- `test:integration` (called by CI from root) is unchanged at its name boundary — it still internally calls `yarn e2e:ci`, which now resolves to Playwright.

### Dependencies

- **Removed:** `cypress`, `start-server-and-test`.
- **Added:** `@playwright/test@1.61.0` (root). The integration links it via `file:../../node_modules/@playwright/test`, mirroring the previous Cypress wiring.

### CI

- `.github/actions/setup/action.yml` gets a single new step: `yarn playwright install --with-deps chromium`. On Linux runners `--with-deps` installs the chromium system-lib dependencies in one step; no-op on macOS/Windows.
- Workflows (`pr-validation`, `trunk`, `release`) are **unchanged** — they call `yarn integration:ng22` and that script name is preserved.
- `.circleci/config.yml`: the (workflow-commented-out) `cypress` job is renamed to `e2e` for hygiene.
- The artifact-upload action's path glob (`./integrations/**/dist-integration/**/main*.js`) is unaffected — Playwright doesn't change the Angular build output.

### Local verification

- `yarn integration:ng22` exits **0**: vitest (3 passed) + Angular production build + Playwright (2 passed in ~2.5 s).
- Zero remaining `cypress` references in source (only `.nx/workspace-data/` cache references which Nx refreshes on next run).

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```

The CI entry point (`yarn integration:ng22`) and project-build scripts are preserved at their name boundaries. Local developers will see a different e2e command shape (`playwright test --ui` instead of Cypress's GUI launcher) and need a one-time `yarn playwright install chromium` after pull.

## Other information

### Deferred follow-ups (intentionally out of this PR's scope)

Recorded in `.plans/cypress-to-playwright.md` under "Deferred Follow-ups":

1. **Convert to `@nx/playwright` plugin** — wire e2e into Nx via `nx run integration:e2e`, gain Nx caching and project-graph awareness. Defer until standalone Playwright is stable through a release cycle.
2. **Convert SSR organization from env-var to Playwright projects** — currently `SSR=true` toggles `testMatch` + `webServer.command`. Playwright's `projects` array could model this idiomatically with `--project=ssr`. Defer so we can assess the two approaches side-by-side.
3. **Pre-existing root `integration` app serve infrastructure issues** — surfaced during this migration but **not caused by it**:
   - `integration/project.json` `serve` target uses deprecated `browserTarget` instead of `buildTarget`, so `yarn serve:integration` errors.
   - `serve:integration:static` points at `dist-integration` but the Angular `outputMode: "server"` build puts the browser bundle under `dist-integration/browser/`.
   - The SSR server returns an empty `<app-root></app-root>` shell at `/list` rather than rendered content, blocking the SSR specs' assertions.

   Until these are fixed, the root `e2e/list-page.spec.ts` and `e2e/ssr/ssr.spec.ts` cannot be locally validated. The spec ports are verified line-for-line against their Cypress originals. CI is unaffected — only `yarn integration:ng22` (against `hello-world-ng22`) runs in workflows.

### Commit history

16 small semantic commits, structured as three phases:

- **Cypress fixes (2)**: bump Cypress to 14 for Node 22 compat, silence TS 6.0 deprecation warnings.
- **Phase A — Root migration (5)**: scaffold Playwright, port list-page spec, port SSR specs, swap yarn scripts, delete legacy Cypress files.
- **Phase B — Integration migration (4)**: swap dep, create config + spec, swap yarn scripts, delete legacy Cypress files.
- **Phase C — CI wiring (1)**: install Playwright chromium in setup action.
- **Plan tracking (4)**: plan create + refine + per-task progress.

## What
New capability: capture/restore individual Windows OS-preference values — the part of the "clean-install tax" not covered by per-app modules.

Engine (value-level registry primitives):
- registry-set restore — sets one named HKCU value; mandatory pre-write backup of the prior value (or "absent"); idempotent skip-if-equal; dry-run safe; creates key if missing.
- registryValues capture — reads specific named values (never whole-key, so co-resident values are never captured or clobbered).
- registry-value-equals verify — compares value DATA (extends the exists-only check).
- Full revert (restore-prior-or-delete). HKCU-only; no new CLI flag; cmd/endstate/ untouched.

Modules (8 windows-settings groups): personalization (dark mode), explorer (extensions/hidden), taskbar (alignment), privacy (ad ID + Start suggestions), mouse (no acceleration), keyboard (fast repeat), taskbar-extra (search icon / no task view / clock seconds), explorer-launch (open to This PC).

body:
Fixes a flake in `TestIntegration_FaultedProjection`.

- **`integration_test.go`** The test raced the server's faulting transition. A faulting projection's status passes through a transitional `Running/FaultedStopping` substate, which classifies as faulted while `StateReason` is still empty, so `waitForState(StateFaulted)` could return before `FaultReason` was populated and fail the assertion.
- **`waitForStatus`** Generalised `waitForState` into a predicate-based helper, and the faulted test now waits for `State == Faulted` *and* a non-empty `FaultReason` rather than state alone.

author: linuxdynasty
body:
## What & why

Fixes #3114. The supply-chain impact reducer left `image_ref` / `runtime_reachability=image_sbom` off published findings whenever the SBOM, attachment, and image identity arrived in their own ingestion scopes (`sbom://…`, `oci-registry://…`) while the vulnerability finding lived in `vuln-intel://…`. Surfaced during the #3080 live ECR image-identity proof.

**Root cause:** `sbom.component` and `vulnerability.affected_package` never shared a correlation key. The affected package carries the canonical identity `package_id` (e.g. `npm://registry.npmjs.org/lodash`) and OSV's versionless purl; the SBOM component carried only a version-qualified purl (`pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.11`). So `componentMatchesAffectedPackage` and the cross-scope active-load both missed in both directions.

## Change

- **`collector/sbomdocument`** — emit `package_id` (canonical identity derived from the component purl) on every CycloneDX/SPDX component. The existing storage active-load predicate `payload->>'package_id' = ANY(...)` now bridges the cross-scope load with **no hot-path SQL change**.
- **`packageidentity`** — add shared `PackageIDFromPURL` + `DefaultRegistry` so SBOM and vulnerability sources derive the same canonical `PackageID` from a bare purl (one source of truth for registry defaults).
- **`reducer`** — read the component `package_id`, expand the active-load filter by it, and match components to affected packages by version-stripped purl as defense-in-depth (per the approved "A + reducer purl-strip safety" approach).

## Honesty contract

Preserved. A component without subject-digest/referrer attachment still refuses the image path, and version gating (`NotAffectedKnownFixed`/fail-closed) runs before the component path, so a patched in-image version is not marked affected. Covered by a negative test.

## Tests / verification

- `reducer`: cross-scope match by canonical package_id; match by version-stripped purl; filter expansion by package_id; negative no-attachment refusal. All RED before the fix.
- `packageidentity`: `PackageIDFromPURL` value pinning across npm/scoped/pypi/maven + agreement with the manual `RawIdentity` path (guards against drift from the vuln collector).
- `sbomdocument`: CycloneDX component emits the canonical `package_id`.
- Gates run green: `go test ./internal/reducer ./internal/packageidentity ./internal/collector/sbomdocument ./internal/collector/vulnerabilityintelligence ./internal/storage/postgres ./internal/query ./internal/projector ./internal/mcp ./cmd/eshu`; `golangci-lint run` (0 issues); `go vet`; `git diff --check` clean. SBOM parser benchmark unchanged (~118µs/doc) — per-component identity derivation is negligible.

Refs #3080

author: vaaraio
body:
## What

Phase A's credential broker mints a grant that pins exact arguments: the gateway enforces byte-equality, so one grant authorizes one frozen call. That proves a call was mediated but cannot express a bounded class of calls.

This adds capability scopes. A grant can carry typed constraints over named arguments, and the gateway enforces each at call time:

- `amount le 500` (numeric upper bound)
- `vendor in [acme, globex]` (membership)
- `destination eq 0xABC` (pin)

Coverage is closed: every runtime argument must be named by a capability or the call is rejected. Pin the arguments you do not want to vary with `eq`; bound the ones you do. One credential authorizes a bounded class of calls instead of one frozen call, which is the authority-layer move from proving what happened to controlling what is allowed.

## How

- New `_grant_capability.py`: the `Capability` type, closed-schema serialize and parse (rejects floats and bools in signed values), and `evaluate()` doing closed coverage plus per-op predicate checks. Numeric bounds are decimal-as-string compared via `Decimal`; a malformed value or bound fails closed.
- The optional `capabilities` block is signed and threaded through types, emit, parse, and verify.
- Backward compatible: capabilities absent keeps Phase A exact-args mode with a byte-identical signing preimage, so existing vectors and the independent-recompute conformance check are unchanged.
- In capability mode `verify_grant` enforces the predicates and skips the exact args commitment, which becomes a mint-time audit anchor.

## Tests

13 new cases (bounds, set membership, pinning, closed coverage, signed-ness, closed-schema rejection). Full suite green (1866 passed, 13 skipped), ruff and mypy clean.

## Out of scope

A policy engine that generates capability templates, nested arg paths, and auto-minting capability grants in the proxy (opt-in via `emit_grant(capabilities=...)` until policy lands).

author: konstantinosanagn
body:
## Summary
Builds the full **v2 tiered index** on top of the complete v1, then does a thorough
query-correctness, coverage, and data-fidelity pass so every user surface (SDK / CLI / MCP)
returns the same correct results, served instantly from the static index with zero ATS contact.

## v2 tiered index
- **Slim broad-query tier** — `index-slim.sqlite.gz` (snippet/years/heavy cols nulled). Broad
  structured-filter queries download ~2.3× less, identical results. Dogfooded on the live 380K set.
- **v2.1 row-level deltas** — `index-delta.sqlite.gz`; a returning user one build behind applies a
  ~45× smaller delta instead of re-downloading. `apply_delta` reproduces the full rebuild exactly.
- Full tiered e2e test (fresh + returning user, all tiers, CI-safe).

## Query correctness — index ⇄ SDK parity (a recurring bug class, now structurally prevented)
A property-based fuzz test (`test_index_matches_parity.py`, 200 random queries × 80 jobs) asserts the
index SQL and `SearchQuery.matches()` agree on every structured filter. It surfaced and fixed:
- **City** — metro-aware (NYC boroughs / "NYC" / "New York City", "SF"); +47% NYC recall, no
  state/suburb false positives.
- **Country** — alias-aware (USA/US/U.S. → United States, UK/England); was returning **0** results.
- **Remote** — precise (remote/hybrid or a remote location signal); was 131k untagged in SDK / strict
  in index.
- **Salary** — index now honors `salary_currency` (was returning 868 non-USD for a USD floor) +
  COALESCE range semantics for partial ranges.
- **Years** (`min_years`/`max_years`) and **employment_type** — were **ignored by the index entirely**.
- **`posted_after`** — was only used for sorting, never filtered.
- **Data fidelity** — `from_row` dropped `employment_type`/`posted_at`/`updated_at`, so every
  index-read job reported them as unknown/None (this also silently disabled `posted_after`). Fixed.

## Coverage
- **Sector** — exact company-name map for large opaque brands (Domino's, Starbucks, JPMC, Citi, TJX,
  Qualcomm, SpaceX, …). Live unknown-sector **67% → 50%** (~180k jobs reclassified), deterministic.
- **Level** — plural "New Grads" + "Campus Hire" title markers now classify as entry.

## Surfaces
- **MCP** and **CLI** now expose the full filter set (years/employment/currency/recency + `--city`),
  in parity with the SDK — so a friend can query "SWE, 0–2 yrs, SF, USD ≥ $140k, posted this month".

## Verification (this branch)
- ruff + ruff format + mypy + **885 tests** ✅ (incl. the parity fuzz + tiered e2e + per-filter tests)
- Throttle-proof confirmed in production: **~0 throttled boards** across builds crawling 23k+ boards;
  query-time serves from the static index (0 ATS calls). Live build gates all pass, 1.07M rows growing.

(Also includes parallel-session registry/giants captures: ceipal, zwayam, BNP, residual giants.)

author: philipwilson
body:
`psh --format` produced broken, sometimes **non-re-parseable** output. Found while adding the v0.504.0 examples. Behavior preservation is now pinned by new round-trip tests.

## Before → After

```
# before                  # after
if                        if true; then
  true                      echo yes
then                      fi
  echo yes
fi
```

Nested `else`/`fi`/`done` previously collapsed to column 0; heredoc bodies were dropped entirely (`cat <<EOF` with no body!).

## Formatter (`psh/visitor/formatter_visitor.py`)
- **Headers**: `if`/`while`/`until` now join the condition and `then`/`do` on one line (matching bash `declare -f`); `for`/C-style-`for`/`select` join `do`.
- **Nested indentation**: a single-command `Pipeline` is now transparent (every statement is wrapped `AndOrList → Pipeline → cmd`; `visit_Pipeline` used to reset indent to 0 and re-indent only the first line, collapsing nested compounds).
- **Lossy redirects** — all now preserved (previously produced broken shell):
  - heredoc bodies (dropped → emitted after the command at column 0, incl. compound commands `while …; done <<EOF` and groups)
  - quoted heredoc delimiter `<<'EOF'` (→ `<<EOF`, re-enabling expansion)
  - quoted file target `> "my file"` (→ `>my file`)
  - here-string `<<< "a b"` (→ `<<<a b`)
  - the 9 duplicated compound-redirect blocks are unified in `_append_redirects`.

## Parser bugfix (pre-existing, surfaced here)
`populate_heredoc_content` iterated a group node's `.statements` (a `StatementList` wrapper, not a list), so `{ …; } <<EOF` and `( … ) <<EOF` raised `TypeError: 'StatementList' object is not iterable` **at parse time** — breaking both execution and analysis. Unwrapped like the sibling `commands` branch; `{ read a; read b; …; } <<EOF` now matches bash.

## Tests
- New `tests/unit/visitor/test_formatter_roundtrip.py`: header shapes, nested indentation, idempotence, and **behavior preservation** (run original vs. formatted) incl. heredocs/here-strings/quoted targets.
- Updated the until-loop header pin in `test_ast_coverage_matrix.py` (it pinned the old broken `until`-alone line).

## Gate
- Full suite green: **8,168 passed / 315 skipped / 16 xfailed**
- `ruff check psh tests` clean; `mypy` clean (238 files)

author: pratyushsharma-creator
body:
## Why
We just turned on the **Taboola pixel** site-wide (`NEXT_PUBLIC_TABOOLA_ID`), but it was only firing **page views**. The main marketplace checkout and the site's lead forms fired **no conversion events at all** — only the EV report flow (`ThankYouTracking` / `AnalystLeadForm`) did. Without conversion events, Taboola (and Google Ads / Bing later) can't attribute or optimize against the actions that matter.

## What
Two new aggregate helpers in `src/lib/analytics/events.ts`:
- **`trackPurchaseConversion({ value, currency, transactionId })`** → GA4 `purchase` + Google Ads + Bing `purchase` + Taboola `make_purchase`
- **`trackLeadConversion({ category, label })`** → GA4 `generate_lead` + Google Ads (lead label) + Bing `lead` + Taboola `lead`

Each underlying helper already no-ops until its ID is configured, so **Taboola + GA4 fire now**; **Google Ads + Bing stay dormant** until their env IDs are set.

Wired into:
| Event | Location |
|---|---|
| `make_purchase` | `checkout/confirmation` — via new `PurchaseTracking` component, fired once after the Stripe session is server-verified |

### Motivation
- Tornar a ação de “Mover pasta” confiável ponta a ponta garantindo que o `parent_id` seja realmente alterado no banco antes de sinalizar sucesso. 
- Evitar casos falsos de sucesso (UPDATE não aplicado, destino inválido, mover para descendente, duplicidade de nome ou uso de coluna inexistente `path`).
- Oferecer diagnósticos melhores (logs) e garantir auditoria e invalidação de cache após commit.

### Description
- Reforcei a validação e o fluxo transacional em `GedFolderMoveService.MoveAsync` para: carregar origem com `FOR UPDATE`, validar destino/ativo/tenant, bloquear mover para si mesmo, detectar destinos descendentes via CTE, checar duplicidade de nome no destino, executar `UPDATE` e reconsultar `parent_id` antes do commit; adicionei logs de início/êxito/erro e invalidação de cache; fiz a auditoria após o `tx.Commit` (arquivo `InovaGed.Infrastructure/Ged/Folders/GedFolderMoveService.cs`).

- Ajustei o controller `POST /Ged/Folders/Move` para só retornar sucesso quando `RowsAffected > 0` e resposta confirmada pelo serviço, preservando payload com `folderId`, `oldParentId`, `newParentId`, `oldPath`, `newPath` e `rowsAffected` (arquivo `InovaGed.Web/Controller/GedController.cs`).
- Adicionei migration idempotente que cria `updated_at`, `updated_by` e índice `ix_folder_tenant_parent_name` sem criar coluna `path`, e incluí sua entrada em `apply_all_required_migrations.sql` (arquivos `database/migrations/2026_06_fix_folder_move_columns.sql` e `database/apply_all_required_migrations.sql`).

body:
Fixes #18192

## Summary

When a human-in-the-loop (HITL) tool approval is declined, `@mastra/core` currently feeds the model a hard-coded English string as the tool result:

```ts
result: 'Tool call was not approved by the user'
```

This change returns a structured object instead:

```ts
result: {
  status: 'denied',
  approved: false,
  reason: typeof resumeData.reason === 'string' ? resumeData.reason : null,
}
```

## Problem

- **Not machine-readable** — consumers must string-match the exact English phrase to detect a denial
- **English-only, baked into core** — no way to localize or override
- **No channel to carry *why*** the user declined the tool call

## Changes

### Source files (3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/core/src/loop/workflows/agentic-execution/tool-call-step.ts` | Return `{ status: 'denied', approved, reason }` instead of hard-coded string |
| `packages/core/src/agent/durable/workflows/steps/tool-call.ts` | Same change for durable-agent path |
| `packages/core/src/loop/network/index.ts` | Return structured result; remove dead `toolCallDeclined` variable and English-dependent `finalText` append |

| `packages/core/src/agent/__tests__/supervisor-integration.test.ts` | Update assertion to `toMatchObject({ status: 'denied', approved: false })` |
| `packages/core/src/agent/agent-network.test.ts` | Update string equality check to property check; update assertion to `toMatchObject` |

### Other

| `packages/core/__recordings__/core-src-agent-__tests__-tool-approval.e2e/test-e3f1ad60.json` | Deleted (stale recording, will regenerate on e2e run) |

author: rushsinging
body:
## 背景

Issue #363 的 P0 根因：`auto_compact` 直接 `*messages = compacted` 原地截断 `messages`，导致 `session.json` 持久化的是压缩后的残缺对话。resume 后用户看到的是丢失了大量上下文的对话，原始内容永久丢失。

## 改动

核心思路：**分离「真相源」（messages，永不截断）与「LLM 视图」（compact 后的截断版本）**。

### `compact/micro.rs`
- `microcompact` 签名从 `&mut [Message]` 改为 `&[Message] -> Vec<Message>`
- 内部 clone 后截断，不修改原始 messages

### `compact/summary.rs`
- 两处 `microcompact` 调用同步更新（`compact_messages` + `compact_messages_with_llm`）

### `chat/looping/compact.rs`
- `auto_compact` 签名从 `messages: &mut Vec<Message> -> bool` 改为 `messages: &[Message] -> Option<Vec<Message>>`
- 不再 `*messages = compacted`，而是构造 `view` 并返回 `Some(view)`
- 返回 `None` 表示不需要 compact，调用方使用原始 messages

### `chat/looping/loop_runner.rs`
- 每个 turn 声明 `let llm_view = auto_compact(...).await`
- `build_api_messages` 用 `llm_view.as_deref().unwrap_or(&messages)` 获取 LLM 输入
- messages 真相源永不截断，session.json 持久化的是完整对话

### `agent/runner/loop_helpers.rs`
- 子代理的 microcompact 调用同步更新（`self.messages = microcompact(&self.messages, 4)`）

## 验证

- ✅ `cargo check --workspace` 通过
- ✅ `cargo clippy --workspace` 无新增警告
- ✅ `cargo test -p runtime --lib`（298 passed）
- ✅ `cargo fmt --check` 合规

Refs #363
