author: 0xartex
body:
## Problem
A TikTok post drives a headless browser for **2–5 minutes** (upload + 90s caption-editor wait + 60s publish-confirm). That's longer than Cloudflare's tunnel timeout (~100s), so the synchronous handler **settled payment, then 524'd the caller before the post finished** — the agent was charged but never learned if its video posted. Observed in prod 2026-06-19 (payment settled at 10:45:19, post confirmed at 10:48:34, caller got a 524 in between). It's the #1 blocker for unattended TikTok posting (the Agent Creator Farm).

## Fix — mirror the `domain-registration` async-operation pattern
- **New `src/services/tiktok-post-jobs.ts`** (`tiktok_post_jobs` table + `setImmediate` worker), modelled directly on `domain-registration.ts`. Lifecycle `pending → publishing → posted | failed`.
- **`POST /social/tiktok/post`** now returns **202** immediately with `{ operation_id, status, poll_url, poll_after_seconds, message }` and runs the publish in the background. No x402 change needed — the middleware already captures `<400` responses, so a duplicate payment within 15 min **replays the same `operation_id`** (won't double-charge or double-post).
- **New `GET /social/tiktok/operations/:id`** — owner-scoped poll (404 on mismatch, `requireAuth(0.01)`), returns `status`/`done`/`video_url`/`error`/`refund_status`.
- **Auto-refund** on definitive failure via `refundUsdcToPayer` (idempotent on payment signature).
- **Reconciliation (option A)**: on an ambiguous outcome (UI_TIMEOUT / op threw — Submit may have landed), the worker re-opens a session and scrapes the Studio content manager for the caption (`checkPostedByCaption`, new export reusing `findPostedVideo`): found → `posted`, provably-not → refund, can't-determine → manual review. Never blind-refunds a post that landed.
- **CLI** `tiktok post`/`schedule` polls the operation to completion (6-min cap, ~20s cadence, NDJSON progress to stderr in agent mode); `--no-wait` returns the handle. Legacy sync-server response still handled for back-compat.
- **Startup recovery** wired in `index.ts` (mirrors `startDomainRegistrationRecovery`).

## Design decisions (documented in the service header)
- **Video bytes + cookies are passed to the worker in-memory, not persisted** (no 10 MB blob / session creds at rest). Consequence: a *crash* mid-publish can't be auto-reconciled (cookies gone) → flagged `manual_needed`, **not** auto-refunded (it may have posted). A crash before publish → refund (safe). Normal worker-level reconcile (the common case — op finishes but can't confirm) keeps its in-memory cookies and reconciles fully.
- A worker-reconcile that can't determine the outcome leaves the job `publishing`; since there's no periodic reconcile pass (only startup), it self-heals on the next server restart's recovery sweep. Noted for the future full-orchestration work.

## Agent-facing 202
```json
{ "operation_id":"…","status":"pending","poll_url":"/social/tiktok/operations/…","poll_after_seconds":20,
  "message":"TikTok post started. Browser automation typically lands in ~2-5 minutes. Poll GET … until status is 'posted' (carries video_url) or 'failed' (auto-refunded). Do not resubmit — payment is already captured for this operation." }
```

## Test status
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; full suite **281/281 pass**.
- NOT yet runtime-tested end-to-end (needs deploy). Recommended smoke test post-deploy: `palmyr tiktok post` returns an operation_id fast (no 524), polls to `posted` with a `video_url`; a forced failure auto-refunds. Prod needs a manual `git pull` (and note the divergent prod `social-login.ts` jetfuel hotfix — deploy still needs reconciliation, tracked separately).

author: heywood8
body:
## Summary

Replaces the bottom-sheet category picker that opened from the **"All categories"** shortcut during operation quick-add with an **inline browser** rendered directly in place of the suggested-category chips.

The goal was to make the transition from *suggested* categories to *all* categories feel as smooth and continuous as possible — no modal swapping up from the bottom.

## What changed

- **Same look as suggestions** — the browser reuses the exact shortcut-chip styling, so moving from the suggested categories to the full list reads as one continuous, morphing grid rather than a separate modal.
- **Hierarchy preserved** — categories follow the existing parent/subcategory structure:
  - The first slot (where "All categories" was) becomes a **back chip** that pops one folder level, or exits back to the suggestions at the root.
  - **Folders** drill in to show their children.
  - **Leaf entries** select / auto-add exactly like the existing shortcuts (auto-add when an amount is already entered, otherwise just set the category).
- **Animation** — each level change does a short slide-in + fade (forward slides from the right, back from the left), and the container's height change is smoothed with `LayoutAnimation` so the operations list below glides rather than jumping. Content is swapped immediately so the interaction stays responsive and deterministic.
- **Reset on type change** — the browser collapses whenever the operation type switches (so a leftover folder from a previous type can't filter to nothing).
- **Scoped change** — `OperationModal` and the legacy single full-width picker fallback are untouched; the inline browser is only active in the quick-add shortcuts context.

## Testing

- Added tests covering: opening the browser (instead of the modal), drilling into a folder to reveal its children, returning via the back chip, and leaf selection in both the auto-add (amount present) and plain `setValues` (no amount) paths.
- Full suite green: **3626 passed**, lint clean.

author: ogoffart
body:
Cargo unifies features across the whole build, so the `tokio` feature can be turned on by another, independent crate in the workspace even when the application itself uses zbus with async-io. That used to compile the async-io backend out and force every zbus user in the process into a tokio runtime, so the async-io application would panic with "there is no reactor running".

Gate the async-io backend on `feature = "async-io"` rather than `not(feature = "tokio")` so both can be compiled together. When both are enabled, pick the backend at run time: use tokio when a tokio runtime is active on the current thread, and async-io otherwise.

author: morningrevolution
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap that turned yesterday's pre-push gate into a remember-to-mark-it gate. The marker is now written by a script and invalidated automatically on any new commit.

## Why

The `pre-push` hook refuses to push unless `.git/.pr-this-ran` matches `HEAD`. That marker was supposed to be the gate's anchor: "this exact tree state passed the gauntlet, push is allowed." But until this PR, nothing wrote the marker automatically — the previous flow required `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/.pr-this-ran` by hand at the end. Which means the gate has been operating on the honor system since yesterday. Exactly the failure mode we were trying to remove.

## What changed

- **New `scripts/mark-pr-this-ran.sh`**: the canonical way to record `/pr-this` completion. Refuses to run on a dirty working tree, so the marker can't claim coverage of code that isn't actually committed.
- **`scripts/install-hooks.sh`**: now also installs `post-commit` and `post-rewrite` hooks. Both delete the marker on any new commit / amend / rebase, forcing a fresh `/pr-this` pass before the next push.
- **`/pr-this` skill (laptop)**: gained a new step 4o that calls the marker script as the last step.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`**: documents the full hook list + the dirty-tree guarantee.

## What I considered and rejected

1. **Ratchet via `core.hooksPath`** so the hooks could live under `scripts/` directly. Rejected because a fresh clone that skips `bash scripts/install-hooks.sh` would then have no local hooks at all, which is worse than today.
2. **Add a `pre-commit` hook that runs the full leak scan on staged changes.** Rejected for this PR — that's its own scope, and a slow pre-commit hook would tax every commit. Worth doing separately later.
3. **Move all enforcement to CI.** Rejected because CI runs *after* the push lands on GitHub; a private-URL leak in a commit message is already public by then. The local gate exists specifically to catch the leak before it leaves the laptop.

## Risks and trade-offs

- The marker is still local. A contributor who clones fresh and doesn't run `install-hooks.sh` gets no enforcement. Same posture as before this PR; net new exposure is zero. The ruleset on `dev` / `prod` is the server-side belt to this suspenders.
- Adding two new hooks adds two new ways for `install-hooks.sh` to fail silently. The script is idempotent and re-running is safe, but a partial install (one hook installed, others not) is a state the script doesn't recover from. Mitigation: read the output of `bash scripts/install-hooks.sh` — it lists each hook installed. If you see fewer than three "→" lines, something went wrong.

## How to verify

```bash
git checkout chore/pr-this-auto-marker
bash scripts/install-hooks.sh                 # should report 3 hooks installed
ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-push|post-commit|post-rewrite'

# Smoke test the dirty-tree refusal:
echo x > /tmp/dirty-test && bash scripts/mark-pr-this-ran.sh
# Expected: refuses with "Working tree is dirty"

# Make a real commit, watch the marker get invalidated:
echo y > a.txt && git add a.txt && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -m "test"
# Expected: "ℹ /pr-this marker invalidated (commit changed HEAD)."
ls .git/.pr-this-ran
# Expected: no such file
git reset --hard HEAD~1 && rm -f a.txt

# Real path (what an agent does at end of /pr-this):
bash scripts/mark-pr-this-ran.sh
# Expected: writes the marker, push is allowed.
```

## Out of scope

- `pre-commit` hook for leak-scanning staged changes (separate PR if we want it).
- CI-side enforcement (already handled by the branch protection ruleset on `dev` / `prod`).
- Porting these scripts to OWB (separate PR, OWB agent owns).

author: myaisabe
body:
## What
The backend for **"what's on this Mac you can bring in"** — auto-detect known data-source folders, plus the **Claude Code transcript importer** (which also closes the gap from the very start of this work: Claude Code `.jsonl` had no importer).

## Changes
- **`detect-sources.js` (new)** — `detectSources({home})` scans an **allowlist** (Obsidian vaults via `obsidian.json`, Claude Code transcripts `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`) and returns **presence + counts + date range only — never content**. A detector that throws never breaks the scan. + `readClaudeCodeEntries()`.
- **`processClaudeCodeExport`** (`import-parsers.js`) — parses Claude Code `.jsonl`: keeps user/assistant message lines, **preserves the original `timestamp`**, groups by `sessionId`, **dedups on `uuid`**, fail-loud on capture errors. Source **`import-claude-code`** (not `claude-code…`) so it does **not** trip the agent-capture consent gate — an import is intentional ingest, like `claude-import`. *(The gate caught this collision in test — see commit.)*
- **`portal-import.js`** — `GET /import/detect` (allowlist scan, presence-only, explicit user action) + `POST /import/claude-code` (reads `~/.claude` off disk → `captureMessage`).
- **`sources.ts`** — Streams label for the new tag.

## Privacy
Detection is an allowlist, presence/counts/dates only, never reads content, and is invoked only on an explicit "Scan this Mac for data" action. Import reads the user's own transcripts on their own machine into their own vault.

## Verify
New gates **`verify:claude-code-import` 5/5** (ts preserved · block[] content · non-message lines skipped · uuid dedup · fail-loud) + **`verify:import-detect` 5/5** (detects CC + Obsidian w/ counts · no false positives on empty home · binary file doesn't break scan), both in the chain. Regression GO: `import`, `ingest`, `obsidian`, `agent-capture`. portal-app `svelte-check` 0/0.

## Follow-up
Frontend wiring — the catalog calls `/import/detect` on a "Scan this Mac for data" CTA and flips detected sources to **"Found — N · Import"** (Obsidian one-click works now; Claude Code via the new route). Needs a live WKWebView smoke.

author: e6qu
body:
Roadmap **PR 1** — *data protection + log usability* (A1–A3 from BUGS.md).

## A1 (HIGH) — node-trace PII now survives erasure correctly
The decide path sealed the recorded **input** and **output** under the entity key, but each `NodeEvaluated` output was recorded **unsealed** — and node outputs echo input PII (assignment/rule/table targets, code merges, `manual_review` fields), so they survived a crypto-shred erasure that the input/output sealing made unrecoverable. Now each node output is sealed via `sealPII` before emit, and `maskRecord` unseals `rec.Nodes[].Output` (or surfaces `"[erased]"`) at the read boundary. New `TestNodeTraceErasure` proves: sealed at rest → unseals for an authorized read → `"[erased]"` after erasure.

## A2 — Decisions list: filtering, search, pagination, legible time
`history.ListPage` adds flow/env/status/variant filters, decision-id search, a since/until range, and pagination (`limit`/`offset` + `total`). A positive `limit` paginates; `limit<=0` stays unpaginated, so the dashboard/SDK (which aggregate the full set) are unchanged. The page gains filter controls, a prev/next pager with totals, and absolute-time-on-hover.

## A3 — Audit log: pagination + hide the node-evaluated noise
`audit.ReadPage` adds `offset`+`total` (the stream/actor/type/resource/time filters already existed), plus an `exclude_type` param. The page gains a date range, a **Hide node steps** toggle (drops the high-volume `node_evaluated` rows), a pager, and absolute timestamps. CSV export still covers the whole filtered set, independent of the on-screen page.

## Verified
Full strict gate green (gofmt/vet/lint/sast/deadcode/dupl, `-race` tests, prettier/eslint/svelte-check/vitest). End-to-end against the embedded binary: Decisions (13 total) paged/filtered/searched correctly; Audit (109 total) paged, with the node-steps split 54 + 55 = 109.

Backward compatible: both list endpoints still return `{decisions:[...]}` / `{entries:[...]}` (now plus `total/limit/offset`).

author: marcosalves90
body:
## Closing
- Use a GitHub closing keyword when applicable: `Closes #<issue>`, `Fixes #<issue>`, or `Resolves #<issue>`.
- Closing issue(s): None.

## Environment
- Model and version: Codex GPT-5 via `codex-cli 0.141.0`
- Harness and version: Codex CLI `0.141.0`
- Installed plugins or skills packs: go-beast
- Human reviewer of the full diff: Not yet

## Summary
- Add a stateful anti-drift guard for go-beast sessions.
- Re-anchor Codex on each user prompt and bootstrap sessions on repeated Stop-time drift.
- Record the requirements, approach, and architecture contracts that justify the change.

## Problem
- Agents regularly lose the active go-beast workflow, stop following the intended beast sequence, or drift away from the expected persona and enforcement posture during longer sessions.

## Root Cause
- go-beast relied too heavily on initial session context plus static instructions.
- After enough turns, there was no shared runtime state or harness-level re-anchor mechanism to restore the current beast, required artifact, or implementation gate.

## Alternatives Considered
- Tighten instruction files only: rejected because it improves policy but does not restore state once the session drifts.
- Stateless reminder hooks: rejected because they cannot tell which beast or artifact is currently active.
- Broad blocker hooks on every suspected drift signal: rejected because the false-positive risk is too high.

## Change
- Added anti-drift runtime hooks and shared state under `~/.go-beast`:
  - `go-beast-session-state.sh`
  - `go-beast-user-prompt-context.sh`
  - `go-beast-stop-reanchor.sh`
  - `go-beast-drift-lib.sh`
- Registered the hooks in the shared manifest and documented them in the pack docs.
- Tightened `AGENTS.global.md`, `AGENTS.bootstrap.md`, and `AGENTS.md` so context retention and anti-drift behavior are explicit policy, not only hook behavior.
- Added deterministic shell coverage, live hook wiring coverage, and hook-eval cases.
- Checked in the discovery and architecture artifacts (`REQUIREMENTS.md`, `APPROACH.md`, `docs/architecture/{STACK.md,ADR.md,DIAGRAM.md,CONTRACTS.md}`) that unlocked the implementation.
- This approach was chosen because it keeps the high-confidence blocker path narrow while still giving the harness enough memory to re-anchor the session.

## Core Fit
- This belongs in go-beast core because the problem is session-wide pack behavior across supported harnesses, not project-local product behavior.
- The solution needs shared instructions, shared hook wiring, shared state conventions, and shared validation coverage for both Codex and Claude Code.

## Validation
- [x] Relevant automated checks ran.
- [x] Manual verification completed, if applicable.
- Exact commands run:
- `bash tests/plugin/test-go-beast-drift-hooks.sh`
- `bash tests/plugin/test-hook-wire.sh`
- `GO_BEAST_RUN_LIVE_AGENT_TESTS=1 bash tests/codex/test-hook-wire.sh`
- `GO_BEAST_RUN_LIVE_AGENT_TESTS=1 bash tests/claude-code/test-hook-wire.sh`
- Behavioral evidence or session evidence:
- Deterministic hook test covers session init, prompt re-anchor output, repeated Stop drift, and state reset after a valid re-anchor.
- Live Codex and Claude hook-wire tests confirm the new anti-drift hooks are rewired without disturbing external hook entries.

## Risks
- The Stop-time re-anchor logic uses heuristic message inspection, so future wording changes could reduce sensitivity until the hook is adjusted.
- `UserPromptSubmit` re-anchoring is Codex-only; Claude currently relies on the shared instruction layer plus Stop-time enforcement.

## Existing PRs / Prior Art
- [x] I checked open and closed PRs/issues for duplicates or prior attempts.
- Related items:
- #17 `[agents] harden global and bootstrap instruction contracts`
- #19 `[agents] define operational protocols for maintainer workflows`
- #15 `[pack] improve the agent harness and bootstrap architecture`

## Follow-ups
- Consider extending live runtime tests from hook wiring into full conversational anti-drift scenarios on Codex and Claude.
- Revisit whether part of the state update path should be driven by explicit beast/artifact markers instead of message heuristics.

## Human Review
- [x] A human reviewed the complete proposed diff before submission.

author: olafkfreund
body:
## What

Closes **#363** — the last open child of security epic **#318**. The coding agent runs under `permission_mode="bypassPermissions"` with only the soft command allowlist as a compensating control (finding **H1**); this adds the missing **OS boundary (AC1)**.

The bwrap sandbox already existed (#363 slice 2) but was **inert on the deployed k3d cluster**: its `fs` mode used `--unshare-pid` + a fresh `/proc`, which an unprivileged pod can't mount — `Can't mount proc on /newroot/proc: Operation not permitted`. So in production there was no OS boundary, only the pod + allowlist.

## Changes

- **`server/services/sandbox.py`** — make PID-namespace isolation **opt-in** (`AIFACTORY_AGENT_SANDBOX_PIDNS`). The default now keeps the host PID namespace with a **read-only `/proc`**, which runs **unprivileged in-pod** while still binding the worktree read-write and everything else read-only.
- **`tests/test_sandbox_escape_corpus.py`** — un-skip the two AC1 escape tests (write-outside-worktree, read-host-secret) → real assertions against a live bwrap boundary; skip only where no usable bwrap exists.
- **`tests/test_agent_sandbox.py`** — unit tests for the pidns default (ro `/proc`, no `--unshare-pid`) vs opt-in (`--unshare-pid` + fresh `/proc`).
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — install `bubblewrap` in the backend job and relax Ubuntu 24.04's unprivileged-userns AppArmor restriction so the AC1 tests run for real (not skip).
- **Helm** — `sandbox.agent.mode` defaults to `"fs"` → sets `AIFACTORY_AGENT_SANDBOX` on the deployment, so the boundary is **active in production** (was passthrough). PID-ns stays off (`sandbox.agent.pidNamespace: false`).

## Proof

Enforcement verified **inside the live k3d AIFactory pod** (nonroot, no added caps):
- write outside worktree (`touch /usr/x`) → `Read-only file system` (rejected)
- read host secret outside the binds → `No such file or directory` (absent)
- worktree writes still succeed

AC1 corpus tests pass where bwrap can run (proven in a container + the live pod); 24 passed / 2 skip locally on the Nix dev box (no usable in-sandbox shell there). Ruff clean.

AC2 (env-scrub), AC3 (egress), AC4 (fail-closed hook) already held — the hook stays as defense-in-depth, not the perimeter. Note: gVisor (the originally-deferred route) can't even launch on GitHub runners per `gvisor-smoke.yml`; unprivileged bwrap is the better default and needs no node prerequisites.

Closes #363.

author: liliwashere
body:
## Summary

- Adds a backwards-numbering guard to `sendCatchUpEmails()`: if any subscriber already received a higher-numbered issue than the current `issue_number` state, the catch-up aborts with a clear warning instead of double-delivering
- Tightens the pending-subscriber filter from `!== issueNumber` to `< issueNumber`, so new subscribers (`last_emailed_issue = null`) are always correctly included

## Why

On 2026-06-16, a double-send occurred after the June 15 accidental publish:
1. Issue #7 was sent on June 15 → subscribers marked `last_emailed_issue = 7`

author: nkwiatkowski
body:
## What
Fix sorting executions by **Duration** on PostgreSQL. The `executions.state_duration` generated column used `EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM interval)`, which returns only the seconds field of the interval (0–59999) and drops minutes/hours. A `7m59.45s` execution was stored as `59450` instead of `479450`, so duration sort was wrong for any execution ≥ 1 minute. Replaced with `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM interval) * 1000` (total milliseconds).

PostgreSQL only — MySQL and H2 already read the value as total seconds. Distinct from #11593/#13132 (NULL duration for running execs), which is unrelated to this.

Closes #16908

## How
Edit the fresh-install baseline and add incremental migration **2.0.11** (`V2_0_11StateDurationFixMigration` + SQL) for existing installs. Column kept nullable.

`state_duration` is a `STORED` generated column, so the migration drops and re-creates it (backfilling all rows; takes a brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on large tables) and recreates the `executions_state_duration` index.

## Tests
Added `findShouldSortByTotalDurationAcrossMinuteBoundary` asserting a 5-minute execution sorts above a 20-second one (and vice versa). Verified passing on Postgres and H2; confirmed it fails without the fix.

---
Companion PRs: develop + releases/v1.3.x + releases/v1.0.x.

author: yinli-systems
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

- Closes #22799.

## Rationale for this change

`any_value` is a common aggregate in SQL engines for queries that need one representative non-null value from each group without imposing an ordering requirement. DataFusion currently has `first_value`, but that aggregate is order-sensitive, so exposing `any_value` gives users the intended arbitrary-value semantics directly.

## What changes are included in this PR?

- Adds an `any_value(expression)` aggregate UDF and registers it with the default aggregate functions.
- Reuses the existing trivial first-value accumulator with nulls ignored, so evaluation short-circuits after the first non-null value.
- Marks the aggregate as order-insensitive and preserves the input field metadata/type in the return field.
- Adds sqllogictest coverage for scalar, grouped, all-null, empty-input, and string return-type cases.

## Are these changes tested?

Yes. I ran:

```
cargo fmt --all
cargo test -p datafusion-functions-aggregate
cargo test -p datafusion-sqllogictest --test sqllogictests -- aggregate_any_value.slt
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

## Are there any user-facing changes?

Yes. This adds a new SQL aggregate function, `any_value`.

I used AI assistance to help inspect the codebase and run validation, and I reviewed the resulting implementation and tests.

author: asgeirf
body:
Prototype of the handwriting mode you asked for — **not A/B, a cascade**: PP-OCRv5 reads every line fast, and only the **low-confidence** lines are re-read by **TrOCR**. Each model plays to its strength (PP-OCR speed on clean text, TrOCR accuracy on hard lines), and you pay TrOCR's cost only where PP-OCR was unsure.

- **In-browser**: TrOCR runs via **transformers.js** over onnxruntime-web (`Xenova/trocr-small-handwritten`, fetched from the CORS-enabled HF Hub), **lazy-loaded** on first escalation.
- **Vision Lab UI**: a "✍ Handwriting fallback" toggle + a confidence-threshold slider; escalated lines are badged `✍ TrOCR` and drawn purple.
- **Bridge**: `ocr(img, base, { handwriting, hwThreshold })` — escalates a line when its PP-OCR confidence is below the threshold (or it read nothing).

**Verified in-browser (Playwright)**: forcing the threshold high, all lines escalated and were re-read by the real TrOCR model (loaded + ran, 0 console errors).

### Honest finding
On font-rendered "handwriting" (Snell Roundhand) PP-OCRv5 is already excellent (~97%), and TrOCR-small actually did *worse* — because **TrOCR-small-handwritten is trained on real human handwriting (IAM)**, not cursive fonts. So the cascade *mechanism* is solid; the payoff shows on real messy handwriting, and model/threshold choice matters. Worth deciding: keep lab-only for now, try `trocr-base-handwritten`, or wire it into the native plugin too.

Holding merge — it's a prototype and pulls in transformers.js (sizeable dep). Your call on whether/where to land it.

body:
Raising min_replicas on an idle model had no effect: should_scale_up only triggered on queue load above target_queue_depth, and should_scale_down treated min_replicas merely as a lower bound. With no traffic, both paths returned None and the replica count never moved.

Add a floor check at the top of should_scale_up so a running model (current_replicas >= 1) below its configured min_replicas scales up to the floor immediately, independent of queue load.

body:
## What

Add an analysis history page where users can see their past analyses, expand any
one to view the full result, with a score color that reflects how strong the 
match is.

## Why

Analyses were saved but had no way to view past results — refreshing lost the 
result on screen. With the backend history endpoint in place, this surfaces that
data: a list of past analyses, each expandable to the full breakdown.

## How

- **`AnalysisHistoryPage`**: loads `GET /api/analyses` on mount, renders each as
a card showing the CV/job identity snapshot, score, date, and a two-line 
feedback preview (`line-clamp-2`).
- **Expandable details**: a "View details / Collapse" button toggles 
`expandedId`; the expanded card renders the shared `AnalysisResult` component 
with the full breakdown. Reusing `AnalysisResult` keeps the display consistent 
with the live analysis page.
- **Score color**: the score is colored by the same thresholds as the result's 
progress bar, so the list and the expanded view agree visually.
- **Snapshot fallback**: records created before the snapshot feature have null 
CV/job names, shown as "Unknown CV / Unknown Job".
- **Navbar + route**: a protected `/history` route and a "History" nav link.

## Testing

- History lists past analyses, newest first.
- Expanding a card shows the full result; collapsing hides it.
- Score color matches between the list and the expanded progress bar.
- Old records (pre-snapshot) show the fallback labels.

## Lessons Learned

- **Reusing a component keeps two views in sync**: the history detail and the 
live analysis render through the same `AnalysisResult`.
- **Truncation is a display concern**: the backend returns full feedback; the 
list truncates with `line-clamp` and the detail shows it in full — no backend 
change needed.

## Updates (June 19, 2026) — CodeQL Alert Resolution

- **stream.rs**: Replaced zero-initialized buffer patterns (`let mut salt = [0u8; 16]`) with dynamic generation (`rand::random()` / `try_into()`) to fix 2 production-code false positives
- **42 test vector suppressions**: Added `// codeql[cpp/hardcoded-credentials]` inline comments to all hardcoded nonce/password/salt lines in `#[cfg(test)]` blocks across 9 crypto-core Rust files

CrytoTool follows Protocol-3305 (https://github.com/ObscuritySecurity/protocol-3305).
✓ = compliant, X = violation (blocking).

| Art. | Principle | Status | Notes |
| ---- | --------- | ------ | ----- |
| 0 | Ethical Monetization | ✓ | No monetization changes; remains free and open-source |
| 1 | Privacy by Design | ✓ | Rust crypto-core compiles to WASM - everything runs client-side |
| 2 | Security by Default | ✓ | Threat model tiers enforce stronger defaults; crypto uses audited Rust crates |
| 3 | Zero Trust | ✓ | All key derivation and encryption verified locally |
| 4 | Zero Knowledge | ✓ | Encryption keys derived from master password - never leave device |
| 5 | Zero Personal Data Collection | ✓ | No PII collection added; Rust core has no network capabilities |
| 6 | Zero Activity Logs | ✓ | No logging, telemetry, or activity tracking in any layer |
| 7 | Open Source | ✓ | Remains AGPL-3.0; crypto-core source fully auditable |
| 8 | Zero Non-Essential Permissions | ✓ | No new OS permissions; removed biometry plugin |

---

- [ ] PR does NOT modify cryptographic code, key derivation, or encryption algorithms
- [ ] Tested on target platform(s)
- [ ] npx tsc --noEmit passed
- [ ] Docs updated

Underlying algorithms remain identical (AES-256-GCM, AES-CTR+HMAC-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305, XChaCha20-Poly1305, Salsa20-Poly1305) - only implementation language changed. author: raghavchamadiya
body:
The workspace surfaces so far are descriptive and per-relationship: every service, every typed edge, every cycle, every conformance violation. None of them answers the one evaluative question a team actually asks: how coupled is this whole system, and which services are its architectural core?

This adds the standard architecture-complexity metrics (MacCormack / Baldwin / Sturtevant) over the existing system graph and rolls them into one deterministic 1-10 architecture score. Structural edges only (co-change is excluded); no LLM anywhere.

## What it computes

- **Propagation cost** the share of other services the average service can reach transitively (0% fully decoupled, 100% everything reaches everything).
- **Cyclic core** the largest cyclic group of services (largest strongly-connected component), with its size and ratio.
- **Per-service role** Core (in the cyclic group), Shared (high fan-in, low fan-out), Control (high fan-out, low fan-in), or Peripheral, from each service's visibility profile.
- **Architecture type** core-periphery or hierarchical, from the core ratio.
- **Architecture score** a deterministic 1-10 roll-up (matching the code-health convention) from propagation cost, core ratio, dependency-cycle count, and conformance violation count. Lower coupling and a smaller core score higher.

## Surfaces

- **core** new pure `workspace/architecture_metrics.py`. Builds a cycle-safe visibility matrix, computes propagation cost as its off-diagonal density, reuses NetworkX SCC for the core and `detect_cycles` for the cycle count. Every weight and cutoff in one constants block.
- **REST** `GET /api/workspace/architecture` returns the metrics plus per-service roles, computed at request time from the system graph (no new artifact); the conformance violation count is folded in when a report exists.
- **CLI** `repowise workspace metrics [--json]`.
- **MCP** new workspace-only `get_architecture` tool.
- **web** the DSM header shows score / propagation cost / core size and tints each service's diagonal cell by role; the Live System Map gains a Core overlay toggle and shows role + visibility in the inspector; both pages show the score as a stat.

## Tests

`tests/unit/workspace/test_architecture_metrics.py` with hand-computed fixtures: layered DAG, fully cyclic graph, a core-periphery system with one service per role, an off-diagonal propagation-cost check, a structural-only guard (a co-change edge changes nothing), a determinism/shape snapshot, the conformance-violation penalty, and empty/single/independent guards.

Workspace suite and server/MCP/router suites green; types/ui/web typecheck clean; web lint clean.

Hosted backend and frontend propagation will follow separately.

Greptile Summary

 This PR extends the existing S3 signing diagnostics by adding a non-reversible credential "shape" (length, base64 charset check, whitespace flags, provider-type classification) that is logged alongside request framing details when a `SignatureDoesNotMatch` or related signing error is caught. The credential values themselves are never surfaced. - Introduces `S3CredentialShape` and `summarizeCredentialShape` in `s3SigningDiagnostics.ts`; the shape is purely diagnostic metadata computed once at client construction and stored in the middleware context. - Wires the shape into `addS3SigningDiagnosticsMiddleware` in `StorageService.ts` via a single new `credentials` property on `S3SigningDiagnosticsContext`. - Test coverage is comprehensive across the main paths; the NBSP test comment contains a factual error (modern JS `trim()` does strip U+00A0) and the test is missing assertions on `secretHasSurroundingWhitespace` and `secretHasWhitespace`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge — the change is additive and diagnostic-only; no credential values are exposed in logs. The credential shape computation is correct and the values logged are genuinely non-reversible. The only gap is a misleading comment in the NBSP test that attributes the detection to secretHasNonAscii alone, when secretHasSurroundingWhitespace and secretHasWhitespace would also fire in modern Node.js — leaving those code paths untested. This doesn't affect runtime behaviour but could mislead future maintainers or mask a regression in those flags. packages/shared/src/server/services/s3SigningDiagnostics.test.ts — the NBSP test case needs corrected comment and additional assertions.

author: nkwiatkowski
body:
## What
Fix sorting executions by **Duration** on PostgreSQL. The `executions.state_duration` generated column used `EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM interval)`, which returns only the seconds field of the interval (0–59999) and drops minutes/hours. A `7m59.45s` execution was stored as `59450` instead of `479450`, so duration sort was wrong for any execution ≥ 1 minute. Replaced with `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM interval) * 1000` (total milliseconds).

PostgreSQL only — MySQL and H2 already read the value as total seconds. Distinct from #11593/#13132 (NULL duration for running execs), which is unrelated to this.

Closes #16908

## How
Add Flyway migration **V1_45**. Column kept `NOT NULL`, matching this release line.

`state_duration` is a `STORED` generated column, so the migration drops and re-creates it (backfilling all rows; takes a brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on large tables) and recreates the `executions_state_duration` index.

## Tests
Added `findShouldSortByTotalDurationAcrossMinuteBoundary` asserting a 5-minute execution sorts above a 20-second one (and vice versa). Verified passing on Postgres and H2; confirmed it fails without the fix.

---

author: devops-thiago
body:
## What type of PR is this?

- [x] ✨ Feature
- [x] 📝 Documentation
- [x] ✅ Test

## Description

Reviews were one-shot: the bot posted findings, but a maintainer couldn't reply to a finding to ask for clarification or push back — only a fresh `/review` re-ran everything. This adds **conversational replies**.

The bot now detects:
- a **reply to one of its review findings** (a `pull_request_review_comment` on the bot's thread), and
- a bare **`@thrillhousebot` mention** (on an inline review comment or a top-level PR comment) that isn't the `/review` command,

and answers in context.

**How it works:** the cheap detection (action, bot-loop guard, mention/reply check, feature flag) runs on the webhook ACK path. The slow work is handed to the existing review executor (`MaintainerReplyDispatcher` → `MaintainerReplyService`), which loads the original finding, the surrounding diff / diff-hunk, and the prior thread replies, calls a new `ReplyAssistant` (LangChain4j, plain-Markdown output — no JSON schema), and posts the answer back into the same review thread (`POST .../comments/{id}/replies`) or as a PR comment for top-level mentions.

**Design notes for reviewers:**
- **Loop safety:** the existing `isBotComment` guard means the bot never answers its own comments, at the controller level, so its own posted replies can't re-trigger.
- **Authorization & cost:** replies are gated to the same write-access / allowlisted users as a manual `/review`, and behind a kill switch `REVIEW_CONVERSATIONAL_REPLIES_ENABLED` (default `true`). Authorization runs in the **async worker**, not on the ACK path, so it doesn't add a GitHub round-trip to the 200 (sidesteps the #92 concern for this new path).
- **Fail-soft:** every step swallows failures after logging — a maintainer asking a question can never break, and a failure means no reply rather than a noisy error comment.
- **Prompt-injection:** all untrusted inputs (question, finding, diff, thread) go through the existing `PromptTemplateEscaper`.
- **Scope decision:** gating to write-access matches the issue's "maintainer" framing and is the cost-safe default; easy to relax to PR authors later if desired.

Also subscribes the GitHub App to the new `pull_request_review_comment` event (`manifest.json`) — **existing installations must accept the added event subscription** for review-thread replies to fire.

## Related Issues

Fixes #31

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests

- New unit tests: `MaintainerReplyServiceTest` (7 — authorized/unauthorized, bot-thread reply with finding+thread context, human-thread with/without mention, issue-comment mention fetches diff, blank reply, assistant failure swallowed), `TriggerDetectorTest` (mention detection incl. word-boundary), `WebhookControllerTest` (7 — mention, replies-disabled, review-thread reply, mention-on-new-line, neither-reply-nor-mention, own comment, edited).
- **Full suite: 1000 tests pass, 0 failures** — including the `@QuarkusTest` app-boot tests, which confirm the new CDI beans (`MaintainerReplyService`, `MaintainerReplyDispatcher`, the `@RegisterAiService` `ReplyAssistant`) wire correctly.
- `spotless:check` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's coding standards
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have added tests that prove my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings or errors

## Additional Notes

Docs updated: `README.md` (feature bullet + config row), `.env.example`, `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased), and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (new sequence diagram + package table). The config key is `thrillhousebot.review.conversational-replies-enabled` (env `REVIEW_CONVERSATIONAL_REPLIES_ENABLED`).

(cache-busted), removing the old link once the replacement loads so there
is no flash — and all app state survives. Any non-CSS change is still a
full reload, and if no stylesheet matches the changed path the client
falls back to a reload so an edit is never dropped.

Component-level stateful HMR remains out of reach without a compiler (no
component boundaries/markers to swap a module in against) — CSS is the
slice of stateful HMR that is actually reachable in this runtime-JSX,
no-VDOM design, and it covers the highest-frequency inner-loop edit.

## Testing

- **Unit (`bun test`, runs in CI):** the message decision is a pure
  helper (`changeMessage`), and the client hot-swap is a real, exported
  function (`swapCss`) serialised into the dev page via `toString()` —
  both are unit-tested against mocks (matching swap + cache-busting,
  old-link removal on load/error, and the no-match reload fallback). All
  source stays at 100% coverage.
- **End-to-end (Playwright, new `tests/e2e` lane in CI):** drives the
  real dev server in Chromium to close the loop through the actual
  serve → file watcher → WebSocket → client `swapCss` path. A `.css`
  edit applies the new style while an in-memory counter survives (proving
  no reload); a non-CSS edit triggers a full reload (counter resets).
  Playwright stays CI-only (`--no-save`), so the zero-dependency rule
  holds.

Docs updated bilingually with a new "CSS HMR (Phase 6)" section.

author: vivekchand
body:
## What

Surfaces the resolved upgrade / cancellation CTA payload inline on `/api/entitlement` so the paywall renders in one round trip instead of two.

Today the dashboard's "Upgrade to ___" CTA needs:

1. `GET /api/entitlement` → read `next_tier`
2. `GET /api/entitlement/upgrade-diff?target=<next_tier>` → read `added_features` / `added_runtimes`

Same pattern for the cancellation surface against `prev_tier` + `/api/entitlement/downgrade-diff`. Both diffs are deterministic for the next / previous purchasable tier, so the second hop is pure round-trip cost.

This PR resolves them inline:

- `Entitlement.next_tier_diff()` — `upgrade_diff(next_purchasable_tier())` or `None` when already at the ceiling
- `Entitlement.previous_tier_diff()` — `downgrade_diff(previous_purchasable_tier())` or `None` when already at the floor
- `to_dict()` now carries `next_tier_diff` + `prev_tier_diff` keys (and the never-raise fallback shape in `routes/entitlement.py` is widened to match)
- Module-level `next_tier_diff()` / `previous_tier_diff()` mirroring the existing `next_purchasable_tier()` / `previous_purchasable_tier()` module wrappers

The natural follow-up to #3179 (`next_purchasable_tier`), #3183 (`previous_purchasable_tier`), and #3182 (`downgrade_diff`).

## Wire shape

Pure additive. Two new keys on `/api/entitlement`:

```json
{
  "next_tier_diff": {
    "target": "cloud_starter",
    "added_features": ["channel_history_30d", "..."],
    "added_runtimes": ["claude_code", "..."]
  },
  "prev_tier_diff": null
}
```

`null` once the install is at the corresponding end of the ladder (Enterprise for `next_tier_diff`, OSS-free for `prev_tier_diff`), so the dashboard short-circuits the CTA render instead of drawing "Upgrade to nothing". Same shape as the existing `/api/entitlement/upgrade-diff` / `/api/entitlement/downgrade-diff` responses so callers can read either source interchangeably.

Existing endpoints (`/api/entitlement/upgrade-diff?target=<tier>` etc.) untouched — a frontend still chaining the two-call flow keeps working identically.

## Tests

New `tests/test_entitlement_tier_diff.py` (20 tests):

- Shape pinning (matches `upgrade_diff` / `downgrade_diff` exactly)
- Ceiling / floor short-circuit (Enterprise → `None` on next; OSS & cloud_free → `None` on prev)
- Content sanity (OSS → Starter unlocks `STARTER_FEATURES`; cloud_pro → cloud_starter loses `PRO_ONLY_FEATURES`)
- Source-aware cluster picks (cloud_starter cancels to cloud_free, self-hosted pro cancels to its self-hosted floor)
- `to_dict()` + `/api/entitlement` surface
- Module-level helpers agree with bound methods
- Never-raise contract under a flaky resolver (both method + module-level)

```
tests/test_entitlement_tier_diff.py  20 passed in 0.21s
```

Re-ran the existing entitlement / paywall suite to confirm no regression:

```
tests/test_entitlement_api.py
tests/test_entitlements.py
tests/test_entitlements_catalogue.py
tests/test_entitlement_next_tier.py
tests/test_entitlement_prev_tier.py
tests/test_entitlement_upgrade_diff.py
tests/test_entitlement_channel_limit.py
tests/test_entitlement_effective_retention.py
tests/test_entitlement_expiry.py
→ 222 passed in 1.51s
```

`ruff check clawmetry/entitlements.py routes/entitlement.py tests/test_entitlement_tier_diff.py` → clean.

`python3 -m py_compile` on all three changed files → clean.

The wider `make lint` and the wider entitlement-grep suite each have pre-existing failures on `origin/main` (3 paywall HTML / runtime-switcher tests + 200+ ruff hits on `dashboard.py`); confirmed via `git stash` round-trip that none of them are touched by this branch.

## Grace / enforce

Pure additive read surface. Grace-mode behaviour unchanged — the new fields are derived from `next_purchasable_tier` / `previous_purchasable_tier` / `upgrade_diff` / `downgrade_diff`, all of which already exist and are unaffected. No new gate, no `@gate` decorator, no `CLAWMETRY_ENFORCE` interaction. Frontend / CTA semantics identical between grace and enforce; this just collapses the round trip.

## Local operator verification checklist

Since this agent runs without access to the local daemon, `~/.openclaw`, the live cloud snapshot, or a browser, the local operator should:

1. `git fetch origin feat/entitlement-to-dict-next-prev-tier-diff && git checkout feat/entitlement-to-dict-next-prev-tier-diff`
2. Copy the changed files into the live install:
   ```bash
   cp clawmetry/entitlements.py ~/.clawmetry/lib/python3.*/site-packages/clawmetry/entitlements.py
   cp routes/entitlement.py     ~/.clawmetry/lib/python3.*/site-packages/routes/entitlement.py
   ```
3. Clear caches: `find ~/.clawmetry/lib -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +`
4. Restart the daemon: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.clawmetry.sync`
5. Hit `/api/entitlement` and confirm:
   - `next_tier_diff` is present and matches `/api/entitlement/upgrade-diff?target=<next_tier>`
   - `prev_tier_diff` is present and matches `/api/entitlement/downgrade-diff?target=<prev_tier>`
   - On an Enterprise install: `next_tier_diff` is `null`
   - On an OSS / cloud_free install: `prev_tier_diff` is `null`
6. Decrypt the live cloud snapshot — the new keys ride on the existing `/api/entitlement` payload so the cloud relay picks them up automatically.
7. Browser-check the upgrade CTA still renders identically (no behaviour change for the existing two-call flow); the one-call flow becomes available for any future frontend refactor.

This PR is **draft-only**: not flipping to ready-for-review, not editing `__version__`, not opening a `[RELEASE]` PR, not enforcing any gate. Grace mode stays on.

author: devops-thiago
body:
## What type of PR is this?

- [x] ✨ Feature
- [x] ✅ Test
- [x] 📝 Documentation

## Description

The only PR command surface was `/review`. This adds a richer, intentionally-designed
set of comment commands so the bot can be operated directly from the PR:

| Command | What it does | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `/help` | List the available commands | anyone |
| `/review` | Run (or re-run) a full review (unchanged) | write |
| `/summary` | Post the PR summary, **only when none has been generated yet** (otherwise a no-op) | write |
| `/resolve` | Resolve ThrillhouseBot's outstanding finding threads on the PR | write |
| `/pause` | Silence the bot on the PR | write |
| `/resume` | Re-enable the bot on a paused PR | write |

Each command also accepts the `@Thrillhousebot <word>` mention form.

**Design**
- Detection moves from a boolean trigger to a `CommentCommand` enum (`TriggerDetector.detectCommand`); `isReviewTrigger` now delegates to it, so existing behavior and callers are unchanged.
- Non-review commands run **asynchronously** on the shared `@ReviewExecutor`, so the webhook 200-ack thread is never blocked by GitHub API calls. `/review` keeps its **synchronous** authorize-then-dispatch path to preserve the #89 dedup-rollback contract.
- **`/summary`** (per the issue's "regenerate the summary" intent, as clarified): if no completed review exists for the PR it dispatches a review (which posts the summary as the first review); if a summary already exists it does nothing.
- **`/pause`** silences *everything* — automatic reviews on push/open *and* manual `/review` / `/summary` — until `/resume`. Pause state is a persisted per-PR row (`PausedPr`, Hibernate auto-DDL — no migration; the project has no Flyway/Liquibase). `/help` and `/resolve` keep working while paused. An explicit `/review` or `/summary` on a paused PR gets a one-line "paused" reply; automatic events stay silent.
- Every command except `/help` requires repository write access, reusing the existing `ManualReviewAuthorizer` (reviews spend the operator's AI budget).

README gains a **Commands** section (table, access rules, pause semantics) and a Features bullet.

## Related Issues

Closes #32 (milestone v0.2.0).

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Unit tests

New / expanded tests:
- `TriggerDetectorTest` — `detectCommand` for every `/word` and mention form, `NONE` for non-commands, review-precedence, and similar-word disambiguation (`/resume` vs `/resolve` vs `/review`).
- `WebhookControllerTest` — non-review commands route to the command service; paused PR skips both the automatic review and the `/review` dispatch (posting the paused notice).
- `CommentCommandServiceTest` (new) — help posts without auth; summary dispatches only when no summary exists, no-ops when one exists, replies when paused, and is rejected for unauthorized users; resolve resolves only the bot's own unresolved threads; pause/resume persist and confirm.
- `PrPauseServiceTest` (new, `@QuarkusTest`) — pause/isPaused/resume, idempotent pause, per-PR scoping.

Local verification:
- `./mvnw test` → **1009 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (BUILD SUCCESS), Spotless check clean.
  - Note: run with `-Djacoco.skip=true -Dquarkus.jacoco.enabled=false` because the JaCoCo 0.8.15 agent crashes at JVM startup under JDK 25 with `-XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders` (a pre-existing local-tooling incompatibility, unrelated to this change).

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's coding standards
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have added tests that prove my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings or errors

## Additional Notes

The manual GitHub smoke test (live App install + Smee) was not run; the automated tests cover the routing, authorization, pause gating, and each command's effect.

﻿## Converge Phase 4 — slice C1: unified grading-queue read

First slice of the grading-UI unification ([plan](../blob/main/plans/260614-0004-converge-to-one-model/phase-04-grading-ui-unification.md)).
Server-only; builds the feed the Grading workspace (C2) will consume.

### What
`GET /api/assessment/grading-queue` (capability `assessment.manage`) returns the staff
"to-grade" feed across **both** assessment modes, as gradable **units**:
- **quiz** — published assessments that contain a `short_text` item, with attempt counts.
  Admin/Coordinator see all; a Teacher is scoped to accessible cohorts (`visibleCohortIdsForTeacher`).
- **rubric** — team-world (English) classes with evaluation counts. Only Admin/Teacher record
  rubric evaluations → others get an empty `rubric` list; cohort-world (`self_enroll`/`nomination`)

### Design
**Gradable units** (an assessment for quiz, a class for rubric), not individual pending items —
the native entry modals (`ManualGradingModal` / rubric entry) are already per-unit, so the
workspace just opens them in place. The `assessment.manage` gate = the union (every rubric grader,
Admin or Teacher, holds it) — matching the resolved decision Q3 (no rubric authz regression; each
modal still enforces its own server-side authz on write).

### Safety
Additive **read** across use-cases/repository/dto/controller/routes — **no writes, not audited,
no change** to the grading or evaluation write paths or their authz.

## Problema

No desktop (≥1024px), ao clicar em um lote no mapa, o card (`LotBottomSheet`) abria mas fechava imediatamente — o comportamento "abre e fecha" reportado pelo usuário.

**Causa raiz:** O backdrop (`fixed inset-0 z-[9998]`) com `onClick={onClose}` cobria toda a tela, incluindo a área do mapa. No mobile, o sheet ocupa quase toda a tela e o usuário interage apenas com o sheet. No desktop, o mapa fica visível acima do sheet, e qualquer clique do usuário no mapa (tentar selecionar outro lote, arrastar, etc.) era interceptado pelo backdrop → `onClose` chamado → card fechava.

## Fix

Adicionado `lg:pointer-events-none` nos backdrops do `LotBottomSheet` e `AmenityBottomSheet`. No desktop (≥1024px):
- Cliques passam pelo overlay diretamente para o mapa/SVG
- O usuário pode selecionar lotes, arrastar e interagir com o mapa enquanto o card está aberto
- O card fecha via: botão X, tecla Escape, ou clique no fundo do SVG (`handleBgClick → setSelectedLot(null)`)

No mobile: comportamento inalterado — o backdrop bloqueia cliques e fecha ao tocar fora do sheet.

## Alterações

- `AltoBellevuePlanView.tsx`: 2 linhas alteradas (backdrop `LotBottomSheet` + `AmenityBottomSheet`)

author: jeffmhopkins
body:
## Follow-up to #338 / #339 — the actual root fix

#338 and #339 each merged with only part of the work; this carries the final, decisive change that was pushed after #339 had already merged.

`main` still bind-mounts a **single file** (`./searxng/settings.yml:/etc/searxng/settings.yml`). That is the root footgun behind the recurring crash loop:

```
cp: '/etc/searxng/settings.yml' is a directory
!!! ERROR  "/etc/searxng/settings.yml" is not a valid file, exiting...
```

The SearXNG image entrypoint runs `check_directory` on `/etc/searxng` and manages `settings.yml` itself. With a single-file bind, the instant compose runs while the host file is missing, Docker creates an empty **directory** at that path, the entrypoint sees `settings.yml` as a directory, and the container crash-loops permanently — and copying the file in afterward just nests it inside the directory.

## Fix

Bind the whole **`/etc/searxng` directory** (`./searxng:/etc/searxng`) — the canonical searxng-docker pattern. A directory bind can only ever be a directory, so a missing host dir simply boots from the image template instead of crash-looping.

## Verified locally in Docker

- Reproduced the exact crash with the single-file bind.
- Directory mount + the repo's real `settings.yml` → container **running**, `/search?format=json` returns **HTTP 200** with valid JSON.
- Directory mount with an empty host dir → boots cleanly, no crash (footgun eliminated).
- Reproduced the owner's broken box (`settings.yml` as a stale dir) → heal + recreate → running, clean.

## Tests

`backend/tests/unit/test_searxng_compose.py` asserts the directory mount and rejects any single-file `settings.yml` bind. 3 passed.

## After merge

A single `jbrain update` is enough — the mount fix lives in the compose file itself, so once the host's docker-compose.yml is refreshed the directory mount takes over and this class of failure cannot recur.

author: joshua-quek-sonarsource
body:
## Problem

After a `transfer`, the migrated SonarCloud project rendered incorrectly in two ways:

1. **"The main branch of this project is empty"** — even though the project, quality gate, issues, and hotspots all migrated.
2. **No SCM blame in the Code view** — every line showed a synthetic stub author and the analysis date, instead of who actually changed the line and when (which SonarQube Server shows).

## Root causes

1. **No measures.** `buildBranchReport` handed `PackageReport` an empty `Measures` map, so the report carried zero `measures-*.pb`. SonarCloud's CE aggregates project `ncloc` from per-file measures; with none, project `ncloc` is null and the empty-branch overlay fires.
2. **Blame ignored.** The extract already pulled real per-line blame via `getProjectSCMData` (`/api/sources/scm`), but the migrate side never read it — it always emitted a synthetic single changeset, then overwrote it with issue-date-only entries during backdating.

## Changes

**Measures (empty branch)**
- `extract`: widen component-tree `metricKeys` from `ncloc` alone to `ncloc,comment_lines,complexity,cognitive_complexity,functions,statements,classes` (the scalar metrics the API allows; `ncloc_data`/`executable_lines_data` are rejected by `component_tree` and would require per-file `api/measures/component` calls — documented as a follow-up).
- `migrate`: new `loadComponentMeasures` reads the per-file measures and feeds `scanreport.BuildMeasures` instead of an empty map.

**SCM blame (Code view)**
- `migrate`: new `loadExtractedSCM` reads `getProjectSCMData`; `/api/sources/scm` is run-length encoded, so `scanreport.BuildChangesetsFromBlame` dedups `(revision, author, date)` and expands runs forward across every line.
- Backdating is now **blame-preserving**: it overrides only the *date* on issue lines (so issue creation dates stay accurate) while keeping each line's real author/revision. Falls back to the synthetic changeset only when the source has no blame.

## Verification (live, against sc-staging)

Transferred the full `okorach-oss_sonar-tools` (which has real git history) and queried the target API:

- **Main branch measures:** `ncloc = 17,379` plus statements 15,702, comment_lines 5,216, complexity 4,663, cognitive_complexity 4,433, functions 1,451, classes 68 — branch is no longer empty.
- **Blame:** `/api/sources/scm` on the target returns real authors / dates / 40-char revisions, matching the source line-for-line.

Note: the `-test` project clone has no blame at the source (analyzed without git history), so it can only ever show synthetic authors — the full project is the correct fixture for the blame fix.

## Tests
- New `TestBuildChangesetsFromBlame` (run-length expansion, commit dedup, zero-date fallback, nil-on-empty).
- Existing `backdate_test.go` cases still pass (the blame-preserving refactor keeps the asserted dates/indices).
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `internal/{migrate,scanreport,extract}` tests all green after rebasing onto latest `main`.

## Notes
- Docs: `docs/EMPTY-MAIN-BRANCH-REPORT-DIFF.md` (updated) + `docs/SCM-BLAME-MIGRATION.md` (new).
- The final `chore` commit adds throwaway report diagnostics (`tmp_pbdump/`, `zz_dumpreport_test.go`, gated/CI-skipped) and gitignores `transfer-run.out`; drop that commit if you'd rather not carry the diagnostics.

body:
## Summary

Adds a reproducible **backend test-coverage harness** and raises backend line coverage from **42% → 99%** (1585 tests passing: 238 httpx integration + 1347 in-process unit), fixing the real bugs the tests exposed along the way.

The coverage environment is fully **isolated** (its own ephemeral pgvector + redis) and **never touches the production database**.

## Coverage harness
- `docker-compose.test.yml` — ephemeral pgvector + redis test stack (tmpfs, offline, CPU-only).
- `run-coverage.sh` — 3-way `coverage combine`:
  - **Run B**: `backend/tests/test_*.py` httpx integration tests against an instrumented server (handler bodies).
  - **Run C**: `backend/tests/unit/` in-process unit tests with DB/ML/genai mocked (services + ML/external paths integration can't reach offline).
  - **Run A**: import-under-coverage for module-level lines.
- `backend/tests/_coverage_launcher.py` — imports the app **before** `coverage.start()` to dodge two hard crashes on this stack: the `torch _has_torch_function` docstring `RuntimeError` and the SQLAlchemy-async/asyncpg **greenlet segfault** under coverage's C tracer.
- `backend/tests/unit/` — ~1350 unit tests (`mock_db` AsyncMock + `make_result` helpers).
- Docs: new **"Backend test coverage"** section in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Bug fixes surfaced by the coverage work
1. `main.py` — request-validation errors now return standard **422** (was a non-standard 400).
2. `routers/chat.py` — rename thread `await db.refresh()` before serializing; was **500 MissingGreenlet**.
3. `routers/proteins.py` — compute-embedding returns **404** (not 400) for a missing protein.
4. `routers/embeddings.py` — fix undefined `all_have_umap` **NameError** on the FOV-UMAP success path.
5. `services/data_export_service.py` — `export_ranking_comparisons` used **nonexistent `Comparison` columns** (`loser_id`/`source`/`created_at`); rewritten to derive the loser from `crop_a_id`/`crop_b_id`/`winner_id` and use `timestamp`.
6. `services/rag_service.py` — `import json` moved to module top (was used before its late import); skip the embedding-model load when nothing is indexed.
7. `services/gemini_agent_service.py` — drop redundant function-local `from datetime import datetime` that shadowed the name and broke the agent-memory paths (`UnboundLocalError`).

## Not deployed
All changes are code/tests only. **Production still runs the old code** — a backend rebuild (`docker-compose.prod.yml`) is intentionally left to a separate, explicit deploy step.

author: alecdray
body:
# Summary

## What
`review` and `tags` HTTP adapters no longer import `library/adapters/views`. After a rating or tag mutation they broadcast a generic `album-changed` HTMX event (carrying `albumId` + `scope`); library owns the refresh via a new `GET /app/library/album-surfaces` endpoint and a hidden listener in its header bar that re-renders the affected album surfaces as OOB swaps. This closes the lone entry in `docs/architecture/known-gaps.md`.

## Why
The domain-module archetype forbids a peer importing another module's `adapters/`/`adapters/views/` package. `review` and `tags` violated this by rendering library's templ fragments directly to swap album UI after mutating state. Closing it keeps the module boundary clean: peers signal "an album changed"; library decides which of its own surfaces refresh.

## How
- New domain-free `httpx.SetHXTrigger(w, event, detail)` helper sets the `HX-Trigger` response header.
- `review`/`tags` handlers set `HX-Trigger: album-changed` (detail `{albumId, scope}`) and render only their own close-modal frag; their `library/adapters/views` imports are removed.
- Library exposes `GET /app/library/album-surfaces` (scoped by mutation kind so a rating change and a tag change each refresh exactly the surfaces they did before) and an `AlbumSurfaceListenerFrag` rendered in `LibraryHeaderBarFrag`.
- The surface refresh is now asynchronous (mutation response → event → follow-up GET); the only true closure of the gap, since library's `*Service` can't return a renderer (import cycle) and option B still imports `library/adapters`.

# Validation
- [x] Go unit suite passes (`go test ./src/internal/...`), incl. a new `SetHXTrigger` test
- [x] Gap closed: `grep -rn "library/adapters/views" src/internal/review src/internal/tags` is empty
- [x] Feature e2e (`reviews`, `tags`, `rating-lifecycle`, `album_detail`) pass deterministically at `--workers=1` (34/34)
- [ ] Full `task test/e2e` at default parallelism — see Notes

# Notes
- One shared e2e helper (`deleteEntry`) switched from waiting on the mutation response to waiting on the observable DOM change, per the suite's DOM-signal rule (the refresh is now async).
- The full suite at default (multi-worker) parallelism intermittently fails with `database is locked` — pre-existing SQLite contention reproduced on the untouched base commit, unrelated to this change. Logged in `docs/backlog.md` (options: WAL + busy_timeout, `workers: 1`, or per-spec data isolation).
- Backlog also notes migrating library's existing raw `HX-Trigger` header writes to `httpx.SetHXTrigger`.

body:
## Summary

The `GET /copilot_internal/user` endpoint no longer returns the legacy `limited_user_quotas` / `monthly_quotas` fields the provider parsed, so paid/enterprise accounts showed empty (0) Copilot usage. This switches the provider to read `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` — the user's **AI credits** budget — which is the meaningful metric today.

## Changes

- **`CopilotProvider.swift`**
  - Replaced the legacy response model fields with `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` (`entitlement`, `remaining`, `percent_remaining`, `unlimited`, overage flags) plus `quota_reset_date` / `quota_reset_date_utc`.
  - Rewrote `mapToSnapshot` to build a single usage window: `used = entitlement − remaining`, `utilization = 100 − percent_remaining`, sublabel `"{used} / {entitlement} used"` (thousands-separated), reset parsed from the UTC timestamp. Gracefully shows "Unlimited" when the snapshot is unlimited/absent.
  - Hardened `planLabel` to map newer SKUs (e.g. `copilot_enterprise_seat_multi_quota` → "Enterprise") via contains-matching.
- **Renamed the metric to "AI credits"** (the current GitHub term) in the ring label and related copy/doc comments (`HowItWorksView`, `Provider`, `SettingsService`).
- **Tests:** removed the obsolete legacy fixtures; added `copilot_user_premium.json` and `copilot_user_unlimited.json`; rewrote `CopilotProviderParsingTests` (6 tests) covering decode, used count, utilization, enterprise plan label, UTC reset-date parsing, and the unlimited path.

## Testing

- `CopilotProviderParsingTests` — all pass.
- Verified against the live API response and a local ad-hoc build: the Copilot tab now shows the **AI credits** ring (e.g. ~18,363 / 40,000 used) instead of an empty display.

Note: 3 pre-existing `NotificationContentTests` failures are unrelated to this change (confirmed they fail on the base branch too).

author: jleonardopl1
body:
## Fase 0 — edge function de cotações

**Contexto:** a `cotacao-worker` estava descrita como "duas versões sobrepostas / não compila". Ao investigar, a versão commitada **já compilava limpo** e estava em versão única (o merge `cea36b1` "cotações reais" já havia reconciliado as duas versões). Conforme combinado, o foco desta PR é **endurecer** a função — sem alterar schema, env vars nem o contrato de resposta.

### O que mudou
- **Parser único `num`** — unifica `num`/`num2`. Só trata formato BR (`1.234,56`) quando há vírgula, evitando que `"128.50"` (ponto decimal) vire `12850`. Preserva variação negativa.
- **`fetchJson` com timeout (AbortController, 8s)** — uma fonte travada (brapi/CEPEA) não trava mais o cron de 15 min.
- **Descarte de valores inválidos** — preço/câmbio `<= 0` ou não-numérico não é gravado.
- **Inserts independentes/best-effort** — falha em `cotacoes_cache` não bloqueia `cambio_cache`; erros vão na resposta (`status 500`) e `inseridas`/`cambio` passam a refletir o que foi de fato gravado.
- **`try/catch` de topo** no handler — resposta JSON limpa em erro inesperado.

### Compatibilidade
- Schema inalterado (`cotacoes_cache`, `cambio_cache`, `cooperativas.estado`); constraints de `fonte`/`tipo` respeitadas.
- Resposta mantém as chaves `ok`, `inseridas`, `cambio`, `fontes`, `ufs` (adiciona `errors[]` opcional). Nada no front consome esse JSON — ele lê os caches direto.

### Verificação
- `deno check` com os **tipos reais** do `@supabase/supabase-js@2` (npm 2.108.2): **0 erros**.
- `deno lint`: apenas `no-import-prefix` no `import "jsr:…"` — é o padrão do Supabase e idêntico em todas as outras functions (não é erro de compilação).
- Teste unitário do parser `num` cobrindo casos BR/US/borda: 13/13 ✅.

body:
Adds [llmtrim](https://github.com/fkiene/llmtrim) under **Frameworks & Libraries -> Utilities & Processing**.

llmtrim is a Rust-to-WebAssembly engine (`@llmtrim/wasm` / `@llmtrim/js` on npm, v0.2.1) that compresses LLM prompts, tool outputs, and replies to cut token cost, with a quality gate that reverts any step that would not save. The wasm build has no network or filesystem access, so it runs inside a Worker for token estimation and prompt compression at the edge.

On the Cloudflare-specificity question: it is a portable wasm package (no wrangler binding required), in the same spirit as the existing portable-wasm entries in this subsection (HTML Rewriter WASM, Cabidela). The edge/Worker use case is the reason it fits here. Open source (MPL-2.0).

author: drzeeb
body:
# 🌍 More countries, smarter search, About screen & navigation screen-on

Builds on the bundled **France 🇫🇷 & Luxembourg 🇱🇺** datasets and adds the surrounding UX so the multi-country data is actually discoverable — plus a couple of quality-of-life fixes.

## ✨ Added

- **More countries — France & Luxembourg bike-parking coverage**
  Two pre-built SQLite assets (`bike_parking_france.db`, `bike_parking_luxembourg.db`) are merged into the single on-device database via a data-only Room migration (`BikeParkingDatabase` v3 → v4). The map's bounding-box queries transparently return parking spots in these countries too. Works on fresh installs **and** upgrades, preserving favourites and Germany data (`INSERT OR IGNORE`, OSM element IDs are globally unique).

- **Multi-country address search with home-country bias**
  Nominatim forward-geocoding now covers `countrycodes=de,fr,lu` instead of Germany only. When the user's location is known, results are biased toward their surroundings via a `viewbox` (≈ 110 km half-span) with `bounded=0` — so matches in the country you're currently in rank first, without excluding the others.

- **About screen** (menu → *About*)
  A sheet showing the app name, a link to the website (`https://velospot.app`), the per-country dataset status (Germany 08.08.2026, France & Luxembourg 18.06.2026) and a link to the privacy policy (`https://velospot.app/privacy`). Localised across all eight supported languages.

- **Keep the screen awake during navigation**
  While a route is being navigated the display no longer dims or locks; the `keepScreenOn` flag is set on the map view for the duration of active navigation and cleared automatically when navigation ends.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Crash on first open with the multi-country database**
  Bumping the DB to v4 made Room run its full post-migration `TableInfo` validation, which failed because the `idx_parking_lat_lon` index present in the bundled assets wasn't declared on `BikeParkingSpaceEntity` (`Migration didn't properly handle: bike_parking_spaces`). The index is now declared on the entity so the expected schema matches the seeded database (and it speeds up bounding-box queries).

## ✅ Verification

- `:app:testGooglePlayDebugUnitTest` and `:app:lintFdroidDebug` — **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**
- Built & installed on a physical device (OnePlus 7T, Android 12): app launches without the migration crash, search returns FR/LU results, About sheet links open, display stays on during navigation.

author: zaviermeekz-cpu
body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

GraphRAG `set_graph()` embeds entities and relations one‑by‑one, causing extreme slowness (10-50x slower) for large graphs (17,000+ edges). This PR batches embedding calls to improve performance.

### Solution

- Add `GRAPHRAG_EMBED_BATCH_SIZE` environment variable (default 64).
- Refactor `graph_node_to_chunk` and `graph_edge_to_chunk` to separate chunk building from embedding application.
- Batch cache misses in groups of `_EMBED_BATCH_SIZE` and encode in a single HTTP call.
- Reuse existing Redis cache to avoid redundant embedding.
- Fix cache key mismatch (check was using "A->B", store was using "A->B: description").
- Add progress callbacks for batch encoding phases.

### Performance impact

- Before: 17,000+ individual HTTP requests for embedding.
- After: ~265 batched requests (17,000 / 64).
- Measured speedup: 10-50x depending on graph size and network latency.

### How has this been tested?

- Verified with a small document (entities/relations indexed correctly).
- Verified with a large document (17,000+ edges) – completion time significantly reduced.
- Redis cache is populated and reused as expected.

### Related Issue

Closes #16205

author: tphakala
body:
## Summary

Reworks the per-model **Last heard** view on the AI Models & Inference page from a chronological ring of saved detections into a diagnostic feed of what each model is actually firing on, with cross-model correlation aids.

**Backend** (`internal/analysis/processor`)
- **Per-species throttle**: a species is recorded at most once per the model's segment-aligned interval (`clip x round(9s/clip)` -> 9s for BirdNET, 10s for Perch), so a continuously singing bird does not flood the feed while its cadence stays visible. The blind circular buffer becomes a slice-backed most-recent-first list, cap 20.
- **All above-threshold predictions**: recording moved into `processResults`, before the range and privacy filters, so the feed shows non-bird classes, human vocalizations, and out-of-range birds, each tagged with an `inRange` flag.
- The **save path is unchanged** (DB rows + audio clips): human and out-of-range species are still never saved.

**API** (`internal/api/v2`): `LastDetectionInfo` gains `inRange` (additive; existing fields unchanged).

**Frontend** (`SystemInference.svelte`)
- Two newspaper columns of ten (20 total), newest first.
- Absolute 24-hour timestamps (`HH:MM:SS`, full date+time on hover) for cross-model correlation.
- "Also" column listing other models that detected the same species within +/-3s.
- A range-filter icon next to species the filter rejects (diagnostic, not saved) and a caption explaining the feed.
- Empty latency sparkline draws a flat 0 baseline until samples arrive.
- Spec label "Clip length" renamed to "Segment length" across all 16 locales.

## Privacy note

This view now surfaces **human vocalization classes** (and other non-bird/out-of-range predictions) so the model's raw above-threshold output can be inspected, e.g. to troubleshoot the privacy filter. This is **shown only**, never recorded:
- The feed is an **in-memory ring** on the processor: label + scientific name + confidence + timestamp + range flag. **No audio**, never written to the database or disk, not included in support dumps or telemetry, cleared on restart.
- The **save path is unchanged** - human and out-of-range species are not persisted as detections or clips.
- The view is behind the existing authenticated system endpoint.

## Test Plan

- [x] `go test -race ./internal/analysis/processor/` and the inference API tests pass
- [x] `golangci-lint` clean on changed packages
- [x] Frontend `npm run check:all` (typecheck, lint, ast) clean; component tests pass; i18n in sync across 16 locales
- [ ] Manual: verify the two-column feed, absolute timestamps, the "Also" co-detection column, the range-filter icon on non-bird/out-of-range entries, and that human/out-of-range entries appear in the feed but are not saved as detections

author: eltonsoares
body:
## Mérito gigante trava o L3 (JSON malformado → indeterminado)

**Sintoma:** mérito 680046 (re-cascateado pós-fix-L1) passou L1+L2 mas o **L3 (`merito_synthesis`) falha com JSON parse error** (`Expecting ',' delimiter: line 5312 column 6 (char 145572)`) → 5 retries → indeterminado.

**Investigação (artefatos reais):**
- 680046 tem só **3 processos ativos** → input do L3 ≈ 35KB.
- Dominado pelo card L2 do processo de **1940 movs** (`01116834320088260008`): **16.162 output_tokens / 28KB**, dos quais **`lifecycle_garantia` = 22.723 chars** (os outros campos somam <6KB).
- `_summarize_processo_synthesis` (prompts.py:160) renderizava **todos** os ~280 eventos no prompt → o L3 ecoava+amplificava em `ciclo_garantia` → **output 145KB / 5312 linhas** (um card de risco de 3 procs deveria ter ~poucos KB → ~30-50× = degeneração) → JSON malformado.

**Mesmo padrão do bound de doc grande no L1** — artefato intermediário sem limite.

**Fix:** head+tail (20+20 eventos) no render do lifecycle. Preserva origem (apresentação/aceitação) + estado atual da garantia; o miolo repetido vira marcador. Processo normal (poucos eventos) **inalterado**. 3 testes; zero falha nova (as 8 do `merito_synthesis_routing/sem_cap` são stale pré-existentes, não relacionadas).

**Caveat honesto:** não vi o raw de 145KB (o ai-agents só loga a msg do erro). O veredicto vem da desproporção input/output + o campo gordo identificado. Validação real = re-cascatear 680046 pós-deploy e ver o L3 fechar.

**Follow-up possível:** suavizar o schema de output `ciclo_garantia` ("todos os eventos") se o output ainda inflar mesmo com input limitado.

author: mhsnook
body:
## What

Commands now route by PR, not by run. The route moves from

```
POST /api/runs/:runId/commands
```

to

```
POST /api/cloud/repos/:owner/:name/pr/:number/commands
```

mirroring the viewer WS, with the body becoming `{ command, runId? }`.

## Why

This was the last place `runId` acted as an **address**. The PR coordinator DO is named by PR (`idFromName(\`${repo}#${prNumber}\`)`), but the command route was keyed by run, so the worker had to bridge the two with a `SELECT repo, pr_number FROM runs WHERE id = ?1` on every command — the leftover pattern from #13.

The PR is the unit of value; a run is one unit of work. Addressing commands by run quietly reasserts "the run is the unit" at every new call site. Routing by the PR (which the page already knows) and demoting `runId` to an optional field in the body fixes that: the run is data riding in the envelope, not the address.

This also closes out #13 — its viewer-WS half was already designed away (the viewer channel is PR-scoped), and this removes the last instance of the runId→PR translation. Notably *not* via that issue's recommended migration: `do_name` would have been a denormalized concat of two columns that saved zero round-trips.

## Changes

- **`index.ts`** — route moved under the PR namespace, alongside `…/pr/:number/ws`.
- **`postRunCommand` → `postPrCommand`** (`scenetest-bridge/routes.ts`) — repo/PR from the path, zero D1; body `{ command, runId? }`.
- **DO `/command`** — `runId` optional; relayed to the box only when present, so the box-agent contract is unchanged.
- **e2e** — exercises both paths: a run-agnostic command (no runId, accepted + queued) and a runId-tagged command passed through to the box's per-run command file.
- **docs** — the "commands on the PR transport" open decision is now resolved; diagram + design note updated.

## What's deliberately left out

`run:stop/pause/resume/replay` all act on the PR's *active* run, so they ride run-agnostic today. The box agent (`infra/box/agent.mjs`) still *requires* `msg.runId` and silently drops a runId-less command — teaching it to act on one is a follow-up for when a run-targeting UI needs it, and it's now a payload/agent concern rather than a routing one. (There's a related cross-team ask going to the scenetest-js team about the command-consumption side / receiver-core.)

## Validation

`pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm e2e` 63/63 passing.
