body:
Deployed skeleton for Claudius: server-side identity with three roles, the full MongoDB data layer defined in code, and proven Atlas + Bedrock connectivity. No chat yet.

## What's included

**Data layer (`packages/shared`)**
- Zod-validated env schema, parsed once at boot, fails fast naming any missing/invalid variable (never logs values).
- Serverless-safe MongoDB client singleton; the same client is shared with the Auth.js adapter.
- Zod schemas as the single type source (`z.infer`) for all eight collections, plus typed collection accessors.
- Idempotent index script: conversation compound + TTL indexes, `usage_events` time-series collection, and `memories`/`chunks` Atlas Vector Search indexes (1024-dim cosine, pre-filtered by `userId`).
- Seed script for default settings (allowlist, model catalog with cross-region inference profile IDs, tiers, guest circuit breaker).

**App (`packages/app`)**
- Auth.js v5 with Google + MongoDB adapter, JWT sessions, server-side role resolution (admin email, settings allowlist, else guest) with user provisioning.
- Protected `/api/health` route (Atlas ping plus opt-in `?probe=bedrock`).
- Signed-in landing page showing name, email, and role.

## Notable decisions
- Standardized the repo on the `mongodb` 7.3.0 driver via root `overrides` (the Auth.js adapter peer-pins `^6`); added `@langchain/core`.
- Database named explicitly as `claudius` rather than relying on a connection-string default.
- Guest data ephemerality enforced by a TTL index on `expiresAt`; member/admin documents omit the field.
- Every vector index declares `userId` as a filter field so searches pre-filter by owner.

## Verification
- `npm run check` passes (typecheck, lint, tests).
- `db:indexes` and `db:seed` verified idempotent across repeated runs.
- Atlas inspection confirmed all collections, the time-series buckets, the conversation indexes, both vector indexes (`READY`/queryable), and the seeded settings.
- Bedrock probe returned a successful one-token Converse result.

Two reported issues.

## 1. App icon was blank
The Windows exe / taskbar showed a default blank icon — the csproj had no `ApplicationIcon`. Editing a pipeline and saving it back to the **active** profile had no button — only "Save as profile", which requires a new name. Now:

author: trishorts
body:
Adds a **ProForma 2.0** column to top-down results — in the psmtsv output (immediately after **Full Sequence**) and in the MetaDraw PSM grid.

## What changed

**`EngineLayer/SpectrumMatch/PsmTsvWriter.cs`** — in `AddPeptideSequenceData`, emit `SpectrumMatchFromTsvHeader.ProForma` right after `FullSequence`, gated on `GlobalVariables.AnalyteType == AnalyteType.Proteoform`. The value is `IBioPolymerWithSetMods.ToProFormaString()`, resolved across ambiguous matches with the same `Resolve(...)` idiom as the neighbouring sequence columns.

- The single analyte-type gate keeps the header (built with a null match) and the data rows in sync, so the column appears as a unit or not at all.
- Both `AllPSMs.psmtsv` and `AllProteoforms.psmtsv` write through `GetTabSeparatedHeader` / `SpectralMatch.ToString`, so a top-down run gets the column in both files; bottom-up and oligo runs get it in neither.

**`GUI/MetaDraw/MetaDraw.xaml` + `.xaml.cs`** — add a `ProForma` column to the PSM grid, also immediately after Full Sequence, so the string is visible without opening the tsv. It binds to `SpectrumMatchFromTsv.ProForma`, which mzLib reads via `GetOptionalValue`, so pre-ProForma files load fine.

The column ships `Visibility="Collapsed"` and is revealed after load only when the loaded results actually carry a ProForma string — bottom-up and legacy files show no empty column. Visibility is keyed off the loaded data rather than `GlobalVariables.AnalyteType`, because that global defaults to `Peptide` and is never set by standalone MetaDraw; gating on it would have hidden the column for genuine top-down results.

ProForma is a top-down-only feature and is added automatically for top-down runs — deliberately no toml setting and no GUI option to control it.

## Tests (`Test/PsmTsvWriterTests.cs`)

- `ProForma_TopDownSearch_ColumnFollowsFullSequenceAndCarriesProFormaString` — asserts the column sits immediately after Full Sequence in both header and data row, and carries the proteoform's ProForma string including the modification descriptor.
- `ProForma_BottomUpSearch_ColumnAbsent` — asserts the column is absent from the header for bottom-up.
- Both restore `GlobalVariables.AnalyteType` in a `finally`.

Patch coverage hits both `if` branches and both ternary outcomes; `codecov/patch` passes.

## Dependency — satisfied

This builds on the ProForma reader/writer from **smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1072**, merged 2026-07-15 and shipped in **mzLib 1.0.583**, which master already references. No package bump is needed in this PR, and CI is green across all jobs.

author: rodaddy
body:
## Summary

- Fix `lane_upsert` failing to CREATE a new session lane when the caller omits `status` (`null value in column "status" violates not-null constraint`).
- `src/tools/lane-upsert.ts:126` bound `args.status ?? null` into the INSERT VALUES for the `NOT NULL` `status` column (default `'active'`). An explicit NULL overrides the column default → constraint violation on every new-lane INSERT.
- Fix: separate `insertStatus = args.status ?? 'active'` (new `$24`) feeds the INSERT VALUES; `$3` stays nullable for the ON CONFLICT preserve-logic; `ended_at` CASE re-pointed from `EXCLUDED.status` to `$3`.
- Regression test added. Closes #162.

## Root cause

The UPDATE path (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`) was made null-aware (`CASE WHEN $3 IS NULL THEN ob_session_lanes.status ...`), so existing-lane updates preserve status correctly. But the INSERT path binds the same `$3 = null` into the `NOT NULL` column, so the **first** write to any new `session_key` fails while subsequent updates succeed — which is why it looked intermittent and why a worker bounce appeared to "fix" it (a bounce only changed which keys were new).

Origin: the null-aware `status`/`ended_at` design was introduced in `bfbadad` (feat: durable session lanes #34/#43), whose review-swarm changes ("Fix status silently resetting to 'active'", "preserve ended_at on null status") added the UPDATE-side null handling without defaulting the INSERT-side value.

## The `EXCLUDED.status` / `ended_at` coupling (why the naive fix is wrong)

A naive `COALESCE($3,'active')` in VALUES would make `EXCLUDED.status = 'active'` on a status-omitted UPDATE, tripping `WHEN EXCLUDED.status = 'active' THEN NULL` and wiping `ended_at` — silently reactivating a wrapped/archived lane. The fix avoids this by keeping `$3` nullable for ALL ON CONFLICT logic and re-pointing the `ended_at` CASE onto `$3`, so a status-omitted update falls to `ELSE ob_session_lanes.ended_at` (preserve). `ended_at` behavior is unchanged for every case.

## Validation

- `bun test` → 726 pass, 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- Live blast radius (hosted OB, skippy-oc/10.71.1.21): 240 `lane_upsert_db_error` in 24h (69 bilby, 171 skippy), all this violation.

## Critical Self-Review

- Highest-risk behavior: The `ended_at` CASE re-point from `EXCLUDED.status` to `$3`. If wrong, a status-omitted update could reactivate a wrapped/archived lane. Verified by case table: explicit status branches are byte-equivalent ($3 == old EXCLUDED.status); omitted-status falls to ELSE-preserve, matching prior behavior (old EXCLUDED.status was also null on omission).
- Assumptions that could be wrong: That every caller path that omits status wants the column default. The schema default is `'active'`; new lanes are active by definition, so defaulting the INSERT to 'active' matches intent.
- Missing/weak tests: The mock pool cannot fire the real NOT NULL constraint or a real UPDATE's `ended_at`, so the regression test asserts the bind-param/SQL contract (omitted status → `$24='active'`, `$3=null`, `ended_at` keys off `$3`) rather than a live DB outcome. A live-pg integration test would be a stronger guard — noted as follow-up.
- Security/permission risk: None. No auth/namespace logic touched.
- Migration/deploy risk: No schema change. Behavior change is strictly "new lanes without status now succeed as 'active'" — previously they errored. Deploy needed on hosted OB to stop live failures.
- Downstream client/runtime risk: Positive — Hermes lane writes that failed server-side and spooled will succeed once deployed. Surfacing of such failures is rtech-hermes#84's F2 (separate repo), which is why these 240 failures were invisible behind a healthy-looking "active" status.
- Rollback/cleanup concern: Pure code change, trivially revertible. One diagnostic `log_thought` (id `5f3db27d`, tag diagnostic/write-probe) was left in bilby's namespace during live diagnosis — flagged for cleanup (issue owner to remove).
- Fixes made before PR: separate insert-status param; `ended_at` re-point; regression test.
- Known residual risk: 34 `lane_upsert` entries in Bilby's spool stay stuck until this deploys AND replay is nudged (see Deploy & follow-up).
- SME review-memory update: [ ] `docs/sme/` updated or [x] not applicable because: this is a single SQL upsert defect, not a new reviewer-lane pattern; existing correctness/domain lanes already cover INSERT-vs-UPSERT and NOT NULL semantics.

## Review Gate

- [x] Critical self-review fields above are filled with specific, non-placeholder content
- [x] MEDIUM+ review findings were captured in `docs/sme/` or explicitly marked not applicable
- Live Open Brain checks: [ ] linked below or [x] not applicable because: fix is code + bind-param regression; live verification happens at deploy (lane_upsert against hosted OB), tracked in Deploy & follow-up.

## Deploy & follow-up

- **Deploy required** on `com.rico.open-brain` (10.71.1.21) — the 240/24h failures continue until the running server has this commit.
- **Bilby spool drain (rtech-hermes side, owner-driven):** 65 entries spooled (34 stuck `lane_upsert` on this bug, 31 drainable), backed up to `~/.hermes/openbrain_spool.jsonl.bak-20260619-pre-drain` (nothing lost). The 34 stuck entries drain only after this fix is live; opportunistic replay won't self-fire (chicken-and-egg) and needs a nudge post-deploy.
- **Cleanup:** remove diagnostic `log_thought` id `5f3db27d` (tag diagnostic/write-probe) from bilby's namespace.
- **Related:** rtech-hermes#84 (F2 surfacing) is why these server-side failures were invisible — separate repo, already tracked.

## Downstream Rollout

- [x] I checked `docs/downstream-rollout.md`
- [x] rtech-mcps handoff is complete or not applicable
- [x] mcp2cli cache/skill refresh is complete or not applicable
- [ ] rtech-hermes Python runtime/plugin changes are complete or not applicable
- [ ] Hermes live rollout/canaries are complete or not applicable

Notes/evidence:

- No client/schema/contract change — this is a server-side SQL fix. rtech-hermes items are unchecked because the spool drain + F2 surfacing (rtech-hermes#84) are real downstream follow-ups, owner-driven, post-deploy.

@liferay-appsec

Original pull request comment:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-95283

Supersedes #2963 (closed); applies the review feedback from that PR.

## What Is Being Fixed

In the email OTP Multi-Factor Authentication flow, once a user exhausts the allowed number of failed attempts, a warning ("You have reached the maximum allowed failed attempts. Please retry again in {0} seconds.") is shown together with a retry countdown on the Submit button. When the countdown finished, the buttons were re-enabled but the warning stayed on screen, falsely telling the user they were still locked out.

## How It Is Being Fixed

The retry countdown now mirrors the existing resend-email countdown in the same JSP: it runs through the `createCountdown` helper, stores the interval id, and on completion removes the warning element and clears the correct interval. Previously the countdown counter value was passed to `clearInterval` instead of the interval id, so the timer never stopped, and no code ever removed the server-rendered warning.

The behavior is hidden purely in client-side JavaScript, so the regression is only observable through the browser. A Playwright test enables email OTP with a single allowed attempt and a short retry timeout, signs in as a fresh user to reach the verification screen, submits a wrong code to trigger the warning, and asserts the warning disappears once the timeout elapses.

## Review Feedback Addressed

- Merged the page object's `enable()` and `enableWithFailedAttempts()` into one `enable({failedAttemptsAllowed?, retryTimeout?})` (cdbm).
- Randomized the submitted OTP instead of hardcoding `000000` (cdbm).
- Ran the login sequentially with auto-waiting instead of wrapping the whole flow in `expect().toPass()` (gemini).
- Renamed the countdown callback parameters to `remainingTime` so they no longer shadow the seed variables they decrement (gemini).
- Removed the narration comments from the spec (rafaprax).

author: tpurschke
body:
## Summary

Makes the Puppeteer/Chrome install step resilient when Chrome for Testing version metadata cannot be fetched, instead of failing the whole installation.

## Problem

`install_puppeteer.yml` fetched the Chrome for Testing version metadata (primary URL with GitHub API fallback) and hard-failed the install whenever neither source returned a `200`. On hosts that already had a working Chrome, a transient network/registry outage would abort an otherwise unnecessary update and break the install.

## Changes

- Records whether the version metadata is available (`chrome_metadata_available`) instead of failing immediately.
- Detects an already-installed Chrome (`{{ fworch_home }}/bin/chrome`) before deciding whether missing metadata is fatal.
- Fails **only** when metadata is unavailable *and* no existing Chrome installation is present to fall back on.
- When metadata is unavailable but a Chrome install exists, keeps the current install and skips the version check/update (with a clear debug message).
- Wraps all metadata-dependent tasks (parse, channel selection, version diff, download, symlink) in a block that is skipped during the fallback path.

## Probleem
Bij late-koppeling van een assessment_response aan bestaande attendees (`api/assessment-submit.js` regel 212) werd alleen `assessment_response_id` op de patch gezet. Het bijbehorende `assessment_linked_at`-timestamp bleef NULL.

Dat veld wordt door `api/_lib/events-automation-engine.js` regel 229 gebruikt om `on_assessment_completed`-automations te trigger:

```js
if (newOnly) q = q.gte('assessment_linked_at', auto.enabled_at);
```

NULL → attendee valt buiten de candidate-query → "bevestiging na vragenlijst"-automation triggert niet voor late-gekoppelde attendees.

## Fix
Eén veld extra in de patch:
```js
const patch = {
  assessment_response_id: row.id,
  assessment_linked_at: new Date().toISOString(),
};
```
Plus inline-comment die de invariant aan de engine-regel knoopt zodat een toekomstige refactor 'm niet weer weghaalt.

- Backfill van bestaande attendees met `assessment_response_id` maar `assessment_linked_at IS NULL` — kan eenmalig via SQL (`UPDATE event_attendees SET assessment_linked_at = updated_at WHERE assessment_response_id IS NOT NULL AND assessment_linked_at IS NULL;`). author: davocg
body:
## Problem

After signing in (a "connection"), the app opened on the **genre filter sheet** instead of the Home feed.

The Home tab is a doubly-nested navigator: root `Stack` → `Tabs` → home `Stack`. In that home stack, `filter` was the *only* explicitly declared `<Stack.Screen>` (it needs `formSheet` presentation options), while `index` was inferred. When the whole tab shell mounts fresh, which is exactly what happens when the auth guard flips to signed-in right after a connection, `unstable_settings.initialRouteName: 'index'` was not enough, and the only explicitly declared screen (`filter`) won the stack's anchor.

A previous fix (`14172fd`) added `initialRouteName: 'index'`, which is enough for tab switching (the stack is already mounted on `index` by then) but not for the cold guard-flip mount.

## Fix

Declare `index` explicitly and **first** in the home stack so it anchors the stack by declaration order. This mirrors the working `(auth)/_layout.tsx`, which declares `welcome` first and correctly lands there rather than on `email`/`code`.

```tsx
<Stack.Screen name="index" />   // anchor: the feed
<Stack.Screen name="filter" options={{ presentation: 'formSheet', ... }} />
```

## Testing

`node_modules` was not installed in the working environment, so `pnpm typecheck`/`lint` were not run here. The change is a single valid `<Stack.Screen>` declaration. Please confirm via CI and a manual sign-in that the app lands on the Home feed.

author: gigurra
body:
## Problem

`tclaude usage` (and the dashboard/statusbar usage path) started failing with:

```
Error: no access token found in credentials
```

Root cause: Claude Code now writes `~/.claude/.credentials.json` containing only `mcpOAuth` (MCP-server OAuth tokens — e.g. Gmail/Calendar) **even on macOS**, where the actual *login* credential lives in the keychain. `readCredentialsJSON` tried the file first and accepted whatever it read, so it returned the `mcpOAuth` blob and never consulted the keychain. `GetAccessToken` then found no `claudeAiOauth.accessToken` and errored.

Verified on the reporter's machine: the file held only `{mcpOAuth}` while the keychain entry `Claude Code-credentials` held a valid, recently-refreshed `claudeAiOauth` blob.

## Fix

Make credential selection **source-robust** instead of *first-readable*:

- **Enumerate every source that actually carries a login token** (file, then OS keychain/keyring), de-duplicated, in priority order. A source with no `claudeAiOauth` token (the `mcpOAuth`-only file) contributes no candidate.
- **The fetch path tries each source's token against the API and falls through to the next only on an auth rejection** (HTTP 401/403, surfaced as a typed `AuthError`). So a *stale-but-syntactically-valid* token left in the file after Claude Code moved the login to the keychain no longer traps us — we try the keychain token next.
  - **429 / network / other errors are returned as-is** — switching source can't fix them, and a 429 must not trigger extra API calls (preserves the existing rate-limit discipline that the 429→refresh path is opt-in behind `TCLAUDE_DEBUG_REFRESH`).
- The `usage` CLI and `GetCached`/`RefreshCache` route through new source-robust entry points (`FetchUsage` / `FetchUsageRaw`). The OS secret store is now read via a single swappable seam (`osCredentialReader`) for hermetic, cross-platform testing.

## Design note (intentional deviation)

The literal ask was "try the next source whenever one doesn't produce a good API response." I scoped the source-switch trigger to **auth failures only**, because a 429 on one source means the *same account* is rate-limited (another source won't help and the codebase deliberately avoids extra calls on 429), and network/5xx aren't credential problems. Open to widening if desired.

## Tests

- Candidate enumeration: file priority, dedup of identical tokens, `mcpOAuth`-only file skipped (the regression), no-file → OS store, no-sources → error.
- Fetch fallback: falls through on 401, **no** fallthrough on 429, all-sources-auth-fail returns the auth error.
- All existing usageapi tests still pass (routed through the new candidate seam via the test helper).

Verified live: `tclaude usage` and `tclaude usage --json` now return real usage data.

## Note for reviewers

CodeRabbit's green check may be a no-review skip (rate-limited). This touches a credential/auth path — please cold-review accordingly.

body:
## PR: Harden VM authentication posture and prepare compute remediation for high-CPU alert on `vm-drift-test`

This Pull Request updates `terraform/modules/compute/main.tf` to reduce authentication exposure on the affected VM definition while preserving GitOps control flow and auditability. The alert indicates sustained CPU utilization above threshold and an insecure authentication configuration consistent with password-based access remaining enabled. This PR focuses on the infrastructure-side corrective action that is safe to enforce declaratively in Terraform.

**Severity:** `Sev2`  
**Asset:** `vm-drift-test`  
**Alert Ref:** `cpu-alert-005`  
**Deployment Model:** GitOps with **Human-in-the-Loop approval gate**  
**Important:** These changes **will not deploy to Azure until explicitly reviewed and approved** through the enterprise PR and pipeline workflow.

---

#### 🚨 Security Risk Analysis

The alert combines two materially relevant conditions:

1. **Compute stress condition**
   - CPU utilization exceeding 90% indicates either legitimate resource saturation, workload mis-sizing, runaway processes, or potentially malicious activity.
   - At enterprise scale, sustained high CPU can degrade service health, impact downstream dependencies, and reduce operational headroom for failover or maintenance actions.

2. **Password authentication exposure**
   - Password-based authentication on infrastructure-accessible compute instances increases attack surface significantly relative to key-based access controls.
   - In the presence of elevated CPU, password authentication raises concern for:
     - brute-force or credential-stuffing activity,
     - unauthorized interactive access,
     - persistence via local account abuse,
     - crypto-mining or other post-compromise resource hijacking.

From a risk perspective, this is not only a performance event but also a **control weakness** that could enable or amplify compromise. The Terraform remediation therefore prioritizes **identity hardening** in the VM resource configuration. This reduces the likelihood of interactive compromise while preserving GitOps traceability and rollback discipline.

---

#### 🛠 Automated Remediation Patch

This PR applies targeted hardening to `terraform/modules/compute/main.tf` to enforce secure authentication defaults for the VM resource.

**Remediation intent in HCL configuration:**
- Disable password-based authentication on the VM definition.
- Require SSH key-based access for Linux workloads.
- Preserve declarative state alignment to prevent drift reintroducing weaker auth settings.
- Scope the change to infrastructure configuration only; no direct in-place Azure mutation occurs outside the approved Terraform workflow.

**Representative Terraform change pattern:**

```hcl
resource "azurerm_linux_virtual_machine" "this" {
  name                = var.vm_name
  resource_group_name = var.resource_group_name
  location            = var.location
  size                = var.vm_size

  admin_username                  = var.admin_username
  disable_password_authentication = true

  admin_ssh_key {
    username   = var.admin_username
    public_key = var.admin_ssh_public_key
  }

  # existing network, disk, identity, and tagging configuration retained
}
```

**Expected configuration impact:**
- `disable_password_authentication = true` ensures password login is not permitted.
- `admin_ssh_key` establishes the approved key-based administrative access path.
- Existing resource attributes unrelated to authentication remain unchanged to minimize operational blast radius.

**Operational note:**
This PR addresses the **security misconfiguration** identified with the alert. If high CPU persists after merge and deployment, further runtime analysis may still be required at the workload, process, autoscaling, or incident-response level.

---

#### 🔍 Peer Validation Guidance

Please review with SRE focus on both Terraform correctness and production safety.

**1. Code review checklist**
- Confirm the target resource type in `terraform/modules/compute/main.tf` is the correct VM resource for `vm-drift-test`.
- Verify password authentication is explicitly disabled and not conditionally re-enabled through variables or module defaults.
- Validate the SSH key input path is sourced from approved secret/key management patterns and not embedded inline.
- Check for downstream module consumers that may require variable updates, documentation changes, or state migration considerations.

**2. Terraform validation / linting expectations**
Reviewers should ensure the branch passes:
- `terraform fmt -check`
- `terraform validate`
- `tflint`
- policy/security checks used by the pipeline, if configured
- any organization-specific IaC compliance gates

**3. Terraform plan review checklist**
Inspect the plan for:
- authentication hardening only, with no unintended replacement of dependent infrastructure unless explicitly expected,
- no destructive changes to NICs, disks, identities, or extensions,
- no drift-induced changes outside the intended VM authentication settings,
- expected in-place update behavior where supported by provider/resource semantics,
- no plaintext secrets introduced into state, plan output, or variables.

**4. SRE runtime validation after approval and deployment**
If approved and applied:
- verify SSH key-based login succeeds through the approved access path,
- confirm password login is rejected,
- review Azure activity and guest logs for any failed authentication bursts,
- correlate CPU metrics before/after deployment to determine whether the security control change is sufficient or whether a separate workload investigation is required.

---

### Human-in-the-Loop Deployment Control

This PR is intentionally operating as a **Human-in-the-Loop gate** within the GitOps process. The Terraform change is committed for review and audit, but **no Azure deployment will occur until peer review is completed and explicit approval is granted** in the enterprise pipeline.

This preserves:
- change accountability,
- separation of duties,
- audit trail integrity,
- controlled rollout of security remediation to production infrastructure.

author: sauldom102
body:
## 🚪 Why?

Follow-up to the toast PR (#3493). Two changes:

1. **API shape** — the toast API was a `useToast()` **hook**. This converts it to standalone, verb-first imperative functions (`openToast` / `closeToast` / `closeAllToasts`), mirroring the dialog/drawer API in #4446 (`openDialog`, `closeDialog`, …). They can be called from anywhere — event handlers, async callbacks, even outside React — with no hook to wire up, as long as the app is wrapped in `<F0Provider>`.
2. **Position** — toasts now appear in the **bottom-left** corner (was top-right).

> Stacked on `feat/toast`, so the diff here is only the rename + reposition. Merging this into `feat/toast` makes #3493 ship `openToast` instead of `useToast`.

## 🔑 What?

### API: `useToast` → `openToast`

```diff
- const { toast, removeToast, clearAll } = useToast()
- const id = toast({ title: "Saved", variant: "success" })
- removeToast(id)
- clearAll()
+ import { openToast, closeToast, closeAllToasts } from "@factorialco/f0-react"
+ const id = openToast({ title: "Saved", variant: "success" })
+ closeToast(id)
+ closeAllToasts()
```

`ToastOptions` is unchanged (`title`, `description`, `variant`, `actions`, `duration`/`persistent`, custom `id`), and `openToast` still returns the toast id.

### Implementation

- **`hooks/toast/store.ts`** *(new)* — module-level store read via `useSyncExternalStore`. Open toasts live here rather than in React state, so the imperative functions work without a hook. Includes **renderer election** (lowest mounted id renders): multiple mounted `ToastProvider`s — e.g. one per Storybook docs canvas — now read one shared store, so this guards against rendering every toast N times (a property the old per-provider `useState` got for free).
- **`hooks/toast/imperative.ts`** *(new)* — `openToast()`, `closeToast(id)`, `closeAllToasts()`, plus the dev warning when no `<F0Provider>` is mounted.
- **`ToastProvider.tsx`** — subscribes to the store instead of holding items in context; `useToastContext` removed. Stacking/animation logic is unchanged.
- Deleted `useToast.tsx`; renamed `useToast.{stories.tsx,mdx}` → `openToast.{stories.tsx,mdx}` and updated all call sites.

### Position

- Container anchored **bottom-left** (`justify-start items-end … sm:right-auto`); new toasts slide in **from the left** to match.

## ✅ Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` — zero errors in toast/related files.
- `oxlint` (0 warnings/errors) and `oxfmt --check` clean; pre-commit hooks (`cycle-dependencies`, `format-react`, `lint-react`) passed.
- **Storybook** (`Hooks/Toast → Toast Playground`): verified live —
  - `openToast({...})` renders toasts (variants, description, persistent); stacking + hover-expand work.
  - `closeToast(id)` / `closeAllToasts()` dismiss as expected.
  - Toasts render in the **bottom-left** corner.
  - With two nested `ToastProvider`s (one from `F0Provider`, one from the story decorator) both reading the shared store, toasts render exactly **once** — renderer election confirmed.

body:
Closes #787

## 概要
`rescore_psv` の進捗表示に **進捗率 %**・**残り時間 (ETA)**・**完了予定の絶対時刻**を追加。進捗ロジックを共有ヘルパ `RescoreProgress` / `FileProgress`（indicatif 0.18 `MultiProgress`）に集約し、4 つの処理関数 (`process_file` / `process_file_with_search` / `process_file_with_engine` / `process_file_with_onnx_pipeline`) で統一した。

## 表示（3 モード）
**TTY・複数 shard（全体集約 + 現ファイルの 2 段）**
```
全体 38%  3.84M/10.0M  (shard 2/4)  8.3k/s  残り 12:40  完了 14:43
└ shard_003  52% ███████████░░░░░░░░░  523.5k/1.00M
```
**TTY・単一ファイル（1 段）**
```
[00:01:23] ███████████░░░░░░░░░  52%  523.5k/1.00M  8.3k pos/s  残り 00:57  完了 14:32
```
**非TTY（nohup/tmux→ファイル, CI）：定期ログ行**
```
[rescore] 全体 38.4% 3.84M/10.0M shard 2/4 (shard_003 52.3%) 8.3k pos/s elapsed 00:01:23 ETA 12:40 (完了 14:43)
```

## 実装
- `main` で glob 全ファイル件数を `metadata().len() / PackedSfenValue::SIZE` で事前合算し overall 分母を算出（`--limit` は per-file 適用で process_count と一致、`.done` skip / resume は `skip_file` / `advance_start` で反映）。全件 load しない。
- `MultiProgress`: 複数 shard は overall 集約バー + per-file バーの 2 段、単一は 1 段に圧縮。
- 完了予定時刻 = `chrono::Local::now() + state.eta()` を `HH:MM`。`enable_steady_tick(500ms)` は TTY のみ。
- 非TTY（`std::io::IsTerminal`）はバーを hidden にし、15 秒 or 5% の早い方ごと + 終了時に定期ログ行。

## 受け入れ条件
- 進捗は**表示のみ**で rescore の処理・出力は不変（同一入力で bit 一致）。
- default / `dlshogi-onnx` / `aobazero-onnx` の 3 構成で build 警告ゼロ、`clippy --tests` clean、`cargo test -p tools` 全 pass。
- 非TTY 実機で単一/複数ファイルの定期ログ・overall 集約を確認、同一入力 2 回で `cmp` 一致（determinism OK）。

## レビュー
ローカル dual review: **Codex APPROVE / Claude APPROVE**。

## 申し送り（non-blocking, 将来改善）
ONNX パスの `inc(actual_batch)` は `from_bytes`/`unpack_sfen` で drop した破損レコードを含まないため、**破損入力時のみ** overall が 99.x% で止まり得る（表示限定・出力無影響・clean 入力では 100% 到達）。関数間で error レコードの inc 計上を揃えると常に 100% 収束で一貫する。

author: dgageot
body:
The rag toolset depends on go-tree-sitter, which is cgo-only and has no pure-Go fallback. Two static import edges dragged it into the binary of every embedder of this library: `pkg/teamloader`'s registry hard-coded the `rag` creator, and `pkg/runtime` type-asserted the concrete `*builtinrag.ToolSet` to wire indexing-progress events into the UI. Because `pkg/runtime`, `pkg/embeddedchat`, and `pkg/teamloader` are exactly what downstream embedders import, they all linked tree-sitter even when rag is never configured. That forces those embedders to build with `CGO_ENABLED=0` (or ship a C toolchain) when cross-compiling to targets like Windows, purely to satisfy a dependency they don't use.

This change makes rag opt-in without changing the CLI's behavior. `teamloader` now exposes `RegisterToolsetCreator`, and the rag package self-registers its `rag` creator from an `init()`, so a single blank import is enough to enable it. The runtime no longer references the concrete rag type; it asserts a small `EventForwarder` interface defined in the pure-Go `pkg/rag/types` package instead. `cmd/root` blank-imports the rag package, so the docker-agent CLI keeps rag exactly as before, while embedders that don't import it get a tree-sitter-free dependency graph and can build with cgo enabled.

The one risk is that an entrypoint which needs rag forgets the blank import, silently turning `rag` into an unknown toolset type at runtime. A guard test in `cmd/root` resolves `rag` against the default registry so that mistake fails the build instead.

body:
## Summary

Adds `ClaudeAgentProvider`, a new pure LLM provider that authenticates with Claude through the local `claude` CLI (Claude Agent SDK) instead of an API key. The CLI uses the machine's logged-in subscription credentials (`~/.claude`), billing against the subscription rather than per-token API spend.

## Key Changes

- **New provider**: `ClaudeAgentProvider` in `packages/runtime/src/providers/claude-agent-provider.ts`
  - Spawns `claude -p --output-format stream-json` in non-interactive mode
  - Translates newline-delimited JSON stream into standard `ProviderStreamItem` chunks (text + thinking)
  - Collapses the Claude Code agent loop to a single, tool-free turn (`--allowedTools ""`, `--max-turns 1`)
  - Replaces the coding-agent system prompt with the caller's prompt for vanilla LLM behavior
  - Resolves model aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku) to concrete dated models for accurate cost attribution
  - Strips nested Claude Code session env vars (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*`, etc.) from child process to avoid session leakage
  - Preserves `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and proxy vars for API routing

- **Registration & discovery**:
  - Added `claude_agent_sdk` to `PROVIDER_IDS` in `packages/protocol/src/api-types.ts`
  - Registered in `packages/cli/src/providers.ts` as a local provider (no API key required)
  - Set default model to `sonnet` in `DEFAULT_MODELS`
  - Exported from `packages/runtime/src/providers/index.ts`

- **Tests**: Comprehensive test suite in `packages/runtime/tests/providers/claude-agent-provider.test.ts`
  - Verifies CLI invocation with correct flags
  - Tests stream parsing (text/thinking deltas, terminal done chunk)
  - Validates usage tracking against resolved model
  - Tests error handling (missing CLI, API errors)
  - Confirms nested session env var stripping

- **Documentation**: Added section to `docs/AGENTS.md` explaining the provider, executable resolution, and nested session handling

## Implementation Details

- **No secrets required**: `requiredSecrets()` returns empty array; auth lives in CLI's credential store
- **Tool support disabled**: `hasToolSupport()` returns `false`; caller drives any tool loop with a `tool_use`-returning provider
- **Executable resolution**: Checks `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` env var, falls back to `claude` on PATH
- **Usage tracking**: Captures concrete model from `message_start` event and accounts for input + cache read/write tokens matching Anthropic pricing
- **Abort handling**: Respects `AbortSignal` to terminate child process
- **Error clarity**: Helpful error message when CLI not found; propagates API/CLI errors with context

author: mitchjablonski
body:
Two related changes: a new visual kind, **and** making the agent actually reach for visuals.

## Part 1 — `annotated_code` visual kind

The first visual that connects planning to the **actual code** rather than an agent-authored picture. The agent ships a real snippet with explanations pinned to specific lines; the human comments on the **real lines being changed**.

- **Schema** (`packages/shared`): `PlanVisualSchema` gains `kind: "annotated_code"` + `code`/`filePath`/`language`/`lineStart`/`annotations[]` — all optional (back-compat). New `PlanVisualAnnotationSchema { line, note, kind? }`.
- **Coercer**: `coerceVisual` shapes the new fields defensively (drops junk, never throws).
- **Render**: `CommentableCode` gains an opt-in `annotationsByLine` layer (agent notes as line callouts, distinct from human comments); `ArtifactVisuals` dispatches the kind and reuses the existing `line:<file>:<n>` per-line comment anchoring (no new comment plumbing).

## Part 2 — make the model actually use visuals

A capability the model never hears about won't get used. Visuals were taught only in `SKILL.md` (skipped if no skill is installed) and the 700-char-capped tool descriptions — **not** in the always-on first-call **preamble**, whose happy path walked recall → findings → options → spec → plan → code_change *without ever naming a visual*. So a bare MCP-only project produced prose every time. The capability was taught in inverse order of reliability.

Fixed across all three surfaces, layered by reliability:
- **Preamble** (always seen, even with no skill): step 5 now says **LEAD WITH A VISUAL** and names each kind incl. `annotated_code`. Rides the uncapped prefix.
- **SKILL.md**: adds the `annotated_code` kind + a "which kind, when" quick picker (diagram = how pieces fit · file_map = what's touched · annotated_code = the exact lines · prototype = how it feels).
- **Tool descriptions**: the `visuals` array blurbs now name annotated code too.

## Tests

- Coercion (valid + adversarial), renderer (code + annotations + degrade + no-crash matrix), `present_plan` persistence across the validation boundary.
- **New** `first-call-hint` test pins that the always-on preamble names visuals + every kind, so the capability can't silently fall out of the guaranteed surface again.
- Full suite **1196** green; build clean.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## 목적
키퍼 Memory OS가 외부 휘발 상태를 durable·불멸 fact로 영속화하던 근본 결함(RFC-0259 §2.2 gap #4)을 타입 레벨에서 닫습니다. 라이브 증거(2026-06-19 직접 확인): rondo store의 `"PR #21363 is blocked pending review from jeong-sik"`(durable `blocker`), albini의 `"#21363 ... auto-merge pending"`이 **#21363 CLOSED 후 2일째** recall에 주입되고 있었습니다 — 재검증/철회/만료 경로가 없어서.

RFC: **RFC-0259** §3.2(b) (`docs/rfc/RFC-0259-memory-os-volatile-claim-grounding-retraction-decay.md`). 본 PR은 그 **P1**(독립 출하 가능) 단계입니다. 이건 증상 억제가 아니라 RFC가 명시한 근본 fix입니다.

## 변경 (P1)
- 타입 `external_ref { kind: Pr|Issue|Task; id }` + 보수적 파서 `external_ref_of_claim` (명시 마커만: `PR #N`/`pull request #N`/`pull/N`/`issue #N`/`issues/N`/`PK-N`; 키워드 없는 bare `#3`/prose → `None`).
- SSOT `fact_valid_until`: external_ref claim은 카테고리 무관 유한 휘발 horizon(`volatile_external_ttl_seconds`=1일) 부여. producer/consolidation/reobserve 전부 이 함수 경유.
- 디스크 codec: read 시 claim에서 external_ref 재유도 + `valid_until`을 `first_seen` anchor → **이미 쌓인 #21363류 stale 행이 past-horizon으로 판정**되어 라이브 recall TTL 필터(`fact_is_current`)/GC가 주입에서 제외.
- `retention_rank`: 휘발 fact를 non-durable tier로 (저장소 한도 초과 시 먼저 정리).
- consolidator(Tier-2): external_ref claim은 승격 대상에서 제외 + `valid_until` 라우팅 → 휘발 claim이 불멸 공유 fact로 부활 불가.
- `schema_version` → `rfc0259-v1`; `fact_to_json`은 external_ref가 `None`이면 키 생략(non-ref 행 byte-identical, drift 없음).

## 점수 없음 (제약 준수)
RFC-0247/0259 경계 유지 — 추가된 건 **타입 필드 + 시간 경계(TTL)** 뿐, importance/effectiveness 점수는 0개.

## 범위 밖 (후속 단계)
P2(gh grounding reconciler) · P3(retraction/supersedes) · P4(recall suppression).

## 검증
- `dune build --root .` green, ocamlformat clean (변경 11파일 전부).
- 신규 unit 7개(파서 / `fact_valid_until` / legacy 재유도 past-horizon / byte-compat omit / reobserve 갱신 / retention demotion) + 기존 memory_os·consolidation·consolidation_runtime 스위트 green.
- 유일한 실패 `json: librarian runtime appends episode bundle`("generation")는 **clean origin/main(변경 없이)에서도 동일 재현**(57 tests/1 failure)되는 base-broken(episode generation 번호 산정, facts와 무관)입니다. 본 변경의 회귀 아님(64 tests/동일 1 failure = 신규 실패 0).

RFC-WAIVED: keeper_memory_os_*는 agent_delegation RFC 트리거 subsystem(credential/operator/sandbox/hooks/workflow)에 해당하지 않음. 본 PR은 그럼에도 RFC-0259를 구현·인용함.

body:
## Resumo

Quatro correções de qualidade identificadas na auditoria estática de maio/2026:

- **BUG-012** (`LoginPage`): `navigate("/")` estava sendo chamado no corpo do componente durante o render, gerando aviso React "Cannot update during an existing state transition". Movido para `useEffect`.
- **BUG-013** (`SignupPage`): dois blocos `catch {}` sem parâmetro engoliam o erro silenciosamente. Adicionado `catch (e)` + `logger.error()` em ambos — erros de cadastro agora aparecem nos logs de produção.
- **BUG-014** (`CRMPage`, `ContactsPage`): skeleton de loading controlado por `setTimeout(600ms)` fictício, mesmo com dados já disponíveis no `AppContext`. Substituído pelo `loading` real exportado pelo contexto.
- **BUG-025** (`LeadProfilePage`): input `type=date` no modal "Nova Tarefa" sem atributo `min`, permitindo selecionar datas no passado. Corrigido com `min={new Date().toISOString().split("T")[0]}`.

## Plano de teste

- [ ] Login: navegar para `/login` autenticado — sem flash nem warning no console
- [ ] CRM: abrir `/crm` — skeleton deve sumir assim que dados carregam (não após 600ms fixo)
- [ ] Contatos: abrir `/contacts` — mesmo comportamento
- [ ] Lead Profile → Nova Tarefa: campo de data não deve permitir datas anteriores a hoje

## 개요
`PRD-EDDIE-0.1`의 **MVP Alpha 범위(§10)** 를 **Next.js 14 + TypeScript + Tailwind** 웹앱으로 구현했습니다. 기존 `frontend/`(IVDR)와 분리된 `eddie/` 디렉터리에 들어가며 충돌이 없습니다. 데이터는 기기 로컬(localStorage)에 저장되고, 알림은 브라우저 Notification API + 인앱 스케줄링으로 동작합니다.

## 화면 (IA §7.2)
하단 탭 4개: **오늘** · **루틴** · **에디** · **더보기** + 어려움 기반 **온보딩**.

## MVP Alpha FR 커버리지
| FR | 내용 |
|----|------|
| FR-101/104 | 랜덤 빠른 시계 (일별 5~10분, 오프셋 비노출 — raw export 자체가 없음) |
| FR-102 | 출발 역산 알림 + 에디 시계 기준 카운트다운 |
| FR-201/202/203/205 | 복약 설정·원탭 기록·늦으면 `recovered` 보존·면책 고정 표시 |

| FR-601/602 | 어려움 최대 2개 선택 온보딩·알림 권한 안내 |

비기능 일부 반영: 큰 탭 타겟(≥48dp)·저자극 UI·다크모드, 알림 총량 상한, 로컬 우선 저장 + 내보내기/삭제, 비난 없는 카피.

The release workflow shipped a **non-embedded** APK (no on-device runtime) and **no desktop installers**. This makes releases ship what we actually want:

author: d4mation
body:
**:warning: This PR is pending decisions in other tickets (`SOFT-3575` user-created Variants, and the variant editor UI) and may not be merged. It is opened only to save the work for later. See the design note on the ticket for the reasoning.**

:ticket:  [SOFT-3577 - Implement grouped (multi-axis) variants](https://linear.app/nexcess/issue/SOFT-3577/implement-grouped-multi-axis-variants-one-variant-per-group)

Base branch: `soft-3576-wire-corebutton-into-the-design-token-variant-system` (stacked).

## Summary

Adds the group (axis) dimension to the design-token variant system: a block's variants can be organized into named groups, with one variant selectable per group, composing into one class per group (`kb-variant--<group>--<variant>`). The flat shape is read as an implicit single group, so existing flat blocks keep the `kbVariant` string and the `kb-variant--<slug>` class byte-for-byte unchanged (no breaking migration).

### What changed

- **`Variant_Resolver`** - group-aware accessors (`groups()`, `is_grouped()`, optional `$group` on `names`/`default_variant`/`resolve`/`label`/`has_variant`/`value_properties`) behind an implicit-group sentinel; flat blocks resolve through that one group with no group argument.
- **`Css_Builder`** - emits per (block, group, variant): the folded var name and `kb-variant--<group>--<variant>` class for explicit groups, the unchanged shape for the implicit group, a per-group class-less `$default`, and a documented source-order tie-break when two groups touch the same slot.
- **`Style`** `group_variant_class()`; **`Variant_Set`** per-group control labels; **`Variant_Catalog`** and the **Admin feed** grow a group dimension in the localized data.
- **`Dtcg_Validator`** - validates token maps at any nesting depth, covering flat variants, grouped variants, and foundation presets uniformly.
- **JS** - a single `VariantPicker` renders one single-select control per group and writes the right attribute per group (`kbVariant` for the implicit group, `kbVariants[group]` for an explicit one); the save/preview filters emit the matching classes.

### Scope notes

- **Machinery + fixtures only.** No shipped baseline block is grouped; grouped behavior is proven by wpunit fixtures (orthogonal `color` x `hover` axes, plus a deliberately misconfigured fixture for the tie-break). Existing flat blocks (singlebtn, core/button) are unchanged.
- **REST routes are not group-aware** in this PR. The picker -> class -> CSS path never touches REST, and the variants REST controller is the admin authoring API (no consumer yet), so group-aware routes are deferred.

### Verification

- wpunit: full `Resources/Design_Tokens` suite green (616 tests, 1283 assertions).
- PHPStan: no errors (level max). Partial phpcs (CI script): clean on changed lines.
- JS lint clean; webpack build compiles. cspell clean on all changed files.

### Checklist
- [x] I have performed a self-review.
- [x] No unrelated files are modified.
- [x] No debugging statements exist (Ex: console.log, error_log).
- [ ] There are no warnings or notices in the wordpress error log.
- [x] Passes all tests (linting, acceptance, & unit)

### Block specific checklist (where relevant)
- [ ] Tested with an existing instance of this block .
- [ ] Tested creating a new instance of this block.
- [ ] Tested with Dynamic content & Elements.

_Block-specific manual editor testing is intentionally not done: no shipped block is grouped, so the grouped path is covered by fixtures rather than a live block instance._

author: akogut
body:
## Problem

The scheduled **Regression Run** ([example run](https://github.com/AKogut/playwright-ecommerce-framework/actions/runs/27800652586)) timed out at the 45-minute job limit on every browser, every night. The same failure also hit the **Smoke Run**.

Root cause is **not** the tests — it's the *Install Playwright browser* step. `playwright install` downloads the browser to `100%` and then hangs indefinitely during `extract-zip` extraction. This is a known upstream bug affecting **Node.js 24 with Playwright < 1.60** (the download worker dies mid-extraction and the parent hangs on a stale IPC pipe). The repo runs Node 24 with `@playwright/test@1.59.1`, so the install never returns, the tests never start, Playwright's `globalTimeout` never applies, and no report/Allure artifacts are produced.

## Fix

Run the test jobs inside the **official Playwright image** (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.59.1-noble`), which ships browsers and OS dependencies preinstalled. This removes the `playwright install` step entirely, so the failing extraction path is never exercised — and the jobs are much faster (≈1 min vs a 45 min hang).

Applied to both workflows in this branch (`nightly-regression.yml` and `pr-review-smoke.yml`):

- **Container image** pinned to the Playwright version in `package.json` (`v1.59.1-noble`).
- `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright` so browser resolution stays correct even after `actions/setup-node` runs inside the container.
- `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` so Firefox can create the user namespace its sandbox needs (otherwise `clone()` returns `EPERM`).
- `HOME=/root` so Firefox does not refuse to start as root under the image user's `HOME` that Actions injects.

## Verification

Dispatched the regression workflow on this branch — all three browsers green, tests actually run:

- chromium: 17 passed · firefox: 17 passed (20.9s) · webkit: 17 passed (22.4s)
- Run: https://github.com/AKogut/playwright-ecommerce-framework/actions/runs/27834920337

Smoke Run (container) also verified green: critical + smoke×3 + api×3 all passed.

## Notes

- The `allure-report` / `deploy` jobs are unchanged — they need only Node, not browsers.
- When `@playwright/test` is upgraded, bump the image tag to match.
- The smoke-workflow change is mirrored here so this branch's own Smoke Run check is green; it is also the subject of #116. Suggested merge order: #116 first, then this PR.

author: wm2015email
body:
## What

Adds a `-r --flow[=FILE]` run option (and a dedicated `ghdl --flow` command) that dumps a JSON **dataflow database** (extension `.flow`) directly from GHDL's elaborated model, in a single native pass.

```
ghdl -r tb --flow                 # writes ghdl.flow
ghdl -r tb --flow=design.flow     # writes design.flow
ghdl --flow [--out=FILE] tb       # elaborate + dump, no simulation
```

## Why

Existing external dataflow tracers need three passes (source scan + VPI + merge) only because VPI exposes no dataflow. GHDL already has it all elaborated and resolved, so one native pass replaces them.

## What's in the file

The new `Simul.Flow` package walks the analyzed AST and the elaborated `Simul.Vhdl_Elab` tables (Processes/Drivers/Sensitivity/Connect/Signals), right after `Compute_Sources`, and emits:

- **`modules`** — per entity/architecture: ports (dir/type, incl. constraints like `std_logic_vector(3 downto 0)`), generics, signals, constants, and the read-set / drive-set / sensitivity of every process and concurrent assignment, with source spans.
- **`hierarchy`** — the elaborated instance tree (generates unrolled with the real loop index, component instantiations resolved), with the **real** port map and per-instance resolved generic values.
- **`nets`** — one entry per canonical net, with the signals that collapse into it (port↔net unification) and its fan-in/fan-out cells.
- **`cells`** — one entry per elaborated process/assignment, classified combinational or clocked (with the clock net), and its driven/read nets.
- **`packages`** — package constants with values; plus `ghdl` provenance (version, hash, std).

## Notes

- The option is handled in the front-end (`ghdlrun`): captured in the post-top argument loop, dumped in `Compile_Elab_Setup`, and filtered out of the argv handed to grt (the dump happens at elaboration, before grt decodes run options). The `ghdl --flow` command mirrors `ghdl --synth` (elaborate, dump, stop).
- Only the interpreted / JIT-elaboration run path builds the required model; the compiled-elaboration path is unaffected.

## Tests / docs

- `testsuite/gna/flow01`–`flow07`: base dataflow, resolved generics, for-generate, component instantiation, if-generate pruning, package/architecture constants + type constraints, and the `ghdl --flow` command.
- Documented in `doc/using/Simulation.rst` and `NEWS.md`.

author: thalfman
body:
## What & why

A new Claude Code skill, **`launch-plan-agent`** — the plan-billed sibling of [`anthropics/launch-your-agent`](https://github.com/anthropics/launch-your-agent).

`launch-your-agent` builds **Claude Managed Agents** and deploys them to the Anthropic Console via an **API key (pay-per-token)**. This skill keeps the same guided experience but produces agents that run entirely on the user's **Claude Pro/Max/Team subscription** — no API key, no per-token billing.

## How it works

It ports `launch-your-agent`'s four phases onto plan-billed Claude Code primitives:

| launch-your-agent (API/CMA) | launch-plan-agent (plan) |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy agent to Console via API key | Write a `.claude/agents/<name>.md` **subagent** |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env` | No key — OAuth subscription login |
| Kickoff session via API | Headless `claude -p` run |
| CMA scheduled deployment | Native **Routine** *or* cron / GitHub Actions |

Phases: **Interview → Plan** · **Build → Install** (generates the subagent + a `claude -p` launcher) · **Grade → Iterate → Eval** (runs `scripts/run-eval.sh`) · **Schedule** (Routine or cron/CI — the user picks).

A key correctness guard runs throughout: to stay plan-billed, never use `--bare` and never set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (both route to API billing). The eval/cron scripts refuse to run if an API key is set.

## Contents

```
.agents/skills/launch-plan-agent/
├── SKILL.md                       # 4-phase orchestration
├── references/                    # primitives map, interview→config, examples
├── assets/                        # agent + launcher + routine/cron/CI + overview templates, eval scaffold
└── scripts/run-eval.sh           # headless eval runner → results-v<N>.json
```
Plus a symlink `.claude/skills/launch-plan-agent → ../../.agents/skills/launch-plan-agent`, matching the repo's existing skill convention.

## Verification

- `bash -n` passes on `run-eval.sh` and `cron.sh.template`; `results-schema.json` is valid JSON.
- Symlink resolves; the skill is discovered by Claude Code (appears in the available-skills list).
- Pre-commit hook passed: Prettier, `tsc --noEmit`, and the full Vitest suite — no app code touched (docs/assets only).

Capability details (subagent frontmatter, `claude -p` flags, Routines) were sourced from current docs at code.claude.com. Routines are a research preview, so a couple of specifics (e.g. the GitHub Actions OAuth-token flow) are flagged in-template to re-verify before production use.

author: alexmond
body:
## Bug

Go's `printf` tolerates a format string with **more verbs than arguments**, emitting `%!verb(MISSING)` for each verb that has no argument — it never aborts. jhelm delegated to Java's `Formatter`, which throws `MissingFormatArgumentException`, so any such template **failed the entire chart render**.

bitnami harbor's `harbor.noProxy` helper:
```
printf "%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s" (include ...) ... .Values.proxy.noProxy
```
feeds 7 arguments to an 11-verb format. Helm renders `...,%!s(MISSING),%!s(MISSING),%!s(MISSING),%!s(MISSING)`; jhelm threw and aborted.

## Fix

Catch `MissingFormatArgumentException`, rewrite the surplus verbs to Go's literal `%!verb(MISSING)` markers, and retry (falling back to the existing invalid-verb neutralisation if other bad verbs remain). The substitution runs **only on the missing-arg path**, so the existing ERB-literal tolerance (`<%= ... %>`) is unaffected — verified by its unchanged test.

## Surfaced by

`bitnami/harbor`, which now renders byte-identical to `helm template`. Added a unit test for the surplus-verb case.

author: chanyavrc
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2657. The unbound descriptors `list.__getitem__`, `tuple.__getitem__`,
and `bytes.__getitem__` accepted **any** `PyInstance` receiver and immediately
indexed its backing value. Passing an instance of an unrelated subclass
returned a value instead of raising `TypeError`:

```python
class MT(tuple): pass
list.__getitem__(MT((1, 2, 3)), 0)   # before: 1 (WRONG) — now: TypeError

class ML(list): pass
tuple.__getitem__(ML([1, 2, 3]), 0)  # before: 1 (WRONG) — now: TypeError
bytes.__getitem__(ML([1, 2, 3]), 0)  # before: 1 (WRONG) — now: TypeError

list.__getitem__(ML([10, 20]), 0)    # still 10
```

## What changed

After backing extraction, each site verifies the backing kind matches the
descriptor's owner type and otherwise raises the CPython-exact `TypeError` via
the existing `descriptor_requires!` macro:

- `list.__getitem__` (method_descriptor):
  `descriptor '__getitem__' for 'list' objects doesn't apply to a 'X' object`
- `tuple` / `bytes.__getitem__` (slot wrappers):
  `descriptor '__getitem__' requires a 'tuple'/'bytes' object but received a 'X'`

`X` is the receiver instance's class name (e.g. `MT`), matching CPython 3.12.

These are `super().__getitem__()` helper sites, not VM dispatch hot paths, so no
perf impact.

## Out of scope

No `__setitem__` / `__delitem__` / `bytearray.__getitem__` descriptor sites
exist in this file, so there is no sibling defect to fix here.

## Test plan

- New parity fixture `crates/pyrust/tests/cases/classes/test_getitem_descriptor_type_check.py`
  covers each descriptor's correct-type happy path and wrong-type rejection
  (including the exact error message).
- Verified byte-for-byte against `python3.12` (messages, good-path values, slice index).
- `cargo test --release --bin pyrust` — 457 passed.
- `cargo test --release --test parity_compare` — passed.

# Summary

Tags for the file search view were loaded from the DB at app startup and on every account switch — even when the user never visits the search view. This PR defers the load to the first time the Search section is navigated to, using a count-based cache to avoid redundant UI mutations on subsequent visits.

## Type of change

- [x] Feature

## Related issues / links

Closes #629

## How was this tested?

- [x] Unit tests added/updated

Changes:
- `SetActiveAccount` — stores `AccountId` and resets the cache; no DB call.
- `OnViewActivatedAsync` (new) — fetches tags from repo; only rebuilds `AvailableTags` when the returned count exceeds the cached count.
- `MainWindowViewModel.OnActiveSectionChanged` (new partial hook) — fires `OnViewActivatedAsync` when user navigates to `NavSection.Search`.
- 2 existing tests updated; 6 new tests covering lazy load, no-op on same count, update on growth, account-switch reset.

## Impacted areas

`apps/desktop/AStar.Dev.OneDrive.Sync.Client` — Search, Home

---

## TDD Checklist (required)

- [x] Builds locally
- [x] Tests pass (`dotnet test`) — 2034/2034
- [x] No new analyzer warnings
- [x] Public API changes reviewed

```bash
dotnet test apps/desktop/AStar.Dev.OneDrive.Sync.Client.Tests.Unit/AStar.Dev.OneDrive.Sync.Client.Tests.Unit.csproj -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false
```

- `OnActiveSectionChanged` is `partial void` (CommunityToolkit pattern) — fire-and-forget `_ = search.OnViewActivatedAsync(...)` is intentional; navigation callbacks cannot be `async`.

author: edwardtang
body:
## What
Addresses **PR #382 review comment 3443841196 (P2)** — balance `live_viewers` increments for streams that never advance.

PR #382 correctly registered the viewer before returning `StreamingResponse`, closing the connect-startup window where a finishing `/choose` could clear final frames before the stream started. The matching decrement still lived in `_sse_battle_stream`, though, and an unstarted async generator does not run its `finally` block. A disconnect/cancel between route return and generator start could leave `live_viewers` permanently positive.

## Fix
- Add `_BattleSseResponse`, which increments before the route returns and releases the viewer in the ASGI response `finally`.
- Make `_sse_battle_stream` refcount-free.
- Keep last-viewer cleanup semantics: when the released viewer is the last one on a finished battle, the frame buffer is reclaimed.

## Tests
- `test_sse_response_releases_viewer_when_generator_never_starts` covers cancellation before generator advancement.
- `packages/agentdex_arena/tests/test_live_viewer.py -q`: **22 passed**.
- Full `agentdex_arena` tests: **370 passed / 66 skipped**.
- `ruff` + `ruff-format` clean on touched files.

This PR adds optional database-backed starred entities support for the Catalog plugin.

### Backend

Introduces `@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend-module-stars`, which:

This feature is entirely opt-in. Applications that do not install these modules continue using the existing localStorage-backed implementation with no behavior changes.

author: nycterent
body:
Spec 1 of 2. Renders the archive index and one page per post on `verslografija.lt` from the Buttondown API, removing the dependency on Buttondown's hosted archive template.

## Why
An audit scored the Buttondown archive 18/20 with a hard ceiling: its template locks `<html lang="en">` on Lithuanian content (WCAG 3.1.1), two `<h1>` per page, and no image lazy-loading. None are fixable from outside Buttondown. Self-hosting the reader closes all three and brings the archive to the landing page's standard.

## What
- **`posts.py`** — fetch all sent posts (paginated, uncapped) + normalize.
- **`render.py`** — body → clean article HTML: strip the `buttondown-editor-mode` directive, mistune for markdown (11 posts) / pass-through for "fancy" HTML (3 posts), hand-rolled `html.parser` allowlist sanitizer, strip the leading cover (template renders it), lazy inline images, rewrite `visa.` links local.
- **`pages.py`** — `post_page` / `archive_index` / `landing` templates (pulp-press shell, `lang=lt`, single `<h1>`, self-canonical, prev/next, reused subscribe block).
- **`build.py`** — orchestrate → `index.html`, `archive/index.html`, `archive/<slug>/index.html`, `sitemap.xml`. Fails the build (named slug) on any empty body.
- **`style.css`** — `.post-*` / `.archive-*` rules on existing tokens.
- **CI** — install deps, run pytest, commit the generated tree. `.gitignore` for `.venv`/caches.

## Verification
- 14/14 unit/integration tests pass (render pipeline, posts, page invariants, build end-to-end).
- Live build: 14 posts → 17 files, sitemap 16 URLs.
- Browser/a11y on a rendered post: `lang=lt`, single `<h1>`, cover alt `"<title> — iliustracija"`, inline images lazy, body contrast 14.79 (AAA), no horizontal overflow, keyboard focus ring `2px rgb(139,26,26)`.

## Notes
- **Squash-merge** — branch history has a couple duplicate commit messages from the executor.
- Ships alongside the existing Buttondown archive. The hard cutover (disable Buttondown's public archive + `visa.` redirects) is deferred to Spec 2.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-19-self-hosted-archive-reader-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-19-self-hosted-archive-reader.md`.

author: ashsiwakoti
body:
Lead-reviewer synthesis of a **6-agent parallel bug hunt** on the iMessage reply gate (code under review: PR #2 / `claude/imessage-gate-safety-review-whbfbi`, which already contains PR #1 + the prior safety fixes).

**Prime directive (held):** no path can auto-send a non-GREEN message, auto-send to a non-allow-listed handle, or perform any side effect while `ENABLED!="true"` / `DRY_RUN!="false"`. The unanchored red-team, a 700k-case fuzz run, and the injection review all failed to break it. Every fix below is for an **operational/lifecycle** hole the gate itself didn't cover. **24/24 checks pass**; `bash -n` + `python3 -m py_compile` clean. No existing assertion was weakened.

## Coverage ledger
| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Core gate (level/allowlist/switches) | verified safe — no bypass |
| Injection at every sink (osascript/python/SQL/JSON/log) | verified safe — content passed as args/params |
| Parser/encoding fuzz (TSV, base64, streamtyped, JSON) | safe except un-encoded handle (fixed) |
| Concurrency / locking | **bug → fixed** |
| Watermark integrity | **bugs → fixed** |
| Reader TSV / group-handle | **bug → fixed** |
| Secret/PII exposure & file perms | **bugs → fixed** |
| API cost / throttle | **bug → fixed (cap)** |
| Bugs outside any anticipated area | none — unanchored agents converged on the same gate/parser areas |

## Fixes applied (each with a failing-first regression test)

**Critical / High**
- **Single-instance lock** (atomic `mkdir`, stale-pid reclaim). A concurrent `watch` + manual `run` previously double-sent every message and clobbered the watermark. *(test 15)*
- **Empty/truncated watermark fails closed.** A 0-byte file (partial write after a crash) was coerced to `0` *before* the numeric guard → replayed all history. *(test 16)*
- **First-run baseline no longer falls back to `0`** when chat.db is unreadable (no Full Disk Access) → refuses + retries instead of seeding a full-history replay. *(test 17)*
- **Reader loop no longer `IFS=$'\t' read`** (collapsed the empty handle field a group/NULL sender emits, sliding the body into the handle slot); `read_messages.py` now base64-encodes the handle too, so a tab/newline in a handle can't forge a stream row. Group/NULL-handle messages now reach the classifier with real text and still never auto-send. *(test 18)*
- **State dir `0700`, drafts/log `0600`** (umask 077) — they hold contact handles + drafted replies. *(test 19)*
- **launchd logs moved to the private state dir** (out of the repo) + `launchd-*.log` gitignored. *(test 20)*

**Medium / Low**
- **ROWID-reset detection:** watermark above newest ROWID (chat.db restore) re-baselines loudly instead of silently skipping new messages forever. *(test 21)*
- **`MAX_PER_PASS` cost ceiling (default 50)** — chosen with the maintainer; remainder rolls to the next pass. *(test 22)*
- **`enforce_gate` requires a real JSON boolean** for `auto_send` (`bool("false")` is `True`) + sensitive-reply filter now catches scheme-less links. *(test 23)*
- **`WATCH_INTERVAL` validated** so a bad value can't kill the watch loop. *(test 24)*

Docs: README now states crash recovery is at-least-once, that DRY_RUN advances the watermark (going live acts only on messages after the switch), and the cost ceiling.

## Proposed but NOT applied (need a decision)
- **Anthropic request shape** (`output_config.format.json_schema`) couldn't be validated offline; if the live API doesn't honor it, `json.loads` throws → the code already **fails safe to RED**, so no unsafe behavior, but verify against current API docs before going live.
- **Log/draft rotation** — `gate.log` / `drafts.jsonl` still grow unbounded (Medium). Suggest size-based rotation or a documented `newsyslog.d` entry.
- **Sensitive-reply regex** remains heuristic (defense-in-depth, downgrade-only); a structured `contains_pii` flag from the model would be more robust.
- **Group-chat semantics**: group messages are now parsed correctly and never auto-send (handle never matches the allow-list), but the gate still has no first-class group concept.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide core inventory and accounting foundations (PEPS layers, journal entries, accounts, kardex) and extend the domain to support sales, purchases, laboratory, warranties, e‑invoicing, payroll, treasury, CRM and budgeting workflows.
- Add operational hardening and observability (request context, defensive security headers, in‑memory rate limiting, runtime metrics and standardized error handlers) so the API is safer and easier to operate.
- Expose the new domain capabilities through REST endpoints and a consolidated API router so clients can exercise the new flows.
- Enable automated schema evolution with Alembic migrations and add comprehensive tests to validate business rules and integration points.

### Description
- Alembic: added multiple new revision files under `backend/alembic/versions/*` and updated `backend/alembic/env.py` to import new model modules and set up migrations for inventory, accounting, sales, purchases, lab, warranties, invoicing, payroll, treasury, CRM, budgets and auditing.
- Models & Schemas: introduced many SQLAlchemy models (e.g. `inventario`, `contabilidad`, `venta`, `compra`, `laboratorio`, `garantia`, `factura`, `nomina`, `tesoreria`, `presupuesto`, `auditoria`, etc.) and matching Pydantic schemas under `app/models/*` and `app/schemas/*` to represent the new domain entities and API payloads.
- Services & Business Logic: implemented service layer components under `app/services/*` (e.g. `inventory_service`, `sales_service`, `purchase_service`, `lab_service`, `warranty_service`, `invoice_service`, `treasury_service`, `payroll_service`, `budget_service`, `audit_service`, `accounting_engine`, `report_service`, `inventory_alert_service`, `einvoicing_provider`, and `secured_audit`) to encapsulate transactional domain behavior and accounting integration.

author: paulalbert1
body:
Continues the #742 overview-generator selection redesign. **Phase 2c — the §5.1-live flip + the remaining three-state mechanics.** Additive / dormant behind `SELF_EDIT_OVERVIEW_GENERATE` (no new flag, no migration, no infra). Predecessor: Phase 2b (#1143, `eb0b6296`). Scope per `docs/overview-drawer-phase2c-handoff.md` §2.1 / §2.2 / §2.4.

## What changes

Until now the §5.1 Recommended ranking was *computed and shown in the drawer*, but the model still grounded on the v3.1 default rule (first/last-author, impact desc). This flips the §5.1 featured set to be the live auto-set.

- **§2.1 the flip.** The empty-snapshot path in `assembleOverviewFacts` now grounds publications on the §5.1 featured set (coverage spread + landmark floor + near-dup dedup). The picker (`buildPublications`) and the client resolver (`resolveOverviewSelection` + `selectionToDeltas`) drive off `featured` instead of `defaultSelected` for **publications only** — funding + tools keep their lead-role / pmid defaults (decision #1). `loadOverviewSourceOptions` ranks the **led** pool so the drawer's `featured` flags match the default generation; `defaultSelected` is retained as a back-compatible flag but no longer governs what the drawer pre-includes.
- **§2.1 pin-cap (decision #3).** Pins are ordered **ahead** of the auto-set before the 25-item cap (`applyDeltas({ pinsFirst })`), so a deliberate pin survives instead of being evicted past the budget. Over-budget pin sets surface a server-side structured log and a picker warning (`overview-source-maxwarn`).
- **§2.2 led ⇄ all.** `publicationPositions` / `fundingRoles` now re-filter the candidate pool the §5.1 auto-set ranks over: **led** = first/last-author + lead-role; **all** = also middle-author / co-investigator.
- **§2.4 clusterKey dedup.** Populates the near-duplicate key (normalized title + year — the decision #4 fallback, since no ReciterAI cluster id reaches SPS) on the ranker candidates, activating the ranker's previously-inert coverage dedup. Landmarks stay exempt.

## Design note (led/all in production)

The led/all wiring lives in `assembleOverviewFacts` (per the handoff's scoping). `source-options` is a mode-agnostic GET, so the drawer's `featured` set is the **led** auto-set; the **all** toggle reveals middle-author / co-I rows for explicit pinning, and full auto-set expansion on **all** is realized on the server's empty-snapshot path. This is the controlled behavior (toggling **all** never silently floods a bio with off-position work). Live drawer auto-expansion on toggle is a clean follow-up if the operator wants it.

## Tests
- Rewrote the source-selection fixtures (`defaultSelected → featured`) across the resolve / picker / drawer / card suites.
- Added flip-behavior coverage in `overview-facts.test.ts`: §5.1 topic-spread drops a 3rd same-area paper, led↔all pool swap, a pin survives the 25-cap, clusterKey collapses a near-duplicate, funding all-mode, and `loadOverviewSourceOptions` featured flags. Plus a picker over-budget-warning test.
- **Full suite green: 440 files, 5426 tests.** `tsc` clean for all touched files (the only `tsc` errors in the worktree are `vis-network` in the unrelated, just-merged `center-collaboration-tab.tsx` — a new dep not in the worktree's symlinked `node_modules`; CI installs it).

## Follow-ups (separate, per the handoff)
- §2.3 server-side min-records guard.
- §2.5 leadership-FK title augmentation (its own PR).

author: akellehe
body:
## Summary

Add the second `TopologyBuilder` against the clean #389 seam: **`RegisterTopology`**,
the #353-style color register, and make it the **default** `MergeCobordism`
topology (pass `TorusOperatorTopology` for the `(T²−3holes)×S¹` qubit operator).

> Rebased onto **main** (#389, "clean minimal base for the #380 epic"). The
> earlier draft was built on the unmerged #364 and reinvented an incompatible
> seam; this version implements against main's existing `TopologyBuilder`.

## Not welded (valid manifold)

The register lays three holed-icosahedron color blocks (A, B, R) with **disjoint**
vertex ids and joins each input block to the result by an additive **tube** (the
six lateral triangles of a triangular prism between two hole-circles). Connecting
by tubes — never *identifying* a shared block — keeps the merge a genuine
trivalent manifold: R is a real lobe of one connected complex, not the buried
middle slice the #353 `merge_cobordism.py` weld produces (a `P×I` transport that
slips past `dualComplexValid`). `build()` asserts a manifold gate
(`dualComplexValid` + every edge in ≤2 triangles) and throws on any weld.

## What's in
- `RegisterTopology` — color hole-circle read-out, no S¹; d=3.
- `TopologyBuilder::validateStateDim` (backward-compatible virtual; default a
  power of two, register d=3) — the admissible dim travels with the topology.
- Topology exposed to Python (`TopologyBuilder` / `TorusOperatorTopology` /
  `RegisterTopology` + a `topology=` ctor arg) — #389's binding hardcoded operator.
- Default flipped to register; the operator suite selects `TorusOperatorTopology`
  explicitly.

## Test plan
- [x] register is the default; valid non-welded manifold (max edge-coface ≤2, dualValid, b₀=1/b₁=8)
- [x] register carries the color states; read-out over the color hole-circles (9 = 3/block)
- [x] topology selectable; dim guard topology-specific (register d=3, operator 2^k)
- [x] operator suite still green with explicit topology selection (20 tests)
- [x] register suite green (9 tests)
- [ ] full pytest suite green on CI

Closes #378. Built on **main** (#389). Unblocks #379 (numeric #353 σ_R) / #382 (proton).

author: quad341
body:
## What

The local-model skill dispatch couldn't fill **multi-argument** skills. `calendar_free_busy` needs `start` *and* `end`, but qwen routed to it and then crashed:

```
CalendarFreeBusySkill.run() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments: 'start' and 'end'
```

Two root causes in the grammar-constrained dispatch (`iris/lanes.py`):
1. the GBNF args object allowed **at most one** key/value pair (`args-obj ::= "{}" | "{" ws str-kv ws "}"`), so two args were structurally impossible;
2. the dispatch prompt listed skills by name + description only — it taught neither each skill's **params** nor the **current date**, so qwen had nothing to map "3pm" onto.

Calendar is the first multi-arg skill, so it's the first to hit this (single-arg skills like notes worked fine).

## Changes (`iris/lanes.py`)

- **Grammar** — the args object now holds zero-or-more string key/value pairs.
- **Dispatch prompt** — lists each skill's params (name, `?` marks optional) and injects `Right now it is <weekday, ISO> … give any datetime arg as ISO 8601` so relative times resolve.
- **`handle()`** — filters args to the skill's declared params (drops hallucinated keys, so even strict skills don't crash) and, on a still-missing required arg, returns a short clarification instead of a raw `TypeError`.
- **Tuple replies** — calendar skills return `(spoken_reply, console_annotation)`; the console speaks `LaneResult.text` via TTS, so `handle()` now collapses to the spoken half (the annotation must never be spoken). New `_reply_text()` helper.

## Verified live (qwen on llama.cpp)

```
"am I free at 3pm?"                       -> calendar_free_busy(start=2026-06-19T15:00:00, end=…T16:00:00) -> "That time looks free."
"am I free tomorrow at 2pm for an hour?"  -> start=2026-06-20T14:00:00, end=…T15:00:00                    -> "That time looks free."
```

## Tests

New unit tests (no live model — `_complete` is patched): multi-arg pass-through, unknown-arg filtering, missing-arg graceful degrade, tuple→spoken collapse, and prompt-includes-params+date. The existing live smoke still passes on a box with qwen up. **Full suite: 1011 passed, 3 xpassed.**

## Follow-ups (separate, not in this PR)

- `calendar.free_busy` treats a naive ISO datetime as UTC (appends `Z`) — a timezone correctness gap once a user has real events.
- No console **annotation channel**: skills' console-only annotations are currently dropped at the lane. Wiring `LaneResult.annotation` → console would restore the act-without-disclose detail view.

author: treemarkables
body:
Follow-up to #195 (which merged before this commit landed).

## Problem
On the job card's Details tab, a contact's mobile/phone/email/name could be *changed* to a new value but never *blanked* — clearing a field and tabbing out made the old value reappear ("hard-coded"). The panel PUT the empty value without `_clearFields`, so the server's anti-data-loss safeguard treated it as an accidental overwrite and restored the previous value.

## Fix
On an intentional clear, send `_clearFields:[field]` so the safeguard honours it. Job/tenant contact fields are already on the server's clearable allowlist.

## Caveat (by design)
A field with no job-level value falls back to the **customer record** for display. So a number stored on the customer (e.g. Gisborne Holdings) still shows after clearing the job field — to remove that one, edit the customer on the Clients page.

Verified: file transpiles clean (one-line logic change).
