body:
## What changed

Updated `docs/email-sequencer.md` in two places:

1. Corrected the `Minimum time between sends` schedule-settings bullet to use the actual UI label `Min time between emails (min)` and the correct range (3–30 minutes, not 5–30), plus added a note that this field only appears under Custom schedule.
2. Added a new FAQ entry — **"Why is the expected campaign completion time so long?"** — explaining the `Expected time to complete campaign` metric, the math behind the daily send rate cap, and how to reduce campaign duration.

**Stacking note:** This PR targets `docsbot/doc-651-intercom-tag-0619-db5d1b7c` (PR #978's head branch) as its base. `docs/email-sequencer.md` has the same SHA on that branch as on `main` — PR #978 does not modify this file, so there is no content conflict.

## Why

Customer Anishka Agarwal (Intercom conversation #215474742305935) launched a campaign with 1,163 leads, saw "0 in progress," and the expected completion time showed 475 days. The root cause was the `Min time between emails` setting at 20 minutes, which — with an 08:00 AM–07:00 PM window — capped sending to ~33 emails/day per sender account. The human support agent (Atharv Kulkarni) identified the fix and sent a screenshot of the Schedule settings panel. The doc had two gaps: (a) it listed the wrong field name (`Minimum time between sends` vs. actual `Min time between emails (min)`) and the wrong range (5–30 vs. 3–30), and (b) there was no FAQ explaining how the minimum-time setting translates to a daily send rate or what the "Expected time to complete campaign" metric means.

## Source link(s)

- Intercom conversation: https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/w28k1kwz/inbox/inbox/conversation/215474742305935
- Screenshot in Intercom conversation part #48 (support agent Atharv Kulkarni's screenshot) shows the Schedule settings panel with the 20-minute minimum, "Expected time to complete campaign: 475 days," and the UI info box "At most 33 emails will be sent per day per sender account"
- Verifier (code): `clay-base/apps/frontend/src/components/Campaigns/ScheduleSection.tsx:264` — `label="Min time between emails (min)"`, range `min=3 max=30`
- Verifier (math): `clay-base/apps/frontend/src/components/Campaigns/estimateCampaignCompletionDays.ts:81` — formula `Math.floor((workingMinutes - 1) / effectiveMinTimeBetweenSteps) + 1` confirms 33 emails/day for 660-min window at 20-min minimum
- Stacked on: PR #978 (https://github.com/clay-run/public-docs/pull/978)

## Uncertainties

The code label is `"Min time between emails (min)"` but the customer screenshot (sent by the Clay support agent from their browser) shows `"Minimum time between emails per sender account (minutes)"`. The discrepancy likely means the screenshot was taken from a slightly older build or a staging environment. Code is the source of truth per policy, so the doc uses the code label. No plan-tier gate was found on this feature; it is available to all users under Custom schedule.

## Related observations

The verifier noted that timezone, days of week, start/end time, and campaign start date fields are also conditional on schedule type (non-ASAP or custom respectively), but updating those other bullets is out of scope for this trigger.

Closes DOC-652

author: vedarthamsaaket
body:
## Summary

Replaces the curated `EXCLUSION_VOCAB` + `SYNONYMS` dictionaries with a fully **dynamic** exclusion engine. Whatever the user types in the "Genres or music types to exclude" textbox is honoured verbatim — there is no curated whitelist of recognised genres anymore. Translation from a typed phrase ("rap", "Hindi music", "k-pop") to the tracks that actually belong to that space happens at playlist-generation time using **three live signals**, none of which depend on a hardcoded vocabulary on our side.

## The three dynamic signals

1. **Spotify artist genre tags** — for every candidate track we batch-fetch the artist's `genres` array via `/v1/artists?ids=` and drop the track if any tag contains any user keyword as a substring. This **is** the translation layer:
   - User types `rap` → Travis Scott is dropped because Spotify tags him `("rap", "hip hop", "trap")`.
   - User types `Hindi music` → Arijit Singh is dropped because his tags include `"hindi indie pop"` and `"modern bollywood"`.
   - User types `vaporwave` → made-up sub-genres work too because Spotify already uses them as tags.
2. **Query-bank content scan** — at search-query build time we scan every bank's key plus each query string in its value list, and skip the whole bank if any user keyword appears. So `rap` dynamically suppresses the hip-hop bank (its queries contain `"rap"`), without us hardcoding any `rap → hip-hop` mapping.
3. **Track metadata text** — title / artist / album word-bounded substring match, as a cheap pre-fetch pass. Catches anything that names the disliked term in its own metadata.

## What changed

### `backend/exclusions.py` — full rewrite (~295 LOC removed, ~330 added)

- **Deleted**: `EXCLUSION_VOCAB` (37 hardcoded entries), `SYNONYMS` (~45 entries), `_canonicalise`, canonical-token plumbing.
- **Kept / reworked**:
  - `_atomise(phrase)` filler-word stripper, now also drops negators (`no`, `not`, `without`, `except`, `but`, `skip`, `avoid`, `minus`) so a leaked mood-text negation doesn't taint atoms (`"no country music"` → `"country"`).
  - `parse_dislikes_from_text(mood_text)` — still lifts dislikes from `"I hate X"` / `"no X"` / `"anything but X"` phrasings.
  - `Exclusions` class with **three match methods**: `text_matches`, `matches_any_genre_tag`, `matches_query_text`.
- `bool(excl)` is now true whenever any keyword is present (no curated token gate).

### `backend/mood_engine.py` — `build_search_queries`

- Param renamed `excluded_genre_keys: set` → `exclusions: Optional[Exclusions]`.
- Every prospective query (language × genre cross, Indian-film bank, genre bank, mood bank) is gated through `_ok(q)` which calls `exclusions.matches_query_text(q)`.
- User-selected genre keys that overlap a typed dislike are dropped via the same predicate.

### `backend/spotify.py`

- `normalise_track` now stashes `artistId` so the batched artist-genre call can run at the end of a bucket without re-walking the raw payload.
- New `fetch_artist_genres_batch(token, artist_ids) → {id: (tags, …)}`. Chunks at 50 ids per call. Process-lifetime cache so repeat artists across queries / buckets / playlists are free. Failures cache empty so a transient 5xx doesn't busy-loop.
- New `_filter_by_artist_genres(tracks, token, exclusions)` — single batched call over the bucket's full candidate pool, drops tracks whose primary-artist tags substring-match a user keyword. Logs the drop count.
- `get_recommendations_for_bucket`:
  - Passes the full `Exclusions` object to `build_search_queries`.
  - Over-fetches `track_count * 3` (vs `* 2` without exclusions) so the artist-genre drop step still leaves enough tracks to hit the target.
  - Runs `_filter_by_artist_genres` on movie-album results AND on the main candidate pool before slicing to `track_count`.

## Audit vs. spec

| User requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Don't hardcode exclusion logic | ✅ `EXCLUSION_VOCAB` and `SYNONYMS` deleted. Only filler-word stoplist remains, and that's not a vocabulary — it's punctuation. |
| Once user types a genre / music type, strictly excluded | ✅ Three independent filters; misses are documented (see Limitations). |
| Logic must be dynamic | ✅ Translation happens via live Spotify artist-genre fetch at generation time. Bank skip is a content scan, not a key lookup. |
| Translate excluded genre properly during playlist creation | ✅ Spotify's own tagging is the translation table. |

## Test plan

- [ ] Generator: type `Mainstream music, Hindi music, minimalist stuff` in the dislikes textbox → resulting playlist has no Bollywood / Arijit Singh / Pritam / Sachet–Parampara tracks, no albums or songs named with "minimalist" / "bollywood" / "mainstream"
- [ ] Generator: type `rap` only → no Travis Scott, Drake, Kendrick, etc. (all tagged with `"rap"` or `"hip hop"`)
- [ ] Generator: type `kpop` only → no BTS, Blackpink, etc. (tagged `"k-pop"`)
- [ ] Generator: type a made-up sub-genre like `vaporwave` or `phonk` → those tagged artists drop (proves no hardcoded vocabulary is needed)
- [ ] Mood box only: `"chill night drive but I hate edm and no country music"` (empty dislikes textbox) → still drops EDM + country
- [ ] Empty dislikes → behaves exactly as before, no extra API calls beyond the existing flow (`_filter_by_artist_genres` early-returns)
- [ ] Backend logs show `[DISLIKE] active keywords=…` and `[DISLIKE] artist-genre filter dropped N track(s)`
- [ ] Playlist size still hits the requested range (the `track_count * 3` headroom should absorb the drops)

## Limitations (documented, out of scope)

`"Mainstream music"` alone won't drop a Miley Cyrus `"pop"`-tagged track because the literal substring `"mainstream"` doesn't appear anywhere in her metadata or her Spotify genre tags. Catching that class of match would need Spotify popularity-score data (tracks > 70 ≈ mainstream), which would be a separate change.

author: jonathanchang31
body:
## Summary

Adds a `## Relationship to Subnet Registration` section to the Subnet article. The official [Create a Subnet](https://docs.learnbittensor.org/subnets/create-a-subnet) documentation describes subnet registration as the on-chain creation step that pays the registration burn, assigns a new netuid, and opens a new incentive market. The Subnet article previously had no vocabulary section contrasting the running market with the creation step, even though the official Managing Subnets pages place both concepts back-to-back.

## Change Type

- Documentation

## Problem

The Subnet article covers the subnet's relationship to the Network, Multiple Mechanisms, Yuma Consensus, and Crowdloans, but never explicitly names subnet registration as the lifecycle event that creates the running market. Readers who land on the Subnet article from the glossary or from search have no inline context for the creation step that brings a subnet into existence on the chain.

## Expected Behavior

The Subnet article should explicitly describe how subnet registration relates to the running market: registration is the on-chain act that produces the netuid and opens the incentive market, while the subnet is the operational market that runs after registration completes. A reader should be able to tell that registration creates the subnet, that deregistration removes it, and that both act on the 128-slot cap.

## Root Cause

The Subnet article pre-dated the Subnet Registration and Subnet Deregistration concept articles being added to Taopedia (Subnet Registration merged as PR #1520, Subnet Deregistration merged as PR #1364). The official docs already describe both events as the lifecycle of a subnet, but the Subnet article was never updated to reference the creation step by name.

## Solution

Added a new `## Relationship to Subnet Registration` section (21 lines) between the existing `## Relationship to Crowdloans` section and `## Reader Boundary`. The new section:

1. Defines both terms in the same paragraph: a subnet is the operational market that miners and validators participate in, while subnet registration is the on-chain creation step that brings a new subnet into existence.
2. Cites the official Create a Subnet documentation's description of registration as paying the registration burn to assign a new netuid and open an incentive market.
3. Cites the official Subnet Deregistration documentation's framing of registration and deregistration as the two lifecycle events that move a subnet in and out of the 128-subnet limit.
4. Explicitly contrasts the two for readers: the subnet is the running market, subnet registration is the act that brought that market into existence on the chain.
5. Includes a References block pointing at the Create a Subnet and Subnet Deregistration documentation pages, matching the style of the existing relationship sections.

No front matter changes. No fenced code blocks. No `[[wiki links]]` (only external source links to docs.learnbittensor.org). The `content/index/articles.jsonl` is left untouched — CI regenerates it.

## Reproduction Evidence

Before this PR:

```bash
$ grep -E '^## ' content/pages/subnet/index.mdx
# Subnet
## Market Scope
## Miner and Validator Roles
## Relationship to the Network
## Relationship to Multiple Mechanisms
## Relationship to Yuma Consensus
## Relationship to Crowdloans
## Reader Boundary
## Further Reading
```

There is no Subnet Registration section. After this PR:

```bash
$ grep -E '^## ' content/pages/subnet/index.mdx
# Subnet
## Market Scope
## Miner and Validator Roles
## Relationship to the Network
## Relationship to Multiple Mechanisms
## Relationship to Yuma Consensus
## Relationship to Crowdloans
## Relationship to Subnet Registration
## Reader Boundary
## Further Reading
```

## Verification

Local checks (all pass on the branch):

```bash
$ npm run format:check
Prettier config safety check passed
Checking formatting...
All matched files use Prettier code style!

$ npm run validate
Validated 309 articles
```

The new section adds 21 lines to one existing article. No new files. No `package.json` change. No `.github/workflows` change. No generation artifacts committed.

## Checklist

- [x] Issue verified (missing Relationship to Subnet Registration section in Subnet)
- [x] Root cause identified (article pre-dated the Subnet Registration concept; never received a relationship section)
- [x] Fix implemented
- [x] Tests pass locally (format:check, validate)
- [x] CI expected to pass (npm ci + format:check + validate run on PRs)

## Why

The "Re-authorize" button still silently does nothing in prod. The #969 fix relaxed CSP `form-action` on the **POST** `/admin/brightspace/authorize` response — but browsers enforce `form-action` using the CSP of the page that **contains the form** (the `GET /admin/brightspace` render), not the navigation/redirect response. So the form was still blocked from 303-ing cross-origin to the LMS, and the button appeared dead.

## Fix

Move `SecurityHeadersMiddleware.allowFormAction(lmsOrigin)` into `brightspacePage` (the GET render), exactly where the working **MCP consent** flow does it (`MCPOAuthRoutes.authorizeForm`). Removed the no-op call from the POST handler.

`swift build` clean; `swift-format` clean. Follow-up to #966/#969/#970 — this is the piece that makes the in-app Authorize button actually navigate.

- **go_semver_to_version_identity** — projects GoSemVer → VersionIdentity (opaque extdeps.version surface) via go_semver_label.
- **go_semver_compare** — structural Int ordering over major/minor/patch; prerelease presence per semver §11 (no-prerelease > same-version-with-prerelease); prerelease string ordering scaffolded pending parse_go_semver builtin.
- **go_module_version_scheme: VersionScheme** — data row implementing the extdeps.version VersionScheme interface; equality case correct; ordering scaffold dissolve-on: parse_go_semver lands.
- **GoMajorVersionSuffix** (v0/v1 no suffix, v2+ /vN; major field refined to Int where range(min: 2)) + **go_major_suffix_str** render fn.
- **GoReplaceTarget** coproduct — splits the replace RHS into \`ModuleRedirect { path, version }\` vs \`LocalDirRedirect { path }\`; upstream shapes are structurally distinct (module redirect requires version, local dir must not have one); collapsing them into \`target_path: GoModulePath + target_version: GoSemVer?\` admitted illegal states (§2/§3 violation).
- **GoModFile** — full go.mod structure (module, go, toolchain?, require, replace, exclude, retract directives).
- **go_manifest_file = "go.mod"** — single authority lives in emit.dag (v1-seed, load-bearing); module.dag imports it, does not re-declare.
- **go_mvs_properties** — closed enum facts about the MVS algorithm (DeterministicMinimal, ContentHashLocked, MainModuleOnly).
- **17 witnesses** in \`dsl/test/claim/go_module_versioning_witness_test.dag\` — major-suffix rendering, semver label variants, MVS count, identity projection, compare ordering (less/greater/equal/prerelease); all green by execution.

author: stephane-segning
body:
## 1. Summary

This PR changes:

- Adds two **stdio MCP servers** OpenCode spawns to investigate a repo (official `rmcp` SDK), bundled in the agent-runner image:
  - `lightbridge-vector-mcp`: `lightbridge_vector_semantic_search(query, limit?)` — embeds the query, calls the control plane's scoped `/search`.
  - `lightbridge-graph-mcp`: `lightbridge_graph_find_symbol(term, limit?)` + `lightbridge_graph_get_callers(node_id, limit?)` — call `/graph/query`.
- Per **ADR-0020**, they are thin clients of the slice-4a retrieval API, **not** of the datastores: they hold only `AGENT_RUNNER_TOKEN` + `TASK_ID` (+ the embeddings key for vector), never Postgres/Neo4j creds, and every query is scoped server-side to the task's repo.
- Dockerfile builds + ships both MCP bins; `ChunkHit`/`SymbolHit` gain `Serialize`.

It solves:

- epic #5 slice 4 — part 4b (the MCP server binaries), wrapping the 4a endpoints (#36).

**Source of truth:** epic #5, #36 (retrieval endpoints), [docs/opencode-acp-mcp.md](docs/opencode-acp-mcp.md).

## 2. Intent

> Give OpenCode the read tools, while keeping datastore creds out of the untrusted Job. This **diverges from the design doc**, whose example config puts `NEO4J_*` in the MCP env — a cross-tenant read-credential risk, since the stores hold every repo's index. The MCP servers hold only the runner bearer.

## 3. Scope

### In Scope
- The two stdio MCP server binaries + image bundling + ADR-0020

### Out of Scope
- **Slice 5**: the OpenCode ACP runner + the `opencode.json` config that wires these servers (and a GitHub MCP — the runner already holds the install token, so it can call GitHub directly)
- Pagination / richer result shaping

## 4. Verification

I verified this change by:

- [x] Running automated tests
- [x] Running manual tests

Commands run:

```bash
cargo clippy -p agent-runner -p control-plane --all-targets   # clean
cargo test -p agent-runner -p control-plane                   # 24 + 12 + 7
# Live MCP over stdio against the compiled binary:
printf initialize+initialized+tools/list | lightbridge-graph-mcp
printf initialize+initialized+tools/call | lightbridge-graph-mcp   # against a stub control plane
```

Results:

```text
initialize -> serverInfo {name: rmcp, version: 1.7.0}
tools/list -> [lightbridge_graph_find_symbol, lightbridge_graph_get_callers]
tools/call find_symbol -> [ { node_id: src_math_add, label: add(), source_file: src/math.rs, start_line: 2 } ]
clippy: clean; tests: 24 control-plane + 12 runner unit + 7 contract pass
```

The `tools/call` proves the full path: MCP protocol → tool handler → `ControlPlaneClient` → HTTP → rendered JSON back through the protocol.

## 5. Screenshots / Evidence

stdio MCP transcript above (initialize / tools/list / tools/call).

## 6. Risk Assessment

Risk level:
* [x] Low

Potential risks:
* `rmcp` is a new dependency (official MCP SDK; large but well-scoped)
* MCP → control-plane hop adds latency vs a direct DB connection

Mitigation:
* Servers are tiny glue over the wiremock-tested 4a client; no DB drivers in them
* Scope + limit enforced server-side; no datastore creds in the Job

## Seed-expansion milestone 4 — the now()-anchored class, fully covered

Covers `view_rum`'s web-vitals + error-trend sections (app.py 17451, 17488-92, 17505-06, 17529-32, 17542-44, 17576-79, 17581, 17593-95, 17632-33) — the hardest remaining cluster, reached only by **recent (now()-windowed) seeded data**. No block deferred; **no Go change** (`handlers_rum.go` was already a faithful port, just never exercised by populated now()-window data).

### Technique (reuses the proven `metricsauto` pattern)
New isolated profile **`rumvitals`** seeds `hyperdx_sessions` at `now()`-relative fixed offsets with CONSTANT values, so derived quantities are deterministic regardless of wall-clock capture time:
- 4× `web-vital` LCP rows (value 1200) at now()-10/15/20/25min → hotspot `HAVING total>=3` fires (`p75=1200.0`, `poor_rate=0.0`); `quantileExact(0.75)` of a constant = that constant; rolling baseline `stddev=0` → `anomaly_state='normal'`.
- 5 recent + 1 prior `error`/`unhandledrejection` rows → trend `up`, `by_type={error:5, unhandledrejection:1}`, sparkline.
- All offsets keep ≥5min margin from window boundaries so second-level drift never flips a row.

The wall-clock bucket timestamps still drift capture↔replay → **3 masks** (sparkline `"t"`, full-form date-time, and a time-only `HH:MM:SS.mmm` session-ts span the date-anchored mask doesn't reach — found via mask-aware byte-diff). Everything else (counts, values, ratings, states) byte-compared.

### Verification
- Scoped parity **GREEN**, stable across 2 fresh captures + a replay-only recheck (proves the masks absorb now()-drift); re-verified GREEN in the integration env (316978B).
- Combined rum suite **GREEN 8/0** (7 existing rum routes + new) — no regression.
- Oracle coverage 66.54% → **66.65%**; `COVERAGE_FLOOR` ratcheted 66.5 → 66.6.

author: roboomp
body:
## Repro
The reported early-render command reproduced the crash before the fix: `bun -e 'import { CustomEditor } from "./packages/coding-agent/src/modes/components/custom-editor.ts"; const e = new CustomEditor({}); e.imageLinks = ["/tmp/example.png"]; console.log(e.decorateText("[Image #1]"));'` exited 1 with `Settings not initialized. Call Settings.init() first.` from `packages/coding-agent/src/tui/hyperlink.ts`.

## Cause
`CustomEditor.decorateText(...)` renders image placeholders through `imageReferenceHyperlink(...)`, which calls `fileHyperlink(...)`; `fileHyperlink(...)` called `isHyperlinkEnabled()`, and `isHyperlinkEnabled()` unconditionally read `settings.get("tui.hyperlinks")` before `Settings.init()` had completed.

## Fix
- Guarded `isHyperlinkEnabled()` with `isSettingsInitialized()` so uninitialized settings behave like hyperlinks are disabled.
- Guarded `urlHyperlinkAlways(...)` with the same pre-init fallback, keeping all hyperlink helpers plain-text safe until settings exist.
- Added a regression test covering pre-init plain-text fallback for `isHyperlinkEnabled()`, `fileHyperlink(...)`, and `urlHyperlinkAlways(...)`.
- Added the coding-agent changelog entry for #3064.

## Verification
Ran `bun -e 'import { CustomEditor } from "./packages/coding-agent/src/modes/components/custom-editor.ts"; const e = new CustomEditor({}); e.imageLinks = ["/tmp/example.png"]; console.log(e.decorateText("[Image #1]"));'` and it printed `[Image #1]`. Ran `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/tui/hyperlink.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/modes/image-references.test.ts`: 35 pass, 0 fail. `gh_push_branch` completed its pre-publish gate and pushed `farm/867a4231/image-paste-placeholder-crash`. Fixes #3064

body:
## What

Foundation for the chat-console redesign: surface a **build version** and an **agent-editable UI config** through the web bootstrap.

- `/api/v1/web/bootstrap` now returns `version` (`mimir.__version__`) and `ui: { agent_name, skin }`.
- The UI config is an **agent-owned file**: `<home>/web_ui.json`. The agent edits it itself (e.g. during onboarding) to set its display name and active skin — it's a plain file in the home dir the agent already operates in.
- `read_web_ui_config()` reads it per-request (same pattern as the other `<home>/` reads), falling back to defaults (`Mimir` / `neon-terminal`) when missing/malformed/partial. The skin string is passed through verbatim for the frontend to validate against its registry.
- `ensure_web_ui_config()` seeds the file with defaults **at startup** (in `register_routes`) so there's always a discoverable, well-formed file to edit; **existing files are never overwritten**, so agent edits survive restarts.
- Regenerated `contracts.ts` for the new `WebBootstrapData` fields.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)
- **Frontend** (stacked next): consume `version` + `ui` in the chat console redesign (header build label, agent dossier name, default skin).
- **Onboarding behavior**: prompt/skill so the agent asks the user for its name and offers skins when the file is first seeded.

## Test

author: rafalablewski
body:
## Summary
Introduces a shared semantic color vocabulary (`@hybrid/core/semantic.ts`) that maps application states (readiness, HPI, injury risk, accountability) to brand accent colors, ensuring web and mobile agree on what each color means. Also adds comprehensive Aurora analytics dashboards for athletes, coaches, and operators, plus Aurora logger settings UI and session finish celebration screens.

## Key Changes

### Semantic Color System
- **New `packages/core/src/semantic.ts`**: Single source of truth for state→color mappings
  - `ROLE_COLOR`: Maps semantic roles (`go`, `info`, `premium`, `caution`, `danger`, `neutral`) to brand accents
  - `readinessRole()`, `hpiRole()`, `riskRole()`, `accountabilityRole()`, `phaseRole()`: Convert numeric/string states to semantic roles
  - Replaces hardcoded color logic scattered across web/mobile components
  - Includes comprehensive unit tests (`semantic.test.ts`)

### Aurora Analytics Dashboards
- **New `apps/web/components/aurora/analytics.tsx`**: Three-tier analytics (athlete/coach/operator)
  - `AuroraAthleteAnalytics`: Sessions, volume, e1RM trends, PRs, readiness
  - `AuroraCoachAnalytics`: Roster adherence, team volume, client performance
  - `AuroraOperatorAnalytics`: Organization-wide metrics, team comparisons
  - Reusable `AStat`, `AFrame`, `AEmpty` components with Aurora design system (28px radius, soft shadows)

### Aurora Logger Settings & Session Finish
- **New `apps/mobile/components/aurora/logger-settings.tsx`**: Rounded, segmented-control UI for logger preferences
- **Web logger finish celebration**: `FinishData` type + celebration screen showing sets, volume, PRs, and first-ever achievements
- Mobile workout summary already had celebration; web now matches parity

### Layout & Navigation Improvements
- **New `apps/mobile/lib/layout.ts`**: `auroraScrollClearance()` — single source of truth for floating pill nav clearance (replaces magic numbers)
- **Aurora screen entrance animation**: Subtle fade + rise on every screen focus (mobile `AuroraScreen`, web `AuroraToday`)
- **Keyboard handling**: `KeyboardAvoidingView` on mobile, proper scroll clearance on both platforms
- **Aurora global nav**: Blur background, text labels under icons, improved visual hierarchy

### Component Updates
- **Web `aurora/today.tsx`**: Uses semantic roles for readiness/HPI/risk/accountability colors; adds 14-day HPI trajectory sparkline
- **Mobile `aurora/home.tsx`**: Semantic role colors, entrance animation, improved readiness/HPI/risk display
- **Mobile `aurora/kit.tsx`**: `Ring` (readiness dial), `Spark` (sparkline), entrance animation, keyboard avoidance
- **Mobile `aurora/ai-coach.tsx`**: `embedded` prop for card-within-card rendering (Home "Ask your coach" card)
- **Mobile `aurora/global-nav.tsx`**: Blur background, icon labels, improved styling

### Cross-Client Consistency
- Updated all color-mapping code in web/mobile to use `semantic.ts` functions
- `apps/web/lib/ui.tsx`: New `roleHex()` helper for CSS color resolution
- `apps/mobile/lib/theme.tsx`: New `roleColor()` helper for palette resolution
- Ensures readiness/HPI/risk/accountability thresholds and meanings are identical across platforms

### Capabilities Registry
- Updated `packages/core/src/capabilities.ts` to reflect new analytics dashboards and semantic system as `shipped`

## Implementation Details
- Semantic roles are **not** theme-aware; they resolve to brand accents, which each client then maps to their own palette/CSS variables
- Aurora analytics reuse exact same data engines (`totalVolume`, `bestE1rmByLift`, `e1rmSeries`, etc.) as classic screens
- Layout clearance is now derived from real bar height + safe-area inset, not hand-copied magic numbers
- Session finish celebration is a new screen state (not a navigation away), matching mobile

author: nikolareljin
body:
## Context

VigilantCore today is a mature single-node monitor (v0.9.0): it aggregates events from RSS/news/search, dedups/normalizes, scores impact with local Ollama, and shows results in web + Qt UIs. The goal is to grow it into the **coordinating centerpiece for emergency action** — monitoring adverse events; reacting with or without internet or grid power; communicating over LoRa/Meshtastic mesh, satellite, BLE, and MQTT; informing other systems; and using local AI to fuse and prioritize.

This PR delivers **Phase 1 — Architecture & Contracts**: the foundation every later capability plugs into. It is fully **additive and backward compatible** — with no plugins configured, behavior is identical to v0.9.0.

## What's included

### `contracts/` — the canonical `EmergencyEvent` (v2.0)
A strict superset of the existing v1.0 normalized alert, so current alerts upgrade losslessly via `from_normalized()`. Adds a stable `event_id` (ULID), `origin_node_id`, `hazard_type`, `trust` tier (the #70 injection boundary), mesh `ttl_hops`/`seen_nodes`, and `actions`. Ships a JSON Schema + validator and dependency-free ULID/geohash helpers so the Python hub, the dashboard, the MQTT bus, and future Rust/Go edge daemons all agree on one shape.

### `plugins/` — the kernel
Four plugin kinds (`Source`/`Transport`/`Device`/`Sink`), an in-process `EventBus` that replaces the engine's single `on_new_alert` callback, a config-driven loader (#12), uniform health telemetry (reusing the v0.8.0 source-health shape), and three reference plugins:
- **RSS source** — proves the ingest seam
- **MQTT transport** — publishes schema-valid events to `intel/events/normalized` + `intel/events/high_priority` (#57/#58/#59/#60)
- **Notify device** — high-severity local notification

### `mesh/` — node identity + store-and-forward
Persistent `node_id` with role (`hub`/`edge`/`relay`) and a SQLite-backed store-and-forward queue implementing gossip / flood-with-suppression: duplicate and looped events suppressed, `ttl_hops` bounds flooding (#33/#34). Survives power loss. Phase 1 ships the model + reference algorithm; Phase 2's radios drive it.

### Wiring (additive, graceful degradation)
- `engine/monitor.py` — `gather_items()` pulls source plugins; `process_items()` emits each stored alert as an `EmergencyEvent` to the mesh queue and egress plugins. If an optional plugin/transport dependency is missing, monitoring still runs.
- `utils/config.py` — `node` + `plugins` config sections (existing `_coerce_*` pattern).
- `docs/architecture.md` + `docs/emergency-event-schema.md` (indexed); `requirements.txt` adds `jsonschema` + `paho-mqtt`.

## Testing
- **106 tests pass** (existing suite + 39 new: contract round-trip/schema/upgrade, event bus + registry routing + loader, store-and-forward dedup/loop/TTL/restart).
- **ruff clean** repo-wide.
- End-to-end verified: an item flows ingest → store → MQTT (both topics) → siren → forwarding queue, with stable node identity and restart-persistent dedup.

## Scope / follow-ups
Later phases land as their own PRs against these contracts: multi-channel routing (#42), LoRa/Meshtastic/BLE/satellite transports (#25–#29) + Rust/Go edge daemons with solar/power management, encrypted offline storage (#39), LLM gateway (#67), AI fusion (#35), prompt-injection hardening (#70), and event signing.

Closes #12. Lays the contract/schema groundwork for #57, #58, #59, #60. Advances #19, #40, #33, #34.

## What

Corrects the `context_length` for the `("zai", "glm-5.2")` model spec from `200000` to `1000000`.

## Why

Z.AI's official docs ([docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.2](https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.2)) state GLM-5.2 has a **"truly usable 1M-token context"** (1,000,000 tokens). The spec understated this as 200K, so Kolega's context accounting — token budgeting, compaction triggers, and the "context remaining" UI — treated GLM-5.2 as a 200K model when it actually supports 5× that.

`1000000` matches the file's existing convention for 1M-context models (Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, Grok, Qwen all use `1000000`).

author: enoch85
body:
Fixes #3127.

A Streamystats watchlist holds the **show** item ID, so the existing item-only `isInWatchlist` / `watchlistedByUsers` props return empty when a rule is evaluated at the season/episode level. A `NOT_CONTAINS <user>` protection rule then wrongly matches a watchlisted show's seasons and sweeps them into deletion/unmonitoring.

- Adds `isInWatchlist_including_parent` and `watchlistedByUsers_including_parent` (show-only, `season`/`episode`), mirroring the existing Jellyfin `sw_favoritedBy_including_parent` precedent.
- Resolves the parent chain through the media server's `getMetadata` — the same canonical path the Jellyfin/Emby/Plex getters use — so parent IDs come from the mapper's hierarchy resolution (`SeriesId` for seasons, not the library-folder `parentId`). Gated on the server-agnostic `type` so a movie is never rolled up.
- Skips (returns `undefined`, transient) when metadata can't be fetched, rather than falling back to an item-only check that could let a protected item match a destructive rule.
- Base props remain item-only (no behavioral change); union/dedupe reuses the shared `definedUniqueValues` helper.

author: thewoolleyman
body:
Mirror the closed-loop CI-telemetry export just merged in livespec CORE (PR thewoolleyman/livespec#477, commit `b1e875d`).

## What
Each CI run on `master`/`merge_group` exports its per-job timings to Honeycomb (dataset `github-ci`) as OTLP/HTTP-JSON spans, and **FAILS the job if Honeycomb does not accept them** — a closed-loop self-verification: the run that produced the data confirms its own telemetry landed. A broken telemetry pipeline can't die silently; it reddens master CI and fires the existing CI-failure notification.

PRs are untouched (the job is gated to `push`/`merge_group`), so PR feedback latency is unchanged.

## Changes
- `.github/scripts/export-ci-telemetry.sh` — byte-for-byte copy of the CORE reference. Repo-agnostic; driven by `$REPO`/`$RUN_ID` from the workflow env. Emits one `ci.run` root span + one `ci.job.<name>` child per completed job.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `export-telemetry` job that `needs: [setup, check-python, check-metadata, e2e-cli]` (every top-level job in this repo) so it runs last and reads each job's final timing.

## Notes
- The ingest secret `HONEYCOMB_GITHUB_CI_INGEST_KEY_LIVESPEC` is already set in this repo.
- `export-telemetry` is SKIPPED on this PR (gated to push) — that is expected. It runs on the post-merge master push.
- Config-only (.yml + .sh, no product .py): `chore(ci)` subject, Red-Green-Replay exempt.

author: reuzehagel
body:
## Why

A traffic surge (~750% visits, ~450% page views) pushed the Hyperdrive **Free-plan daily query count** toward its cap. On the Free plan, queries past the cap **fail with an error** (they aren't billed), so hitting it would take down every DB-backed feature (builds, likes, bookmarks, auth) until the 00:00 UTC reset.

Most of the load is **anonymous** (site browsing + Discord/embed traffic), so the highest-leverage fix is the anonymous edge cache (Cloudflare Cache API) — every hit is a request that never reaches Postgres/Hyperdrive.

> The structural ceiling-remover is still upgrading to the **Workers Paid plan** (~$5/mo → unlimited Hyperdrive queries). This PR is the code-side headroom on top of that, and a genuine inefficiency fix regardless.

## What changed

- **Edge-cache `GET /builds/:slug/partners`** (`maxAge: 300`). The "Related builds" strip fires this on **every full build-detail page view**, but the route had no `edgeCache` middleware and hit Postgres uncached every time — even for anonymous viewers — roughly **doubling** the DB queries per anon detail view (cached detail + uncached partners). This is the main win.
- **Raise `GET /builds` list cache TTL 120s → 300s.** Helps the hot keys (default browse / page 1).
- **Refresh `edge-cache.ts` comments**: drop the stale Neon-autosuspend rationale (we're on PlanetScale now), reframe around the Hyperdrive query cap, and fix the 120s → 300s reference.

## Reviewer notes

- **Cache safety is unchanged from the detail route's model.** `edgeCache` bypasses the cache whenever a session cookie is present, so authenticated viewers still get their viewer-specific partner visibility. Only cookieless (anonymous) responses — which see a stable PUBLIC/UNLISTED partner set — are stored.
- **Accepted staleness on partners**, same class as the existing list cache: partner mutations don't purge this path (no tractable per-key eviction in the Cache API), so an unlinked or newly-private partner can linger in an anon entry for up to 300s. Bounded and low-risk — the strip only renders a title/thumbnail, never the loadout. Documented inline.
- **List TTL tradeoff:** a new/edited build now takes up to 5 min (was 2) to surface in listings.
- **Detail TTL left at 300s on purpose.** Anonymous view-counting only runs on a cache *miss*, so raising the detail TTL would suppress view-count accrual on popular builds. Not worth trading view-count fidelity for during an active traffic spike.

## Verification

`just check` (typecheck + oxlint + oxfmt) passes across web + api + shared; scripts typecheck clean.

body:
## Summary

The seed's `configure-openclaw-agent.sh` invokes `/usr/local/bin/openrouter-provision` (this repo's `scripts/openrouter-provision.py`) to mint per-agent child keys. Before this commit, no install path placed the binary on the VM — the gateway clone brought it to `/tmp/openclaw-gateway/...` on the runner but nothing copied it to `/usr/local/bin/` on the target VM. `configure-openclaw-agent.sh` then silently fell back to the shared `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on every deploy (incident: linux-desktop-seed run 27833801264, 2026-06-19).

This commit adds the install as **step 4b of `scripts/install/deploy.sh`**:
- `install -m 0755` (preferred over `cp` + `chmod` per the AGENTS.md deploy-snapshot incident).
- Idempotent by SHA: skips when source and destination match.
- Warns (not fails) when the source file is missing.

Also updates `docs/concepts/per-agent-openrouter-keys.md` to make the two install paths explicit (CLI on every deploy vs master key by hand) and adds a new failure-mode row covering the FATAL from the seed side when the CLI is missing.

## Why not the master-key installer?

`scripts/install/install-openrouter-provisioning.sh` is the master-key installer (writes `OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY` to the systemd override) and is correctly documented as a one-time, by-hand operator step in the existing docs. The CLI install is a different artifact on a different cadence — it should run on every deploy, not once by hand — so it belongs in `deploy.sh` rather than next to the master-key installer.

## Test plan

- [x] `bats tests/install-openrouter-provision-cli.bats` — 7/7 pass (install, mode 0755, byte-identical copy, idempotency, drift re-install, missing-source warn-not-fail, pre-existing-dest overwrite)
- [x] `bats tests/deploy-skills-sync.bats` — all pass
- [x] `bats tests/viz-service-installer.bats` — 12/13 pass (1 pre-existing failure on `main` unrelated to this commit)
- [x] `shellcheck -x -S error scripts/install/deploy.sh` — clean

## Acceptance criteria

- After this deploys, `/usr/local/bin/openrouter-provision` exists on the VM and is byte-identical to `scripts/openrouter-provision.py` in this repo.
- Re-running `deploy.sh` on an unchanged repo is a no-op for the CLI install (idempotent).
- `configure-openclaw-agent.sh` no longer hits the missing-binary branch when `OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY` is set.
- The seed's post-deploy verify step (PR #920) passes the per-agent OpenRouter check end-to-end.

## Related

- linux-desktop-seed PR #920 — turns the silent shared-key fallback into a hard fail
- linux-desktop-seed issue #918 — misleading 'Leaked GitHub token' warning (separate fix)
- Run 27833801264 — the prod deploy that surfaced the regression

author: razzaque
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in **Streamable-HTTP** transport so a remote MCP client (e.g. the Trellios governed MCP proxy) can reach this server over the network — not only as a spawned stdio process. **stdio remains the default**, so existing Claude/Cursor configs are unaffected.

## How
- `MCP_HTTP_PORT` enables HTTP mode; absent → stdio (unchanged).
- `MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN` (optional) requires a matching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request (401 otherwise). Distinct from `BUGSINK_TOKEN`, which is the upstream Bugsink API token.
- Stateless `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` (`enableJsonResponse`): a fresh server + transport is built **per request** — a single stateless transport cannot serve sequential requests. Server creation + tool registration are wrapped in `createServer()`.

## Verified locally against the live Bugsink API
- `tools/list` with valid bearer → 200
- wrong bearer → 401
- `list_projects` read → returns real data
- `Accept: application/json` without `text/event-stream` → 406 (clients must accept both, per the MCP spec)

Build: `npm run build` clean.

author: gburd
body:
## Stage 2: asynchronous I/O for the buffer pool

A pluggable `os_aio` layer so buffer-pool writeback (checkpoint/sync and
trickle) can issue page writes asynchronously instead of blocking a
foreground thread on each device write, with native completion engines per
platform and a portable fallback.

### Backends (selected at runtime, in order)

1. **io_uring** (Linux) — native, reused from libxtc.
2. **IOCP** (Windows) — native, reused from libxtc.
3. **kqueue + aio** (FreeBSD/BSD) — `aiocb` with `SIGEV_KEVENT`, reaped via
   `kevent`. Gated on `sigev_notify_kqueue`; macOS lacks it and uses POSIX aio.
4. **POSIX aio** (Solaris/illumos, macOS) — `aio_read`/`aio_write` +
   `aio_suspend`/`aio_error`/`aio_return`.
5. **thread-pool offload** — last-resort portable fallback.

Without any backend, `os_aio` falls back to synchronous I/O (behaviour
preserving). `configure.ac` autodetects each (`HAVE_IO_URING`,
`HAVE_AIO_KQUEUE`, `HAVE_AIO_POSIX`, `HAVE_AIO_THREADPOOL`).

### Integration

- `__memp_pgwrite` split into prep (WAL flush + pgout — the WAL rule stays
  before submission) / submit / finish.
- Checkpoint/sync (`__memp_sync_int`) submits a bounded in-flight window and
  drains it; trickle uses the same path, so trickle writeback is async too.
- Foreground eviction stays synchronous by design (prefer-clean eviction +
  trickle keep dirty pages away from the evictor; an async evictor would hold
  latches waiting on its own completion).
- Multi-process safe: AIO contexts are per-process; a page marked in-flight by
  one process is reaped only by that process, others use the existing
  `mtx_buf` in-transit wait.

### Thread-pool fork safety

The pool is process-wide, lazy, and fork-safe: a live-context registry lets the
`pthread_atfork` child handler reset every context's completion FIFO and
in-flight count (workers do not survive fork) **without running completions** —
running a write completion in the child would clear `BH_DIRTY` and drop a pin
for I/O the child never performed, corrupting inherited copy-on-write state.

### Build

The tree is K&R C; Autoconf >= 2.72 `AC_PROG_CC` adopts `-std=gnu23`, under
which K&R definitions are a hard error. Pinned `-std=gnu99` and silenced the two
inherent K&R diagnostics behind compiler-support probes. `configure` regenerated
with Autoconf 2.73 (the dev-flake toolchain).

### Status / not yet done

- **Draft pending at-scale measurement.** `rrand` (the read-scaling workload) is
  100% cache hits with zero I/O, so AIO cannot move that curve; benefit must be
  shown on a write/cache-pressure workload. To be measured on the Linux box
  (io_uring) and FreeBSD (kqueue aio).
- **Prefetch / readahead is deferred** to a follow-up (Stage 2b): it is the only
  read-side async feature, is correctness-heavy (buffer reservation, in-transit
  handshake, per-process reap constraint), and should be built against measured
  evidence rather than speculatively.

Maps to ROADMAP #8. Companion to the design doc (PR #20).

author: pauljsnider
body:
Closes #2291

## What changed
- added typed Firestore record interfaces for chat conversations, messages, and attachments
- added chat-specific mapper functions that normalize partial sender, attachment, reaction, and preview metadata
- updated `chatService` read paths to map SDK and native REST chat reads through the typed mapper boundary instead of returning raw decoded payloads
- added focused regression tests for valid and partial chat message and conversation Firestore records

## Root Cause
`chatService` was letting chat message and inbox-preview data cross the Firestore boundary as raw `any`-decoded objects. That meant missing sender metadata, malformed reactions, attachment fields, and partial conversation preview fields were never normalized before inbox rendering consumed them.

## Prevention / Learning
When migrating Firestore reads, add explicit record interfaces and mapper functions at the service boundary first, then route both SDK and native REST reads through the same normalization path. Cover valid and partial documents in tests before wiring the UI to the data.

## Regression Tests
- `npx vitest run src/lib/chatService.test.ts src/lib/badgeService.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `npm run app:build`

author: andlog0713
body:
**Sprint tracker — Category: Analysis pipeline. Do NOT merge — Andrew regenerates one report and confirms the fix lines read behavioral first.**

## Step 0 finding (why this is a prompt edit, not a string swap)

The two FIX lines flagged for softening — a parlay line with "+EV"/"negative expected value" and an NFL-spread line with "key number"/"line movement"/"take the alternate" — are **LLM-authored at generation time, not hardcoded**. None of those exact phrases exist as literals anywhere in `lib/`, `app/`, or `components/` (only in blog articles and an explainer keyword array). The advice the user sees comes from:
- bias `fix` → `claudeBias?.fix` (`lib/autopsy-engine.ts:3101`)
- `recommendations` → `claudeData.recommendations` (`:3138`)
- `personal_rules` → `claudeData.personal_rules` (`:3144`)

So softening means steering the prompt, not editing strings. Confirmed with the requester, who chose prompt-guidance-only.

## Change

One `BEHAVIORAL FRAMING RULE` added to the full-report `SYSTEM_PROMPT` (after the SPORTSBOOK RULE, before Critical Rules). It is **scoped to the prescriptive advice fields only** (`fix`, `recommendations`, `personal_rules`, `edge_profile.reallocation_advice`) and explicitly does **not** touch `description`/`evidence`/`executive_diagnosis`, which keep their factual latitude (e.g. "losses pushed through certain margins" stays sayable).

In the advice fields it forbids:
- expected-value language (`+EV`, positive/negative expected value, `EV`)
- `key number` / `key numbers`
- `line movement` / `wait for the line to move`
- `take the alternate` / `alternate line`
- staking-system prescriptions (`1% of bankroll`, `unit size`, `set your unit`, `X units`)

…and instructs behavioral discipline framing (what to stop doing and why it cost them, plain language, pre-bet checkpoint), keeping the existing "sharp friend / behavioral psychologist" voice — a vocabulary constraint, not a tone change. Two worked examples included (parlay → stop at 2 legs; NFL spread → pre-bet checkpoint, "betting the game in front of you or chasing the last one", "NFL spreads are your weak spot").

The snapshot path is pure-compute (no LLM, `fix=''`), so the full-report prompt is the only generation surface.

## Gates

tsc 0 · vitest 378/378. LLM output isn't unit-tested (the prompt is a const string; deterministic suites are unaffected) — the real verification is regenerating a report, which is the requester's pre-merge step.

author: thiernoyunus
body:
## Why

Projects disappeared from the dashboard after **1 hour** — the cleanup task purged each output dir by mtime (`JOB_RETENTION_SECONDS = 3600`), so cards went `expired` and their videos 404'd. The delete button only removed the localStorage card, never the server files.

## What

Make projects **permanent until the user deletes them**, and give the delete button a real server-side delete.

- **`JOB_RETENTION_SECONDS` now defaults to `0` = permanent** (env-overridable to re-enable a TTL). `cleanup_jobs` only time-purges projects when it's `> 0`.
- Raw uploads still prune on their own **`UPLOAD_RETENTION_SECONDS`** (default 1h) — they're transient inputs, not projects.
- **New `DELETE /api/jobs/{job_id}`** — removes the output dir + in-memory job state. Hardened against path traversal: rejects separators and `.`/`..`, and verifies the resolved path stays inside `OUTPUT_DIR` before `rmtree`.
- Dashboard delete button calls `DELETE /api/jobs/{id}` (best-effort) before dropping the local card, so deleting actually frees disk.

## Verification

`TestClient` covers: delete-existing (output dir removed), delete-missing (`removed:false`), and `..`/`.` traversal — blocked, with `OUTPUT_DIR` **and its parent confirmed intact**. `app.py` compiles; dashboard lint clean (no new warnings).

## Note

Takes effect after a **backend restart** (the running server holds the old `JOB_RETENTION_SECONDS`). To keep existing already-`expired` projects, nothing can be done — their files were already purged before this change; this prevents it going forward.

author: louisburroughs
body:
## Why
Investigation (prompted by `admin.alpha` being a `User` with no `Person` on alpha) found:
- Violation of **ADR-0015 §3** ("a User must be linked to a Person") with no enforcement mechanism.
- **Two divergent linkage stores**: `pos-people.user_person_links` vs `pos-security-service.users.person_id` — neither populated for admin.alpha.
- Token **`personId` claim nullable/absent** for unlinked users (undermines ADR-0022).
- Self-defeating seed: the admin link insert is guarded on a person that is never inserted.

Data/seed fix tracked separately in durion-positivity-backend#714.

## Changes
- **ADR-0015** — new **§7 User–Person Linkage Invariants (I5–I7)**: single authoritative link store, every ACTIVE user resolves to exactly one person, no `userId`/`personId` conflation (translation mandatory). Changelog updated.
- **ADR-0039 (PROPOSED)** — *User–Person Linkage Authority and Translation*: names `pos-people.user_person_links` as the sole authority, makes `users.person_id` a derived cache (or removes it), derives the token `personId` from the link, mandates `UserPersonTranslationService` / `GET /v1/people/users/{userId}/person` at the boundary, and adds reconcile + seed-validation enforcement plus a self-service ownership check.

## Follow-ups
- ADR-0039 is PROPOSED — needs Architecture/Backend/Security sign-off.
- Implementation + seed fix: durion-positivity-backend#714.

author: leonardoaraujosantos
body:
## Summary

Extends the heavy-algorithm-engines work (Gruntz limits, incomplete gamma, `assuming`/refine) with a series of always-green increments. 22 commits, source changes confined to the limit engine, special-function classes, and refine, plus regression tests for every fix and a docs/openspec sync.

## Limit engine (Gruntz)

- **Special-function asymptotic series**: `erfc`/`erf` (Gaussian tail), `Ei`, Riemann `ζ`, digamma / higher polygamma, log-Stirling `loggamma`, Tricomi–Erdélyi gamma-ratio subleading term, and `atan`/`acot` (`x·(atan x−π/2)→−1`, with subleading).
- **Log of a dominated sum**: dominant-summand extraction for exponential-dominated sums with polynomial terms (`log(x+eˣ)/log(x+e²ˣ)→1/2`) and logarithmic-rate sums (`log(log x+log log x)−log log x→0`).
- **MRV exponential differences in a product**: `M·(eᵖ−eᵍ)`, `p−q→0` — Gruntz's flagship `eˣ·(e^{1/x−e⁻ˣ}−e^{1/x})→−1` (read off algebraically, no numeric guard).
- **Tower products** via log-exp reduction (`xˣ/(x+1)^{x+1}→0`).
- **Series core × non-polynomial multiplier** (`eˣ·((1+1/x)ˣ−e)→−∞`, `√x·(…)→0`).
- **Termination/perf**: dominant-term rule before the conjugate for different-rate radical `∞−∞` (`log log x−√(log x·log log x)`), dropping a ~41 s pathological limit to milliseconds.

## Special-function derivatives (correctness)

- `∂ₛγ(s,x)`, `∂ₛΓ(s,x)`, `∂ₙψ⁽ⁿ⁾(x)`: were a silently-wrong `0`; now an honest unevaluated `Derivative`.
- Closed forms added: `∂ₐΒ(a,b)=Β(a,b)(ψ(a)−ψ(a+b))` (symmetric), `H′(x)=polygamma(1,x+1)`.

## Refine / assumptions

- `re(x)→0`, `im(x)→−i·x` for a purely imaginary argument (under `assuming(Q.imaginary)` or an imaginary symbol).

## Docs / openspec

- README + docs test counts updated (1554 tests / 5488 assertions; 672 oracle-validated).
- `gruntz-limits`, `incomplete-gamma`, `assuming-context` specs extended with the new requirements; Purpose sections filled in; all validate.
- `docs/09-known-issues.md` carries a "Fixed" entry per increment.

## Testing

Full suite green: **5488 assertions / 1554 cases**, zero regressions. Every fix verified against the SymPy oracle.

body:
## Summary

Implements the full 18-task multi-tenant gateway plan from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-19-hermes-multi-tenant-gateway.md`.

## New Modules

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `gateway/tenancy.py` | Tenant data layer — columns, policy walls, tenant-scoped queries |
| `gateway/routing.py` | 8-tier binding router ported from openclaw-python |
| `hermes_cli/migration.py` | `hermes gateway migrate` CLI + config.yaml tenant sections |
| `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/tenant_tokens.py` | Dashboard tenant-scoped auth tokens |
| `tools/relay_tool.py` | Tenant-aware relay with content-only stripping |
| `tui_gateway/authz.py` | TUI per-RPC authz policy (shipped + tested, not wired — single-operator TUI) |

## Key Design Decisions

- **RBAC**: Three roles — operator (all tenants), tenant_admin (own tenant), client (own sessions).
- **Session key**: `tenant_session_key` column added to sessions table (not `session_key` — avoids topic-mode rollback guard collision).
- **Agent identity**: `_agent_id_for_source()` method on `GatewayRunner` for agent-scoped session keys.
- **Memory isolation**: Per-tenant memory roots via tenant-aware tool policy.
- **Delegation pinning**: Subagents inherit tenant context.

## Deferred (documented, not dead code)

- Per-tenant skill-file discovery in `skills_tool` — needs agent identity in tool dispatch.
- `tui_gateway/server.py` per-RPC authz gate — needs per-connection tenant identity (stdio TUI is single operator).

- Tenancy + desktop test suites: **75/75 green**.

- Non-gateway touched dirs (state, tools, cron, dashboard, run_agent): **2,306/2,306 green**.
- Full suite: **31,523 pass**, 15 xdist flakes (pass individually — not caused by this change).

author: sernafernando
body:
## Problema

El buscador de proveedor en el modal de carga de pedido exigía el permiso **`administracion.ver_proveedores`** (de la sección Administración → Proveedores). Un usuario cuyo trabajo es cargar pedidos de compra no necesariamente tiene ese permiso "raro", así que el autocomplete no le funcionaba.

## Causa

El autocomplete (`ProveedorComprasAutocomplete`) llama a:
- `GET /administracion/proveedores?search=` (búsqueda)
- `GET /administracion/proveedores/{id}` (precarga del proveedor al editar)

Ambos hacían `_check_permiso(..., 'administracion.ver_proveedores')`.

## Fix

Esos **dos** endpoints de lectura ahora aceptan cualquiera de:
- `administracion.ver_proveedores`
- `administracion.ver_ordenes_compra`
- `administracion.gestionar_ordenes_compra`

vía `_check_permiso_lectura_proveedor` (any-of). El resto de sub-endpoints de proveedor (datos-fiscales, direcciones, bancos, contactos, marcas) **siguen exigiendo `ver_proveedores`** — no se amplió nada de más. Sin ningún permiso relevante → 403.

## Verificación (auth)

- Test: con `gestionar_ordenes_compra` el buscador ya **no da 403**.
- Test: sin permiso relevante → **403**.
- Regresión: **400 passed** (proveedor + compras + permisos). `ver_proveedores` intacto en el resto.
- Solo lectura, sin migración. Rollback: revertir el commit.

## QA

Con un usuario que tiene permiso de compras pero NO `ver_proveedores`: abrí el modal de carga de pedido y buscá un proveedor → debe listar y dejarte seleccionar.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
# Problem Statement
The current CI strategy does not efficiently skip heavy checks (linting, tests, security, deployment) when a commit contains no actual code changes relative to its parent, leading to wasted CI cycles and resource usage.

# Goal
Implement an optimized CI strategy that skips heavy checks for commits with no code changes, thereby improving CI efficiency and resource utilization.

# Non-Goals
None.

# Proposed Approach
1. **Foundational Gate Job:** Add a `verify-changes` job to all primary workflows that uses `git diff --quiet HEAD~1 HEAD` to detect empty patches.
2. **Conditional Execution:** Update downstream jobs to depend on the gate and only run if code modifications are detected.
3. **Workflow Consolidation:** Integrate Oxlint, Gitleaks, Semgrep, and Merge Conflict checks into the main `ci.yml` to centralize gated validation.
4. **Auto-Blocking Failsafe:** Create `block-empty-jules-patches.yml` to automatically comment on and close Pull Requests that contain zero changes.
5. **Version Maintenance:** Standardize `actions/checkout` to `@v4` across touched files to fix invalid versioning.

# Alternatives Considered
None.

# Architectural Impact
These changes will satisfy the repository's No-Op Protection Policy and optimize runner usage for both human and AI-generated patches.

# Scope
The scope includes the implementation of the proposed CI optimizations across all primary workflows in the repository.

# UNDERSTAND THE ISSUE
The current system executes all heavy checks regardless of whether the commits contain actual changes, leading to inefficiencies.

# DETERMINE APPROACH
The approach involves creating a gate job to check for code changes and modifying existing workflows to conditionally execute based on this check.

# SPECIFY SCOPE
The implementation will focus on adding the `verify-changes` job, updating downstream jobs, consolidating workflows, creating the failsafe, and standardizing versioning.

# DEFINITION OF DONE
- `verify-changes` job is implemented and correctly detects empty patches.
- Downstream jobs are updated to depend on the `verify-changes` job.
- Oxlint, Gitleaks, Semgrep, and Merge Conflict checks are integrated into the main `ci.yml`.
- `block-empty-jules-patches.yml` is created and operational.
- `actions/checkout` is standardized to `@v4` across all touched files.
- CI runs successfully with the new strategy in place and shows no failures related to empty commits.

author: mistakeknot
body:
## What

Step 1 found RQ1 "inverts" across two families — within Hermes-4 (non-reasoning) metacognitive efficiency *rises* with scale, within Qwen3.5 (reasoning) it *falls*. With n=2 that could be family noise (→ scale is the wrong axis). PR #22's ablation showed reasoning *mode* drives efficiency on a fixed model. This run tests the resulting hypothesis: **does rise-vs-fall track reasoning mode rather than family/scale?**

Adds 3 within-family size ladders (48 runs, all `success`), balanced by reasoning mode, to the 2 published ladders → **5 families, 14 models**.

## Pre-registered hypothesis → result

**Hypothesis:** non-reasoning ladders rise with scale (like Hermes), reasoning ladders fall (like Qwen3.5).
**Result: supported for reasoning (2/2 fall), partial for non-reasoning.** Pooled-verbalized; read **type-2 AUROC** as the ratio-free sensitivity measure (M-ratio is capability-normalized efficiency):

| family | mode | rung | acc | type-2 AUROC | M-ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ministral | non-reason | 3b→8b→14b | .64/.73/.78 | 0.695 → 0.623 → 0.631 | 1.67† / 0.61 / 0.52 |
| Gemma 3 | non-reason | 12b→27b | .73/.78 | 0.623 → **0.681** | 0.61 → **0.73** |
| Hermes-4 | non-reason | 70b→405b | .73/.80 | 0.536 → **0.612** | 0.18 → **0.40** |
| Qwen3 | **reason** | 8b→14b→32b | .80/.83/.82 | 0.745 → 0.719 → **0.635** | 0.93 → 0.72 → **0.45** |
| Qwen3.5 | **reason** | 9b→397b | .86/.92 | 0.794 → **0.763** | 0.92 → **0.61** |

† Ministral-3b M-ratio>1 is an **unstable low-d′ artifact** (acc .64, d′ .52, ECE .33 — meta-d′/d′ blows up as d′→0); trust its AUROC cell.

### Reading (`figures/rq1_crossfamily.png`)

1. **Reasoning families decline with scale — robustly, both of them.** Qwen3 AUROC 0.745→0.635, Qwen3.5 0.79→0.76; M-ratio 0.93→0.45 and 0.92→0.61. The decline shows on the **ratio-free AUROC**, so it isn't a d′-denominator artifact. Capability outruns metacognition in reasoning models.
2. **Non-reasoning families do not decline.** Hermes rises, Gemma3 rises, Ministral flat on AUROC. None fall on the trustworthy measure.
3. **At small scale reasoning models are markedly more metacognitively sensitive** (AUROC ~0.75 vs ~0.55–0.70), but the edge erodes as they grow.

**So the RQ1 "inversion" is not random family noise.** Cleaner statement: *metacognitive efficiency declines with scale in reasoning models — capability outruns introspection — while non-reasoning models hold or improve.* This unifies RQ1 with the PR #22 ablation: reasoning buys efficiency, but the bought efficiency doesn't keep pace as the reasoning model scales.

## Notable side-findings

- **Llama 3.1 dropped at the smoke gate:** 8b emits no `CONFIDENCE` line (0/2 parsed), 70b only 3/4 — it doesn't follow the elicitation protocol, so its ladder has no usable small-rung data. (Protocol non-compliance as a model property, cf. the 122B collapse in PR #22.)
- **Logprobs aren't dead after all (new):** probing newer open models, `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b` delivers usable answer-token logprobs *end-to-end through the harness* (`elicitation=logprob`, not the fallback); `stepfun/step-3.7-flash` and `inclusionai/ling-2.6-flash` deliver raw token logprobs too (Ling flaky through the solver). Every newer *frontier*-open model still returns `null` (DeepSeek V4, GLM-5.1, Gemma 4, Qwen3.6, MiniMax M3). This revives the RQ3 logprob arm on open weights — filed as the next experiment (granite three-way: logprob vs verbalized vs sampling on the anchors), and the cheap precursor to the Step-2 introspection flagship.

## Verification

- 39 tests pass, `validate_pipeline.py` → PIPELINE OK (CI from #21 runs both).
- All 48 runs `status: success`; smoke-gated each family (caught the Llama non-compliance and the reflect-arm parse weakness on small models before the full matrix).
- Cross-family figure recomputes pooled metrics from raw logs across both this run and the published runs dir (`scripts/rq1_crossfamily.py`).

## Caveats

- 5 families is still small; the non-reasoning side is genuinely mixed (Ministral neither clearly rises nor cleanly falls once the 3b artifact is set aside).
- "reasoning vs non-reasoning" is a coarse binary, confounded with family/training recipe; the clean comparison is the within-family scale trend.
- Custom-set domain cells are n=15; pooled numbers lean on the 300–817-item anchors.

## Bead candidates

- **RQ3 logprob revival** on granite-4.1-8b (+ step-3.7-flash): three-way logprob/verbalized/sampling sensitivity on the anchors, where granite isn't pegged at conf=100.
- Reasoning-mode ablation on the *new* reasoning family (Qwen3 dense on/off) to confirm the decline tracks reasoning within yet another family.
- Robustness pass on frontier-open families (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.x) — verbalized/sampling only (no logprobs).

## E1 — Folders + nested + drag-drop reparent

First Plan E (file manager) item. The `folders` table existed but was unused; this wires the full folder foundation.

### Data layer
- **`folder-tree.ts`** (pure, db-free, client-safe): `buildTree` (orphan-safe nesting, name-sorted), `folderPath` (root→leaf, cycle-safe), `wouldCreateCycle` (rejects self/descendant moves). 16 unit tests.
- **`folders-repo.ts`**: `createFolder`, `listFolders`, `renameFolder`, `moveFolder` (cycle-guarded), `deleteFolder` (transactionally reparents child folders **and** docs to the grandparent so nothing is orphaned). All owner-scoped.
- **`repo.ts`**: `listDocumentsInFolder(ownerId, folderId|null)`, `moveDocument`. 7 integration tests (real Postgres via testcontainers).

### API
- `/api/folders` GET/POST · `/api/folders/[id]` PATCH (rename / move → **409 on cycle**) / DELETE · `/api/docs/[id]/move` POST · `/api/docs?folder=<id|root>` GET. All `authenticateRequest`-gated.

### UI — `/files` is now a client `FileManager`
Nested folder tree (left rail), breadcrumb navigation, subfolder + document rows, "+ New folder". Native HTML5 drag-drop reparenting: drag a doc or folder onto any folder (tree or list) or the Root zone; cycle attempts surface an alert.

### Verification (production build)
- ✅ Create folder + nested subfolder; navigate via tree + breadcrumb
- ✅ Drag a doc into a folder (root list 23→22, doc present in target folder)
- ✅ Drag a folder onto its own descendant → blocked (409 → "Can't move a folder into itself")
- ✅ Drag a folder to Root → valid reparent (depth 0)

author: tzero78
body:
## Was

Die virtuelle IP wird aus **zwei** Bytes von `SHA-256(pubkey)` abgeleitet statt aus einem — also `10.66.X.Y` über ein `/16` statt `10.66.0.X` über ein `/24`.

## Warum

Vorbereitung für **Multi-Buddy** (BuddyShare): dort authentifiziert die virtuelle IP den Peer. Mit nur 1 Byte (254 Adressen) liegt der Birthday-Bound bei ~20 Nodes — zwei Buddies könnten sich dieselbe IP teilen. Mit 2 Bytes (~65534 Adressen) steigt er auf ~300 Nodes bei 1% Kollisionswahrscheinlichkeit.

## Reserviert

Nur die all-zeros Netzadresse (`10.66.0.0`) und der all-ones Broadcast (`10.66.255.255`) werden auf `.0.1` / `.255.254` gefaltet.

## Breaking change

Jede Node bekommt eine **neue** virtuelle IP → Buddies müssen nach dem Update neu pinnen. Protocol `Version` 4 → 5.

## Tests

`gofmt` clean, `go vet` clean, `go test -race ./...` grün, `go build ./...` ok.

author: w4rppy
body:
Kafka Connect never auto-restarts a task once it goes FAILED. A Debezium source task that hits the producer delivery.timeout.ms (e.g. a brief WarpStream produce-path outage) fails permanently, and while it is down its Postgres logical-replication slot stops advancing -- retained WAL grows until the source disk fills.

Add an opt-out CronJob (every 2 min, enabled by default when connectors are declared) that polls the worker REST API and restarts only the FAILED parts of any affected connector via
POST /connectors/<name>/restart?includeTasks=true&onlyFailed=true. It needs no RBAC and runs under a deny-by-default egress NetworkPolicy (worker REST port + DNS only).

- new template connector-autorestart-cronjob.yaml (CronJob + NetworkPolicy)
- values: connectorAutoRestart.{enabled,schedule,image,networkPolicy}
- bump chart 0.5.1 -> 0.6.0 and document the safety net in the README

## What

`inderes forum momentum` — ranks **every cached topic** by how much it's heating up, descending. For each topic it computes the same momentum read as `forum activity` (latest bucket vs the average of the rest) and sorts. Table output + `--json`; `--bucket`/`--periods` like `activity`.

This is the cross-topic payoff of the cache: cache a watchlist, `forum refresh-all` to keep it current, then `forum momentum` to see which company the crowd is suddenly talking about.

## Honest framing

An attention/interest signal over **cached** data — noisy (small-sample ratios can rank tiny threads high; the output shows `latest`/`avg` so you can judge), and only as fresh as your last refresh. Output says so. Deterministic; no model.

## Notes

- Pure glue over existing tested pieces: `cache.activity()` + the `momentum()` helper; topics with <2 active buckets are excluded from the ranking.
- Documented in README + all three skills.

## Testing

- `momentum()` math is unit-tested; bucketing is unit-tested.
- `fmt` + `clippy -D warnings` + `cargo test` (165 tests) + markdownlint clean.
- Live: cached 3 topics → ranked table (1.2x / 0.9x / 0.4x) → `--json` → empty-cache message.

body:
## Summary

Two presentation-layer fixes to the overworld tileset rendering in `WorldMap.jsx`:

1. **Eager tilesheet preload**: PNG loading now begins at module evaluation time (not just on first `MapTile` mount), eliminating intermittent flat-color tile pop-in during early exploration.

2. **Directional fog edge mask**: Replaced the single radial-gradient fog edge effect with per-direction linear-gradient masks that fade tiles only on unrevealed sides. Gradients are composited with `mask-composite: intersect` so fades multiply at corners, creating a more natural boundary effect.

No engine or state changes.

## Key Changes

- **`src/ui/overworld/WorldMap.jsx`**
  - Call `_startSheetLoad()` at module scope (line 60) to begin PNG loading at import time
  - Replace `isFogEdge: boolean` prop with `fogSides: {w, e, n, s} | null` to track unrevealed directions per tile
  - Build composite `mask-image` from directional linear-gradients in `MapTile` render
  - Apply `mask-composite: intersect` (and webkit equivalent `source-in`) so each direction's fade applies independently
  - Add `data-fog-sides` attribute to revealed boundary tiles for test assertions
  - Remove `.ow-fog-edge` CSS rule; box-shadow and mask now applied inline

- **`tests/e2e/overworld-tileset.spec.ts`**
  - Add 3 new Playwright tests per viewport (desktop + mobile):
    - Eager preload 2 s budget assertion
    - Directional gradient shape and direction validation via `data-fog-sides`
    - Interior tile no-mask check after movement

- **`docs/MECHANICS_INDEX.md` & `docs/CURRENT_SPRINT.md`**
  - Document fixes with implementation details and test coverage

## Implementation Details

- Directional masks use `linear-gradient(to <direction>, transparent 0%, black 35%)` per active side
- `mask-composite: intersect` multiplies alpha channels so pixels only stay opaque where every active gradient allows it
- Corners naturally darken where two fades overlap
- `data-fog-sides` attribute lists active sides as comma-separated string (e.g., `"w,n"`) for Playwright test hooks
- Interior tiles (all neighbors revealed) have `fogSides: null` and no mask applied

### Motivation
- Provide a pluggable managed S3-compatible backend so Temps can keep `rustfs` as the default while allowing operators to choose other S3-compatible engines (first-class support for `garage`) without compiling AGPL code into the main binary.
- Let S3/Blob services preserve the same app-facing S3 environment variables while making backend lifecycle (provision, bucket/key management, credentials, health, backup/restore, migration) backend-specific and manageable by either in-process drivers or out-of-process provider binaries.

### Description
- Add a new managed-S3 protocol module `crates/temps-providers/src/externalsvc/managed_s3.rs` which defines `ManagedS3BackendKind`, `ManagedS3BackendSelection`, request/response types, and the `ManagedS3Backend` trait for lifecycle hooks.

author: randallmlough
body:
## PowerSync PR-A — additive backend infrastructure (unwired)

First of the 6-PR PowerSync migration (**A → B → C1 → C2 → D → E**). Lands the **entire new backend** as additive, off-graph infrastructure: Postgres schema + migrations, the self-hosted PowerSync service + sync-stream config, the self-host docker-compose, the node-postgres client, and the developer-owned `/api/data` write endpoint with full Tier-1/Tier-2 hardening.

**Nothing in the running app imports any of it.** The app still boots on Turso; `make verify` stays green. Landing the backend first makes the later irreversible cutover (PR-C2) a small re-point instead of a big bang.

Executed from `plans/020-powersync-pr-a-backend-infra.md` (reconciled to baseline `35f6d0a0`).

## What's in it

- **pg schema** (`db/schema/postgres/{directory,product,index}.ts`) — `pg-core` mirror of the libsql directory + product tables.
- **Migrations** — generated `0000` + hand-authored `0001_powersync_publication.sql` (`CREATE PUBLICATION powersync …`) with journal/snapshot.
- **`db/server/pg-client.ts`** + `readPostgresConfig()` in `lib/env.ts` (additive; unwired).
- **`/api/data`** — `lib/api/data/{handler,columns}.ts` + thin lazy route `app/api/data+api.ts`. Sub-only Clerk `verifyToken` (no `getUser` round-trip) → `clerk_user_id → users.id`; one pg transaction; per-op table + per-column allow-listing; per-row membership authz; LWW by `updated_at`; tombstone monotonicity; `updated_at` clamp; 4xx-terminal vs 5xx-transient status classing.
- **Infra** — `infra/powersync/{service,sync-config}.yaml` (production form: Clerk `jwks_uri` only, **no static dev JWKS**, no `api.tokens`) + `infra/docker-compose.yaml` (`wal_level=logical`, schema authority = drizzle migrations).
- **Acceptance tools** — `tools/{clerk-token-test,synced-rows}.mjs` (real Clerk tokens; no `jose`/static key).

## Decisions recorded here

- **Type divergence** — pg `items.quantity` = `text`, `items.position` = `double precision` (mirrors the authoritative libsql model; the spike's `integer`/`integer` is rejected).
- **Membership active-predicate** — `removed_at IS NULL` (no `status` column), consistent across the schema index, handler authz, and all sync streams.
- **Decision-9 `item_checks`** — `id` pk, `item_id` UNIQUE, `checked_at`, `checked_by_user_id`, `updated_at` (no `user_id`, no composite, no `deleted_at`). Uncheck sets `checked_at = NULL` — never hard-deletes.
- **pg `households` deliberately omits** `turso_db_name` / `provisioning_completed_at` — those are libsql/Turso-only, survive through PR-C1, and are dropped in PR-C2.

## Cross-PR ownership pins

- **PR-A owns** `db/schema/postgres/*`, `postgres.config.ts`, the pg migrations + `0001` publication, `pg-client.ts`, `/api/data`, `infra/**`, and the two `.mjs` tools. The `service.yaml` production form is finalized here (PR-E only verifies it).
- PR-C1 keeps Turso provisioning reading `turso_db_name`/`provisioning_completed_at` from the **surviving libsql directory**; **PR-C2 is the sole PR that drops them**.

## Verification

- `make verify` → **exit 0** (typecheck + Biome + eslint-rules + ESLint + 66 suites / 609 Jest tests).
- `env -u DATABASE_URL make db-generate` → idempotent; no libsql migration regression; no pg clobber.
- libsql world **byte-identical** to baseline; app/service import graph never reaches the new pg code (only the unwired route references the handler).
- `lib/api/data/handler.test.ts` — 12 unit tests over injected deps (no live Postgres): 401, 4xx-terminal (unknown table / disallowed column / malformed batch), 403 authz, 5xx-transient, LWW skip, tombstone monotonicity (409), `updated_at` clamp, Decision-9 uncheck, `item_checks` LWW conflict.

## Deferred — operator action

- **Step 14 (live acceptance gate) is NOT run** and is the reason this is a **draft**: bring up `infra/docker-compose.yaml`, apply the pg migrations + publication, then `tools/clerk-token-test.mjs` (expect HTTP 200 from `/sync/stream`) and `tools/synced-rows.mjs` (prove the 3-level `item_checks` join scopes to Members only). If the join proof fails, the documented Plan B (denormalize `household_id`) is an operator decision.
- The YAML/compose/`.mjs` are **outside `make verify`**; their live correctness rests on Step 14. `ctx7`/find-docs hit a monthly quota, so the PowerSync edition-3 schema could not be doc-verified — ported from the spike with the mandated production edits.

## Notes for deferred-hardening (PR-D)

The production `/api/data` path opens two pg pools per request (auth + transaction), and an unresolvable Household (empty resolution set) currently passes authz — both fine for an unwired, operator-gated endpoint, worth a line in `powersync-deferred-hardening.md`.

## Why

A parent asked why **Journal** and **Why This Path** both look like places to journal, and why they (a non-student) could see Why This Path at all.

- They're different jobs: **Journal** = things *done* (volunteering, hours, leadership, awards → résumé fuel). **Why This Path** = *why* you're pursuing the path (motivations/reflections → essay + interview fuel, read by the AI for essay help). The Journal blurb saying "…reflections" is what made them feel redundant.
- Why This Path was visible to everyone because its nav entry had no role gating (only authorship + per-entry privacy were gated).

## Changes

1. **Journal copy** (`JournalPage.tsx`): drop "reflections" from the header; the empty state now points the *why* to Why This Path. No more duplicate-journal feel.
2. **Why This Path student-only** (`motivation/nav.manifest.ts`): add `roles: ['student']`. `assembleNav` filters **both the menu and the route** by role, so parents/admins no longer see or can reach `/motivations`. The backend already enforces per-entry privacy; this removes the surface entirely for non-students.

## Verification

- frontend `tsc --noEmit` ✅
- nav + journal + motivation tests ✅ (29 passing; `canSee`/`assembleNav` role-gating covered)

## Note

This makes Why This Path student-only, which diverges from the spec's "family-visible-by-default, per-entry private" framing — parents can no longer see/encourage shared "why" entries. Done at your request; happy to update the spec to match.
