author: juherr
body:
## Summary

This PR moves TestNG away from maintaining its own assertion library, as discussed in testng-team/testng-asserts#15 and
testng-team/testng#3197. It deprecates `org.testng.Assert`, migrates TestNG's own tests to AssertJ, starts delegating
`Assert` to AssertJ where it is safe to do so, and turns `testng-asserts` into a separate, optional
published artifact.

The work is split into self-contained commits so it can be reviewed phase by phase.

## Motivation

- testng-team/testng-asserts#15 — deprecate the internal assertion API and let users pick their preferred library.
- testng-team/testng#3197 — make the `testng-asserts` module optional.

The OpenRewrite recipe `org.openrewrite.java.testing.testng.TestNgToAssertj`
(rewrite-testing-frameworks ≥ 3.39.0) now covers the whole `Assert` class, so users can migrate
automatically. That makes deprecation realistic.

## What's in this PR

| Commit | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Deprecate `org.testng.Assert` | `@Deprecated(since = "7.13.0", forRemoval = true)` + a migration guide (`docs/MIGRATING_ASSERTIONS.md`). |
| Migrate internal tests | ~500 `testng-core` test files rewritten off `org.testng.Assert` to AssertJ via a one-shot OpenRewrite run (no plugin left in the build); `assertj-core` bumped 3.23.1 → 3.27.7. |
| Delegate behaviour-identical checks | `assertNull`/`assertNotNull`/`assertSame`/`assertNotSame` now delegate to AssertJ. |
| Delegate `assertThrows` | `assertThrows` now delegates to AssertJ; `expectThrows` is kept (it returns the caught exception). |
| Publish `testng-asserts` standalone | Removed from the `testng` fat jar; published as `org.testng:testng-asserts` depending only on AssertJ. |
| Document OSGi limitation | `testng-asserts` ships as a plain jar for now (see below). |

## Design decisions

- **Targeted, not full, delegation.** Only assertions whose semantics are identical to AssertJ are
  delegated (`assertNull`/`NotNull`/`Same`/`NotSame`, `assertThrows`). `assertEquals`/`assertNotEquals`
  and the collection/map/array variants **keep TestNG's own comparison semantics**, which differ from
  AssertJ on purpose (symmetric equals, `equals()` not trusted against `null`, nested arrays compared
  by reference unless using `assertEqualsDeep`). This preserves the existing behaviour contract and
  its regression tests (#2483, testng-team/testng#2486, testng-team/testng#2490, testng-team/testng#2500, `ArrayEqualityAssertTest`). The divergence is
  documented with a `NOTE` comment in `Assert`.
- **Failure-message changes.** The delegated assertions now produce AssertJ-formatted failure
  messages. This is the only user-visible behaviour change and is noted in `CHANGES.txt`.
- **`expectThrows` unchanged.** It returns the caught exception, which AssertJ's fluent API does not
  expose, so it stays on TestNG's implementation (its exact-message tests keep passing).

## ⚠️ Packaging change for users

`org.testng.Assert` is **no longer bundled** in the `org.testng:testng` jar. To keep using it, add:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.testng</groupId>
  <artifactId>testng-asserts</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

which brings AssertJ transitively. The recommended path is to migrate to AssertJ (see
`docs/MIGRATING_ASSERTIONS.md`).

## OSGi

`testng-asserts` is published as a plain jar, **not** an OSGi bundle: `org.testng.Assert` and
`FileAssert` share the `org.testng` package with the core classes exported by the `testng` bundle,
so a `testng-asserts` bundle re-exporting `org.testng` would create a split package. Proper OSGi
support needs dedicated design and is left as a follow-up.

## Testing

- `:testng-asserts:test` — 181 passed
- `:testng-core:test` — 12474 passed
- `:testng-test-osgi:test` — 4 passed
- `./gradlew autostyleCheck` — clean
- Verified the merged `testng` jar no longer contains `org/testng/Assert*`, and the published
  `testng-asserts` POM depends only on `org.assertj:assertj-core`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- OSGi bundle metadata for `testng-asserts` (split-package handling).
- Wider delegation / further deprecations (e.g. `FileAssert`, the OO `Assertion`/`SoftAssert` API).

author: frankbardon
body:
Effort: storage-backends

Pluggable storage layer for lattice. Single PR; commits streamed in as stories completed across 3 epics.

## What shipped
- **`Store` interface** (`internal/storage`) — dumb blob store addressed by `manifest.id`: `Load`, `Save`, `List`, `Exists`, `Delete` over whole documents.
- **Filesystem backend** — afero-backed, `<id>.json` mapping, atomic temp+rename writes, filename-safe id validation.
- **Git backend** — pure-Go go-git working-tree repo: commit-on-save / commit-on-delete, init-on-absent root, author from repo git config with a lattice fallback, path-scoped staging (never `git add .`).
- **Versioning capability** (`VersionedStore`) — `History(id)` + `LoadAt(id, rev)` (revision = commit hash); implemented by git only, FS opts out.
- **CLI integration** — `--store fs|git` + `--root` on `resolve`/`serve`; positional arg = `manifest.id` when a flag is set, else a file path (direct-path loading retained). Resolver gained `ResolveBytesWithValues` (no pipeline duplication).
- **Docs** — `docs/src/reference/storage.md` + error-codes/out-of-scope updates.

## Epics
- **E1** Filesystem persistence — E1-S1 interface+Load/Save · E1-S2 List/Exists/Delete · E1-S3 tests. (milestone)
- **E2** Versioned git persistence — E2-S1 commit-on-save · E2-S2 History/LoadAt · E2-S3 tests. (milestone)
- **E3** Selection + integration — E3-S1 flags+factory · E3-S2 load-by-id · E3-S3 docs. (milestone)

All 9 stories in-review.

## QA results
- `go test ./...` — all packages green (uncached).
- `gofmt -l .` clean; `go vet ./...` clean; `mdbook build docs` exit 0.
- New coverage: FS suite (round-trip, keying, atomicity, unsafe-id), git suite (commit counts, staging isolation, history, load-at-revision, author fallback — OsFs+t.TempDir, no system git), factory (unknown store → coded error), load-by-id (resolve by id + not-found).
- Direct-path `resolve <file>` unchanged; existing golden/CLI/server tests still pass.
- Included a `chore: gofmt` for pre-existing drift in `internal/variables/override_test.go` to keep CI green.

## Out of scope (documented, future efforts)
JSON Patch apply→save pipeline; database adapter.

Release intent: **minor → 0.2.0** (tagged by \`flow-finalize\` after explicit approval). \`flow-finalize\` merges this PR.

author: tupe12334
body:
## Why

The server resolves its bind/probe address from the `MOADIM_BIND_ADDR` environment variable, falling back to `127.0.0.1:5784` (`src/cli.rs`):

```rust
const BIND_ADDR_ENV: &str = "MOADIM_BIND_ADDR";
pub fn bind_addr() -> String {
    std::env::var(BIND_ADDR_ENV).unwrap_or_else(|_| BIND_ADDR.to_string())
}
```

But the README never documents it — the override was source-only, and every example (plus the `--json` payloads) hardcodes `127.0.0.1:5784`, which misleads anyone who relocates the server. Because the override changes both the bind **and** the client probe target, a client invoked without the same value keeps looking at the default port and wrongly reports the relocated server as not running.

## What

- Adds a **Bind address** subsection under *Running* documenting `MOADIM_BIND_ADDR`.
- Shows the server + client usage (both must share the value) and the export-it-to-persist tip.
- Notes that the `127.0.0.1:5784` addresses elsewhere in the docs/JSON are the default and follow `MOADIM_BIND_ADDR` when set.

Closes #417.

Docs-only change — no `src/`/`ui/` touched, so the changelog gate is exempt. `cargo fmt --check` and `typos` are clean.

author: himanshugoel2797
body:
## What

Adds a namespaced module system to the kernel-resident Lisp so multi-file programs and reusable libraries are possible. Two special forms over the previously-flat global namespace:

- `(define-module NAME (export a b …) body…)` — evaluates `body` in a **fresh** env parented on the global env (internal defines stay private), then publishes the listed bindings as NAME's exports.
- `(import SPEC …)` — `SPEC` is `name`, `(name (prefix p:))`, or `(name (only a b))`. Loads each module **once** (idempotent), then binds its chosen exports into the caller's env, optionally prefixed/restricted so same-named exports from different libraries coexist.

Source is fetched by name through a pluggable loader hook (`lisp_set_module_loader`): the kernel maps a name to `./lisp/<name>.clp` in the initrd; host tests use an in-memory table. The returned byte range need not be NUL-terminated (the reader is bounded).

## Why it's sound

The module registry lives **inside the global env** (a hidden `%modules` binding), not a C static — the system-heap collector roots conservatively from the C stack + intern table, so a static `lisp_value` would be collected while anything hung off the always-reachable global env survives for free. The consequence: loading runs in the **single-core boot window** (before `lisp_gc_set_multicore` freezes the system heap), the same rule `load_clp` already follows. A `%loading` sentinel detects circular imports; a partial-failure tombstones its registry entry so a retry reports the real error.

## Verification

- **Host**: new `test_modules.c` — export/use, private bindings, transitive imports, prefix/only, idempotency (`eq?` identity of a re-imported export), empty module, multi-spec, unknown-module + cycle errors, failed-load retry. 20/20; full host suite green.
- **In-OS**: `virtio_net.clp` becomes the first multi-file program — it imports a new `driver-util` library (`nth`, the mutable word `cell`). Full QEMU boot (`NIC=virtio-net`): self-test `ALL TESTS PASSED`, driver reaches DRIVER_OK, ARP who-has/reply round-trip completes end-to-end.

Stacked on `claude/kernel-lisp` (depends on the interpreter). One reviewer pass already applied (sentinel cleanup, overflow-safe prefix buffer, `fail_b` consistency).

author: scoop
body:
## Problem

In the New Task launcher's **SEED FROM** picker (`PromptSources.svelte`), the sticky **mine & unassigned** chip (Issues tab) and the sticky search input (Commands tab) did not cover the rows scrolling behind them — mid-scroll, row text bled **above and around** the bar. "Looks really shitty" per the report:


## Root cause (reproduced in an isolated copy of the exact CSS at 360px)

1. `.ps-body { padding: 4px 2px }` — the **4px top padding** sits inside the scroll area, constraining the sticky bar to pin *below* it, leaving a band where a scrolled row shows **above** the bar.
2. `.ps-filter-bar` & `.cmd-filter` used `margin: 0 8px 4px` — the **8px side margins** made each sticky element narrower than the full-width rows, so text bled **around** it.

Both sticky elements shared the defect (Issues chip + Commands search input). `IssuesPanel.svelte` (Backlog) was already correct — no top padding, no side margin — and is untouched.

## Fix (CSS + one small markup wrap, scoped to `PromptSources.svelte`)

- Drop `.ps-body` top padding; relocate the breathing room to `.ps-head { margin-bottom }` — **outside** the scroll area, so no bleed band returns and the To-Do / non-overflowing lists aren't cramped.
- Make `.ps-filter-bar` full-width opaque (`margin: 0 0 4px`), insetting its content 12px via `padding: 0 10px` to align with the rows' text. Coverage comes from the flex-column `.ps-body`'s `align-items: stretch` (commented inline so a later edit doesn't break it).
- Wrap the Commands `<input>` in the **same** `.ps-filter-bar` the chip uses, so both tabs align identically and the input gets full-width coverage (a margin-inset input would re-open the side bleed).

## Verification

- New `PromptSources.browser.test.ts` (real-browser layout, same harness as `IssuesPanel.browser.test.ts`) asserts, while scrolled, the sticky bar (a) stays pinned to the scrollport top and (b) spans the full row width — on both the Issues and Commands tabs. **Both assertions fail on the pre-fix CSS** (verified by temporarily reverting), pass after.
- `cd ui && bun run check` clean; full UI suite green (**1720 passed**).
- Re-screenshotted all three tabs mid-scroll at mobile width: no bleed; chip/input aligned with rows; To-Do tab not cramped.

`fix:` shipping no new user-facing capability, no new/changed message keys → `[no-feature-entry]`, no i18n/catalog work due.

## Summary
PR-2 of the cloud-asset inventory series (extends #2961's AWS scanner to Azure + GCP), continuing to close the audit's top Wiz-parity gap.

- `cloud/azure_inventory.py` — storage accounts → `DATA_STORE`, VMs + NSGs → `CLOUD_RESOURCE`, managed identities → `MANAGED_IDENTITY` principals. `azure-identity` token/credential auth.

Azure NSGs / GCP firewalls aren't 1:1 with instances (subnet/NIC and network-tag scoped), so NSG/firewall nodes carry their own `internet_exposed`/`network_exposure` for the CNAPP overlay but no fabricated per-instance `EXPOSED_TO` edges. AWS instance↔SG linking unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Three small, surgical UI fixes requested in feedback — each commit is independent and touches only the relevant file/section.

1. **Trade Sheet header** — remove the green/red gradient background and coloured icon tile (Buy = green, Sell = red). Header is now neutral.
2. **QR Pay success messages** — clean up the cramped, awkwardly-punctuated success text into a proper title + subtitle layout.
3. **QR Pay account-number masking** — add an eye-toggle that hides the first digits of account numbers by default.

## Related issues

None — these are polish fixes on already-merged features (Stock Trading and QR Pay).

## Phase

- [x] Chore / polish (no functional change)

## Type of change

- [x] UI / UX polish

## What's included

### Commit 1: `42e74c6` — Trade Sheet header colors removed

File: `app/trading/page.tsx` (only the trade sheet header section)

| Element | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Buy header background | `bg-emerald-500/10 border-emerald-500/20` (green gradient) | Plain (no background tint) |
| Buy icon tile | `bg-emerald-600 text-white shadow-md` (solid green) | `bg-muted text-muted-foreground` (neutral gray) |
| Sell header background | `bg-destructive/10 border-destructive/20` (red gradient) | Plain (no background tint) |
| Sell icon tile | `bg-destructive text-white shadow-md` (solid red) | `bg-muted text-muted-foreground` (neutral gray) |

The icons themselves (ShoppingCartIcon for Buy, TagIcon for Sell) stay. The 'Buy Order' / 'Sell Order' title text still tells the user which mode they're in. Diff: +3 / −13 lines.

### Commit 2: `5f8a29e` — QR Pay success messages cleaned up

File: `app/qr-pay/page.tsx` (only the success-state construction + rendering)

**Before:**
- Single pay: `Paid Rs. 1,234.50 successfully!` — period in 'Rs.', comma in the number, exclamation mark, all crammed into one h2
- Group split: `Split created — settle your share in "Shared with me".` — em-dash, curly quotes, grammatically awkward 'in'

**After:** restructured the success card to show a clean title + subtitle.

Single pay:
- Title: `Payment Successful`
- Subtitle: `Rs. 1,234.50 paid to <requester name>`

Group split:
- Title: `Split Created`
- Subtitle: `Settle your share under Shared with me`

Implementation:
- `done` state changed from `string | null` to `{ title: string; subtitle?: string } | null`
- Success card layout updated: title in h2, subtitle in a muted text-sm paragraph (max-w-xs so it wraps cleanly), Done button with a small top margin, gap reduced from 4 to 3 for tighter grouping
- SinglePay `onDone` prop type updated from `(msg: string) => void` to `(result: { title: string; subtitle?: string }) => void`
- SinglePay success call now passes the amount + requester_name in the subtitle
- GroupSplit onDone now passes a clean title + subtitle

### Commit 3: `70fe5d5` — Account-number masking with eye toggle

File: `app/qr-pay/page.tsx` (new `MaskedAccount` component + 2 usage sites)

Account numbers in the QR Pay payment-request summary were displayed in full — a privacy concern when screens are shared or someone is looking over the user's shoulder.

New `MaskedAccount` component:
- **Defaults to hidden** — shows only the last 4 digits prefixed with four bullet characters (e.g. `1234567890` → `••••7890`)
- Eye icon button next to the number toggles reveal/hide
- `EyeIcon` when hidden (click to reveal), `EyeOffIcon` when shown (click to hide)
- Short values (≤4 chars) are shown as-is since masking is pointless
- Accessible: `aria-label` switches between 'Show account number' and 'Hide account number' based on state
- Accepts a `className` prop so callers can match surrounding text weight (e.g. `font-medium`)

Applied in two places where the raw account number was previously shown in plain text:
1. The `CardDescription` subtitle (`To account 1234567890` → `To account ••••7890 [eye]`)
2. The payment-summary box 'To account' row

Account numbers in the `SelectItem` dropdowns are NOT masked — those show `account_name + balance`, not the raw number, so masking doesn't apply.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch name follows `fix/` convention
- [x] All 3 commits authored by `ruwithma <itsruwithma@gmail.com>`
- [x] Each commit is surgical — only touches the relevant file/section
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes locally (exit 0)

- [x] No `console.log` introduced
- [x] No secrets or `.env.local` content in the diff
- [x] No database / schema changes
- [x] No API contract changes

## Notes for reviewer

### Three independent commits

Each commit is self-contained and can be reviewed independently. If you want to land only some of them, you can cherry-pick. They don't depend on each other.

### No conflicts expected

All three commits modify files that no other open PR touches (`app/trading/page.tsx` and `app/qr-pay/page.tsx`). The branch was cut off the latest `main` after the QR Pay feature merged.

### Accessibility

The eye-toggle button has proper `aria-label` that updates based on revealed state, so screen readers will announce 'Show account number' / 'Hide account number' correctly.

- `npx biome check app/trading/page.tsx app/qr-pay/page.tsx` → no errors

The user-facing defaults are locked for safer streamer use: local install under `~/Applications`, native AppKit setup, OBS + local overlay protection once OBS is ready, source-toggle OBS blackout mode, Safe sensitivity by default, and email/phone/secrets enabled while SSN/cards/national IDs remain off by default. ## Root cause / user impact The previous experience exposed internal tuning concepts (guard modes, pipeline names, raw OCR/lab status) directly in the menu bar and allowed unsafe starts when OBS protection had not been verified. That made the app easier to misconfigure and risked streamers believing viewer protection was active when the required OBS scene/source path was not proven. ## Changes - Added CLI-compatible packaging and lifecycle targets: - `make app` creates `.build/Stream Guard.app` - `make install` copies it to `~/Applications/Stream Guard.app` - `make uninstall` removes the installed app and LaunchAgent - Added LaunchAgent support for Launch at Login without requiring Xcode.app or generated projects. - Added a native AppKit setup/settings window with ordered readiness checks for Screen Recording, OBS websocket/auth, protected scene, blackout source, blackout test, and detector settings. - Made Start Protection refuse unsafe OBS protection until OBS readiness is verified. - Added OBS websocket password auth, Keychain-only OBS password storage, explicit OBS readiness states, and one-click Test Blackout. - Bundled the OBS Lua helper in app resources and show its path in setup. - Added user-facing config concepts for protection mode, Safe/Balanced sensitivity, sensitive text, safe text, and setup/readiness models while keeping JSON config compatible. - Added structured OCR observations with text, confidence, and bounding box. - Added block-first secret/token detectors for GitHub, OpenAI/API-key-like strings, AWS access key IDs, Slack tokens, JWT-looking strings, and private key headers. - Changed default pipeline to the existing ROI cascade/smart-crop path with full-frame remaining available internally. - Hardened diagnostics privacy by binding the local server to loopback, opening `127.0.0.1:8765`, and removing default wildcard CORS from JSON responses. ## Validation - Confirmed Command Line Tools path and tools: - `xcode-select -p` -> `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools` - `swift --version` - `clang --version` - `xcrun --find notarytool` - `make build` - `make test` - `make app` - `make install` plus installed app existence/executable checks - `make uninstall` plus installed app and LaunchAgent removal checks - `swift build -c release -Xlinker -sectcreate -Xlinker __TEXT -Xlinker __info_plist -Xlinker Resources/Info.plist` - `git diff --check` ## Known limitations This is still a local v1 install path and is not notarized for public distribution. Live OBS blackout behavior requires the user’s OBS instance and Screen Recording grant, so the automated checks cover readiness modeling, config/privacy behavior, packaging, and build/test paths rather than a real OBS session. --- ## Summary by cubic Rebuilt Stream Guard into a one-button, safer flow with a small menu bar UI and verified OBS protection. Adds a native setup window, Launch at Login via LaunchAgent, Keychain-based OBS auth, a local-only diagnostics server, and more reliable OBS readiness that ignores stale websocket failures; OBS protection now defaults to source-toggle mode. - **New Features** - Menu bar shows protection status, Start/Stop, Setup/Settings, Launch at Login, Advanced Diagnostics, and Quit; Start Protection is blocked until OBS readiness is proven. - New AppKit setup window with ordered checks (Screen Recording, OBS websocket/auth, protected scene, blackout source), one-click Test Blackout, Keychain storage for the OBS password, and a Launch at Login checkbox. - OBS client now supports password auth (challenge hashing), explicit readiness states, safe scene/source verification, ignores stale websocket failures during reconnect/readiness, and source-toggle blackout; bundled Lua helper is included and its path is shown. OBS protection is enabled by default and uses source control. - Packaging and login: `make app|install|uninstall` for a CLI flow; app installs under `~/Applications`; Launch at Login uses a LaunchAgent (no Xcode required). - Detection and defaults: OCR now returns structured observations (text+confidence+box); added secret/token detectors (GitHub/OpenAI/AWS/Slack/JWT/private key/API‑key‑like); default pipeline is ROI cascade; user settings for protection mode and sensitivity (Safe by default) are persisted; cards/national IDs remain off by default. - Privacy hardening: diagnostics bind to 127.0.0.1 and drop wildcard CORS; diagnostics page copy updated. - **Migration** - Build and install: run `make app` then `make install`, launch from `~/Applications`. - In Setup, save the OBS websocket password to Keychain, run Test Blackout, and grant Screen Recording. - Choose protection mode and sensitivity; edit sensitive/safe text; optionally enable Launch at Login. - Start Protection from the menu or Setup once all checks are green. Written for commit a7272c7bcc0aa2bc37121b3a6014943675923acf. Summary will update on new commits.

author: budokai-msi
body:
## What

Two self-contained UX/perf wins, both verified in-browser.

### 1. Route prefetch on hover/focus
`Link` now warms the destination route's `lazy()` chunk the moment a visitor hovers or focuses it, via a new `src/lib/routePrefetch.js` registry. The import specifiers mirror `App.jsx`, so Vite resolves them to the same chunk — hover warms it, click reuses it, navigation is instant instead of waiting on the dynamic import.

- Respects `Save-Data` and `slow-2g`/`2g` (no speculative downloads on metered/slow links).
- Each chunk warms at most once.
- Handles exact routes, dynamic detail prefixes (`/blog/`, `/compare/`, `/why/`, `/glossary/`), and single-segment city vs industry slugs.

### 2. Returning-visitor form autofill
New `src/lib/contactProfile.js` saves the visitor's OWN typed details (name/email/phone/company) to `localStorage` on a successful submit, and the booking form pre-fills them on return. First-party, local-only, strictly functional — not analytics, so no consent gating (and a visitor can clear it any time).

Wired into the booking form (`Book.jsx`) as the flagship; the helper is ready to drop into the other forms (Support, Exit-intent, Newsletter) next.

## Verification (browser, dev server)
- Hovering a `/book` link loads `Book.jsx` **before** the click (confirmed via `performance` resource entries).
- Seeding a saved profile and loading `/book` pre-fills all four fields.
- No console errors. `npm run build` + `eslint` clean.

## Note
Most of what was requested (code-splitting, view-transition animations, first-party session/cookie analytics, consent, lead capture) already existed and is untouched. These two were the genuine gaps.


## Summary by Sourcery

Prefetch route chunks on link hover/focus and add local contact-profile autofill for returning visitors on the booking form.

New Features:
- Warm route lazy-load chunks when links are hovered or focused to make subsequent navigation feel instant.
- Persist a visitor's typed contact details in local storage after successful submission and prefill the booking form on return visits.

Enhancements:
- Respect data-saver and very slow network conditions when deciding whether to prefetch route chunks.
- Support prefetch resolution for exact, prefixed, and city/industry slug routes via a shared route prefetch registry module.

## Why

`SWEEP_SCHEDULE` was documented as a cron expression and read into config — but **nothing consumed it**. The scheduler only ever used `SWEEP_INTERVAL`, so "run every day at midnight" was impossible. This finishes the feature.

## What

- **`internal/sweep/cron.go`** — a **zero-dependency** standard 5-field cron parser (go.mod stays dep-free). Supports `*`, values, ranges, lists, `*/n` steps, the dom/dow OR rule, and Sunday as `0` or `7`; `Next(t)` returns the next matching minute.
- **`scheduler.DueIn`** — with a cron schedule set, waits for the next matching time (and **does not** fire immediately on startup, unlike interval mode). Fixed-interval behaviour is unchanged. An invalid `SWEEP_SCHEDULE` **warns and falls back to the interval** (never fatal).
- **Banner** shows the cron expression when set.
- **Setup wizard** — new optional sweep section: enable sweeps, pick tasks from the **live catalog**, set a cron schedule + max tasks, with a validation hint, and a pointer for contributors on **how to add a task** (`internal/sweep/task_*.go`).
- **Docs** — `.env.example` sweep block, `CLAUDE.md` config table + loop diagram.

## Result

```bash
SWEEP_SCHEDULE="0 0 * * *"   # every day at midnight
```

## Tests

Cron parser: invalid-expression rejection, daily-midnight, specific-hour (strictly-after), `*/15`, weekday ranges, dom/dow OR, Sunday-as-7. Existing scheduler tests updated for the new signature. `go test ./...` + `go vet ./...` + gofmt clean.

author: fw-bot
body:
This commit does not bring native support for EPD on credit notes, only makes custom support a little easier and cleaner.

It is quite easy to support EPD (early payment discounts) on refunds by extending
- `_early_payment_discount_move_types`
- `_is_eligible_for_early_payment_discount`

However, this approach breaks when it reaches `inverse_tax_rep` in `_get_invoice_counterpart_amls_for_early_payment_discount_per_payment_term_line`, which assumes tax repartition lines with `document_type == 'invoice'` and raises when called on `tax_rep` lines of 'refund' type instead.

This commit fixes that by selecting source and target repartition lines according to the `tax_rep`'s document type, which ensures:
- the `.index()` no longer raises a `ValueError`, as `tax_rep` is now looked up in the matching set (`refund_` for refunds, `invoice_` otherwise)
- `inverse_tax_rep` returns the corresponding line in the opposite set, preserving the original invoice->refund mapping while adding the refund->invoice one

Since `inverse_tax_rep` is a closure, downstream modules cannot patch it without copying the whole ~170-line method. Making it symmetric here lets custom EPD-on-refund support work without that duplication.

author: jurij
body:
Closes #70.

## Problem

Only the current/last message rendered its picture in the notch; older image messages in the history were text-only — a `📷` placeholder with a caption or count — so a past album could never be viewed.

## Change

- **`HistoryEntry`** now carries its `[IncomingImage]`, the album's raw `caption`, and the per-image full-resolution `loadFull` loader. `Equatable` becomes **by-id only** (a stored closure isn't comparable, and entries are never reassigned after construction).
- **`NotchPresenter`** populates those fields when it builds the entry — so even a **live-absorbed** message (one arriving while the notch is already expanded) keeps its images and loader, without routing through the per-message `model.imageLoaders`.
- **Collapsed history row is unchanged** (still the `📷` label, one line). When the history is **expanded**, an image entry renders a new `HistoryAlbumGrid`: a lone picture fits its aspect, an album packs up to four square thumbnails per row — a compact echo of the current message's grid. Each `HistoryAlbumCell` paints its inline thumbnail at once, then upgrades to full resolution via the entry's loader, **caching the bytes on the shared model** (keyed by the unique r2Key) so a collapse→expand toggle re-decodes from cache instead of re-fetching.
- The history cells carry **no per-image copy glyph or hover Quick-Look preview** — those stay on the current message; the history echo is a read-only thumbnail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `HistoryEntry` carries its `[IncomingImage]` (+ per-image full-res loader)
- [x] Collapsed history row stays as-is (`📷` + caption/count)
- [x] Expanded history renders album thumbnails, lazily upgrading to full resolution like the current message
- [x] History stays RAM-only / ephemeral — no persistence of image bytes
- [ ] Verify several past image messages each show their own images *(code path verified; runtime visual check pending — see Test plan)*

## Ephemerality & capture safety

- RAM-only: entries live in `NotchPresenter.history`, pruned at the 60s window; full-res bytes live only in the `@Published` `model.fullImages` cache and deallocate when the next message replaces the model. No persistence path (`FileManager`/`UserDefaults`/`.write(to:)` etc. — none added).
- The loader's R2 GETs stay valid within the window: the blob TTL (66s) mirrors the 60s notch window and a GET is **not** delete-on-fetch, so concurrent re-fetches on expand are safe.
- New views render strictly inside the capture-excluded notch panel — no new `NSWindow`/`NSPanel`/`QLPreviewPanel`/`.help()`.

## Review

Ran a 4-dimension adversarial review (correctness/concurrency, ephemerality+capture invariants, acceptance completeness, layout/UX). **No actionable defects.** One LOW, intentional trade-off surfaced and documented in-code: the expanded history `VStack` is non-lazy (a `LazyVStack` would break the `HistoryHeightKey` measurement that caps the scroll region), so the first expand fetches the whole backlog — bounded by the 60s window, cached thereafter.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` (apps/macos) passes
- [ ] Send several image albums, let them scroll into history, expand → each row shows its own album, thumbnails upgrade to full-res
- [ ] Collapse→expand toggle does not re-fetch (served from cache)
- [ ] Captionless album, single portrait/landscape image, 2/3/4/5+ image albums
- [ ] Confirm history images never leak into a screen share (capture exclusion)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Known limitation (tracked: #94)

Cross-model review (`/review`) found that history image full-resolution **plaintext** is cached in `MessageDisplayModel.fullImages`, which is not pruned in step with the 60s history window (nor cleared on hide). So a viewed history album's decrypted bytes linger in RAM past their 60s row until the next message rebuilds the model. RAM-only (nothing on disk) and partly pre-existing for the current message, but #70 extends it to the strictly-bounded history tier. Shipping this PR as-is by decision; fix tracked in **#94** (P1, ~15 lines).

author: grimaldost
body:
## What

Surface a sample of per-run error text on errored trigger/holdout runs, so the cause (401 vs timeout vs network) is visible without a manual `claude -p` probe.

## Why

Dogfooding the harness on 2026-06-19 (`2026-06-19-eval-harness-auth-race` finding #3): an all-errored run reported `recall=0.00` / `specificity=1.00` but gave no hint *why* every spawn failed — the actual `401 Invalid authentication credentials` had to be recovered by probing `claude -p` by hand. `run_skill` captured each run's `is_error` bool but discarded `run.result_text`.

## How

- `distinct_error_samples(texts, limit=3, width=200)` — pure: groups raw error strings into up to 3 distinct samples, most-frequent-first, truncated, with occurrence counts. Stable sort keeps first-seen order on ties, so a single dominant cause reads as "the first non-empty `result_text`".
- `format_error_samples(samples)` — pure renderer; empty list on a clean run (prints nothing).
- `worker` now carries `run.result_text` **only on errored runs** (bounds memory) into `score['error_samples']`.
- Wired into both print sites of `run_triggers.main` (the INVALID all-errored branch **and** the normal partial-error path) and mirrored in `holdout_check.main`.

## Tests

5 new (TDD red→green): grouping/counts/ranking, blank-drop + limit cap, width truncation, renderer, and a `run_skill` integration guard that fails without the worker threading. All 23 `test_run_triggers.py` pass; ruff check + format clean.

No plugin version bump — the harness lives in `evals/harness/`, not a versioned plugin.

author: hakanpak
body:
## What

Telegram mention / command detection now slices message entities by UTF-16 code units, matching how Telegram reports `MessageEntity` offsets.

## Why

`MessageEntity.offset`/`length` are UTF-16 code units, but the parsing did `source_text[offset:offset+length]` — treating them as Python code-point indices. A single non-BMP character before the span (a leading emoji, CJK Ext-B, …) shifts the UTF-16 offset past the code-point index, so the slice misaligns. The concrete impact: in a `require_mention` group, a message like `😀 @hermes_bot help` has its `@mention` entity slice land on the wrong text, `_message_mentions_bot` returns False, and the bot silently ignores a message that explicitly addressed it.

## Change

- Add `utf16_slice()` next to `utf16_len()` in `gateway/platforms/base.py`.
- Use it at all three entity-slicing sites in `telegram.py` (`_extract_bot_mention_usernames` and `_message_mentions_bot`).

I checked the other adapters for the same class: Signal already converts code-point offsets to UTF-16 when building outbound entities, and Discord / Matrix don't address text by offset — so the three Telegram sites are the full surface.

## Tests

- `TestUtf16Slice` in `tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py` — slicing across non-BMP prefixes/spans.
- `test_mention_after_leading_emoji` in `tests/gateway/test_telegram_mention_boundaries.py` — a mention preceded by an emoji is now detected (fails before this change).

   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.1.0
   ```
   =========================

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes
---------------------------------------------------

- `14533 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14533>`_: When using :option:`--doctest-modules`, autouse fixtures with ``module``, ``package`` or ``session`` scope that are defined inline in Python test modules (not plugins or conftests) will now possibly execute twice.

  If this is undesirable, move the fixture definition to a ``conftest.py`` file if possible.

  Technical explanation for those interested:
  When using `--doctest-modules`, pytest possibly collects Python modules twice, once as :class:`pytest.Module` and once as a ``DoctestModule`` (depending on the configuration).
  Due to improvements in pytest's fixture implementation, if e.g. the ``DoctestModule`` collects a fixture, it is now visible to it only, and not to the ``Module``.
  This means that both need to register the fixtures independently.



Deprecations (removal in next major release)
--------------------------------------------

- `10819 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10819>`_: Added a deprecation warning for class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods (without ``classmethod``). Such fixtures set attributes on a different instance than the test methods use, leading to unexpected behavior. Use ``classmethod`` decorator instead -- by :user:`yastcher`.

  See :issue:`10819` and :issue:`14011`.


- `12882 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12882>`_: Calling :meth:`request.getfixturevalue() <pytest.FixtureRequest.getfixturevalue>` during teardown to request a fixture that was not already requested is now deprecated and will become an error in pytest 10.

  See :ref:`dynamic-fixture-request-during-teardown` for details.


- `13409 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13409>`_: Using non-:class:`~collections.abc.Collection` iterables (such as generators, iterators, or custom iterable objects) for the ``argvalues`` parameter in :ref:`pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref>` and :meth:`metafunc.parametrize <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize>` is now deprecated.

  These iterables get exhausted after the first iteration,
  leading to tests getting unexpectedly skipped in cases such as running :func:`pytest.main()` multiple times,
  using class-level parametrize decorators,
  or collecting tests multiple times.

  See :ref:`parametrize-iterators` for details and suggestions.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute is now deprecated.
  Use :meth:`config.getini() <pytest.Config.getini>` to access configuration values instead.

  See :ref:`config-inicfg` for more details.


- `14004 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14004>`_: Passing ``baseid`` to :class:`~pytest.FixtureDef` or ``nodeid`` strings to fixture registration APIs is now deprecated. These are internal pytest APIs that are used by some plugins.

  Use the ``node`` parameter instead for fixture scoping. This enables more robust node-based
  matching instead of string prefix matching.
  If you've used ``nodeid=None``, pass ``node=session`` instead.

  This will be removed in pytest 10.


- `14335 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14335>`_: The method of configuring hooks using markers, deprecated since pytest 7.2, is now scheduled to be removed in pytest 10.
  See :ref:`hook-markers` for more details.


- `14434 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14434>`_: The :option:`--pastebin` option is now deprecated.
  The same functionality is now available in an external plugin, :pypi:`pytest-pastebin`.
  See :ref:`pastebin-deprecated` for more details.


- `14513 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14513>`_: The private ``FixtureDef.has_location`` attribute is now deprecated and will be removed in pytest 10.
  See :ref:`fixturedef-has-location-deprecated` for details.


- `1764 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1764>`_: :func:`pytest.console_main` is now deprecated and will be removed in pytest 10.
  It was never intended for programmatic use; use :func:`pytest.main` instead.



New features
------------

- `12376 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12376>`_: Added :func:`pytest.register_fixture()` to register fixtures using an imperative interface.

  This is an advanced function intended for use by plugins.

  Normally, fixtures should be registered declaratively using the :func:`pytest.fixture <pytest.fixture>` decorator.
  Pytest looks for these fixture definitions during the collection phase and registers them automatically.
  For some plugin usecases the declarative interface can be cumbersome or unviable, in which case this imperative interface can be used.


- `14023 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14023>`_: Added `--report-chars` long CLI option.


- `14371 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14371>`_: Added :option:`--max-warnings` command-line option and :confval:`max_warnings` configuration option to fail the test run when the number of warnings exceeds a given threshold -- by :user:`miketheman`.


- `6757 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6757>`_: Added the :confval:`assertion_text_diff_style` configuration option, allowing
  string equality failures to be rendered as separate ``Left:`` and ``Right:``
  blocks instead of ``ndiff`` output.


- `8395 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8395>`_: Added support for :class:`~datetime.datetime` and :class:`~datetime.timedelta` comparisons with :func:`pytest.approx`. An explicit ``abs`` or ``rel`` tolerance as a :class:`~datetime.timedelta` is required and relative tolerance is not supported for datetime comparisons -- by :user:`hamza-mobeen`.



Improvements in existing functionality
--------------------------------------

- `11225 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11225>`_: :func:`pytest.warns` now shows "Regex pattern did not match" instead of "DID NOT WARN" when warnings were emitted but the ``match`` pattern did not match.


- `11295 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11295>`_: Improved output of ``--fixtures-per-test`` by excluding internal-implementation fixtures generated by ``pytest.mark.parametrize`` and similar.

author: galthran-wq
body:
Completes #23. The issue's first detector — pass-through wrappers (**SLP110**) — shipped in PR #36; this is the second: **single-use single-method classes**.

Flags a class with **exactly one non-dunder method** that is **instantiated in exactly one place** across the project — needless ceremony (a `Strategy`/`Manager` scaffolded for a single concrete case) that could have been a plain function.

```
class `Formatter` has a single method and is instantiated once — consider making it a function
```

## How

Like clone detection, this needs a cross-file view (the instantiation count), so it runs as a **whole-tree pass in the CLI** (a new `single_use` module) rather than a per-file registry rule, and is **preview-gated** (`--preview` or `preview = true`) — like SLP020/SLP090 it's a whole-project analysis, not in the rule registry.

- **Per file** (`scan_file`): collect single-method non-allowlisted classes, `Name(...)` instantiation targets, class bases, and self-instantiations.
- **Across the project** (`findings`, a pure function): flag a candidate iff its name is instantiated **exactly once** AND it's **never used as a base class** AND it **doesn't instantiate itself**.
- **Allowlist**: data/interface/exception classes (`Protocol`/`ABC`/`Enum`/`NamedTuple`/`TypedDict`/`*Error`/`*Exception` bases, or any decorator).

Conservative and name-based by design: a name reused across modules inflates the count and *suppresses* the finding rather than risk a false positive (biases to false negatives, never false positives — right for a preview rule).

## Tests

- **Unit** (`single_use.rs`): per-file scan (candidate detection, `__init__`+1 method, multi/zero-method, allowlists, instantiation/base collection) and the pure project-wide aggregation (instantiated-once flagged, reused/unused not, subclassed suppressed, **self-referential suppressed**, same-name suppression, count is project-wide).
- **Real-binary CLI e2e** (`crates/sloplint/tests/single_use_class_cli.rs`): runs the built binary and asserts, via `check --format json`, that SLP111 fires **only under `--preview`** and **only on the once-instantiated class** (`Formatter`, not the twice-instantiated `Reused`).

Reviewed by an adversarial reviewer subagent: it caught a real false positive — a self-instantiating recursive/builder class (`Node.add` returning `Node()`) was flagged. Fixed by tracking enclosing classes and exempting self-referential ones, guarded by a regression test; re-reviewed → APPROVE. `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and `cargo fmt --check` all clean.

body:
## Slice 4 of the dashboard aesthetic rehaul — Pass-1 #2 (re-point shared primitives)

Re-points the shared **Button** and **Input** primitives at the editorial register so amber (`--action`) is the single, unambiguous action color. Builds on slices 1-3 (#1173, #1177, #1178).

### Changes
- **Button**: new `action` variant — `bg-action text-action-foreground hover:bg-action-hover` (mirrors the existing `default` pattern; `action` is the Tailwind-mapped AA single-source amber `--action`).
- **Primary CTAs (15)**: wired the one genuine primary affirmative action on each *editorial-register* surface (settings / operator / connections) to `variant="action"` — Save, Connect (OAuth), Create, Provision, Send test, Confirm, Save Page, Try again, ... Secondary / add-row / cancel / destructive buttons are left unchanged, so amber marks only the one decisional action per surface.
- **Input**: focus ring now uses amber `--action` instead of the legacy ink `--ring` (inputs are focusable, so a live change, not dead CSS).
- **Tests**: co-located `button.test.tsx` + `input.test.tsx`, RED-proven before impl.

### Scope decisions
- **Onboarding flow NOT amberized**: its CTAs render via inline `style` in the **Stone & Weight** register (`--sw-*` tokens) — a distinct register from the authed editorial one. `variant="action"` is inert there (inline style wins), so wiring it would be dead/misleading and would drop a lone amber button into an otherwise-dark flow. Migrating onboarding wholesale to the editorial register is a separate follow-up slice. (An independent review caught the inert props; they were removed in the second commit.)
- **Brand-green WhatsApp Connect** keeps its `bg-[#008069]` brand color (variant removed); the success-card **Done** stays amber.
- **Excluded** (merge-stop-glob filenames): `settings/billing/page.tsx` Upgrade (`*billing*`) and `settings/governance-mode.tsx` Save (`*governance*`) — deferred to a surfaced follow-up.
- **Badge re-point** split to a follow-up slice (#4b): its real debt is hand-rolled `bg-yellow-500`/`bg-green-600` status colors needing a semantic `--positive`/`--caution` mapping with visual review, not an unused `action` variant.

### Verification
- Local gates green: typecheck, dashboard vitest (2415 tests), lint, format:check, arch:check, local-verify-fast, `next build`.
- Independent adversarial review: VERDICT SHIP; its one finding (inert variant props on style/brand-overridden buttons) was fixed by removing them.
- No schema, routes, env vars, or governance / auth / send-path changes.

body:
## What

Make baasdk shareable without exposing any real database, and tidy the docs.

### Public demo + local runner (`demo/`)
A tracked, **mode-aware** demo:

- **In-memory by default** (the public, spam-proof mode): runs entirely in the visitor's browser on `@baas/adapter-memory` — no server, no database, nothing saved. A banner states the mode. This is what GitHub Pages publishes, so a public visitor can never touch a real backend.
- **Real mode** only when a local `demo/config.js` (gitignored) sets `mode:"real"` with the runner's *own* Supabase + Convex URLs/keys. Never a shared backend.
- **`pnpm demo`** builds the bundle and serves `demo/` at http://localhost:8788. `demo/README.md` documents both paths and includes a copy-paste setup prompt for coding agents.
- **`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** builds the in-memory demo and deploys to Pages.

### Docs cleanup
- Prominent **"weekend project, not a product"** disclaimer at the top of the README (renders as a GitHub warning callout).
- Dropped the repetitive **"honest/honesty"** phrasing across the docs in favour of plainer wording.

## Safety

`demo/bundle.js` (build artifact) and `demo/config.js` (local keys) are gitignored — nothing secret is committed; verified no anon-key JWT appears in any tracked file. `biome.json` relaxes a few demo-only lint rules (a11y attributes, demo CSS, the reduced-motion `!important`, the script's env access) scoped to `demo/` + the runner; packages keep full linting.

## Verified

- `pnpm verify` green (143 tests, capability matrix + README quickstart in sync, no boundary violations).
- `pnpm demo` builds + serves; the in-memory flow tested in a browser: add todos, check off, switch provider → todos migrate across, all with no database.

## After merge

Enable Pages once: **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions**. The workflow then deploys the in-memory demo on every push to `main`.

author: tupe12334
body:
Closes #46

## What

Enables the Clippy restriction lint **`clippy::let_underscore_must_use`** (`deny`) via the `[lints.clippy]` table in `Cargo.toml`.

## Why

`let _ = <expr>;` on a `#[must_use]` value (notably a `Result`) silently discards it with no handling — no `?`, no `match`, no log. mdstore already denies `panic`/`unwrap_used`/`expect_used`/`unwrap_in_result` to catch *loud* error mishandling; this lint catches the *silent* counterpart, so a failed operation can never be thrown away invisibly. Fitting for a storage engine where I/O errors must surface.

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: add `let_underscore_must_use = "deny"` with an explanatory comment.
- No source changes needed — the lint surfaces **zero** violations on the current tree.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy --all-targets` — clean (exit 0)
- `cargo build` — ok
- `cargo test` — 113 passed, 0 failed

body:
## What this is

The **data-gathering** half of the playtest-gated calibration revisit (the largest open game-feel
concern in the close-out ledger): *passive players coast to Final 2 in ~half of seasons, then lose
there.* This lane **quantifies** that pattern and hands a follow-up tuning lane a ranked, concrete
menu. **No calibration constant was changed; no existing gate was weakened.**

## What landed

- **Instrument** — `tests/calibration/calibrationInstrument.test.ts`: plays a configurable number
  of seeded seasons under a **PASSIVE** and a minimal-**ACTIVE** player policy over the **same**
  live runtime `main.ts` composes (`composeRuntime` → registry → orchestrator spine, pure
  turn-driven). Both arms run the **same seeds**, so any gap is a real, attributable effect of play.
  It reuses the existing `juryReach`/`calibrationGradient` seeded-season driver pattern (no
  duplicated loop) and emits a machine-readable JSON + a generated markdown summary.
- **Data artifacts** — `docs/audits/data/2026-06-19-calibration-data.json` (per-season metrics +
  arm summaries) and `docs/audits/data/2026-06-19-calibration-data-summary.md` (generated table).
- **Analysis** — `docs/audits/2026-06-19-calibration-data.md`: measured distributions, the
  mechanical source (cited to the constants/code paths), and **ranked tuning recommendations** for
  the follow-up lane.

## Headline numbers (30 seeds/arm)

| arm | reached F2 | won | **F2-and-lost** | F2 record (W/L) | mean comp wins @F2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **passive** | 43% | 17% | **27%** | 5/8 | 1.15 |
| **active**  | 53% | 7%  | **47%** | 2/14 | 1.25 |

- The concern reproduces: a passive player reaches F2 in **43%** of seasons and **loses there in
  27%** of all seasons (F2 record **5 win / 8 loss**).
- **F2 losses are landslides** — 16 of 22 are ≥5-vote margins (7-2, 8-1, 9-0); only 6 are close.
- **Counter-intuitive but real:** minimal-active play reaches F2 *more* (53%) yet wins *less* (7%
  vs 17%) — protecting allies drags a comp-strong rival to F2, and `gameRespect` is **relative**.
- **Wins are comp-earned cleanly** (winners avg 2.0–2.5 comps vs 0.6–1.1 for losers) — the
  anti-sycophancy teeth hold.

## Mechanical source (cited)

`juryConstants.ts` → `JURY_WEIGHTS.gameRespect: 0.9` (second-largest jury term) over the
**threat-free** `juryLean` (`jury.ts`, the D4/E33 ruling) makes the finale a near-deterministic
verdict on the *relative* public comp resume; an idle player brings no warm-relationship reservoir
to offset it (`relationshipConstants.ts` `IMPACT.*` never fired). `decisionConstants.ts` →
`DECISION.vote.bondKeepWeight: 0.35` + the active policy keep allies alive, so the active arm sits
beside a stronger rival.

## Top recommendation for the follow-up lane

**Lower `JURY_WEIGHTS.gameRespect` (0.9 → ~0.6–0.7)** — highest impact, low risk. It is the
dominant landslide driver and the reason active play wins less; trimming it lets an *earned*
relationship/reliability reservoir compete with a comp resume. Keep it the second-largest term and
re-run the instrument + the `juryReach` `EARNED_WINS` guard so wins stay earned. (Full ranked list,
incl. social-fold magnitudes, `reliability` weights, and `juryManagementWeight`, in the doc.)

## Determinism / Vault Wall

Any future randomized strategy draws from a dedicated `hashSeed`-forked sub-stream (`strategyRng`),
so the competition/vote RNG stream stays byte-identical and the juryReach/gradient gates are
unaffected. The instrument reads only Vault-free public projections; the artifacts are a
dev/calibration record, wired into no runtime player/admin path. Roles only — no houseguest names.

## Testing

`npm run typecheck` passes. The instrument was run as a single bounded vitest file
(`ORWELL_CALIB_SEEDS=30 npx vitest run tests/calibration/calibrationInstrument.test.ts`, ~6 min).
The heavy matrix / juryReach / gradient gates were **not** run here (OOM-prone host) and were **not**
modified — they run in CI's heavy-sims lane.

author: linguistic76
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request changes MonsterUI asset handling from runtime download behavior to committed, repo-managed vendor files, and adds tooling to keep those files in sync.

### What changed
- **MonsterUI vendor assets are now expected to be committed to the repository**
  - The `app/static/vendor/monsterui/` directory was removed from `.gitignore`, so these files are now tracked in git.

- **App startup no longer downloads MonsterUI files automatically**
  - The theme header logic now builds MonsterUI headers only from local vendor files.
  - If a required MonsterUI asset is missing, the app raises a clear error telling developers to run the sync command instead of trying to fetch files at runtime.

- **Added a developer command to re-sync MonsterUI assets**
  - New `./dev sync-monsterui-vendor` command downloads the current MonsterUI files referenced by the installed package and stores them in `app/static/vendor/monsterui/`.

- **Added validation to prevent stale or missing MonsterUI vendor files**
  - New `check_monsterui_vendor.py` script verifies that all expected MonsterUI vendor files exist locally.
  - This check was added into the existing quality checks flow, so upgrades to the `monsterui` package will fail validation until the vendor files are re-synced.

- **Updated developer help output**
  - The `app/dev` help text now documents the new sync command and when to use it.

### Functional impact
- The application now relies on **local, committed MonsterUI assets** instead of downloading them on startup.
- This makes startup behavior **offline-safe and deterministic**, while ensuring package upgrades are accompanied by updated vendor files through explicit sync and quality-check enforcement.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

- Descubrimiento dinámico de tracks: `track1.mp3`, `track2.mp3`, … `trackN.mp3`

### Para activar el carril live, sube los MP3 reales así:

```
# 1. Pon tus fuentes en audio-source/ y edita audio-sources-live.json
# 2. Normaliza:
npm run prepare-audio-live
# → genera audio-live/track1.mp3, track2.mp3, …, rodo.mp3
# 3. Commitea audio-live/*.mp3 (igual que hiciste con audio-test/)
# 4. Mergea y redeploya Railway con RADIO_ENGINE_TEST=1
```

**Formato requerido para los MP3:** 44100 Hz / estéreo / 128 kbps CBR — el script `prepare-audio-live` lo hace automáticamente.

- No toca `/radio/stream` productivo
- No toca `studio.html`, `sucursal.html`, `listen.html`, `panel.html`, `sw.js`

author: eburi
body:
Summary

This PR fixes startup metadata loss for restored sensor entities when discovery data is unavailable, while keeping the existing fail-open setup behavior.

Root cause

When sensor.async_setup_entry() falls back to _registry_sensor_specs() (discovery empty at startup), the fallback rebuilt DiscoveredEntity specs with blank metadata (unit/device_class/state_class/conversion set to None).

Those blank specs can produce units_changed_* and state_class_removed_* repairs warnings after restart.

What changed

custom_components/signalk_ha/sensor.py
- _registry_sensor_specs() now reconstructs metadata from:
  1) explicit mapping via lookup_mapping(path) when present
  2) otherwise entity registry persisted metadata:
     - unit_of_measurement
     - original_device_class / device_class
     - capabilities[state_class]
  3) spec_known=True when mapping or schema is known
- conservative conversion inference for non-mapped paths via schema+registry-unit alignment:
  - K to C (K_TO_C)
  - Pa to hPa (PA_TO_HPA)
  - ratio to percent (RATIO_TO_PERCENT)
  - rad to deg (RAD_TO_DEG)

Important non-change

No startup blocking retry loop was added in __init__.py. Entry setup remains fail-open and non-blocking as on main.

Tests

Updated tests/test_sensor_helpers.py to explicitly cover fallback behavior:
- mapped path restores full metadata + conversion + spec_known
- unmapped path restores persisted registry metadata
- schema-known path infers conversion when unit alignment indicates normalization
- schema-known path does not infer conversion when alignment does not match

Scope

This PR is limited to startup fallback spec reconstruction. It does not change runtime reconciliation behavior for already-created entities.

author: yetval
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sessions that carry recent vision images (a Telegram or Discord photo, a pasted screenshot, an attachment) silently fail to compact. The compaction cut-point estimator charges nothing for image blocks that live in user-message content, so the recent-token accumulator never reaches the keep-recent budget. The cut point stays at the earliest candidate and almost nothing gets summarized. For image-dominated recent turns the trim keeps essentially the entire transcript, the next provider turn re-overflows, and compaction churns without making progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`estimateTokens` in `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts` is asymmetric about images:

- the `toolResult` / `custom` branch charges `4800` chars per image block,
- the preflight estimator (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.ts`) charges `IMAGE_BLOCK_TOKENS = 2000`,
- but the `user` branch only sums `block.type === "text"`, so an image block contributes `0`.

Before (`user` branch):

```ts
} else if (Array.isArray(content)) {
  for (const block of content) {
    if (block.type === "text" && block.text) {
      chars += block.text.length;
    }
  }
}
```

Recent user turns persist image blocks directly into user content (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`). `findCutPoint` (same file) walks backward accumulating `estimateTokens`; with images scored at ~0 it never reaches `keepRecentTokens`, so `cutIndex` stays at `cutPoints[0]` and the trim is a no-op.

This is distinct from the closed issue #39573 ("cache-ttl does not strip image blocks"): that is the pruning mode not stripping image payloads; this is the cut-point estimator under-counting them. No open issue or PR covers it.

## Fix

Count image blocks in the user branch the same way the tool-result branch already does, factored into one shared helper so the two paths cannot drift again:

```ts
const IMAGE_BLOCK_CHARS = 4800;

function countContentBlockChars(content: Array<{ type: string; text?: string }>): number {
  let chars = 0;
  for (const block of content) {
    if (block.type === "text" && block.text) {
      chars += block.text.length;
    } else if (block.type === "image") {
      chars += IMAGE_BLOCK_CHARS;
    }
  }
  return chars;
}
```

Both the `user` and `toolResult` / `custom` branches now call `countContentBlockChars`. This is the right boundary: `estimateTokens` is the single owner of the per-message character heuristic, and the sibling surface (tool results) is folded into the same helper rather than left as a second hand-rolled loop. The preflight estimator keeps its own separate accounting and is unaffected.

## User Impact

Image-heavy sessions now compact correctly: the recent-token accumulator reflects the real cost of recent vision turns, so `findCutPoint` selects a later cut and the summary actually reduces context. This breaks the overflow / futility loop where compaction ran but never reclaimed space.

## Evidence

Regression test `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-image-tokens.test.ts` (3 cases): a 1.5 MB image scores the same as a user turn as it does as a tool result and at least 1200 tokens; and `findCutPoint` trims image-dominated user turns to the same cut point as an equivalent text-cost control instead of keeping the whole transcript.

Local gates (run against an identical copy in a checkout with installed deps):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-image-tokens.test.ts` (3/3)
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>`
- `oxfmt --check <changed files>`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and the core test tsconfig

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: compaction cut-point estimator under-counts user-message image blocks so image-heavy sessions never trim.
Real environment tested: the real `estimateTokens` and `findCutPoint` from `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts`, driven on pristine `origin/main` and on the patched tree with identical input: a transcript of 7 entries whose 3 recent user turns each carry a 1.5 MB screenshot, with `keepRecentTokens = 1500`. A harness fed this transcript through the real functions and recorded the observed cut-point decision.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <harness>` reverting only `compaction.ts` between runs; plus the committed regression test `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-image-tokens.test.ts`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main f9f94e7dcd)
scenario: 7 entries, 3 recent user turns each carry a 1.5MB screenshot
keepRecentTokens budget: 1500
estimateTokens(user turn with one image): 0 tokens
total estimated context tokens: 29
findCutPoint.firstKeptEntryIndex: 0
entries summarized (dropped from live context): 0
recent tokens retained after cut: 29
compaction makes progress: NO (no-op / futility loop)

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
scenario: 7 entries, 3 recent user turns each carry a 1.5MB screenshot
keepRecentTokens budget: 1500
estimateTokens(user turn with one image): 1200 tokens
total estimated context tokens: 3629
findCutPoint.firstKeptEntryIndex: 4
entries summarized (dropped from live context): 4
recent tokens retained after cut: 2406
compaction makes progress: YES
```
Runtime planner proof (the live session compaction path, not the estimator in isolation): a vision-heavy session of 11 entries whose 4 recent user turns each carry a 1.5 MB screenshot was fed through the real `prepareCompaction()` in `src/agents/sessions/compaction/compaction.ts` (the same planner the session runtime calls before `compact()`), with `keepRecentTokens = 3000`:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main f9f94e7dcd)
runtime entry point: src/agents/sessions/compaction/compaction.ts prepareCompaction()
settings: keepRecentTokens=3000 reserveTokens=16384
prepareCompaction returned a plan: yes
estimated context tokens before compaction: 0
messages the planner will summarize away: 0
first kept entry id: entry-0
compaction reclaims context: NO (planner summarizes nothing)

# AFTER (this patch, identical session)
runtime entry point: src/agents/sessions/compaction/compaction.ts prepareCompaction()
settings: keepRecentTokens=3000 reserveTokens=16384
prepareCompaction returned a plan: yes
estimated context tokens before compaction: 1200
messages the planner will summarize away: 6
first kept entry id: entry-6
compaction reclaims context: YES
```
The live planner under-counts the vision turns to 0 context tokens on main and therefore plans to summarize nothing (the futility loop); with the patch it values the images, plans to summarize the 6 older messages, and advances the kept boundary to `entry-6`.

Committed regression test (`compaction-image-tokens.test.ts`, 3 cases): 3 failed on pristine main (`expected +0 to be 4`, `expected +0 to be greater than 0`, user image scores 0), 3 passed with the patch.
Observed result after fix: an image-dominated session that previously summarized 0 entries (cut stuck at index 0, context unchanged, re-overflow loop) now scores each image user turn at 1200 tokens, advances the cut to index 4, and summarizes 4 entries so compaction actually reclaims context.
What was not tested: no live LLM summarization round-trip (the `compact()` call after `prepareCompaction`, which needs a model stream) and no end-to-end channel message run (Telegram/Discord image -> overflow -> compaction). The proof drives the real session compaction planner end to end with representative image and transcript inputs, which is the surface this change affects. Full `pnpm build` not run; the change touches no module/packaging boundary.

author: kojjob
body:
## What

SEO roadmap **Phase 0** — establishes a single source of truth for canonical/Open-Graph URLs and an (initially inert) apex-redirect plug. This is the foundation the rest of the SEO roadmap (Phases 1–6) builds on.

## The governing decision

**Subfolder URLs (`makola.io/s/:slug/...`) are the canonical, indexed surface. Subdomains and custom domains are a branding layer that point `rel=canonical`/`og:url` back to the subfolder.** For a marketplace of many tiny merchants, one strong domain consolidates authority instead of fragmenting it across hundreds of zero-authority hosts. The load-bearing consequence: canonical/OG URLs must be computed from the **configured apex**, never from `conn.host`.

## Changes

- **`EmakolaWeb.SEO.Canonical`** (new) — composes every public URL from `Endpoint.url()` (apex, driven by `PHX_HOST`) + the `/s/:slug/...` form, ignoring the request host. `store_url/1`, `product_url/2`, `category_url/2`, `blog_url/2`, `recipe_url/2`, `page_url/2`, `path/2`, `url/1`.
- **Pinned canonicals** — `product_detail_live`, `store_live`, `product_list_live` `handle_params` and `sitemap_controller` `base_url` now delegate to `Canonical.*` instead of deriving from the request `uri`/`conn.host`. So a page served on any host still emits one apex canonical.
- **`EmakolaWeb.Plugs.CanonicalHost`** (new, wired into `:browser` after `:accepts`) — 301-redirects configured alias hosts (`emakola.com`, `www.*`, Fly default) to the apex, preserving path + query.

## Ships dark 🌑

`CanonicalHost` reads `config :emakola, :canonical_redirect_hosts` which **defaults to `[]`** → pure pass-through until configured. It's wired in now but switches on by config only **after the makola.io DNS + TLS cutover** (redirecting to a host without a valid cert would break visitors). Verified harmless pipeline-wide: full suite green with the plug live.

## ⚠️ Merge order

**Merge this after #163 (the Makola rebrand).** Both touch `lib/emakola_web/components/seo.ex` and `lib/emakola_web/controllers/sitemap_controller.ex` (this PR changes URL logic; #163 changes brand strings — mostly different lines). After #163 lands I'll rebase this on `main` and resolve any trivial overlap.

## Follow-on (not in this PR)

The makola.io cutover config — `PHX_HOST=makola.io`, `marketing_url`, and populating `:canonical_redirect_hosts` (= `emakola.com`, `www.emakola.com`, `emakola.fly.dev`, `emakola.io`) — is the ops step that turns the plug on. Same event as the rebrand's deferred email-domain flip.

## Verification

- ✅ `mix test` — **3112 passed**, 0 failed (2 excluded) — includes the new `canonical_test`, `canonical_host_test`, and canonical assertions in `sitemap_controller_test` + storefront LiveView tests
- ✅ `mix format --check-formatted` · ✅ `mix credo --strict` — no issues
- Branch rebased onto current `main`; stray screenshots accidentally committed in `bd18ff0` removed

author: drquasney
body:
## Phase 2 — provider-aware publish routing (provably safe)

A workspace set to `publish_provider='bundle'` now **posts through the bundle.social adapter**. Buffer — every workspace's default — is **untouched**: the change is a single `if (provider==='bundle') return handleBundlePublish(...)` branch added *after the auth check*, before any Buffer-specific logic. The diff is **+63/−0, purely additive**, so the inline Buffer path is byte-for-byte identical and no Buffer tenant is affected.

**No workspace is on bundle yet**, so this ships as no-behavior-change too — the Move Better trial begins only when it's flipped (a separate, deliberate step).

### How
`api/_routes/publish/buffer.js` → `handleBundlePublish` mirrors the Buffer request/response contract so the client (`src/lib/publish.js`) needs **no change**:
- DELETE `{ bufferUpdateId }` → `BundlePublisher.deletePost`
- POST `{ platform, content, mediaUrls, scheduledAt }` → `BundlePublisher.publish`
- response `{ success, bufferId, scheduledAt, status, profileCount }` (`bufferId` carries the bundle post id, stored as `buffer_update_id` downstream)

### Known limits (ponytail — for the Move Better trial / Phase 2.x)
- **Multi-location GBP fan-out** (one bundle Team per `workspace_locations` row) is **not built** — a bundle GBP post targets the workspace's single Team / active GBP location. First trial covers **IG/FB + a single GBP location**.
- The Buffer-specific **sync/engagement crons** don't understand bundle post ids; they degrade (don't corrupt) for bundle posts.

### Verification
typecheck / lint / build / verify-bundles green. Diff proves the Buffer path unchanged. After deploy, the trial: flip Move Better → connect via portal → post via bundle, verified in your Chrome.

author: lbentovim1-sketch
body: ## Problem After Supabase config was corrected, the top bar (nav + sign-in button) rendered blank and the collector-activity panel stayed stuck on "Loading…". The cause: when Supabase was configured, `renderAuth()` / `renderNav()` / `routeFromPath()` / `loadHomeFeed()` were only called **inside** the `getSession()` promise callback. If that async call was slow, rejected, or resolved in an unexpected shape, the UI shell never drew and the whole header was empty — leaving the user with no way to sign in. ## Fix - Render the shell (auth area, nav, route, home feed) **synchronously on load**, before/independently of the async session check, so the header and "Sign in" button always appear. - The `getSession()` callback now re-renders once the session is known, and is wrapped in `try/catch` + `.catch()` so an auth/network failure can't blank the UI. - `onAuthStateChange` is likewise wrapped in `try/catch`. - Removed the now-redundant `if(!sb)` bootstrap line (the synchronous render covers both configured and unconfigured cases). ## Validation - Extracted client JS syntax-checked with `node --check` ✅ - `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` builds cleanly ✅

author: dheerajchand
body:
Closes #356.

## The bug

`warehouse` migrations `0006_partition_fact_tables` and `0007_monitoring_models` declare their parent dependency with the literal `("warehouse", ...)` instead of the app's registered label `("sw_warehouse", ...)` (`warehouse/apps.py` sets `label = "sw_warehouse"`). The migration loader resolves the mismatched app name to a `DummyNode`, so `manage.py migrate` aborts the whole graph with:

```
NodeNotFoundError: Migration sw_warehouse.0006_partition_fact_tables dependencies
reference nonexistent parent node ('warehouse', '0005_fact_electoral_contest_fk')
```

## Why this matters now

**CI on `develop` has been red since these migrations landed.** The `ci.yml` "Test suite" job runs `manage.py migrate`, which fails at this step for *every* PR — so nothing can reach CI-green. Confirmed via `gh run list --branch develop`: pushes #341–#345 all failed with this exact error. This is the sole reason the F-epic PRs (#352–#355) show CI-blocked despite passing local verification.

## The fix

Two one-line changes: `("warehouse", ...)` → `("sw_warehouse", ...)` in the two migrations' `dependencies`.

## Verification

- `grep` repo-wide: **zero** remaining `("warehouse", ...)` dependencies.
- Graph-consistency check: every `sw_warehouse` intra-app dependency now resolves to an existing migration node (0001–0007 all present).
- The full `migrate` runs under PostGIS in CI (no GIS locally) — this PR's own CI run is the end-to-end test; it should now pass the migrate step that every other PR currently dies on.

Scope-clean: touches only the two broken dependency lines, nothing else.

author: jolestar
body:
## What
- Add a limited GraphQL introspection fallback for providers that reject repeated introspection field usage.
- Detect GitHub-style `INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` errors and retry with a reduced introspection query.
- Normalize root type fields from the `types` index so existing schema parsing continues to work.

## Why
GitHub GraphQL rejects the default full introspection query because introspection fields such as `fields` and `args` are used too many times.

Closes #359

## How
- Keep the existing full introspection path as the default.
- On provider-limit introspection errors, retry once with a limited query that uses `fields` and `args` only once.
- Copy root type fields from the matching type definition before cache/schema parsing.

## Testing
- `cargo test test_limited_introspection --lib`
- `cargo test test_normalize_root_type_fields_from_types --lib`
- `cargo fmt -- --check`

author: tompassarelli
body: ## What A JS **lossless concrete-syntax-tree projector** + **identity-anchored `set-body`** edits, with a working pilot that expresses patch `0011` as a portable claim document instead of a textual diff. ``` tools/projector/ reflector.bjs parse (acorn) -> self-contained lossless CST -> render byte-identically set-body.bjs class-qualified `set-body`: locate (class, method) by identity, replace its body claims.bjs portable claim-doc: set-body verbs <-> JSON pilot-0011.bjs patch 0011 as a claim-doc; the equivalence + churn gates run-pilot.bjs one command: `bun run projector:pilot` ``` ## The reflector Each CST node is `{kind, segs:[literal…], kids:[cst…]}` where `segs` (length `kids+1`) interleaves the literal source between children, mirroring the `kind/v/child/seg` node vocabulary. `render` concatenates segs+kids using **only the stored data** — never the original source — so byte-identity proves the representation is lossless. **Round-trips 40/40 engine `.sys.mjs` files byte-identically.** ## The pilot (`bun run projector:pilot`) Patch 0011 edits two `newChannel` methods in two classes. As a claim-doc that's two **class-qualified** `set-body` verbs anchored to `(class, method)` identity, not line numbers. Against the pinned FF 152.0.1 upstream: - **GATE 1 — equivalence**: replaying the claim-doc onto pristine upstream reproduces patch 0011's output **byte-for-byte**. - **GATE 2 — churn-resilience**: after an upstream reflow (a sibling method inserted + a body line edited) the textual patch **`Hunk #1 FAILED`**, but the name-anchored claim-doc **still applies to valid JS** carrying both edits. ## Notes - Adds **acorn** (devDependency). Standalone tooling — **not** wired into the build or shipped binary. - The `(class, method)` anchor handles the common case (same-named methods across classes); a rename of the method *itself* is the deferred anchor-matcher. Live Fram-store persistence of the AST is a separate step (its ordering layer is mid-rewrite); this PR is the stable verb/CST layer. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: kreativmonkey
body:
Speeds up pipeline runs with two complementary caching layers.

### 1. Persistent dind image/layer store
`dind-storage` moves from `emptyDir` to a **40Gi truenas-iscsi PVC** (`forgejo-runner-dind`). Pulled images (golang, node24, action images) and docker build layers now survive pod restarts instead of being re-pulled every run.

### 2. actions/cache server
- `cache.enabled: true`, `cache.dir: /data/actcache` (persisted on the runner PVC).
- `cache.host: 172.17.0.1` + `container.network: bridge`: the cache server listens in the pod network namespace (shared with dind); job containers on dind's default bridge reach it via the deterministic gateway `172.17.0.1`. Makes `actions/cache` (e.g. `setup-go` module/build cache) work.
- Trade-off of the default bridge: no automatic container-name DNS, which only matters for workflows using `services:`.

### Misc
- `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` avoids recursively re-chowning the large dind image store on every pod start.

`actions/cache` fails soft, so even if cache networking misbehaves, jobs still succeed. Will verify with a real pipeline run after deploy.

author: muslim-adedamola
body:
### Merge reaching, multi-static, and dynamic obstacle envs into one repo

Consolidates the three Kinova Gen3 RL environments, previously split across a branch and a companion repo, into a single codebase. Each environment stays a distinct formulation with its own observation space, reward, scene, and trained policy. A shared config registry (`configs.py`) holds the per-env differences so `train.py` and `test.py` stay generic and dispatch with `--env {reaching, multi_static, dynamic}`.

### Structure
- `reaching/`, `multi_static_obstacle/`, `dynamic_obstacle/`: one package per env (`env.py`, `assets/`, `models/`)
- `common/callbacks.py`: shared checkpointing plus the dynamic curriculum and CSV callbacks
- `kinova_fk.py` (analytic FK for reaching) and `c_func.py` (CasADi FK for both obstacle envs) at root
- `kinova_model_reaching/`, `kinova_model_static/`, `kinova_model_base/`: separate scenes, since the reaching and static scene files differ

### Trained models
- Reaching and dynamic run from a fresh clone with their included policies and stats.
- Multi-static was retrained to regenerate its VecNormalize stats (the originals were lost), so all three now evaluate correctly.

### Notes
- All envs use `SubprocVecEnv` at a modest `n_envs` to avoid the open-file limit that surfaces as a MuJoCo resource-not-found error when many models compile in one process.
- `test.py` adds `--no-normalize` for a raw-observation render when stats are absent.
