## D4 Platform / Docker / Dev-Experience / CI regression (Apone)

Regression-verified the four platform criteria Stephen pinned against `e5eb6f0`.

### Criteria results
| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| **.NET 10.x backend** | ✅ `dotnet 10.0.100`, TFM `net10.0`, Release build of `Mahjong.Autotable.slnx` → **0 errors** |
| **Single Docker image** | ✅ builds + boots; `/health` healthy (db connected), `/autotable/` 200, **non-root UID 1000**, HEALTHCHECK **healthy** |
| **In-container smoke** | ✅ 4-bot Changsha game deals + discards (real motion: discards=3, melds=3, hands [13,14,10,13], 109 tiles, 0 page errors) — proof under `playtest-artifacts/screenshots/apone-regression-d4-*` |
| **VS Code F5** | ⚠️ **drift found + fixed** (below) |
| **CI board** | ✅ all active workflows green; `docker-smoke` stays disabled (stale red) — see below |

### F5 fix (Parcel → Vite drift, P1)
The Phase K W7 Parcel→Vite swap left the dev-experience configs stale, so hitting **F5** would launch a broken frontend watcher (`npx parcel watch …`; parcel is no longer a dependency):
- `package.json`: add `"watch": "vite build --watch"` (single source of truth)
- `.vscode/launch.json`: rename `Autotable (Parcel watch)` → `Autotable (Vite watch)`, command → `npm run watch`, update F5 compound reference
- `.vscode/tasks.json`: `autotable: watch` → `npm run watch`
- `README.md`: Parcel→Vite naming; the documented `npm run watch` now resolves
- add `mahjong-autotable.code-workspace` (README step 1 referenced a missing file)

Backend F5 path verified coherent: `backend: build` task produces the DLL at exactly the `launch.json` program path; `serverReadyAction` opens `/autotable/`. Fresh checkout still needs only one-time `dotnet restore` + `cd src/frontend/autotable-src && npm install`.

### docker-smoke (kept disabled, now with a real boot fix)
The smoke scripts crashed the Production image on boot — they never set a JWT signing key (`JwtSigningKeyProvider.cs:121` refuses to start when `Authentication:JwtSigningKeys[0]` is empty). Minted a per-run `Authentication__JwtSigningKeys__0` in `docker-build` / `auth-flow` / `chat-flow` / `token-rotation` smokes (mirrors Bishop's #96 fix). **4/5 smokes now pass locally.**

Schedule stays **disabled**: `jwt-rotation-smoke` can't green cheaply — `POST /api/auth/token` is now admin-session-gated (`AuthTokenController.cs:71-75` → 401 to the anonymous probe), so the mint→rotate→validate flow needs an admin-cookie bootstrap (Bishop's auth lane). Disable-rationale comment updated with the precise blocker.

🤖 Pure-platform regression pass — no backend/game-logic changes.

`src/` (the daemon — the core of the repo) was `ignore`d by eslint entirely. This brings it into scope.

**Restructured into two layers:**
- **Base (src/ + web/)** — type-aware TS + correctness (recommendedTypeChecked + stylisticTypeChecked). These are the rules **biome can't do** (it has no type info): `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`, `no-unsafe-*`, `await-thenable`. The async-heavy backend is where they pay off most.
- **React (web/ only)** — @eslint-react + react-hooks + jsx-a11y (backend has no JSX). web/ stays 0/0.

**This PR is coverage only — not enforcement.** `src/` surfaces ~1142 findings; the enforced `lint:eslint` stays web-only until src/ is burned down in reviewed batches, so CI stays green. A trial `--fix` broke a sessions test, so the daemon gets careful per-batch fixes, not a blind autofix.

Breakdown of the 1142: ~634 `no-unsafe-*` (typing `any` at JSON/webhook boundaries), ~69 real async-correctness bugs (floating/misused promises, await-thenable, require-await), ~110 empty blocks/fns, the rest mechanical.

author: olaf-scotec
body:
## What Changed

### Revit API — New context layer

Introduced a two-tier context abstraction that replaces ad-hoc `Document` / `UIApplication`
access across the codebase.

**Scoped contexts** (per-invocation lifetime):

- `IRevitContext` — `Application` + `Document`; available inside any event handler or external command.
- `IRevitUiContext : IRevitContext` — adds `UiApplication`, `UiDocument`, `ActiveView`; available in UI event handlers and external commands.
- `RevitContext` / `RevitUiContext` — internal implementations; enforce `IsValidObject` and
  `ObjectDisposedException` guards on every property accessor.

**Global (singleton) contexts** (add-in lifetime):

- `IGlobalRevitContext` — singleton access to `Application`; registered for both `RevitApp` and
  `RevitDbApp` add-ins.
- `IGlobalRevitUiContext : IGlobalRevitContext` — adds `UiApplication`, `UiDocument`,
  `ActiveDocument`, `ActiveView`; registered for `RevitApp` add-ins only.
- `GlobalRevitContext` / `GlobalRevitUiContext` — public implementations. `GlobalRevitUiContext`
  caches the `UIApplication` wrapper (1:1 relationship with `Application`).
- `RevitGlobalContextExtensions.AddGlobalRevitContext(...)` — two overloads for
  `ControlledApplication` (DB add-ins) and `UIControlledApplication` (UI add-ins); called
  automatically from `RevitApp.OnConfigure` and `RevitDbApp.OnConfigure`.

**Supporting utility:**

- `SerialDisposable` — thread-safe container holding at most one `IDisposable`; used internally
  by `GlobalRevitContext` to manage the `ApplicationInitialized` subscription lifetime.

### Revit API — Event handler context creation fixes

- `RevitPreEventHandler` and `RevitSingleEventHandler`: `CreateContext` now returns an
  `IRevitContext` wrapping `Application` when the sender is non-null, instead of always returning
  `null`. This makes `IRevitContext` available in the DI scope for pre-event and single-event
  handlers.
- `RevitPreDocumentEventHandler`: aligned `CreateContext` with post-document behaviour — prefers
  `args.Document` when available, falls back to `Application` sender.
- `RevitUiPreEventHandler`, `RevitUiPreDocumentEventHandler`, `RevitUiSingleEventHandler`:
  `CreateContext` now creates `RevitUiContext` from sender unconditionally, removing the
  `ActiveUIDocument != null` guard that prevented context creation when no document was open.

### DI — `RevitDbApp` global context registration

- `RevitDbApp.OnConfigure` now calls `AddGlobalRevitContext(Application)`, registering
  `IGlobalRevitContext` as a singleton. Previously this registration was missing for DB-level
  add-ins.

### XML Documentation

- All public and internal members across `IRevitContext`, `IRevitUiContext`, `RevitContext`,
  `RevitUiContext`, `IGlobalRevitContext`, `IGlobalRevitUiContext`, `GlobalRevitContext`,
  `GlobalRevitUiContext`, `RevitApp`, `RevitAppBase`, `RevitCommand`, `RevitCommandAvailability`,
  and all event handler convenience base classes received complete XML documentation.
- All `<see cref="..."/>` references across the affected files corrected to fully qualified
  Revit API type names, resolving CS1574 and CS0419 build warnings.

### Documentation

- `Documentation/RevitContext.md` — new developer guide covering the context interface hierarchy,
  lifetimes, injection patterns, registration, and common mistakes.
- `Documentation/RevitContextDesign.md` — updated design rationale explaining why singleton
  document providers are structurally inferior to scoped contexts, with accurate Revit API examples
  and comparison table.

## Risks

- `RevitPreEventHandler.CreateContext` and `RevitSingleEventHandler.CreateContext` now return a
  non-null context when they previously returned `null`. Services resolving `IRevitContext` from
  these scopes will now receive a context wrapping `Application` only (`Document` is `null`).
  Callers that assumed `IRevitContext` would not be resolvable in these handlers will need to
  handle a non-null but document-less context.
- `RevitUiPreEventHandler`/`RevitUiSingleEventHandler` now create `RevitUiContext` even when no
  document is open. `UiDocument` and `ActiveView` will return `null` in that case; code that
  previously relied on the null-context path to bail out early must now null-check these
  properties instead.

## Breaking Changes

- `IRevitContext.Document` is now `Document?` (nullable). Callers that previously treated
  `Document` as always non-null must add null checks.
- `IRevitUiContext.ActiveView` is now `View?` (nullable). Same requirement.
- `RevitDbApp` now registers `IGlobalRevitContext` automatically. Add-ins that registered it
  manually in `OnConfigure` will encounter a duplicate registration.

author: scottschreckengaust
body:
## Summary
Resolves issue #34 in the STACK cluster: unifies the stack's KMS strategy and makes the dead-letter queue observable.

## Root cause + evidence
In `lib/ministack-stack.ts`:
- **Inconsistent KMS strategy** — the Lambda log group used a customer-managed `kms.Key` (with rotation + a scoped key policy), while the DLQ used `sqs.QueueEncryption.KMS_MANAGED` (the `aws/sqs` AWS-managed alias). Two encryption philosophies sat side by side, with comments saying only "KMS-encrypted", not why.
- **Silent DLQ** — the DLQ had no consumer or alarm, so failed async Lambda invocations accumulated unnoticed.

## The fix
- **Unify on customer-managed CMKs.** Added a dedicated rotation-enabled `kms.Key` (`DoublerDlqKey`) and switched the DLQ to `sqs.QueueEncryption.KMS` + `encryptionMasterKey`. Both data stores now share one consistent, rotated, policy-controllable key strategy. A *separate* key (rather than reusing the log key) keeps each key's resource policy scoped to a single purpose. The "why" is documented inline. Synth/cdk-nag stays clean (no new findings, no suppression needed).
- **DLQ depth alarm.** Added a `cloudwatch.Alarm` on the queue's `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible` (MAXIMUM over a 1-min period, `GreaterThanThreshold` 0, `treatMissingData: NOT_BREACHING`) so any failed invocation surfaces.

## Testing
- `npm run build` — pass.
- `JEST_TIER=unit npx jest` — 44 pass. Added fine-grained assertions: DLQ encrypted by a CMK (`KmsMasterKeyId` is an `Fn::GetAtt`, not `alias/aws/sqs`) with >=2 rotated CMKs present; a CloudWatch Alarm on `AWS/SQS` `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible`, `GreaterThanThreshold` 0. Written to fail-first against the old code, then pass.
- `npm run synth` — succeeds; **cdk-nag (AwsSolutions) clean**, no new findings.
- `npm run test:unit -- -u` — snapshot updated and diff inspected: only the DLQ `KmsMasterKeyId` (alias → CMK ref), the new `DoublerDlqKey`, and the new `DoublerDlqDepthAlarm` resource moved. Nothing else.
- Integration tier = CI only. Mutation untouched (no lambda change).
- pre-commit (`eslint`, `tsc`, `prettier`, gitleaks, etc.) — all pass.

## Dependencies / related

author: chrisrogers37
body:
Closes #425.

## Why

The Python `tmux_socket_for_bot` (`claudlobby/paths.py`, used by `doctor`, `status`, `move_bot`) returned `""` when a bot.conf had no `TMUX_SOCKET`/`BOT_SERVICE`, while its **bash twin** (`lib/lib-common.sh`) fail-fasts under `FLEET_NAME`. A misconfigured bot resolved differently across the two paths, and the diagnostics could silently resolve a reconstructed socket instead of surfacing the misconfig (flagged by astrid during #423/#424).

## What

Mirror the bash guard in the Python helper. When neither field resolves:

- **`FLEET_NAME` set** → `raise ValueError` (fail-fast). An empty socket in a real fleet is a misconfigured bot; a bare socket would collide across fleets and reintroduce the shared-server SPOF. Twin of the bash guard's `return 1` + `refusing` stderr.
- **`FLEET_NAME` unset** (CLI / pre-fleet) → return `""`, caller decides its own fallback (unchanged — no regression to CLI usage).

The guard keys on the `FLEET_NAME` env exactly like the bash SSOT, so the twins can't drift. The three callers handle the raise:

| Caller | Behavior on raise |
|--------|-------------------|
| `doctor.py` | Records a `bot-sockets` **fail** finding so the misconfig is *surfaced* (not reported healthy), then falls back to `service_name` so the sweep continues |
| `status.py` | Falls back to the canonical service socket so one bad bot doesn't blank the dashboard |
| `move_bot.py` | Preserves its tolerant empty → default-socket pre-flight |

Exactly 3 production callers; all handled. No socket-binding path bypasses the SSOT.

## Validation (TDD)

- **5 Python-twin guard tests** in `tests/test_lifecycle_sockets.py` (`TestPythonSocketResolution`) — resolve from `TMUX_SOCKET`, fall back to `BOT_SERVICE`, raise on empty+`FLEET_NAME`, raise on missing conf+`FLEET_NAME`, return `""` without `FLEET_NAME` — parity with the bash twin in the same file. Watched them fail (RED) before implementing.
- **doctor regression**: `test_surfaces_misconfigured_bot_when_fleet_name_set` asserts the `bot-sockets` fail finding is emitted (not silently reconstructed). RED→GREEN verified.
- **status regression**: `test_survives_misconfigured_bot_when_fleet_name_set` — `_check_tmux_sessions` doesn't crash. RED verified by stashing only the catch.
- Existing doctor tests pinned to a deterministic `FLEET_NAME` (they model CLI usage).
- **Full suite: 841 passed.** The 2 failures (`test_no_cross_contamination`, `test_finds_bots_with_conf`) are unrelated and fail identically on clean `main` (env artifacts: checkout path contains a bot name; clock/TZ window math).

## Workflow

`/simplify` (4 lenses). **Applied:** flattened the helper's parse + removed a dead `except OSError` no-op; doctor now *surfaces* the misconfig (altitude fix — silent reconstruction would report a misconfigured bot as healthy, contradicting the issue). **Skipped:** a `tmux_socket_for_bot_or` wrapper (would fork a second resolution path — violates consolidate-don't-fork; the 3 fallbacks differ and belong per-site, matching the bash twin which also consumes the failure per-site).

**Follow-up candidate (out of scope):** Python has no shared `bot_conf_get` (bash does) — the bot.conf line-parse idiom is duplicated across `paths.py`, `status.py:_read_service_label`, and `move_bot.py` with inconsistent quote/`export` handling. A shared reader would close that Python/bash divergence.

Human merges (no self-merge).

## Summary

Fixes widespread gene-page 404s on the live site and the related auto-linking gaps. Three concerns:

1. **Workflow reliability** (`generate-pages.yaml`) — the regeneration PR was created as a draft and auto-closed after 1 hour with no auto-merge, so newly added gene reviews had their YAML on `main` but their rendered HTML never published (→ 404s). This removes the stale-close, creates the PR ready-for-review with **auto-merge** enabled (matching `monarch-initiative/dismech`), adds a **safety guard** that aborts if anything outside the generated-artifact allowlist is staged (the bot can never commit source), and fixes trigger paths (`render_projects.py`, nested `projects/**/*.md`).
2. **Backlog cleanup** — renders and commits the **323 gene reviews** that had YAML on `main` but no HTML, resolving the live 404s (additions only; no churn to existing pages).
3. **Case-variant gene auto-linking** (`render_projects.py` + tests, `BGC.md`) — prose like `PqsB`/`EryCIII`/worm `CHE-2` now auto-links to the lowercase gene-symbol directories via two targeted, collision-free rules (no false positives on words like `many`/`app`). ~858 previously-missed links resolved. `BGC.md` drops raw `genes/...` paths in favor of auto-linking.

Full diagnosis and retrospective: #1552.

## Validation

- `render_projects` tests + doctests, ruff, and mypy pass locally (69 tests).
- Safety-guard regex unit-tested: every generated artifact passes; every source path (`*.yaml`, `*-notes.md`, `src/`, `projects/*.md`, schema) is rejected.

author: vorobiovd
body:
## What

Opt-in flag `AIR_MA_COORDINATOR_MODEL` (e.g. `haiku`) routes the multiagent coordinator to a cheaper/faster model.

## Why it's safe

The MA coordinator is a **pure delegate-and-relay** layer — `coordinator.md` TURN 3 Part A outputs the verifier's review **verbatim**; the **verifier is the synthesizer**. So a cheaper coordinator can't degrade synthesis — its only job is faithful relay.

**Relay-fidelity A/B (2026-06-19), Haiku vs Sonnet coordinator, same PRs:**

| run | verifier delivered | coordinator relayed | dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sonnet ×2 | 9, 5 | 9, 5 | 0 |
| Haiku ×2 | 11, 7 | 11, 7 | **0** |

0 findings dropped, gate verdict unchanged. Run-to-run finding differences (incl. a one-off missed finding) traced to **upstream specialist/verifier nondeterminism** — coordinator-independent.

## Design

- Routes to a **separate** `air-coordinator-ma-<alias>` agent (setup.py step 4c) so a per-repo opt-in never mutates the shared default coordinator other callers use.
- Unset / `sonnet` / unknown value → falls back to the standard `air-coordinator-ma` (fail-safe).
- `narrow_env` passes the flag to the setup subprocess so the tiered agent is created before the run routes to it.
- Fixed the hardcoded `via air-coordinator-ma` log line to show the actual coordinator.

## Benefit

~15% lower wall-time (idle-wakes get cheap/fast) + shorter gaps evict the runtime's 5-min prompt cache less. (The cache TTL itself is **not settable** in managed agents — no `cache_control` field in agent/session create; the 1h TTL is raw-Messages-API-only.)

**Not a gate-safety change** — specialists + verifier unchanged. Opt-in, default off.

## Tests

5 new routing tests in test-multiagent.py; full managed suite green (233 passing). Docs in CLAUDE.md + managed/README.md. Anonymized.

author: jkennedyvz
body: Adds experimental media handling around `read_file`, centered on video frame extraction while consolidating the higher-level optional install surface behind `media` extras. > [!IMPORTANT] > Per the LangChain [alpha API policy](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/versioning#alpha-apis), this feature is experimental and subject to changes. It should be used cautiously in production environments while we learn from real media-read workflows. ## Why Video support now spans more than the SDK's low-level frame extractor. The PR keeps the decoder lazy and optional, but aligns user-facing packages around a single media capability: - `deepagents-code[media]` installs the media dependencies used for video frame extraction (`av` and `pillow`). - `deepagents-talon[media]` replaces the separate speech/video install paths by combining local voice transcription dependencies with `deepagents-code[media]`. - Deep Agents Code extras discovery classifies `media` as a standalone extra, so `/install` and extras status output point users at one media install target. - Talon docs, the Talon Docker image, and affected lockfiles now use `--extra media`. Direct SDK usage still gates the frame extractor on optional video dependencies, but the higher-level package story is now `media` wherever media features are bundled. ## Behavior with media/video dependencies installed When the optional media/video dependencies are available, `read_file` treats video reads as frame-extraction requests: - `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.webm`, and `.mkv` are decoded into sampled JPEG frames instead of sending raw video bytes to the model. - `offset` is interpreted as seconds into the source video. - `limit` is interpreted as the number of seconds to sample; omitting it uses the existing default `read_file` window of 100 seconds. - Sampling remains fixed at the middleware level, so agents narrow or widen the inspected window through `offset`/`limit` rather than choosing a sampling rate per call. - The `ToolMessage` stays text-only and reports the sampled frame count; sampled image blocks are attached in a synthetic follow-up human message so provider tool-output rules stay intact. Resource controls cover raw input size, frame count, emitted bytes, decode time, and frame dimensions. Oversized sampled frames are downscaled before JPEG encoding instead of rejecting normal high-resolution videos. ## Behavior without the dependencies installed When the optional dependencies are unavailable, frame extraction stays dormant: - `read_file` does not attempt video decoding. - Existing video files continue through the generic multimodal content-block path. - `.mkv` is read as binary by backends and returned as a generic file block instead of sampled video frames. - The `read_file` tool help keeps the previous text/image/PDF guidance instead of describing video seconds-based pagination. The goal is to preserve existing behavior unless the media/video dependencies are present. ## Example

body: ## Summary Fixes a bug in heuristic triage where capture text like **"next Thursday"** could assign a due date a full week too late. ## Problem `detectDate` in `lib/ai/triage-agent.ts` treated any `"next "` match as requiring at least 7 days out: ```ts if (lower.includes("next")) { delta = delta <= 0 ? delta + 7 : delta; if (delta < 7) delta += 7; // always pushed to next calendar week } ``` When the named weekday was still ahead in the current week (e.g. Monday → "next Thursday"), `delta` was already 3, but the extra `+7` made it 10 days. ## Fix - Capture the matched prefix (`by` / `on` / `next` / `this`) from the regex. - For `next`, only add 7 days when the weekday has already passed this week (`delta <= 0`). - Otherwise keep the natural forward offset to the upcoming occurrence. ## Verification | Today | Text | Before | After | |-------|------|--------|-------| | Monday | next Thursday | 10 days | 3 days | | Friday | next Monday | 10 days | 3 days | | Monday | next Monday | 7 days | 7 days (unchanged) | | Thursday | by Friday | 1 day | 1 day (unchanged) | `pnpm typecheck` passes. author: sebtardif
body:
## Summary

Two bugs in `LLVMRustWriteOutputFile`:

1. **`EC.clear()` swallows DWO file open errors** (Fixes #493): `EC.clear()` was called immediately after constructing the DWO output stream, making the subsequent `if (EC)` check dead code. When `-Csplit-debuginfo=unpacked` is used with an invalid DWO path, rustc silently succeeds but produces missing `.dwo` files.

2. **PassManager leaked on error paths** (Fixes #495): `LLVMDisposePassManager(PMR)` was only called on the success path. Both error returns leaked the pass manager.

## Changes

- Remove the `EC.clear()` call so the DWO file open error is properly detected
- Add `LLVMDisposePassManager(PMR)` before each error return

The fix matches the pattern used for the primary output file (8 lines above) which correctly checks EC without clearing it first.
